# ============================================================
# Mimir - Environment Configuration Example
# ============================================================
# Copy this file to `.env` and fill in your values:
#     cp .env.example .env
#
# NEVER commit your `.env` file - it is gitignored.
# `.env.example` is a safe, secret-free template that IS committed.
# Values below are defaults/examples only.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Core / Daemon
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Where Mimir stores its data (SurrealDB, sessions, the Cortex).
# Default: ~/.mimir
#MIMIR_HOME=

# Port the daemon + GUI listen on. Default: 8420
#MIMIR_PORT=8420

# Log level: debug | info | warn | error. Default: info
#MIMIR_LOG_LEVEL=info

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Encryption (REQUIRED)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Encrypts your provider API keys at rest in SurrealDB.
# Generate one with:  openssl rand -hex 32
MIMIR_ENCRYPTION_KEY=change-me-to-a-random-secret

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# SurrealDB (the Cortex / brain store)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Connection to the SurrealDB companion service.
SURREAL_URL=ws://localhost:8000/rpc
SURREAL_USER=root
SURREAL_PASSWORD=root
SURREAL_NAMESPACE=mimir
SURREAL_DATABASE=mimir

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Managed SurrealDB sidecar credentials (REQUIRED for persistent installs)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# When Mimir runs its own managed SurrealDB sidecar against a persistent
# data path (both docker-compose files do this: /data/surreal on the
# mimir_data volume; a local install does it whenever MIMIR_SURREAL_DATA
# is set or defaults under MIMIR_HOME), these variables MUST be set and
# the password MUST stay the same across restarts. If MIMIR_SURREAL_PASS
# is unset, the sidecar generates a random per-run password instead, and
# a data directory created under that password rejects every later run
# (the F19 lockout). Generate one long random password and keep it:
#     openssl rand -hex 32
# Never commit a real value; .env is gitignored.
#MIMIR_SURREAL_USER=root
#MIMIR_SURREAL_PASS=

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Provider API keys (BYOK)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Referenced via {env:VAR} interpolation in mimir.json.
# Add only the providers you use. Alternatively, store keys via
# `mimir auth login` (saved encrypted to auth.json) instead of env.
#OPENAI_API_KEY=
#ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
#GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY=
#OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
#XAI_API_KEY=
#MISTRAL_API_KEY=
#GROQ_API_KEY=
#DASHSCOPE_API_KEY=
#DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=

# Local models (Ollama / llama.cpp / vLLM) need no key, just the URL:
#OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Sandbox (on-the-fly isolation)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#DOCKER_HOST=

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Remote access / tunnel (mobile + off-machine) - configured later
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#MIMIR_RELAY_URL=
#MIMIR_TUNNEL_TOKEN=

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Engine updates (signed manifests, N7)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Release public key for verifying engine update manifests. This is a
# PUBLIC key, not a secret: it is pinned here so installs refuse engine
# manifests that are unsigned or signed by any other key. Do not change
# it unless the release signing key is rotated and the manifest in
# engines/bin is re-signed with the new key.
MIMIR_ENGINE_PUBKEY=uJQqyXeyx49sJYWeVttFPX9JnHuyIWCh/fk3CLqvuf4=

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Telemetry
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Anonymized usage telemetry (counts, model/tool used, success/error rates, latency)
# to help improve Mimir. ON by default. No code/content/prompts are collected unless
# you explicitly opt in elsewhere. Turn off here or in the GUI Privacy settings.
MIMIR_TELEMETRY=true
# Set to false to disable all telemetry (air-gapped / fully private).

FILE: .github/workflows/ci.yml

name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version: "1.26.x"
      - name: Check formatting
        run: |
          unformatted="$(gofmt -l .)"
          if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then
            echo "These files are not gofmt-clean:"
            echo "$unformatted"
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Vet
        run: go vet ./...
      - name: Test
        run: go test -race ./...

  govulncheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version: "1.26.x"
      - name: govulncheck (non-blocking)
        run: go run golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest ./...

FILE: .golangci.yml
==============================================================================
version: "2"

# Mimir lint baseline (golangci-lint v2).
#
# Every linter stays enabled. The only configuration is a short list of
# errcheck function exclusions for call sites where the error is
# provably meaningless, so real unchecked errors elsewhere still fail
# the run. In particular this config does NOT exclude any parsing or
# decoding call (json.Unmarshal, fmt.Sscanf and friends are checked in
# code, fail closed), and it has no path-based exclusions.
linters:
  settings:
    errcheck:
      exclude-functions:
        # Writes to the terminal, stderr, and strings.Builder cannot be
        # recovered from at the call site: a failed terminal print has
        # nowhere to report itself, and strings.Builder writes never
        # fail. Writes whose failure matters (HTTP response streams)
        # are checked in code instead of relying on this exclusion.
        - fmt.Fprint
        - fmt.Fprintf
        - fmt.Fprintln
        # Deferred Close on files, listeners, and HTTP response bodies:
        # by the time a deferred Close runs, the operation it belonged
        # to has already reported its own result, and a Close error on
        # a read side carries no actionable information. Operations
        # whose success depends on the close (for example writing an
        # email body) check the returned error in code. errcheck names
        # concrete receiver types separately from the interface, so the
        # concrete io.Closer implementations used with defer are listed
        # alongside it; they are the same idiom, not separate policy.
        - (io.Closer).Close
        - (*os.File).Close
        - (net.Listener).Close
        - (*crypto/tls.Conn).Close
        # SMTP Quit sends the polite goodbye after the message writer
        # has already been closed and its error checked; a failed Quit
        # cannot unsend or corrupt the delivered message. Same class as
        # Close above.
        - (*net/smtp.Client).Quit

# CHANGELOG: Mimir

## 2026-10-20: Repo standard jump-back-in set added
- STATUS.md, DECISIONS.md, docs/RUNBOOK.md, CHANGELOG.md, and
  docs/MAP.md created, completing the standard file set on main
  (TODO, IDEA, PLAN, ENDGOAL, and docs/RULES.md landed earlier the
  same day, with the PLAN, TODO cross-reference, and IDEA record
  format upgrades).

## 2026-10-19: Audit fix rounds closed, code verdict SHIP
- David's fix round plus two audit_code passes closed the code
  findings from the 2026-10-18 audit: approval fails closed, steer is
  session-owned, relay pairing hardened with expiry and replay
  rejection, engine updates are https-only with ed25519 manifest
  signature verification implemented, serve auth refuses an
  unauthenticated non-loopback bind, and the compiled-in SurrealDB
  defaults are gone.
- Final state: main at 76e1be1, UI branch engine/gjallarhorn-ui at
  9d1cae0; go build, go vet, gofmt clean, go test -race green on all
  packages, golangci-lint clean, gitleaks gate run (proof: goal
  workspace mimir-fixes-2026-10-19.md, mimir-audit-code-2026-10-19.md,
  mimir-audit-code-2-2026-10-19.md).
- Left open on purpose, tracked in TODO Phases 1 to 4: F22 rotation
  and history purge (David's go), engine signing activation (release
  key), and the operations hardening checks.

## 2026-10-18: First full audit of the pushed core
- Full-tree audit of main at 0c9d034 found 29 findings, 3 critical
  (proof: goal workspace mimir-audit-2026-10-18.md). The findings
  drove the 2026-10-19 fix round above.

## 2026-10-17: Core systems pushed to main by David
- The 7-phase SDLC engine, Huginn-Decider, GitIngest plus the
  Yggdrasil Mind Map into the Cortex, the Epistemic Critic and the
  mimir audit CLI, and the 12+ provider catalog landed on main in
  commit 0c9d034 (proof: TODO items T-0.2 to T-0.6).

## 2026-09-29: Go core verified by repo review
- Repo review verified the shipped core: agent tool loop with a
  fail-closed policy gate, Norse personas (odin, thor, loki,
  heimdall), file memory plus SurrealDB Cortex memory, OTP auth, and
  the web UI on :8420, with build clean and tests green except one
  stale test (proof: TODO T-0.1).

# DECISIONS: Mimir

## 2026-10-19: Engine signing stays inactive until a release key exists
- **Decided:** Ed25519 manifest signature verification is implemented and shipped, but signing is NOT active until David generates a release key offline and MIMIR_ENGINE_PUBKEY is pinned for installs.
- **Why:** A signing system with no real key held by the owner proves nothing; activation is a key custody act, not a code change.
- **Supersedes:** none
- **By:** David (activation step held for him; recorded in TODO Phase 3)

## 2026-10-19: Approval fails closed, everywhere
- **Decided:** RequireApproval with no approver denies the action, on both the gate branch and the ModeEdit branch. Bypass modes waive approval requests, never explicit denies. The interactive shell (F1 posture) stays behind real approval; moving the interactive path to an argv-only jail is a product decision, parked, not a fix.
- **Why:** An approval gate that passes when nobody is there to approve is worse than no gate, because it looks like protection.
- **Supersedes:** the earlier inert approval behavior found in the 2026-10-18 audit
- **By:** David (fix round ordered 2026-10-19; posture note in the fix report)

## 2026-10-18: F22 history purge is held for David's explicit go
- **Decided:** The mail credential in this public repo's git history is treated as live until rotated at Titan Mail. The history purge and force push do NOT happen until David gives an explicit go, because the rewrite breaks his Windows clone and both branches (main and engine/gjallarhorn-ui) need re-syncing after it.
- **Why:** Rotation closes the exposure; the purge is destructive to every clone and is the owner's call to time.
- **Supersedes:** none
- **By:** David (held across four audits, 2026-10-18 to 2026-10-19; recorded in TODO Phase 1)

## 2026-10-15: Build 20 years ahead is the design law
- **Decided:** Every module is designed for the bottleneck that is coming: interface seams at change-prone boundaries (Executor interface, pluggable verify-check registry with targeted and full modes, the full mode stays the hard gate), operational limits as config in run-spec frontmatter with defaults, never compiled-in constants, and data formats carrying version fields.
- **Why:** Models, tools, and hardware will be replaced many times over the life of the harness; the seams are what let a module be swapped without rebuilding the system.
- **Supersedes:** none
- **By:** David (recorded in ~/AGENTS.md and the Mimir blueprint design-law section the same day)

## 2026-10-05: Mimir is standalone, and coding runs go unwatched
- **Decided:** Mimir is David's standalone autonomous coding harness, NOT part of the AlphaFlux SaaS, and stays out of AlphaFlux status updates. It was chosen over MiMo Desktop as the harness direction. Coding runs go start to finish without David watching; the GitHub-integrated harness plus the orchestrator agent keep the build moving and verify it is building correctly.
- **Why:** The harness is a product of its own with its own end goal (a plan-to-ship harness for everyone); folding it into a SaaS status stream would blur both.
- **Supersedes:** the earlier pattern of David coding with MiMo Desktop on his PC
- **By:** David

## 2026-09-30: The product model is 10 stages, unleashed at plan approval, with hard human gates at verify and ship
- **Decided:** A run moves through discover, contract, repo, research, architecture, build, verify, review, ship, handover. The human-guided part ends when the plan is approved; execution is unleashed from there, and it stops for a human at exactly two places: verify and ship.
- **Why:** Planning is where human judgment changes the outcome; execution is where watching adds nothing. The two gates keep shipping a human act.
- **Supersedes:** none
- **By:** David (the end goal model in the goal file, 2026-09-30)

## 2026-09-30: Knowledge is never silently overwritten
- **Decided:** Material the harness ingests lands in a typed knowledge mind map (edges: implements, depends_on, constrains, decided_because, contradicts, supersedes, part_of, learned_from). When two facts contradict, the map flags it and the user resolves it at the plan gate; a merge never silently overwrites.
- **Why:** A memory that quietly rewrites itself cannot be trusted as the record a later run plans against.
- **Supersedes:** none
- **By:** David (knowledge mind map requirement in the goal file, 2026-09-30)

## 2026-09-30: Open-core license model
- **Decided:** The Go harness control plane in this repo is provided openly so developers and teams can run, inspect, and integrate it. The precompiled engines in engines/bin are proprietary to Alpha Flux LLC under the attribution license in LICENSE-ENGINES.md and the NOTICE file.
- **Why:** The harness spreads by being open and inspectable; the engines are the commercial core and keep their attribution terms. (Entry recorded in this log on 2026-10-20 from the repo record: NOTICE and LICENSE-ENGINES.md.)
- **Supersedes:** none
- **By:** David (per NOTICE and LICENSE-ENGINES.md on main)

## 2026-09-29: Go toolchain is pinned
- **Decided:** The repo pins the Go toolchain (go.mod toolchain line, go1.26.9 at the 2026-10-19 audit). Tool versions are part of the gate; a stale linter or scanner is a finding, not a footnote.
- **Why:** A gate run with old tools proves less than it claims; the pin makes every machine prove the same thing. (Pin state verified in audit_code report 2, 2026-10-19.)
- **Supersedes:** none
- **By:** David (recorded in docs/RULES.md, Mimir specifics)

# Pinned release key (public, N7): engine updates must carry a manifest signed by this key.

  CMD wget --no-verbose --tries=1 --spider http://localhost:8420/health || exit 1
ENTRYPOINT ["mimir", "serve", "--addr=:8420"]

# ENDGOAL: Mimir

The end state this project exists to reach, in plain words. TODO.md
and PLAN.md are how we get here; this file is how we know we are
done. Work continues until this end goal is reached. When David
restates or extends the end goal, this file is updated the same day
and PLAN/TODO follow. Sourced from David's stated vision of
2026-09-30, his goal file, and the repo record.

## The end state
A person with a project to build installs Mimir and hands it the
work. Mimir guides them through planning: what the thing is, what
it must do, what already exists. A repository is created or linked
from their forge account, competitors and features are researched,
and the architecture is worked out with them. That is the
human-guided part, and it ends when they approve the plan.

From approval, Mimir runs on its own. It works the 10 stages
(discover, contract, repo, research, architecture, build, verify,
review, ship, handover) as an inspectable graph it can be watched
and steered through, start to finish, with nobody sitting over it.
It writes the code, verifies it against hard gates, and stops for a
human at exactly two places: verify and ship. Gate failures feed
back into the work until the work passes or the run escalates.

Everything Mimir reads along the way, the user's uploads, the repos
it ingests, the research it gathers, lands in a typed knowledge
mind map instead of sitting static in a folder. The map feeds
planning, research, building, and verification on this run and
every later one. When two facts contradict, the map flags it and
the user resolves it at the plan gate; nothing is silently
overwritten.

The harness is for everyone, not a private tool for David: the same
install that runs his projects runs anyone's, on their own machine,
against their own forge accounts and their own choice of model.

## How we will know it is reached
- A new user can install Mimir, register a forge account through
  the OAuth flow, link or create a repository, and start a run
  without David's help (today: OAuth registration is stalled,
  TODO T-6.1).
- A run with an approved plan goes from first stage to shipped
  code with no human watching, and the run itself writes the
  report artifact proving it (today: RunUnattended has no
  production caller, TODO T-2.2; no live end-to-end run has
  happened yet, TODO T-2.3).
- All 10 stages execute as the designed run graph with typed done
  gates at every stage and hard human gates at verify and ship
  (today: the graph is designed, not implemented, TODO T-6.4; the
  shipped engine runs a 7-phase SDLC inside runs).
- Uploaded material demonstrably lands in the mind map through the
  full pipeline (parse, extraction, deterministic dedupe, merge
  with contradiction flagging, integration receipt) and is used by
  later stages and later runs (today: GitIngest and the map exist
  in the Cortex, TODO T-0.4; the pipeline to spec is TODO T-6.3).
- Contradictions in the map surface to the user at the plan gate
  and are resolved there, never silently overwritten (trust rule
  from the goal file).
- Engine updates refuse unsigned or badly signed manifests
  (today: verification code shipped; no release key exists yet,
  TODO Phase 3).
- The repository history carries no live credential (today: F22 is
  open, TODO Phase 1).

## Not in the end state
- Mimir is a standalone project. It is NOT part of AlphaFlux, and
  the end state does not fold it into the AlphaFlux platform.
- Shipping is never fully hands-off: the human gates at verify and
  ship stay human in the end state. Unleashed execution begins at
  plan approval, not before it.
- Knowledge is never silently overwritten: contradiction resolution
  belongs to the user, not the merge.

   - The underlying intelligence, deterministic AST/BM25/sandbox, and bare-metal tensor/VSA engines are the proprietary intellectual property of **Alpha Flux LLC**:

     - **`mimir_alphaflux_engine`** (Source branch: `engine/alphaflux-core`) -- `Huginn-Decider` System-One routing, `Epistemic Critic` verification node, `7-Phase SDLC` gatekeeper, and `Impeccable + 4-Layer SEO/GEO` deterministic web auditor.

# PLAN: Mimir

The whole plan for Mimir, step by step. Sections are numbered (S1,
S2, ...) so TODO.md items can point at them: every TODO item carries a
stable ID and ends with (PLAN S<n>) naming the section it serves, and
each build step below names its TODO phase. When the plan changes,
this file changes first, then TODO.md follows. Facts only: what is
decided is stated, what is open is named as an open question. The
deep engineering plan lives in docs/PROJECT-MASTER-PLAN.md and the
granular engineering checklist in docs/MASTER-TODO.md;
docs/SKEPTICS-AUDIT.md separates working code from blueprint, and
this file follows the skeptics audit where they differ. Shelf repos
from the harvest (~/workspace/google-org-harvest/USE-IT.md) are
worked into the steps that use them, named on the step.

## S1: What Mimir is
Mimir is David's standalone autonomous coding harness: a local-first
agent that takes a project from plan to shipped code without him
watching. It is GitHub-integrated, runs coding runs start to finish
unattended, and keeps a typed knowledge mind map so uploaded material
integrates into the system instead of sitting static. The end goal
(ENDGOAL.md) is a plan-to-ship harness for everyone, not a private
tool for David only. Mimir is its own project; it is NOT part of
AlphaFlux.

The product model is David's 10 stages: discover, contract, repo,
research, architecture, build, verify, review, ship, handover. The
human-guided portion ends when the plan is approved; execution is
unleashed from there, with hard human gates at verify and ship.
Inside a run today, the shipped engine executes a 7-phase SDLC; the
10-stage run graph is designed and lands in S9 below.

## S2: Architecture
The grid: the Go control plane on main, one module per grid slot.

| Module | What it owns |
| :--- | :--- |
| cmd/mimir | CLI entry, subcommands, the mimir audit CLI |
| internal/agent | The agent loop, personas, steering, compaction |
| internal/policy | The fail-closed policy gate every action passes |
| internal/sdlc | The 7-phase SDLC engine inside runs |
| internal/decision | Huginn-Decider, the routing decider |
| internal/ingest | GitIngest and the Yggdrasil Mind Map |
| internal/cortex | Memory: file store and SurrealDB store |
| internal/critic | The Epistemic Critic |
| internal/llm | Provider clients behind one interface (12+ provider catalog in internal/config) |
| internal/runengine | The unattended run engine (on the scaffold branch until S5) |
| internal/engines | Engine updates: manifest, signature verification, platform binary resolution |
| internal/relay | Phone pairing and the E2EE relay |
| internal/server | HTTP server, auth, web UI on :8420 |
| internal/swarm | The multi-agent factory (merge only via Factory.ApproveMerge) |
| internal/tools | The tool set the agent can call |
| internal/tui | The terminal UI |
| internal/plugins | Unwired draft, superseded by the planned Wasm host |

Design law (David, 2026-10-15, build 20 years ahead): interface
seams at every change-prone boundary (Executor interface, pluggable
verify-check registry with targeted and full modes, the full mode
stays the hard gate), operational limits as config in run-spec
frontmatter with defaults, never compiled-in constants, and data
formats carrying version fields. Full law in docs/RULES.md.

Shelf at this seam: adk-go (Google's Agent Development Kit for Go)
is the dependency candidate for agent loops, tool wiring, and eval
at the seams this grid already owns, adapted only there, never as a
replacement for the policy gate or the SDLC engine (harvest verdict:
depend, Apache-2.0).

Planned stacks, not in the main tree today (docs/SKEPTICS-AUDIT.md):
Rust (Tyr-Core), Mojo (Mjolnir-Compute), and Flutter (Gjallarhorn-UI)
are blueprint; the engines ship as precompiled binaries in
engines/bin under LICENSE-ENGINES.md.

## S3: Step 1, ship and harden the Go core (TODO Phase 0)
Ship and harden the Go core: agent loop, policy gate, SDLC engine,
Decider, Mind Map, Critic, provider catalog, then the 2026-10-18 and
2026-10-19 audit fix rounds to a SHIP verdict. Done: main at
76e1be1, UI branch at 9d1cae0, gates green (build, vet, gofmt,
go test -race, golangci-lint, gitleaks gate). The run-engine scaffold
(T-0.14) was built and tested locally as part of this step; landing
it is S5.

## S4: Step 2, close the F22 secret exposure (TODO Phase 1)
Rotate the SMTP credential at Titan Mail, purge it from git history
and force push, then re-run gitleaks over the full history and
record a clean report. The rotation and the purge go-ahead are
David's; the purge breaks his Windows clone and both branches (main
and engine/gjallarhorn-ui) need re-syncing after it.

## S5: Step 3, land the run engine (TODO Phase 2)
Merge the run-engine-scaffold branch into main, give RunUnattended a
production caller, and run the first live end-to-end unattended run
against a real model endpoint (8B to 14B class; the model choice is
David's). Then close the v4 gap items (secret redaction in state
dumps, completion signal, network-namespace isolation, multi-language
verify gate) and land session-scoped steering for /api/mobile/steer.

Shelf at this step:
- substrate (agent-substrate): the zero-trust sandbox runtime whose
  architecture the Executor seam is retrofitted to: no credentials
  inside the sandbox, credentials injected at an egress gateway,
  per-agent identity, snapshot and resume of idle runs (harvest
  verdict: retrofit the architecture; run as-is only if a Kubernetes
  host tier joins).
- gVisor: the application kernel sandbox for running generated and
  actively distrusted code on server-side hosts (harvest verdict:
  take as-is, server side).
- go-git: repo operations inside runs (clone, commit, diff, history)
  become pure-Go library calls instead of shelling out to the git
  binary (harvest verdict: depend, upstream v6 line).
- go-github: the GitHub API client behind Mimir's own GitHub
  interface seam, deleting the hand-written GitHub plumbing
  (harvest verdict: depend, BSD-3-Clause).
- oss-fuzz-gen: the pattern for the verify loop: an LLM writes
  checks and fuzz targets, runs them, and iterates on measured
  results instead of a single pass; the blueprint for how the
  multi-language verify gate grows its check registry (harvest
  verdict: take for the dev pipeline).

## S6: Step 4, activate engine signing (TODO Phase 3)
David generates the ed25519 release key offline; pin

<div align="center">

# Mimir

The agent that remembers. A local-first autonomous coding harness
that takes a project from plan to shipped code, with a knowledge
mind map that keeps what it learns.

![Language: Go](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-Go-00ADD8)
![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.2.0--dev-lightgrey)
![Repo](https://img.shields.io/badge/repo-public-brightgreen)

</div>

**Plan:** [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) · **Tasks:** [TODO.md](TODO.md) · **Ideas:** [IDEA.md](IDEA.md) · **Build rules:** [docs/RULES.md](docs/RULES.md)

Deep docs: [docs/PROJECT-MASTER-PLAN.md](docs/PROJECT-MASTER-PLAN.md) ·
[docs/MASTER-TODO.md](docs/MASTER-TODO.md) ·
[docs/SKEPTICS-AUDIT.md](docs/SKEPTICS-AUDIT.md) (working code vs
blueprint, kept honest)

Named for Mimir of Norse mythology, the rememberer who guards the
well of wisdom beneath Yggdrasil. Domain: mimirmind.com.

## What it is

Mimir is a standalone autonomous coding harness written in Go with a
SurrealDB-backed memory (the Cortex). An agent loop works through a
fail-closed policy gate, routes decisions through the Huginn-Decider,
ingests repositories into a GitIngest Yggdrasil Mind Map it can query
across sessions, critiques its own work with an Epistemic Critic, and
runs a 7-phase SDLC inside each run. It serves a web UI on :8420 and
targets 12+ model providers behind one client interface.

The end goal is bigger than the current build: a plan-to-ship
harness for everyone, running David's 10-stage model (discover,
contract, repo, research, architecture, build, verify, review, ship,
handover), unleashed at plan approval with hard human gates at
verify and ship. The unattended run engine that carries that model
is built and tested on a local branch and lands per TODO Phase 2.

What is NOT built yet, stated plainly per docs/SKEPTICS-AUDIT.md:
the Rust (Tyr-Core), Mojo (Mjolnir-Compute), and Flutter
(Gjallarhorn-UI) stacks are blueprint in the main tree; engines ship
as precompiled binaries under LICENSE-ENGINES.md.

## Quickstart

Requires Go 1.26+ (the repo pins toolchain go1.26.9).

```powershell
# Build the single binary
go build -o bin/mimir.exe ./cmd/mimir

# Bootstrap the local decision model
.\bin\mimir.exe setup

# Ingest any local repo or GitHub URL into the Mind Map in the Cortex
.\bin\mimir.exe ingest .
.\bin\mimir.exe ingest https://github.com/David2024patton/Mimir

# List built-in providers and subscription tiers
.\bin\mimir.exe providers

# View or switch the 7-phase SDLC board (agile | waterfall | devops)
.\bin\mimir.exe sdlc

# Launch the interactive TUI
.\bin\mimir.exe

# Launch the TUI plus the live web UI on :8420
.\bin\mimir.exe --web
```

## The grid: module map

| Module | What it owns |
| :--- | :--- |
| cmd/mimir | CLI entry, subcommands, the mimir audit CLI |
| internal/agent | The agent loop, Norse personas, steering, compaction |
| internal/policy | The fail-closed policy gate |
| internal/sdlc | The 7-phase SDLC engine inside runs |
| internal/decision | Huginn-Decider, the routing decider |
| internal/ingest | GitIngest and the Yggdrasil Mind Map |
| internal/cortex | Memory: file store and SurrealDB store |
| internal/critic | The Epistemic Critic |
| internal/llm | Provider clients behind one interface |
| internal/config | The 12+ provider catalog and discovery |
| internal/runengine | The unattended run engine (scaffold branch) |
| internal/engines | Engine updates and signature verification |
| internal/relay | Phone pairing and the E2EE relay |
| internal/server | HTTP server, auth, web UI on :8420 |
| internal/swarm | The multi-agent factory |
| internal/tools | The tool set the agent can call |
| internal/tui | The terminal UI |
| internal/plugins | Unwired draft, superseded by the planned Wasm host |

## 2026-10-20 (evening EDT): https://github.com/eyaltoledano/claude-task-master
- **What it is:** A real, actively maintained open-source tool (about 28,300 stars, 92 releases), not a prompt dump: an AI task-management system for AI-driven development that drops into Cursor, Lovable, Windsurf, Roo, VS Code, and Claude Code via an MCP server (36 tools) or a CLI (npm package task-master-ai). Core flow: start from a detailed PRD (recommended at .taskmaster/docs/prd.txt), parse it into a structured task graph (tasks.json) with dependencies, priorities, and test strategies; expand any task into subtasks on demand; run a complexity analysis pass that scores tasks and recommends which to expand; ask for the next task and get the dependency-aware next unblocked item; organize parallel workstreams with tags and move tasks across tags with or without their dependencies. It defines three model roles (main, research, fallback) swappable across many providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Perplexity, xAI, OpenRouter, plus Claude Code and Codex CLI with no API key), and a built-in research command that answers with project context. One notable engineering detail: selective MCP tool loading to control context cost (all 36 tools about 21,000 tokens, standard 15 about 10,000, core 7 about 5,000).
- **License:** MIT with Commons Clause. Use, modify, distribute, and sell products built USING Task Master are allowed; selling Task Master itself, offering it as a hosted service, or creating competing products based on it are NOT allowed.
- **Lulu's answer:** RETROFIT the patterns for (B), REFERENCE for (A), TAKE nothing. For Mimir the decomposition model is directly on point: PRD-first intake (a detailed spec produces a better task graph), expand-task as an explicit operation, complexity scoring that decides where to decompose further, and next-task resolution over a dependency graph are patterns Mimir's planning layer should match in its own Go code. The code itself stays out: the Commons Clause bars competing products and hosted services, which is exactly Mimir's shape, so patterns yes, source no. For the AlphaFlux builder it is reference grade: the PRD-first lesson (a detailed customer brief yields a better build plan) and the tiered tool-loading trick (expose agents only the tool subset the step needs) both transfer as ideas.

## 2026-10-20 (evening EDT): https://github.com/elder-plinius/CL4R1T4S/tree/main/REPLIT
- **What it is:** The REPLIT folder holds exactly one file, Replit_Initial_Code_Generation_Prompt.md: Replit's one-shot initial code generation prompt. Input contract: a goal, a task description, and success criteria; output: the complete source of a working app in a single response. Structure: an Input Description section; Output Rules covering directory structure (minimal, flat, frontend and backend coexist rather than splitting into service folders), complete code per file with comments on complex logic, and security hygiene (avoid SQL injection and XSS); a strict markdown output format with a `# Thoughts` section, then a `# directory_structure` section as a JSON array of {path, status: "new" or "overwritten"}, then each file's full contents under a `## file_path:` heading; code-generation rules stating the runtime contract up front (unprivileged Linux container, bind 0.0.0.0, frontend on port 5000, backend on port 8000, API keys from environment variables with fallback, no Docker); development constraints (favor web apps, SVG first for graphics, named asset libraries: Feather Icons and Font Awesome, Bootstrap, Fabric.js and Two.js, Chart.js and D3.js, tone-js); a restricted-files deny list (never generate package.json or requirements.txt because the platform owns them, never emit binary assets like images, audio, or fonts, use libraries and CDNs instead); and a worked example output for a TODO app.
- **License:** The repo carries AGPL-3.0 on the collection; the content is Replit's proprietary prompt, published without Replit's permission; the repo license does not clear the underlying IP. Study only, copy nothing.
- **Lulu's answer:** REFERENCE for both, RETROFIT the output contract. For (A) the manifest-first format is the extractable gem: the generator emits a machine-readable file manifest (path plus new/overwritten status) before any file bodies, which is exactly the contract an AlphaFlux builder needs to show the customer a plan, diff against an existing site, and apply changes safely. The platform-owns-the-manifest deny list (package.json and friends) is the same seam. For (B) it is a reference point only: Mimir's staged SDLC with hard gates is deliberately not a one-shot generator, but this prompt is a clean model for a greenfield scaffolding subtask inside a stage.
- **Techniques worth extracting:**
  - Success criteria are part of the input contract, stated before any generation.
  - Manifest-first output: a JSON directory structure with a per-file status flag precedes all file contents, so a machine can plan, diff, and verify.
  - A separate Thoughts section keeps reasoning out of the artifacts.
  - State the runtime contract (ports, bind host, privileges, available tooling) inside the prompt instead of letting the model guess the environment.
  - Deny list of platform-owned files so the generator and the platform never fight over the same artifacts.
  - Asset strategy: vector and library/CDN assets only, no generated binaries.
  - One complete worked example of the output format at the end of the prompt.
- **Went to:** this file (verdict on record)

## 2026-10-20 (evening EDT): https://github.com/elder-plinius/CL4R1T4S/blob/main/LOVABLE%2FLovable_2.0.txt
- **What it is:** The leaked Lovable 2.0 system prompt, 353 lines, internally dated 2025-04-25. One file in elder-plinius/CL4R1T4S, a collection of extracted system prompts from most major AI products (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Cursor, Devin, Manus, Replit, Vercel v0, and more). The Lovable prompt is a complete app-builder agent spec in XML-tagged sections: a `<role>` block (AI editor with live iframe preview and console-log access); a `<response_format>` block with a triage flow (check whether the request is already implemented before editing; answer questions without touching code; edit only on explicit action words); one single `<lov-code>` block per response wrapping ALL changes, with `<lov-write>`, `<lov-rename>`, `<lov-delete>`, and `<lov-add-dependency>` tags inside it; two full worked examples showing the exact expected output shape; a `<guidelines>` block pinning the stack (React, Tailwind CSS always, shadcn/ui, lucide-react icons, recharts, @tanstack/react-query in object format, errors left to bubble up instead of try/catch, "do not overengineer, don't do more than the user asks"); a `<tools>` block (never name tools to users); per-integration blocks for OpenAI models, Perplexity, and Runware (API keys go in Supabase Edge Function secrets, or a temporary user-entered key field if not connected, never hardcoded); a `<supabase-integration>` gate that refuses to write ANY backend code until the user connects the native Supabase integration; a `<session_replay>` block injecting the user's mouse movements, clicks, and text selections as structured context; and a closing micro-lesson section on JSX quote escaping.
- **License:** The repo carries AGPL-3.0, but the file's content is Lovable's proprietary system prompt, published without Lovable's permission; the repo license does not clear the underlying IP. Study only, copy nothing.
- **Lulu's answer:** REFERENCE for both, with techniques worth RETROFIT into our own original prompts. For (A) this is the closest public blueprint of how the market-leading builder agent behaves: the triage-before-editing flow, the one atomic change block with a file plan up front and a completeness checklist before closing (all imports present, dependencies installed), and the integration gate that stops and routes the user through a native connection instead of generating backend code against missing infrastructure all map directly onto the AlphaFlux builder and its iframe-guided provider setup. For (B) the response discipline (already-implemented check, one-sentence plain summary after the technical block) is a useful pattern for Mimir's user-facing reporting.
- **Techniques worth extracting:**
  - Triage first: verify the request is not already implemented; answer pure questions with no code changes; treat action words as the edit trigger.
  - One atomic change block per turn containing every file operation (write, rename, delete, add dependency), opened with a step-by-step file plan and closed with a completeness review (imports resolve, packages installed).
  - Few-shot by construction: embed two complete worked examples of the desired output format inside the prompt itself.
  - Pin one opinionated stack (framework, CSS system, component library, icon set, chart lib, data-fetching convention) to cut model variance.
  - Secrets pattern: keys live in the platform's secret store; fallback is a temporary user-entered field; keys are never written into generated code.
  - Integration gate: when a capability needs a connected platform service, refuse to generate around it and walk the user through connecting it first.
  - Dynamic context sections: structured session replay (clicks, selections) injected into the prompt alongside the code state.
  - Named failure-mode micro-lessons appended to the prompt as their own sections (the JSX quote-escaping section is the model).
  - Let errors bubble back to the agent instead of swallowing them in generated try/catch, so failures stay visible and fixable.
- **Went to:** this file (verdict on record)

## 2026-10-20 (evening EDT): https://github.com/freestyle-sh/Adorable
- **What it is:** An open-source Lovable clone where every project is a pair of persistent Freestyle VMs: a dev VM the agent edits (hot-reloading dev server behind a preview URL, terminal sessions) and a production VM created on first publish. Publishing rsyncs source to the production VM in about 4 seconds; every publish snapshots the dev VM so any earlier release can be restored as a rollback. A pre-built base snapshot (template cloned, dependencies installed, dev server already compiled) makes a new project's preview live in about 1.7 seconds. State is JSON files on the dev VM; there is no database. Stack: Next.js (App Router, TypeScript, Turbopack), Vercel AI SDK, Tailwind + shadcn/ui, Freestyle VMs. 829 stars, 318 forks, 277 commits, created 2025-04-10.
- **License:** MIT

# Norse Memory

## Design Philosophy

Memory is not linear. It branches, loops, connects, and decays - then reconstitutes from fragments into something new. Norse Memory embraces the idea that knowledge is living architecture: structured yet organic, ancient yet always becoming. Every composition should feel like a diagram of thought itself - a system of interconnected nodes where meaning emerges from relationship, not from any single element. The craftsmanship must be immaculate, every curve and junction placed with the precision of a master calligrapher working in iron.

The visual language draws from two wells: the stark geometric clarity of Norse knotwork (endless lines that weave over and under, never breaking) and the clinical precision of neural network diagrams (nodes, edges, signal paths). Forms interlock like the ribs of a Viking longship - structural beauty born from function. Negative space is not empty; it is the silence between thoughts, the pause where memory consolidates. Every element earns its place through structural necessity. Colors are few and deliberate: deep midnight tones against warm amber or copper, like firelight on ancient metal.

Typography is treated as architecture, not decoration. Letterforms are geometric, monospaced or near-monospaced, carrying the weight of carved runes while maintaining contemporary precision. Text appears sparingly - a name, a glyph, a coordinate. It anchors the composition like a cartographer's label on an unexplored territory. The overall impression should be of something meticulously crafted over countless hours, the product of deep expertise where every pixel, every stroke, every spatial relationship has been labored over with obsessive care.

Scale and rhythm follow the logic of concentric rings - the way memory radiates outward from a core experience, connecting to adjacent memories, gradually fading at the periphery. The center is dense and deliberate; the edges breathe. This creates a natural focal hierarchy without relying on traditional size-based emphasis. The result is an artifact that could be a scientific diagram, a brand mark, or a fragment of an imaginary codex - ambiguous in category but undeniable in craft.

"""Mímir logo - over/under knot rendering, final museum-grade."""
import math
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

W, H = 2400, 2400
BG = (6, 10, 20)
COPPER = (210, 130, 60)
COPPER_H = (240, 178, 100)
COPPER_D = (130, 75, 30)
TEAL = (50, 220, 200)
TEAL_D = (28, 125, 112)
WHITE = (240, 244, 248)
GRAY_L = (140, 150, 168)
GRAY = (100, 112, 130)
DARK = (18, 24, 38)

FONT_DIR = r"C:\Users\David\.config\opencode\skills\canvas-design\canvas-fonts"

def font(name, size):
    try:
        return ImageFont.truetype(f"{FONT_DIR}\\{name}", size)
    except:
        return ImageFont.load_default()

def lerp(a, b, t):
    return int(a + (b - a) * t)

def lerp_c(c1, c2, t):
    return tuple(lerp(a, b, t) for a, b in zip(c1, c2))

def smooth(pts, passes=4):
    """Chaikin subdivision for smooth curves."""
    for _ in range(passes):
        n = len(pts)
        out = []
        for i in range(n):
            p0, p1 = pts[i], pts[(i+1) % n]
            out.append((p0[0]*0.75+p1[0]*0.25, p0[1]*0.75+p1[1]*0.25))
            out.append((p0[0]*0.25+p1[0]*0.75, p0[1]*0.25+p1[1]*0.75))
        pts = out
    return pts

def strand_points(cx, cy, r, offset, N=100):
    """Generate smooth control points for one knot strand."""
    raw = []
    for i in range(N):
        a = offset + 2 * math.pi * i / N
        wave = math.sin(a * 4) * r * 0.22
        cr = r + wave
        raw.append((cx + cr * math.cos(a), cy + cr * math.sin(a)))
    return smooth(raw, 4)

def draw_strand(draw, pts, color, width):
    for i in range(len(pts) - 1):
        draw.line([pts[i], pts[i+1]], fill=color, width=width)

def find_crossings(pts1, pts2, threshold=25):
    """Find where two strands are close enough to cross."""
    crossings = []
    for i in range(0, len(pts1), 8):
        for j in range(0, len(pts2), 8):
            d = math.hypot(pts1[i][0]-pts2[j][0], pts1[i][1]-pts2[j][1])
            if d < threshold:
                crossings.append((i, j, pts1[i]))
    return crossings

def draw_norse_knot(draw, cx, cy, r):
    """Two-strand Norse knot with proper over/under crossings."""
    pts1 = strand_points(cx, cy, r, 0)
    pts2 = strand_points(cx, cy, r, math.pi)

    # Draw the full strand 2 first (background strand)
    draw_strand(draw, pts2, COPPER_D, 12)

    # Draw strand 1 in segments, with gaps where it goes "under" strand 2
    # At even crossings: strand 1 goes UNDER (gap in strand 1)
    # At odd crossings: strand 1 goes OVER (drawn on top)
    crossings = find_crossings(pts1, pts2, 30)

    if not crossings:
        # Fallback: just draw both
        draw_strand(draw, pts1, COPPER, 14)
    else:
        # Build segments of strand 1, alternating over/under
        crossing_indices = sorted(set(c[0] for c in crossings))
        # Group crossings into over/under pairs
        segments = []
        prev = 0
        for ci, idx in enumerate(crossing_indices):
            if ci % 2 == 0:
                # UNDER: draw from prev to idx (this segment is behind)
                segments.append(('under', prev, idx))
            else:
                # OVER: draw from prev to idx (this segment is on top)
                segments.append(('over', prev, idx))
            prev = idx
        segments.append(('under' if len(crossing_indices) % 2 == 0 else 'over', prev, len(pts1)-1))

        # Draw under segments first (darker), then over segments (brighter)
        for layer in ['under', 'over']:
            color = COPPER_D if layer == 'under' else COPPER
            w = 10 if layer == 'under' else 14
            for seg_type, s, e in segments:
                if seg_type == layer and e > s:
                    draw_strand(draw, pts1[s:e+1], color, w)

    # Highlight on strand 1 (top surface)
    draw_strand(draw, pts1, COPPER_H, 3)

    # Crossing markers
    for i in range(8):
        a = 2 * math.pi * i / 8
        wave = math.sin(a * 4) * r * 0.22
        cr = r + wave
        x = cx + cr * math.cos(a)
        y = cy + cr * math.sin(a)
        s = 14
        draw.polygon([(x, y-s), (x+s, y), (x, y+s), (x-s, y)], fill=COPPER_H)

def draw_neural_ring(draw, cx, cy, r, count=12):
    nodes = []
    for i in range(count):
        a = 2 * math.pi * i / count - math.pi / 2
        j = math.sin(a * 7 + i * 1.3) * r * 0.03
        nodes.append((cx + (r+j)*math.cos(a), cy + (r+j)*math.sin(a)))
    for i in range(count):
        draw.line([nodes[i], nodes[(i+1)%count]], fill=TEAL_D, width=2)
        if i % 3 != 0:
            draw.line([nodes[i], nodes[(i+2)%count]], fill=TEAL_D, width=1)
    for x, y in nodes:
        draw.ellipse([x-8, y-8, x+8, y+8], outline=TEAL, width=2)
        draw.ellipse([x-3, y-3, x+3, y+3], fill=TEAL)

def draw_memory_rings(draw, cx, cy):
    for r, w, c in [(220, 2, TEAL_D), (178, 2, COPPER_D), (140, 2, TEAL_D), (108, 1, COPPER_D)]:
        draw.ellipse([cx-r, cy-r, cx+r, cy+r], outline=c, width=w)

def draw_core(draw, cx, cy):
    for r in range(96, 0, -1):
        t = r / 96
        c = lerp_c(COPPER_D, COPPER, (t-0.55)/0.45) if t > 0.55 else lerp_c(COPPER, COPPER_H, t/0.55)
        draw.ellipse([cx-r, cy-r, cx+r, cy+r], fill=c)
    draw.ellipse([cx-36, cy-36, cx+36, cy+36], fill=TEAL)
    draw.ellipse([cx-17, cy-17, cx+17, cy+17], fill=BG)
    draw.ellipse([cx-6, cy-6, cx+6, cy+6], fill=TEAL)
    draw.ellipse([cx-7, cy-11, cx, cy-4], fill=(255, 255, 255))

def draw_spokes(draw, cx, cy, r_in, r_out, count=48):
    for i in range(count):
        a = 2 * math.pi * i / count
        draw.line([(cx+r_in*math.cos(a), cy+r_in*math.sin(a)),
                    (cx+r_out*math.cos(a), cy+r_out*math.sin(a))], fill=DARK, width=1)

def main():
    img = Image.new("RGBA", (W, H), (*BG, 255))
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img, "RGBA")
    cx, cy = W // 2, H // 2 - 140

    for r in range(900, 0, -3):
        t = 1 - r / 900
        draw.ellipse([cx-r, cy-r, cx+r, cy+r], fill=(lerp(6,14,t), lerp(10,12,t), lerp(20,28,t), 255))

    draw_spokes(draw, cx, cy, 300, 480, 48)
    draw_neural_ring(draw, cx, cy, 365, 12)
    draw_norse_knot(draw, cx, cy, 250)
    draw_memory_rings(draw, cx, cy)
    draw_core(draw, cx, cy)

    ty = cy + 395
    f_t = font("GeistMono-Bold.ttf", 175)
    bb = draw.textbbox((0,0), "MIMIR", font=f_t)
    draw.text((cx-(bb[2]-bb[0])//2, ty), "MIMIR", fill=WHITE, font=f_t)
    draw.line([(cx-150, ty+200), (cx+150, ty+200)], fill=COPPER, width=3)
    f_s = font("WorkSans-Regular.ttf", 54)
    bb2 = draw.textbbox((0,0), "the rememberer", font=f_s)
    draw.text((cx-(bb2[2]-bb2[0])//2, ty+220), "the rememberer", fill=GRAY_L, font=f_s)
    f_tag = font("DMMono-Regular.ttf", 24)
    bb3 = draw.textbbox((0,0), "SELF-LEARNING AI AGENT", font=f_tag)
    draw.text((cx-(bb3[2]-bb3[0])//2, ty+305), "SELF-LEARNING AI AGENT", fill=GRAY, font=f_tag)

    cl, m = 45, 90
    for x, y, dx, dy in [(m,m,1,1),(W-m,m,-1,1),(m,H-m,1,-1),(W-m,H-m,-1,-1)]:
        draw.line([(x,y),(x+cl*dx,y)], fill=COPPER_D, width=2)
        draw.line([(x,y),(x,y+cl*dy)], fill=COPPER_D, width=2)

    out = r"E:\BMAD\assets\logo\mimir-logo.png"
    img.convert("RGB").save(out, "PNG")
    print(f"Saved: {out}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

const version = "0.2.0-dev"

const usage = `Mímir - the agent that remembers (tiny self-hosted CLI, TUI & Book-Spine Web UI)

Usage:
  mimir                       launch interactive terminal UI (auto-discovers Ollama/LM Studio/Cloud)
  mimir --web [--addr :8420]  launch interactive TUI + live Book-Spine Web UI simultaneously
  mimir ingest [path|git-url] GitIngest a repo/folder into digest.txt + Yggdrasil Mind Map in Cortex
  mimir sdlc [phase|method]   show or switch the 7-Phase SDLC board & methodology (agile/waterfall/devops)
  mimir review [draft] [ctx]  run the Tier-2 Deterministic Review Gate (Checklist + SDLC + Full Suite + Critic)
  mimir ship [draft] [ctx]    run the Tier-2 Production Ship Gate and advance SDLC to Deployment
  mimir audit <draft> [ctx]   run the Epistemic Critic & Verification Node against a draft report
  mimir audit-web [dir]       run Impeccable anti-slop UI + 4-Layer SEO/GEO & Conversion detectors
  mimir swarm [list|add|run|approve] manage Level 3 Multi-Agent Software Factory queue in isolated worktrees
  mimir engines               show Alpha Flux LLC engine binaries, versions, and integrity
  mimir engines run <id> ...  run an engine binary (attribution handshake added automatically)
  mimir engines publish       (maintainers) rehash engines/bin/* and rewrite manifest.json
  mimir update [--check]      update the harness (git fast-forward + rebuild) and any changed engines
  mimir pair                  generate ASCII QR code to pair mobile companion via Happy E2EE
  mimir handoff               generate .mimir/HANDOFF.md for session continuity
  mimir providers             list built-in BYOK providers + Mímir Well Subscription tiers
  mimir setup                 bootstrap Liquid AI d1-omni-600M local System-One decision model
  mimir -p "your prompt"      headless single-shot prompt (for scripts & CI)
  mimir "your prompt"         run one turn (final reply only)
  mimir trace "your prompt"   run one turn and print recalled memory + every tool call
  mimir serve [--addr :8420]  serve the live book-spine UI + HTTP wire in foreground
  mimir status                show provider, discovered models, tools, and memory status
  mimir version               print version

Flags:

  --addr <:port>              bind address for Web UI (default :8420)

  --effort <off|low|med|high> reasoning effort budget (off = fast /no_think tool loops)
  --model <model-id>          override model id

Provider config (auto-discovered or environment):
  Auto-probed local servers:  Ollama (127.0.0.1:11434), LM Studio (127.0.0.1:1234)
  MIMIR_BASE_URL              OpenAI-compatible base URL, e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1
  MIMIR_API_KEY               bearer key (optional for local servers; also checks MIMO_API_KEY)
  MIMIR_MODEL                 model id (optional)
  MIMIR_PROVIDER_ID           provider id label (default: openai-compatible)

Memory (the Cortex) persists across runs:
  MIMIR_HOME                  memory dir (default: ./.mimir in the working directory)

// isLocalURL reports whether a provider base URL points at a local server (Ollama,
// vLLM, Mímir's own gateway). Local tokens cost $0 on the dashboard (F52).
func isLocalURL(u string) bool {
	return strings.Contains(u, "localhost") || strings.Contains(u, "127.0.0.1") || strings.Contains(u, "0.0.0.0")
}

// buildCortex creates the Cortex store for the configured backend.
func buildCortex(home string) (cortex.Store, cortex.SessionStore, *cortex.AuthStore, string, func(), error) {
	noop := func() {}
	if strings.EqualFold(os.Getenv("MIMIR_CORTEX_BACKEND"), "surreal") {
		surrealAddr := os.Getenv("MIMIR_SURREAL_SERVER")
		var sc *cortex.Sidecar
		ctx := context.Background()
		if surrealAddr == "" {
			addr := os.Getenv("MIMIR_SURREAL_ADDR")
			if addr == "" {
				addr = "127.0.0.1:8000"
			}
			dataPath := os.Getenv("MIMIR_SURREAL_DATA")
			if dataPath == "" {
				dataPath = filepath.Join(home, "surreal")
			}
			sc = &cortex.Sidecar{Addr: addr, DataPath: dataPath}
			var cancel context.CancelFunc
			ctx, cancel = context.WithTimeout(ctx, 25*time.Second)
			defer cancel()
			if err := sc.Start(ctx); err != nil {
				return nil, nil, nil, "", noop, fmt.Errorf("surreal sidecar: %w", err)
			}
			surrealAddr = sc.HTTPAddr()
		}
		embedURL := os.Getenv("MIMIR_EMBED_URL")
		if embedURL == "" {
			embedURL = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimRight(os.Getenv("MIMIR_BASE_URL"), "/"), "/v1")
		}
		if embedURL == "" {
			embedURL = "http://localhost:11434"
		}
		embedModel := os.Getenv("MIMIR_EMBED_MODEL")
		if embedModel == "" {
			embedModel = "nomic-embed-text"
		}
		dim := 768
		if d := os.Getenv("MIMIR_EMBED_DIM"); d != "" {
			if n, err := strconv.Atoi(d); err == nil && n > 0 {
				dim = n
			}
		}
		store, err := cortex.NewSurrealStore(ctx, cortex.SurrealConfig{
			Addr:      surrealAddr,
			Dimension: dim,
			Embedder:  &cortex.OllamaEmbedder{BaseURL: embedURL, Model: embedModel},
		})
		if err != nil {
			if sc != nil {
				sc.Stop()
			}
			return nil, nil, nil, "", noop, fmt.Errorf("surreal store: %w", err)
		}
		cli := store.Client()
		sessStore := cortex.NewSessionStore(cli)
		if err := sessStore.EnsureSessionsTable(ctx); err != nil {
			if sc != nil {
				sc.Stop()
			}
			return nil, nil, nil, "", noop, fmt.Errorf("sessions table: %w", err)
		}
		authStore := cortex.NewAuthStore(cli)
		if err := authStore.EnsureAuthTables(ctx); err != nil {
			if sc != nil {
				sc.Stop()
			}
			return nil, nil, nil, "", noop, fmt.Errorf("auth tables: %w", err)
		}
		// F23: there is no compiled-in default admin. A super admin is seeded
		// only when the operator explicitly configures MIMIR_ADMIN_EMAIL.
		if adminEmail := os.Getenv("MIMIR_ADMIN_EMAIL"); adminEmail != "" {
			if err := authStore.SeedAdmin(ctx, adminEmail); err != nil {
				if sc != nil {
					sc.Stop()
				}
				return nil, nil, nil, "", noop, fmt.Errorf("seed admin: %w", err)
			}
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "auth: super admin %s seeded\n", adminEmail)
		}
		stop := noop
		if sc != nil {
			stop = sc.Stop
		}
		desc := fmt.Sprintf("SurrealDB %s (embed %s, dim %d)", surrealAddr, embedModel, dim)
		return store, sessStore, authStore, desc, stop, nil
	}
	cpath := os.Getenv("MIMIR_CORTEX")
	if cpath == "" {
		cpath = filepath.Join(home, "cortex.json")
	}
	store, err := cortex.NewMemoryStoreAt(cpath)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, nil, nil, "", noop, err
	}
	sessStore, err := cortex.NewFileSessionStore(home)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, nil, nil, "", noop, fmt.Errorf("file session store: %w", err)
	}
	return store, sessStore, nil, "file-backed " + cpath, noop, nil
}

func isInteractiveStdin() bool {
	fi, err := os.Stdin.Stat()
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	return (fi.Mode() & os.ModeCharDevice) != 0
}

// leadingSubcommands are the positional first arguments whose dispatch
// branch returns before the one-shot prompt path. "chat" and "trace" are
// deliberately absent: they are mode words of the prompt path itself.
var leadingSubcommands = map[string]bool{
	"setup": true, "init": true,
	"ingest": true, "gitingest": true,
	"providers": true, "subscribe": true,
	"sdlc": true, "phase": true,
	"audit": true, "critic": true,
	"engines": true, "update": true,
	"swarm": true, "factory": true,
	"audit-web": true, "web-audit": true,
	"review": true, "ship": true,
	"handoff": true, "pair": true,
	"serve": true,
}

// reachesPromptRun reports whether main's dispatch will reach the one-shot
// prompt path with a non-empty prompt: a leading subcommand returns first,
// -p supplies the prompt directly, and a chat/trace prefix is a mode word,
// not prompt text.
func reachesPromptRun(positional []string, promptFlag string) bool {
	if len(positional) > 0 && leadingSubcommands[positional[0]] {
		return false
	}
	if strings.TrimSpace(promptFlag) != "" {
		return true
	}
	args := positional
	if len(args) > 0 && (args[0] == "chat" || args[0] == "trace") {
		args = args[1:]
	}
	return strings.TrimSpace(strings.Join(args, " ")) != ""
}

// approverForRun selects the ApprovalFunc for the agent this process runs.
//
// One-stdin-owner rule: the stdin terminal approver may exist ONLY on the
// one-shot prompt path, where this process reads stdin for nothing else.
// The TUI reads stdin through its own bufio.Scanner, so a second buffered
// reader on the same fd would starve or deadlock it, and the prompt (which
// goes to stderr) is invisible behind the TUI. Under serve/--web the agent
// is driven by remote HTTP callers: the prompt would land on the
// operator's terminal with no caller identity attached, and an unanswered
// prompt would block an HTTP handler goroutine forever. Those paths get a
// nil approver, and RequireApproval denies fail-closed.
func approverForRun(oneShot bool, stdinIsTerminal bool) func(toolName, rawArgs string) bool {
	if oneShot && stdinIsTerminal {
		return terminalApprover
	}
	return nil
}

var (
	approvalMu     sync.Mutex
	approvalReader *bufio.Reader
)

// terminalApprover is the interactive ApprovalFunc wired for one-shot
// prompt runs at a terminal (F2/N1, FIX 2): it prompts on stderr with the
// tool name and truncated
// args and approves only on an explicit y/yes line read from stdin. A read
// error or any other answer denies, keeping the gate fail-closed. Prompts
// are serialized because several runs can share the one terminal.
func terminalApprover(toolName, rawArgs string) bool {
	approvalMu.Lock()
	defer approvalMu.Unlock()
	if approvalReader == nil {
		approvalReader = bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin)
	}
	args := rawArgs
	if len(args) > 200 {
		args = args[:200] + "..."
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\nMimir wants to run tool %q with args: %s\nApprove? [y/N] ", toolName, args)
	line, err := approvalReader.ReadString('\n')
	if err != nil && strings.TrimSpace(line) == "" {
		return false
	}
	switch strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(line)) {
	case "y", "yes":
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// pairingPayload mirrors the JSON returned by the server's /api/pair endpoint.
type pairingPayload struct {
	Session struct {
		ID string `json:"id"`
	} `json:"session"`
	PairURI string `json:"pair_uri"`
	ASCIIQR string `json:"ascii_qr"`
}

// pairServerBase converts the configured listen address into the base URL of
// the already-running local server.
func pairServerBase(addr string) string {
	if strings.HasPrefix(addr, ":") {
		addr = "127.0.0.1" + addr
	}
	return "http://" + addr
}

// fetchPairingPayload asks the running server to create a pairing session and
// returns the QR payload it responds with (N4).
func fetchPairingPayload(base string) (*pairingPayload, error) {
	client := &http.Client{Timeout: 5 * time.Second}
	resp, err := client.Get(base + "/api/pair")
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("server returned %s", resp.Status)
	}
	var payload pairingPayload
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&payload); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if payload.PairURI == "" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("server returned an empty pairing payload")
	}
	return &payload, nil
}

func main() {
	rawArgs := os.Args[1:]
	if len(rawArgs) > 0 {
		switch rawArgs[0] {
		case "version", "--version", "-v":
			fmt.Println("Mímir", version)
			return
		case "-h", "--help", "help":
			fmt.Println(usage)
			return
		}
	}

	// Parse flags across any position
	addr := "127.0.0.1:8420"
	webFlag := false
	tuiFlag := false
	statusFlag := false
	permMode := agent.ModeEdit
	effort := ""
	modelOverride := ""
	promptFlag := ""
	var positional []string

	for i := 0; i < len(rawArgs); i++ {
		arg := rawArgs[i]
		switch {
		case arg == "--web":
			webFlag = true
		case arg == "tui" || arg == "-i" || arg == "--tui":
			tuiFlag = true
		case arg == "status" || arg == "--status":
			statusFlag = true
		case (arg == "--addr" || arg == "-addr") && i+1 < len(rawArgs):
			addr = rawArgs[i+1]
			i++
		case strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--addr="):
			addr = strings.TrimPrefix(arg, "--addr=")
		case (arg == "-p" || arg == "--prompt") && i+1 < len(rawArgs):
			promptFlag = rawArgs[i+1]
			i++
		case strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--prompt="):
			promptFlag = strings.TrimPrefix(arg, "--prompt=")
		case arg == "--mode" && i+1 < len(rawArgs):
			permMode = rawArgs[i+1]
			i++
		case strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--mode="):
			permMode = strings.TrimPrefix(arg, "--mode=")
		case arg == "--effort" && i+1 < len(rawArgs):
			effort = rawArgs[i+1]
			i++
		case strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--effort="):
			effort = strings.TrimPrefix(arg, "--effort=")
		case arg == "--model" && i+1 < len(rawArgs):
			modelOverride = rawArgs[i+1]
			i++
		case strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--model="):
			modelOverride = strings.TrimPrefix(arg, "--model=")
		default:
			positional = append(positional, arg)
		}
	}

	cwd, _ := os.Getwd()
	toolReg := tools.Default(cwd)

	home := os.Getenv("MIMIR_HOME")
	if home == "" {
		home = filepath.Join(cwd, ".mimir")
	}
	store, sessStore, authStore, storeDesc, cleanup, err := buildCortex(home)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "cortex error:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	defer cleanup()
	if t, ok := toolReg.Get("ingest_repo"); ok {
		if it, ok := t.(*tools.IngestRepoTool); ok {
			it.Store = store
		}
	}

	var provider llm.Provider
	model := ""
	local := false
	if ep, ok := config.AutoDiscoverProvider(context.Background()); ok {
		if modelOverride != "" {
			ep.Model = modelOverride
		}
		provider = &llm.OpenAIProvider{
			IDStr: ep.ID, BaseURL: ep.BaseURL, APIKey: ep.APIKey, Model: ep.Model,
		}
		model = ep.Model
		local = isLocalURL(ep.BaseURL)
	}
	tracker := llm.NewTracker()

	// F2/N1 + FIX 2: the terminal approver is installed only when this
	// process will run the one-shot prompt path, the sole path that owns
	// stdin exclusively; see approverForRun for the one-stdin-owner rule.
	// TUI, serve, and --web agents get no stdin approver, and scripts or
	// CI (no terminal) get none either: the gate fails closed there.
	approver := approverForRun(reachesPromptRun(positional, promptFlag), isInteractiveStdin())

	a := agent.New(agent.Config{
		Provider:     provider,
		Tools:        toolReg,
		Cortex:       store,
		Model:        model,
		Usage:        tracker,
		Local:        local,
		Mode:         permMode,
		Effort:       effort,
		Gate:         policy.DefaultDevGate(),
		ApprovalFunc: approver,
		AutoVerify:   true,
	})

	if len(positional) > 0 && (positional[0] == "setup" || positional[0] == "init") {
		fmt.Printf("Mímir %s · Bootstrapping System-One Decision Engine (%s)...\n", version, decision.PrimaryDecisionModel)
		dm, err := decision.EnsureLocalDecisionModel(context.Background(), "", true)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Printf("  note: local Ollama pull skipped (%v); zero-latency heuristic engine active.\n", err)
		} else {
			fmt.Printf("  ✓ Local System-One Decision Model ready: %s\n", dm)
		}
		return
	}

	if len(positional) > 0 && (positional[0] == "ingest" || positional[0] == "gitingest") {
		src := "."
		if len(positional) > 1 {
			src = positional[1]
		}
		outFile := filepath.Join(home, "digest.txt")
		res, err := ingest.Run(context.Background(), ingest.Options{
			Source:        src,
			WriteDigestTo: outFile,
		}, store)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "ingest error:", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		fmt.Println(res.Summary)
		fmt.Printf("Digest written to: %s\n", outFile)
		fmt.Printf("Yggdrasil Mind Map saved to Cortex (%d neurons)\n", res.NeuronsSaved)
		return
	}

	if len(positional) > 0 && (positional[0] == "providers" || positional[0] == "subscribe") {
		fmt.Println("Mímir Well Subscriptions & BYOK Provider Catalog:")
		for _, sub := range config.BuiltinSubscriptionTiers() {
			fmt.Printf("  * %s (%s) - %s\n", sub.Name, sub.Price, sub.Description)
		}
		fmt.Println("\nBuilt-in Providers:")
		for _, p := range config.BuiltinProviders() {
			st := "unset"
			if p.Configured {
				st = "ready"
			}
			fmt.Printf("  [%s] %-28s default=%-22s (%s)\n", p.BillingMode, p.Name, p.DefaultModel, st)
		}
		return
	}

	if len(positional) > 0 && (positional[0] == "sdlc" || positional[0] == "phase") {
		mgr := a.SDLC()
		if len(positional) > 1 {
			sub := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(positional[1]))
			switch sub {
			case "agile", "waterfall", "devops":
				if err := mgr.SetMethodology(sub); err != nil {
					fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "sdlc:", err)
					os.Exit(1)
				}
			case "next", "advance":
				if _, err := mgr.Advance(); err != nil {
					fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "sdlc:", err)
					os.Exit(1)
				}
			default:
				if _, err := mgr.SetPhase(sub); err != nil {
					fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "sdlc:", err)
					os.Exit(1)
				}
			}
		}
		fmt.Println(mgr.FormatBoard())
		return
	}

	if len(positional) > 0 && (positional[0] == "audit" || positional[0] == "critic") {
		if len(positional) < 2 {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: mimir audit <draft-file> [retrieved-context-file]")
			os.Exit(2)
		}
		draftBytes, err := os.ReadFile(positional[1])
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "audit read draft:", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		var ctxBuilder strings.Builder
		if len(positional) > 2 {
			if ctxBytes, err := os.ReadFile(positional[2]); err == nil {
				ctxBuilder.Write(ctxBytes)
			}
		} else {
			for _, n := range store.All() {
				ctxBuilder.WriteString(n.Title + "\n" + n.Content + "\n")
			}
		}
		rep := critic.AuditDeterministic(ctxBuilder.String(), string(draftBytes))
		fmt.Println(rep.FormatMarkdown())
		if !rep.PassAudit {
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		return
	}

	if len(positional) > 0 && positional[0] == "engines" {
		sub := ""
		if len(positional) > 1 {
			sub = positional[1]
		}
		switch sub {
		case "", "status", "list":
			fmt.Println(engines.FormatStatus(cwd))
		case "publish":
			m, err := engines.BuildManifest(context.Background(), cwd)
			if err != nil {
				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "engines publish:", err)
				os.Exit(1)
			}
			for _, e := range m.Engines {
				fmt.Printf("  %-16s v%-8s sha256=%s...\n", e.ID, e.Version, e.SHA256[:12])
			}
			fmt.Println("wrote engines/bin/manifest.json; commit and push main to release.")
		case "run":
			if len(positional) < 3 {
				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: mimir engines run <engine-id> [args...]")
				os.Exit(2)
			}
			out, err := engines.Invoke(context.Background(), cwd, positional[2], positional[3:]...)
			fmt.Println(out)
			if err != nil {
				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "engines run:", err)
				os.Exit(1)
			}
		default:
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "unknown engines subcommand %q (status, run, publish)\n", sub)
			os.Exit(2)
		}
		return
	}

	if len(positional) > 0 && positional[0] == "update" {
		checkOnly := len(positional) > 1 && (positional[1] == "--check" || positional[1] == "check")
		ctx := context.Background()
		base := engines.UpdateBase()
		if !checkOnly {
			hr, err := engines.UpdateHarness(ctx, cwd)
			fmt.Printf("harness (%s): %s\n", hr.Mode, hr.Output)
			if err != nil {
				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "harness update:", err)
				os.Exit(1)
			}
			if hr.Rebuilt {
				fmt.Println("harness rebuilt: bin/mimir updated (restart to use it)")
			}
		}
		plan, err := engines.CheckForUpdates(ctx, cwd, base)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "engine update check:", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		if len(plan.Changes) == 0 {
			fmt.Println("engines: all up to date with", base)
			return
		}
		for _, c := range plan.Changes {
			fmt.Printf("  %-16s %s -> %s (%s)\n", c.ID, c.LocalVersion, c.RemoteVersion, c.Reason)
		}
		if checkOnly {
			fmt.Println("run `mimir update` to install.")
			return
		}
		updated, err := engines.ApplyUpdates(ctx, cwd, plan)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "engine update:", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}

		f := swarm.NewFactory(swarm.FactoryConfig{
			RootDir:      cwd,
			MaxWorkers:   4,
			TargetBranch: "main",
			// Thor (the builder persona) runs a real agent built from this
			// config; without a provider the factory now honestly blocks
			// tasks with ErrNoAgentConfigured instead of fabricating work.
			// Mode is deliberately left unset: the factory's worker default
			// is autonomous bypass with the policy gate still applied, and
			// the human control point is `mimir swarm approve`, not a
			// terminal prompt nobody is watching.
			AgentConfig: agent.Config{
				Provider:   provider,
				Tools:      toolReg,
				Cortex:     store,
				Model:      model,
				Usage:      tracker,

				Effort:     effort,
				Gate:       policy.DefaultDevGate(),
				AutoVerify: true,

		if len(positional) > 1 {
			sub = strings.ToLower(positional[1])
		}
		switch sub {

			fmt.Println(f.FormatStatus())
		case "add", "submit":
			if len(positional) < 3 {
				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: mimir swarm add <title> [description]")
				os.Exit(2)
			}
			title := positional[2]
			desc := "Submitted via CLI."
			if len(positional) > 3 {
				desc = strings.Join(positional[3:], " ")
			}
			t, err := f.Submit(title, desc)
			if err != nil {
				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "swarm submit error:", err)
				os.Exit(1)
			}
			fmt.Printf("✓ Submitted task %s (%q) -> branch: %s\n", t.ID, t.Title, t.Branch)
		case "run":
			if len(positional) < 3 {
				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: mimir swarm run <task-id>")
				os.Exit(2)
			}
			taskID := positional[2]
			fmt.Printf("▸ Running autonomous factory pipeline for %s...\n", taskID)
			if err := f.ExecuteTask(context.Background(), taskID); err != nil {
				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "swarm run failed: %v\n", err)
				os.Exit(1)
			}
			// ExecuteTask stops at the merge gate: passing every persona gate
			// leaves the task awaiting human approval, never auto-merged.
			// A task that cannot be read back after execution is an error
			// (FIX 4): it must never fall through to a success message.
			t, ok := f.GetTask(taskID)
			if !ok {
				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "swarm run: task %s not found after execution\n", taskID)
				os.Exit(1)
			}
			if t.State == swarm.StateMerged {
				fmt.Printf("✓ Task %s passed Odin -> Thor -> Loki -> Heimdall pipeline and merged to main!\n", taskID)
			} else {
				fmt.Printf("✓ Task %s passed Odin -> Thor -> Loki -> Heimdall pipeline (state: %s). Nothing was merged.\n", taskID, t.State)
				fmt.Printf("  Review the task branch, then merge it with: mimir swarm approve %s\n", taskID)
			}
		case "approve":
			if len(positional) < 3 {
				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: mimir swarm approve <task-id>")
				os.Exit(2)
			}
			taskID := positional[2]
			if err := f.ApproveMerge(context.Background(), taskID); err != nil {
				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "swarm approve failed: %v\n", err)
				os.Exit(1)
			}
			fmt.Printf("✓ Task %s approved and merged to main.\n", taskID)
		default:
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "unknown swarm subcommand %q (list, add, run, approve)\n", sub)
			os.Exit(2)
		}
		return
	}

	if len(positional) > 0 && (positional[0] == "audit-web" || positional[0] == "web-audit") {

		if len(positional) > 1 {

	if len(positional) > 0 && (positional[0] == "review" || positional[0] == "ship") {
		eng, err := runengine.New(cwd, nil, runengine.DefaultLimits())
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "runengine init:", err)
			os.Exit(1)

		eng.SDLC = a.SDLC()
		if t, ok := toolReg.Get("todo"); ok {
			if tt, ok := t.(*tools.TodoTool); ok && tt.Store != nil {
				eng.Todos = tt.Store
			}
		}
		var gateOpts runengine.GateOptions
		if len(positional) > 1 {
			if draftBytes, err := os.ReadFile(positional[1]); err == nil {
				gateOpts.DraftReport = string(draftBytes)
			}
		}
		if len(positional) > 2 {
			if ctxBytes, err := os.ReadFile(positional[2]); err == nil {
				gateOpts.RetrievedContext = string(ctxBytes)
			}
		} else if gateOpts.DraftReport != "" {
			var cb strings.Builder
			for _, n := range store.All() {
				cb.WriteString(n.Title + "\n" + n.Content + "\n")
			}
			gateOpts.RetrievedContext = cb.String()
		}
		var rep runengine.GateReport
		if positional[0] == "ship" {
			rep = eng.ShipGate(context.Background(), gateOpts)
		} else {
			rep = eng.ReviewGate(context.Background(), gateOpts)
		}
		fmt.Println(rep.FormatMarkdown())
		if !rep.Passed {
			os.Exit(1)
		}

	}

	if len(positional) > 0 && positional[0] == "handoff" {
		var todos []string
		if t, ok := toolReg.Get("todo"); ok {
			if tt, ok := t.(*tools.TodoTool); ok && tt.Store != nil {
				for _, item := range tt.Store.List() {
					todos = append(todos, fmt.Sprintf("- #%d [%s] %s", item.ID, item.Status, item.Content))
				}
			}
		}
		var history []llm.Message
		sid := "cli-session"
		if sessStore != nil {
			if list, err := sessStore.ListSessions(context.Background(), ""); err == nil && len(list) > 0 {
				sid = list[len(list)-1].ID
				if s, err := sessStore.GetSession(context.Background(), sid); err == nil && s != nil {
					for _, m := range s.Messages {
						history = append(history, llm.Message{Role: m.Role, Content: m.Content})
					}
				}
			}
		}
		summary := ""
		if mm, ok := ingest.LatestMindMap(store); ok {
			summary = fmt.Sprintf("%s (%d files, ~%dk tokens)", mm.RepoName, mm.TotalFiles, mm.EstTokens/1000)
		}
		md := agent.GenerateHandoffMarkdown(sid, history, todos, summary)
		outPath, err := agent.WriteHandoffFile(cwd, md)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "handoff error:", err)
			os.Exit(1)

		fmt.Printf("✓ Handoff generated at: %s\n\n%s\n", outPath, md)

	if len(positional) > 0 && positional[0] == "pair" {
		// N4: the pairing session lives in the RUNNING server's relay manager.
		// Creating one inside this short-lived process produced a QR that could
		// never complete pairing, so request the session from the local server.
		base := pairServerBase(addr)
		payload, err := fetchPairingPayload(base)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "pair: cannot reach the Mimir server at %s (%v)\n", base, err)
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "start the server first with: mimir serve")

	}

	if len(positional) > 0 && positional[0] == "serve" {
		fmt.Println("Mímir serving the live UI at http://localhost" + addr + "/  (Ctrl+C to stop)")
		if err := server.Serve(server.Deps{Agent: a, Store: store, Sessions: sessStore, Auth: authStore, Usage: tracker, Addr: addr}); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "serve:", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		return
	}

	mode := "chat"
	if len(positional) > 0 && (positional[0] == "chat" || positional[0] == "trace") {
		mode = positional[0]
		positional = positional[1:]
	}
	prompt := strings.TrimSpace(promptFlag)
	if prompt == "" {
		prompt = strings.TrimSpace(strings.Join(positional, " "))
	}

	if prompt != "" {
		if provider == nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "no provider configured: run Ollama locally (:11434) or set MIMIR_BASE_URL (+ MIMIR_API_KEY, MIMIR_MODEL)")
			os.Exit(2)
		}
		if mode == "trace" {
			res, err := a.RunFull(context.Background(), prompt, nil)
			if err != nil {
				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "error:", err)
				os.Exit(1)
			}
			for _, c := range res.Recalled {
				fmt.Printf("  [memory] %s\n", strings.Join(strings.Fields(c), " "))
			}
			for i, s := range res.Trace {
				fmt.Printf("[step %d] tool=%s args=%s\n", i+1, s.Name, s.Args)
				fmt.Printf("          -> %s\n", strings.TrimSpace(s.Result))
				if s.Err != "" {
					fmt.Printf("          !! %s\n", s.Err)
				}
			}
			fmt.Println("---")
			fmt.Println(res.Reply)
			return
		}
		reply, err := a.Run(context.Background(), prompt, nil)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "error:", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		fmt.Println(reply)
		return
	}

	// Start background Web UI if --web was passed, or expose a callback for /web in TUI.
	startWeb := func() (string, error) {
		url := "http://localhost" + addr + "/app"
		go func() {
			_ = server.Serve(server.Deps{Agent: a, Store: store, Sessions: sessStore, Auth: authStore, Usage: tracker, Addr: addr})
		}()
		return url, nil
	}
	webURL := ""
	if webFlag {
		webURL, _ = startWeb()
	}

	// Launch interactive TUI when invoked as `mimir` in an interactive terminal, `mimir tui`, or `mimir --web`.
	if !statusFlag && (tuiFlag || webFlag || isInteractiveStdin()) {
		if err := tui.Run(context.Background(), tui.Options{
			Version:    version,
			Agent:      a,
			Tools:      toolReg,
			Cortex:     store,
			Sessions:   sessStore,
			Usage:      tracker,
			StoreDesc:  storeDesc,
			WebURL:     webURL,
			StartWebFn: startWeb,
		}); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "tui error:", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		return
	}

	fmt.Printf("Mímir %s - the agent that remembers\n", version)
	names := make([]string, 0, len(toolReg.All()))
	for _, t := range toolReg.All() {
		names = append(names, t.Name())
	}
	fmt.Println("tools:", strings.Join(names, ", "))
	fmt.Println("memory:", storeDesc)
	if provider == nil {
		fmt.Println("provider: (none configured)")
		fmt.Println("set MIMIR_BASE_URL + MIMIR_API_KEY (+ MIMIR_MODEL), then: mimir \"your prompt\"  or  mimir trace \"...\"")
		return
	}
	fmt.Println("provider:", provider.ID(), "· model:", model)
}
