# RULES: how this project gets built

The build law for this repo, in one page. These rules come from David
Patton and apply to every module, every language, every time.

## Modularity: the grid and the tiles
- The main program or page is a GRID. Every section is a MODULE plugged
  into a grid slot: header, footer, each content block, each tile.
  Modular to the full max, never partial.
- Every feature is its own isolated module with a defined interface.
  One feature, one module, one commit, one push.
- Modules are independently replaceable and updatable on the fly. A
  broken module gets fixed or swapped alone; the system never rebuilds
  around it.

## Build 20 years ahead
- Design for the bottleneck that is COMING, not just today's.
- Interface seams at every change-prone boundary: model providers,
  executors, verifiers, storage, transports.
- Operational limits (timeouts, caps, retry counts, quotas) are config
  with sane defaults, never constants compiled into logic.
- Data formats carry version fields so future versions read today's data.

## Debugging and linting, in every module, from birth
- They are not the same thing. Linting reads the code for mistakes
  without running it. Debugging is finding out why the program
  misbehaved when it ran, backed by diagnostics built into the module.
- Every module ships with BOTH: structured diagnostics, a way to pull
  the bug information out, and lint gates that run clean. A module that
  cannot say what it did and why it refused is not done.

## Check the shelf before building
- Before building anything, check the take-shelf
  (~/workspace/google-org-harvest/USE-IT.md) and the wider harvest: if
  Google or another trusted source already built it under a usable
  license, take it or retrofit it. Rebuilding what exists is waste.
- For any new market or feature area, research the top 10 competitors
  (the customer's list and the platform's list) before designing.

## Security
- No secrets in the repo, ever: keys, tokens, and passwords live in
  secure storage only. Secret scanning (gitleaks or betterleaks) runs
  in the gates.
- Every refusal, overage, and verdict emits through the project's
  diagnostic channel. Nothing fails silently.
- Untrusted input gets a bounded parser and a fuzz target, not trust.

## Verification
- Done means proven: a test with asserted values, a log line, a bench
  note, or a live check. "It compiles" is not proof.
- Never blindly trust delegated work; re-run the gates before merging.
- Emulation-proven is not bench-proven; label which one a claim is.

## Relational diagram
- This project always has a relational diagram: nodes and wires
  showing every feature and module and how they connect, modeled on
  the AlphaFlux relational map.
- The diagram lives in this repo under docs/relational-map/, as
  readable markdown documents (never raw JSON): nodes.md and wires.md
  are canonical, diagram.md draws them, README.md explains the set.
  docs/MAP.md is the entry point and points at the set, together with
  these rules, so any agent who opens the repo can read both.
- Update rule: after every feature build, or any change to any part of
  the project, the diagram is updated in the same push cycle. A
  feature is not fully landed until the diagram matches it.
- The diagram is built from the code. Code beats paper: every node
  carries a state (LIVE, PLANNED, or ABSENT) and its source file, and
  where the paper and the code disagree, the disagreement is named on
  the map, never silently smoothed over.

## Writing
- Plain, direct, technical. No em dashes in prose, docs, or code.
- Brand casing is exact: AlphaVision, AlphaFlux, iTaK, Mimir,
  Patriot Pest Control (full name wherever there are words).
- Project docs: TODO.md tracks the work, PLAN.md holds the plan,
  IDEA.md holds David's ideas in his words.

## Mimir specifics
- Toolchain: Go, pinned at go1.26.9 (go.mod toolchain line). Tool
  versions are part of the gate; a stale linter or scanner is a
  finding, not a footnote.
- The gate suite, all green before a push counts as done: go build,
  go vet, gofmt with no diffs, go test -race on all packages,
  golangci-lint with zero issues, and a gitleaks scan.
- Limits live in run-spec frontmatter (step caps, timeouts, output
  caps), never as constants compiled into the run engine. The full
  verify mode is the hard gate; targeted verify modes never replace
  it at ship time.
- Approval fails closed. If no approver exists, the action is denied;
  bypass modes waive approval requests, never explicit denies.
- Configuration arrives through MIMIR_ environment variables and
  config files, never through compiled-in credentials or admin
  identities.
- Trust boundaries log through slog with no secret values in fields,
  so a refusal can always be traced after the fact.

# RUNBOOK: Mimir

## Build
Requires Go 1.26+ (the repo pins toolchain go1.26.9 in go.mod).

```powershell
# Build the single binary (Windows form, from README.md)
go build -o bin/mimir.exe ./cmd/mimir

# Build everything, no output binary
go build ./...
```

The gate suite, all green before a push counts as done (docs/RULES.md):

```bash
gofmt -l .            # must print nothing
go vet ./...
go test -race ./...
golangci-lint run     # zero issues
gitleaks detect       # secret scan over the tree
```

CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs gofmt check, go vet, and
go test -race on push and pull request, with a non-blocking
govulncheck job. A green server-side CI run is still unverified
(TODO T-4.2); local gate runs are the current proof.

## Run locally

```powershell
# Bootstrap the local decision model
.\bin\mimir.exe setup

# Ingest a local repo or a GitHub URL into the Mind Map in the Cortex
.\bin\mimir.exe ingest .
.\bin\mimir.exe ingest https://github.com/David2024patton/Mimir

# List built-in providers and subscription tiers
.\bin\mimir.exe providers

# View or switch the 7-phase SDLC board (agile | waterfall | devops)
.\bin\mimir.exe sdlc

# Interactive TUI
.\bin\mimir.exe

# TUI plus the live web UI on :8420
.\bin\mimir.exe --web
```

Docker shapes in the repo root: docker-compose.yml for local use and
docker-compose.prod.yml for a persistent install, with the Cortex on
SurrealDB.

## Deploy
Mimir is local-first; there is no hosted production deploy to run.
Distribution is the repo itself plus the built-in updater:

```powershell
mimir update --check   # show what changed, install nothing
mimir update           # git fast-forward main, rebuild bin/mimir, swap in changed engines
```

- The harness update uses git pull --ff-only, so it never merges or
  overwrites local edits. If it refuses, commit or stash first.
- Engines are compared by SHA-256 against engines/bin/manifest.json
  and verified before anything is replaced; a failed check leaves the
  old binary untouched.
- Maintainers ship an engine change with scripts/publish-engines.ps1
  from main (see docs/ENGINES.md); engine source lives on engine
  branches and never lands on main.
- Rollback: return the checkout to the previous known-good commit
  and rebuild. Engine binaries roll back the same way, since every
  engine swap is manifest-verified.

## Verify
Three tiers (docs/TESTING-POLICY.md); a feature is not done until the
unit tier and a live test have both run.

1. Unit tests, offline, always green: `go test ./...` (the gate form
   adds -race, see Build above).
2. Live test against a real model: `go test ./internal/agent -run TestLiveRun -v`
   with MIMIR_LIVE_BASE_URL set (and MIMIR_LIVE_MODEL, plus
   MIMIR_LIVE_API_KEY for a cloud endpoint). It skips automatically
   when MIMIR_LIVE_BASE_URL is unset, so an offline run that skips it
   has NOT proven the live path.
3. CLI smoke: `go run ./cmd/mimir "prompt"` against a real provider,
   or `mimir trace "prompt"` to watch each tool call.

Cross-run memory checks: `go test ./internal/agent -run TestCrossRunMemory -v`
proves memory survives a restart on the file-backed Cortex.

## Where things live
- Source of truth: github.com/David2024patton/Mimir (public), default
  branch main; UI work on branch engine/gjallarhorn-ui.
- Web UI: served by the binary on port 8420 when run with --web.
- Cortex memory: file store at .mimir/cortex.json by default
  (override with the MIMIR_CORTEX and MIMIR_HOME environment
  variables), or SurrealDB in the docker shapes.
- Project record: TODO.md for work state, STATUS.md for the current
  snapshot, docs/SKEPTICS-AUDIT.md for working code versus blueprint,
  docs/MASTER-TODO.md and docs/PROJECT-MASTER-PLAN.md for the deep
  engineering detail.
- Credential storage pointers, names only, never values:
  - SurrealDB credentials for a persistent install: the
    MIMIR_SURREAL_USER and MIMIR_SURREAL_PASS environment variables in
    that deployment's environment.
  - Engine signing: the ed25519 release key exists and is held
    offline (private half outside this repo, never committed);
    installs pin its public half via the MIMIR_ENGINE_PUBKEY
    environment variable. The pinned value of record is
    uJQqyXeyx49sJYWeVttFPX9JnHuyIWCh/fk3CLqvuf4= and it is already
    set in .env.example, both docker-compose files, and the
    Dockerfile. The shipped engines/bin/manifest.json is signed with
    this key; TestShippedManifestSignatureVerifies in
    internal/engines fails if that ever stops being true.
  - Forge OAuth apps (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Gitea/Forgejo):
    registration is stalled until David submits current passwords
    through the secure card flow; no app credentials exist in this
    repo.
  - Live test credentials: supplied per run through the
    MIMIR_LIVE_API_KEY environment variable; never logged, never
    committed.
  - The F22 mail credential: rotation happens at Titan Mail by
    David; nothing about its value belongs in this repo.

## Gotchas
- Restart lockout on persistent SurrealDB installs: set
  MIMIR_SURREAL_USER and MIMIR_SURREAL_PASS in the persistent
  environment BEFORE a restart. Without them, a restart generates a
  new per-run sidecar credential and the existing database cannot be
  opened (fix: set both variables to the install's credentials, then
  restart; TODO T-4.1).
- Unauthenticated non-loopback bind is refused on purpose: serve
  will not bind a non-loopback address with no auth backend unless
  MIMIR_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED=1 is set explicitly (fix: configure an
  auth backend, or set the variable only where that exposure is
  intended).
- Engine signing is ACTIVE: the release key exists, the shipped
  manifest is signed, and MIMIR_ENGINE_PUBKEY is pinned in the
  compose files, the Dockerfile, and .env.example. Installs with the
  pin refuse unsigned or badly signed manifests. Bare-binary installs
  that set their environment by hand must set MIMIR_ENGINE_PUBKEY to
  the pinned value in the credential pointers above, or their engine
  updates run unauthenticated with only a warning.
- RunUnattended has no production caller yet: the unattended path is
  the scaffold on branch run-engine-scaffold, not a main-branch
  command (fix: TODO T-2.1 and T-2.2).
- The F22 history purge, when David approves it, breaks his Windows
  clone and both branches need re-syncing afterward. Do not run it
  without his explicit go (fix: none; it is held, TODO Phase 1).
- A live test that skips proves nothing about the live path: check
  that MIMIR_LIVE_BASE_URL was actually set before counting it
  (docs/TESTING-POLICY.md).

# End-to-End Scenario: Building & Shipping a SaaS Platform With Mímir (Raw Idea to Production)

This walkthrough demonstrates how a developer (or solo founder) takes a SaaS product from a **raw brainstorm idea** all the way to **live production and post-launch maintenance** using Mímir's **7-Phase Zero-Bloat SDLC Engine** (`internal/sdlc`), **Liquid AI `d1-omni-600M` Decision Router** (`internal/decision`), **Yggdrasil Mind Map** (`internal/ingest`), and **4-Layer Web/SEO/GEO Rules** (`internal/agent/rules.go`).

---

## The Scenario Idea: "MapPulse" (Local Service Lead-Response & GBP Review SaaS)
The user wants to build **MapPulse** -- a micro-SaaS for local home-service businesses (pest control, HVAC, plumbing) that:
1. Catches missed inbound phone calls and web leads within 10 seconds via SMS + 1-click human callback escalation.
2. Sends FTC-compliant post-job Google Business Profile (GBP) review requests (never gating on positive sentiment).
3. Publishes a high-converting public SaaS marketing site with transparent pricing tiers, JSON-LD `Schema.org`, and `/llms.txt` for AI search engines.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    P1["1. Planning (Odin)\n01-PLAN.md"] --> P2["2. Analysis (Huginn)\n02-SRS.md"]
    P2 --> P3["3. Design (Odin)\n03-SDD.md"]
    P3 --> P4["4. Implementation (Thor)\n04-BUILD.md"]
    P4 --> P5["5. Testing (Loki)\n05-QA-REPORT.md"]
    P5 --> P6["6. Deployment (Heimdall)\n06-RELEASE.md"]
    P6 --> P7["7. Maintenance (Muninn)\n07-MAINTENANCE.md"]
```

---

## Step 1: Planning (`[SDLC 1/7: PLANNING]` -- Brainstorming, Scope & Charter)

### 1. User Action
The user creates an empty folder `G:\MapPulse`, launches Mímir (`mimir --web`), and types:
> *"I want to build MapPulse, a SaaS for local trades (HVAC, pest control, plumbers) that texts back missed calls in 10 seconds with human escalation and sends FTC-compliant Google Maps review requests after a job closes. Let's brainstorm the project plan, scope, and feasibility charter first."*

### 2. What Mímir's Harness Does Under the Hood
- **SDLC Phase Detection (`internal/sdlc/sdlc.go`)**: `DetectPhaseFromPrompt` sees `"project plan"`, `"scope"`, and `"charter"` and locks into **Step 1: `planning`**.
- **Zero-Bloat Prompt Loaded (`internal/sdlc/phases.go`)**: Instead of loading 2,500 chars of coding/testing/deployment rules, Mímir injects **only** the 29-word Step 1 micro-prompt:
  `[SDLC 1/7: PLANNING (Odin)] Define scope, feasibility, risks, and modular milestones. Record a step-by-step checklist in todo and write the Project Plan & Charter via sdlc before coding.`
- **Tool Whitelist Active**: Only `read_file`, `list_dir`, `ingest_repo`, `todo`, `question`, and `sdlc` are exposed (write/edit tools are held back until Design/Implementation).
- **Persona Activated**: `Odin` (Architect & Planner).

### 3. Mímir's Execution & Deliverable
1. `Odin` calls the `question` tool (`internal/tools/question.go`) to ask 3 quick multiple-choice product questions ( rendered as clickable `[choice]` buttons in the TUI/Web/Phone UI):
   - **Billing stack**: `A) Stripe Checkout + Webhooks` | `B) LemonSqueezy`
   - **Telephony provider**: `A) Twilio Programmable SMS/Voice` | `B) Telnyx`
   - **Database**: `A) SQLite (WAL mode, zero external container)` | `B) Postgres`
2. Once the user clicks `A, A, A`, `Odin` populates the persistent `todo` checklist (`internal/tools/todo.go`) with 7 milestones matching the SDLC phases.
3. `Odin` calls the `sdlc` tool (`action: "save_deliverable"`, `phase: "planning"`) to write **`.mimir/sdlc/01-PLAN.md`** (*Project Plan & Charter*), defining:
   - MVP scope (Missed-Call SMS Responder, 6-Field Lead Record, FTC-Compliant Review Sender, Public SaaS Landing Page).
   - Unit economics (`$49/mo` Starter tier, `$129/mo` Pro tier, estimated SMS/voice pass-through cost).
   - Risk register (TCPA/FCC consent compliance, FTC Oct 2024 review-gating ban, webhook idempotency).

---

## Step 2: Analysis (`[SDLC 2/7: ANALYSIS]` -- Exact System & SEO Requirements)

### 1. User Action
The user runs `/sdlc next` (or says: *"Great, now let's gather the exact SRS requirements and security constraints."*).

### 2. What Mímir's Harness Does Under the Hood
- **SDLC Phase**: Advances to **Step 2: `analysis`** (`Persona: Huginn`).
- **Zero-Bloat Prompt Loaded**: Step 1's prompt is unloaded. Only Step 2's micro-prompt + the 1-line `[Web/SEO Analysis]` overlay (~95 tokens total) are loaded:
  - `[SDLC 2/7: ANALYSIS (Huginn)] Inspect the Yggdrasil Mind Map (ingest_repo/read_file), clarify ambiguities with question, and define exact functional/security constraints in the SRS.`
  - `[Web/SEO Analysis]: Define target entity facts (NAP, pricing units, service areas) and first-party lead conversion fields (source, response_time, contact, outcome).`

### 3. Mímir's Execution & Deliverable
1. `Huginn` maps the exact functional and compliance requirements:
   - **Lead Record Schema (6 Mandatory Fields)**: `lead_id`, `source`, `response_time_ms`, `contact_phone`, `booked_outcome`, `next_action`.
   - **Human Escalation Requirement**: Every automated SMS must disclose it is MapPulse's assistant for the business and offer `"Reply 0 or press 1 to speak directly with the on-call technician"` (preventing undisclosed-AI drop-off).
   - **FTC Review Compliance**: Review requests trigger on `job_status == "completed"` for **all** customers equally -- zero sentiment screening or review gating.
   - **Public SaaS Entity Facts**: Exact pricing tiers (`$49/mo` includes 250 SMS + 1 tracking number; `$129/mo` includes 1,000 SMS + 3 numbers), refund policy, and company contact facts.
2. `Huginn` calls `sdlc` (`action: "save_deliverable"`, `phase: "analysis"`) to write **`.mimir/sdlc/02-SRS.md`** (*Software Requirement Specification*).

---

## Step 3: Design (`[SDLC 3/7: DESIGN]` -- Architecture, DB Schema & Anti-Slop Wireframe)

### 1. User Action
The user types: *"Blueprint the system design, SQLite schema, API routes, and folder structure."*

### 2. What Mímir's Harness Does Under the Hood
- **SDLC Phase**: Auto-switches to **Step 3: `design`** (`Persona: Odin`).
- **Zero-Bloat Prompt Loaded**: Loads only Step 3's micro-prompt + `[Web/SEO Design]` overlay (~105 tokens):
  - `[SDLC 3/7: DESIGN (Odin)] Blueprint modular package/folder boundaries, database schemas, C-ABI/API contracts, and UI wireframes in the SDD before implementation.`
  - `[Web/SEO Design]: Blueprint semantic HTML5 landmarks, JSON-LD Schema.org types (LocalBusiness/SoftwareApplication/FAQPage), /llms.txt structure, and non-formulaic UI layout.`

### 3. Mímir's Execution & Deliverable
1. `Odin` designs a clean, modular folder structure for `G:\MapPulse`:
   ```text
   G:\MapPulse\
   ├── cmd/mappulse/main.go          # Single-binary Go server + static asset embed
   ├── internal/
   │   ├── db/schema.sql             # SQLite WAL tables: tenants, leads, sms_logs, review_requests, beacon_events
   │   ├── telephony/twilio.go       # Missed-call webhook + 10s SMS responder + human escalation router
   │   ├── reviews/dispatcher.go     # FTC-compliant post-job GBP review link sender
   │   ├── billing/stripe.go         # Subscription checkout + webhook handler
   │   └── web/                      # Server-rendered HTML5 + First-Party Retention Beacon
   └── public/
       ├── index.html                # Semantic HTML5 landing page + JSON-LD SoftwareApplication & FAQPage
       ├── llms.txt                  # Machine-readable entity & pricing summary for ChatGPT/Perplexity/Google AI
       ├── robots.txt
       └── sitemap.xml
   ```
2. `Odin` calls `sdlc` (`action: "save_deliverable"`, `phase: "design"`) to save **`.mimir/sdlc/03-SDD.md`** (*System Design Document*).

---

## Step 4: Implementation (`[SDLC 4/7: IMPLEMENTATION]` -- Writing the Code)

### 1. User Action
The user types: *"Build the MapPulse backend, SQLite store, Twilio/Stripe handlers, and the public SaaS site."*
*(If the user walks away from their desk to grab coffee, they run `mimir pair`, scan the terminal QR code with the Mímir Phone App, and approve file writes or steer from their phone.)*

### 2. What Mímir's Harness Does Under the Hood
- **SDLC Phase**: Switches to **Step 4: `implementation`** (`Persona: Thor`).
- **Zero-Bloat Prompt Loaded**: Loads only Step 4's micro-prompt + `[Web/SEO Build]` overlay (~115 tokens):
  - `[SDLC 4/7: IMPLEMENTATION (Thor)] Read target files first, make surgical edit_block changes (<15 lines context), keep packages modular, and never use em dashes or placeholder stubs.`
  - `[Web/SEO Build]: Emit semantic HTML5, JSON-LD Schema.org, /llms.txt, explicit pricing/entity facts, and first-party lead capture with human handoff. Zero AI slop or fake stats ([vendor claim]).`
- **All Build Tools Unlocked**: `write_file`, `edit_block`, `run_shell`, `read_file`, `list_dir`, `todo`, `skills`, `sdlc`.
- **If using a local model (`qwen3:14b` or `muse-glimmer`)**: `⚡SmolMode` automatically activates, disabling chain-of-thought (`Effort: "off"`) on mechanical tool steps `1..N` and compacting older tool outputs to 1-line placeholders.

### 3. Mímir's Execution & Deliverable
1. `Thor` writes the modular Go packages (`internal/db`, `internal/telephony`, `internal/reviews`, `internal/billing`, `internal/web`).
2. `Thor` builds `public/index.html`, `public/llms.txt`, `public/robots.txt`, and `public/sitemap.xml` following every rule in `[Web/SEO Build]`:
   - Semantic `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<section id="pricing">`, `<section id="faq">`, `<footer>`.
   - Embedded `<script type="application/ld+json">` with `SoftwareApplication` (`Offer` tiers `$49` and `$129`) and `FAQPage`.
   - Zero generic "in today's fast-paced world" AI slop, zero em dashes, and zero fabricated ROI numbers (any external study is explicitly cited with `[vendor claim]`).
   - Built-in first-party conversion beacon (`POST /api/beacon`) logging every demo request and signup into SQLite.
3. `Thor` runs `mimir ingest .` (`ingest_repo` tool) so `G:\MapPulse`'s new files and symbols are stored in the **Yggdrasil Mind Map** in Cortex memory, then saves **`.mimir/sdlc/04-BUILD.md`**.

## Step 5: Testing (`[SDLC 5/7: TESTING]` -- Linter, Unit Tests & SEO/Schema QA)

### 1. User Action
The user types: *"Run all unit tests, linter checks, and verify the SEO/GEO requirements against our SRS."*

### 2. What Mímir's Harness Does Under the Hood
- **SDLC Phase**: Switches to **Step 5: `testing`** (`Persona: Loki`, the adversarial QA & Test Critic).
- **Zero-Bloat Prompt Loaded**: Loads only Step 5's micro-prompt + `[Web/SEO QA]` overlay (~95 tokens):
  - `[SDLC 5/7: TESTING (Loki)] Run linter, static analysis, and affected unit/integration tests via run_shell. Fix every failure and record the QA Test Report via sdlc.`
  - `[Web/SEO QA]: Verify valid JSON-LD Schema.org, /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, /llms.txt, zero em dashes, and FTC-compliant factual claims.`
- **Decision Model Test Selection (`internal/decision/decider.go`)**: `SelectAffectedTests` queries the Yggdrasil Mind Map to identify every `*_test.go` file covering `telephony`, `reviews`, `billing`, and `web`.

### 3. Mímir's Execution & Deliverable
1. `Loki` executes `go vet ./... ; go test -v -race -count=1 ./...` via `run_shell`.
2. `Loki` tests edge cases against Step 2's SRS:
   - Simulates duplicate Twilio missed-call webhooks to verify idempotency (ensuring a customer is never double-texted).
   - Simulates a `"1-star angry customer"` job completion to verify the FTC compliance gate (confirming the review dispatcher never blocks or filters unhappy customers).
   - Parses `public/index.html` JSON-LD to verify valid JSON and checks `public/llms.txt` and `public/sitemap.xml`.
3. `Loki` calls `EvaluateStopGate` (`internal/agent/rules.go`) to confirm 0 pending todos and 100% passing verification, then writes **`.mimir/sdlc/05-QA-REPORT.md`**.

### 1. User Action

### 2. What Mímir's Harness Does Under the Hood

### 3. Mímir's Execution & Deliverable

2. `Heimdall` builds and boots the production container locally (`docker compose up -d --build`), curls `http://localhost:48219/healthz`, `http://localhost:48219/llms.txt`, and `http://localhost:48219/api/beacon`, and verifies container logs (`docker compose logs`).
3. `Heimdall` writes **`.mimir/sdlc/06-RELEASE.md`** (*Live Production Release Manifest*) with exact rollback instructions and deploys to the production VPS.

# Skeptic's Audit of the Mímir 4-Stack Polyglot & 7-Phase SDLC Report

**Bottom line**: The Mímir Go codebase (`G:\Mimir`) compiles cleanly, passes all 11 package test suites (`go test ./...`), and runs `mimir ingest`, `mimir sdlc`, `mimir providers`, and the interactive TUI today. However, my report and blueprint mixed **(1) verified, working Go code on disk**, **(2) deterministic heuristic fallbacks that stand in when local/cloud model servers are offline**, **(3) vendor/creator numbers from the `INGEST/` transcripts**, and **(4) unbenchmarked latency targets for the planned Rust, Mojo, and Flutter layers**.

This audit separates **unsupported or unbenchmarked claims**, **vendor/creator-sourced numbers**, and **overstatements**, followed by the **corrected top 5 takeaways with confidence levels**.

---

## 1. Claims I Cannot Back With Measured Evidence (or That Need Narrower Wording)

| Report Claim or Implication | Skeptic's Audit & Narrower Defensible Wording |
| :--- | :--- |
| **"Liquid AI `d1-omni-600M` runs micro-decisions (`Choice`, `Score`, `Noul`, `RoutePrompt`, `SelectAffectedTests`) in `<15ms`."** | **Unbenchmarked for live model weights; true only for the Go heuristic fallback.** In `internal/decision/decider.go`, when a live Ollama/local endpoint serving `liquid/d1-omni-600m` is not running, Mímir falls back to deterministic Go keyword/scoring heuristics (`heuristicChoice`, `heuristicScore`, `heuristicNoul`). Those Go heuristics run in `<1ms`, but a live 600M LLM forward pass over HTTP was not benchmarked on this machine. **Better wording**: *"The Go heuristic fallback runs in `<1ms`; live `d1-omni-600M` inference latency depends on local CPU/GPU hardware and quantization."* |
| **"Disabling thinking (`/no_think`) on tool follow-up steps (`step > 0`) makes local tool loops `3-5x faster`."** | **Plausible engineering hypothesis, not a measured benchmark in `G:\Mimir`.** Skipping chain-of-thought tokens (`<think>...</think>`) mathematically reduces output token generation on reasoning models (like `qwen3` or `deepseek-r1`), which Leon van Zyl noted in `smolcoder`, but we did not run a controlled A/B timing benchmark across tool loops in `G:\Mimir`. **Better wording**: *"Setting `Effort: off` on `step > 0` eliminates reasoning-token overhead on follow-up tool steps; exact speedup depends on how verbose the model's `<think>` blocks are."* |
| **"Mojo SIMD cosine search runs in `<0.2ms`, bare-metal `d1-omni-600M` in `<5ms`, and Rust git worktree rollback in `<5ms`."** | **Target design specifications, not measured results.** Phases 3, 4, and 5 (`crates/mimir-rs/`, `mojo/mimir_mojo/`, and `ui/mimir_flutter/`) are architectural blueprints in `docs/MASTER-TODO.md`, not yet compiled code in the repository. **Better wording**: *"These are engineering latency targets for Phases 3-4, not measured benchmarks."* |
| **"SelectAffectedTests runs only the unit tests affected by edited files instead of a 10-minute full suite."** | **Simplified file-stem/import matching, not a full compiler dependency graph.** Right now, `internal/ingest/ingest.go` extracts regex-based imports/symbols and `SelectAffectedTests` in `internal/decision/decider.go` matches edited file stems and package paths against `*_test.go` candidates. It does not yet build a transitive cross-package compiler call graph. **Better wording**: *"Matches edited files to package/stem test files via the Mind Map; transitive cross-package test impact requires `go list -deps` or `cargo metadata`."* |
| **"Zero bloat in the main prompt: only `<60 tokens` (`~35-60 tokens`) loaded per SDLC phase."** | **Slightly understated token count when `WebOverlay` is included.** A pure backend SDLC micro-prompt in `internal/sdlc/phases.go` plus `CoreIdentityLine` is ~280-330 characters (~70-85 tokens). When `WebOverlay` is appended on a web task, the combined rules block is ~450-520 characters (~115-130 tokens). That is still ~80% smaller than loading all rules at once (~650+ tokens), but calling it `<60 tokens` was too tight. **Better wording**: *"~70-85 tokens for standard tasks and ~115-130 tokens when the phase's Web/SEO overlay is active."* |
| **"47 `.txt` and `.md` files in `INGEST/` are indexed as searchable neurons in Cortex memory."** | **Metadata and symbol/file summaries are indexed in `.mimir/cortex.json`, not full-text chunks of all 29.3 MB.** `persistToCortex` in `internal/ingest/ingest.go` saves a `KindSource` neuron per file containing the file's title, size, summary header, and top 12 extracted `FILE:` / `##` symbols so `.mimir/cortex.json` stays fast (~150 KB) rather than bloating to 30 MB. To read the full body of an `INGEST/` file, Mímir still uses `read_file`. **Better wording**: *"50 index neurons (file titles, summaries, and top symbols) are stored in `.mimir/cortex.json` pointing to the full files in `INGEST/`."* |

---

## 2. Every Number That Came From a Vendor, Creator Transcript, or Unvalidated Estimate

None of the following numbers should be treated as independent scientific facts:

| Number / Figure | Actual Origin & Limitations |
| :--- | :--- |
| **`~400 MB` for `Liquid AI d1-omni-600M`** | **Vendor / quantization estimate** (Liquid AI / 4-bit GGUF parameter math for a 600M parameter model). Actual download size varies by quantization (`Q4_K_M` vs `Q8_0` vs `FP16`) and multimodal projector weights. |
| **`30,000+ tokens` (Claude Code prompt) vs `~1,400 tokens` (`smolcoder`)** | **Creator transcript claim** from Leon van Zyl's YouTube video (`INGEST/YouTube_Video__z1EaBe9oIME_.txt`). Useful architectural contrast, not an independently audited benchmark across all CLI versions. |
| **`37% of users disengage` when trapped in undisclosed AI without human handoff** | **Secondary citation from the `INGEST/ai-marketing-prompt-v2-20261012.md` document** (referencing customer-service survey reporting). Self-reported consumer survey data, not a controlled local-service split test. |
| **`5-10%` brand website share of AI search citations** | **Vendor/industry study figure** cited in `INGEST/ai-marketing-prompt-v2-20261012.md`. Varies heavily by query intent (informational vs local transactional). |
| **`90% use Google`, `74% make a purchase within 24 hours`, `$1,200/day` with Google Maps** | **Sales/marketing pitch figures** from the Merchant / Justin Silverman YouTube interview (`INGEST/He Makes $1200 Per DAY with Google Maps in 2026 (No Experience Needed).txt`). `[vendor claim]` / promotional case anecdote, not a representative census. |
| **`$0/mo` (Sovereign), `$20/mo` (Well Pro), `$100/mo` (Odin Max)** | **My own illustrative product pricing design** in `internal/config/catalog.go`, modeled after `OpenCode` / `Claude Pro` / `Max` price bands. No billing gateway or Stripe backend is wired yet. |
| **`80% context window` handoff trigger & `<15 lines` `edit_block` snippet rule** | **Practical engineering heuristics** from `smolcoder` and harness design experience, not experimentally proven optima across all models. |

---

## 3. What I Overstated Most

1. **I let heuristic-fallback scaffolding sound like live local neural inference.**
   - `internal/decision/decider.go` is genuinely wired to call an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint for `liquid/d1-omni-600m`, and `mimir setup` is wired to pull it via Ollama. However, on this machine right now, `RoutePrompt`, `PruneToolNames`, `SelectMindMapFiles`, and `AssessCommandSafety` succeeded in tests using the **deterministic Go heuristic fallback**, not live `d1-omni-600M` neural weights.
2. **I presented provider catalog entries (`Meta Muse`, `Mímir Well Subscriptions`) as if the remote gateways were already live-tested.**
   - `internal/config/catalog.go` and `discovery.go` genuinely register `META_API_KEY` (`muse-wonder-1.0`, `muse-spark-1.0`, `muse-glimmer`, `muse-voice-transcribe`, `sam-3.1`) and `MIMIR_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY`, routing them through Mímir's OpenAI-compatible client (`internal/llm/openai.go`). However, without a live `META_API_KEY` or hosted `api.mimir.itak.live` gateway, those endpoints have only been tested against local `httptest` mock servers, not live Meta servers.
3. **I blurred the line between Phase 1 (live Go code on disk) and Phases 2-5 (roadmap blueprints).**
   - Even though `docs/MASTER-TODO.md` marks Phase 1 `[x]` and Phases 2-5 `[ ]`, my architectural diagrams and folder trees showed `crates/mimir-rs/`, `mojo/mimir_mojo/`, and `ui/mimir_flutter/` alongside `internal/` as if the polyglot folders already existed on disk. Only the **Go (`Bifrost-Core`)** layer is compiled and running today; **Rust (`Tyr-Core`)**, **Mojo (`Mjolnir-Compute`)**, and **Flutter (`Gjallarhorn-UI`)** are 100% planned `[ ]` work.
4. **I let prompt-injected SEO/GEO rules sound like deterministic HTML/schema enforcement.**
   - `internal/agent/rules.go` injects phase-scoped instructions telling the LLM to emit semantic HTML5, JSON-LD `Schema.org`, `/llms.txt`, and `[vendor claim]` labels. Until we build the deterministic `web_seo_audit` tool in **Phase 2.3**, Mímir is *instructing* the model to follow those rules, not yet *programmatically parsing and rejecting* non-compliant HTML output.

---

## 4. Corrected Top Five Takeaways, With Confidence Levels

*Confidence refers to confidence in the narrowly worded technical claim, backed by the actual code and tests in `G:\Mimir`.*

| # | Corrected Takeaway | Confidence | What the Code & Evidence Actually Support -- and What They Do Not |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | **Phase-scoped SDLC micro-prompts (`internal/sdlc`) cut Mímir's rules prompt overhead by ~80% compared to loading all engineering and SEO rules on every turn.** | **High** for token/character reduction; **Moderate** for downstream LLM task accuracy uplift. | **Supported**: Measured directly in `internal/sdlc/phases.go` and `internal/agent/rules_test.go` (~280-520 chars per turn vs ~2,600+ chars for the full combined rules). `Waterfall` sign-off gates and `.mimir/sdlc/0X-*.md` deliverables are verified by unit tests. **Not yet proven**: Controlled A/B benchmarks showing how much this improves pass rates on 7B-14B models. |
| **2** | **Mímir's Go Control Plane (`Stack 1`) is live, tested (`11/11` packages passing), and committed to GitHub (`a3126af`), while the Rust (`Stack 2`), Mojo (`Stack 3`), and Flutter (`Stack 4`) layers are detailed blueprints in `docs/MASTER-TODO.md`, not yet built.** | **High** (100% verifiable via `git status` and `go test ./...`). | **Supported**: `cmd/mimir`, `internal/agent`, `internal/sdlc`, `internal/decision`, `internal/ingest`, `internal/config`, `internal/cortex`, `internal/llm`, `internal/tools`, `internal/tui`, and `internal/server` compile and pass tests today. **Not built yet**: `crates/mimir-rs/`, `mojo/mimir_mojo/`, and `ui/mimir_flutter/`. |
| **3** | **Built-in `mimir ingest` (`internal/ingest`) generates a `GitIngest` `digest.txt` and indexes repository file/symbol metadata into `.mimir/cortex.json` in `<3s`, but stores compact metadata neurons rather than full-text vector embeddings of 29 MB of raw text.** | **High** for fast structural indexing and `digest.txt` generation; **Low** if expecting full-chunk semantic RAG over 29 MB without SurrealDB/Ollama embeddings enabled. | **Supported**: Verified live on `G:\Mimir` (99 files, 20 neurons) and `G:\Mimir\INGEST` (47 files, 50 index neurons). **Limitation**: File-backed `.mimir/cortex.json` uses substring/keyword search over neuron summaries and symbols; full dense vector search requires running the SurrealDB + Ollama embedder backend (`MIMIR_CORTEX_BACKEND=surreal`) or building Phase 4 Mojo SIMD search. |
| **4** | **`Huginn-Decider` (`internal/decision`) provides a working API contract (`Choice`, `Score`, `Noul`, `RoutePrompt`, `SelectAffectedTests`) with `<1ms` deterministic Go fallbacks today, ready to swap in live `Liquid AI d1-omni-600M` weights when a local model server is running.** | **High** for the Go fallback and OpenAI-compatible wire code; **Low-Moderate** for live `d1-omni-600M` routing accuracy until tested against actual model weights. | **Supported**: `decider_test.go` proves both the deterministic heuristic fallback and HTTP JSON parsing via `httptest`. **Not yet proven**: Live latency and routing accuracy of `liquid/d1-omni-600m` on your local GPU/CPU. |
| **5** | **Phase-scoped Web/SEO/GEO overlays (`internal/sdlc/phases.go`) guide the LLM toward semantic HTML5, JSON-LD `Schema.org`, `/llms.txt`, and `[vendor claim]` provenance, but deterministic enforcement requires building the Phase 2 `HookOnStop` and `web_seo_audit` validator tool.** | **High** that prompt guidance is injected only on web tasks in Steps 2-6; **Low** that prompt instructions alone guarantee 100% compliance without a post-tool linter gate. | **Supported**: `rules_test.go` confirms `WebOverlay` injects only when `DetectWebCreationTask` is true. **Next step required**: Building `internal/agent/hooks.go` (`Phase 2.1`) and `internal/tools/web_audit_tool.go` (`Phase 2.3`) so Mímir programmatically verifies HTML, JSON-LD, `/llms.txt`, and zero AI slop before finishing a turn. |

# Part II: Skeptic's Audit of the "MapPulse" SaaS SDLC Scenario (`docs/SAAS-SDLC-SCENARIO.md`)

**Bottom line**: The `MapPulse` walkthrough illustrates the intended workflow of Mímir's 7-Phase SDLC engine, but it blended **(1) live Go mechanics that execute today**, **(2) prompt-level instructions that rely on the LLM's compliance rather than hard runtime enforcement**, **(3) Phase 2-5 roadmap features (`mimir pair` phone app, `EvaluateStopGate` auto-hook) that are not yet built**, and **(4) fictional product numbers invented for the hypothetical `MapPulse` story**.

## 1. Scenario Claims I Cannot Back With Current Code (or That Need Narrower Wording)

| Scenario Claim or Implication | Skeptic's Audit & Narrower Defensible Wording |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Step 1: "Phase Tool Whitelist: Only `read_file`, `list_directory`, `ingest_repo`, `todo`, `question`, and `sdlc` are active (mutating code tools are held back so the LLM cannot prematurely vibe-code)."** | **True in `waterfall` mode (and `ro` mode), not in default `agile` mode.** In `internal/agent/agent.go` (`schemas()`), `AllowedToolSet()` filters the tool schemas when `Methodology() == MethodWaterfall`. In default `agile` mode (`ModeEdit`), all edit-mode tools remain visible so the developer can iterate freely unless they switch to `/sdlc waterfall` or `/mode ro`. Also, our initial `phases.go` draft listed `"list_dir"` and `"run_shell"` instead of the actual registered tool names `"list_directory"` and `"bash"` (now fixed in `phases.go` and `rules.go`). |
| **Steps 1-7: "Persona Activated: `Odin` / `Huginn` / `Thor` / `Loki` / `Heimdall` / `Muninn`."** | **Label in the phase micro-prompt, not a full persona system-prompt swap.** Each `PhaseSpec` in `internal/sdlc/phases.go` tags the phase micro-prompt with `(Odin)`, `(Huginn)`, `(Thor)`, `(Loki)`, `(Heimdall)`, or `(Muninn)`. However, `buildPromptForInput` in `internal/agent/agent.go` intentionally does **not** inject the full multi-paragraph `Persona.FullPrompt()` from `internal/agent/personas.go` on every turn because doing so would violate our zero-bloat rule. Full persona prompts only load when explicitly selected via `/persona <name>`. |
| **Step 4: "If the user walks away from their desk... they run `mimir pair`, scan the terminal QR code with the Mímir Phone App, and approve file writes or steer from their phone."** | **Unbuilt Phase 5 roadmap feature.** `mimir pair` (`internal/relay/happy_e2ee.go`) and the Flutter Mobile Companion (`ui/mimir_flutter/`) are planned in **Phase 5 (`5.1` - `5.4`)** of `docs/MASTER-TODO.md`. Today, remote approval/steering away from the terminal can only be done via the local/LAN Book-Spine Web UI (`mimir --web` on `:8420`). |
| **Step 5: "`SelectAffectedTests` queries the Yggdrasil Mind Map to identify every `*_test.go` file covering `telephony`, `reviews`, `billing`, and `web`."** | **Available via `/mindmap <query>` and `Decider.SelectAffectedTests()`, not auto-invoked inside `runLoop` yet.** `SelectAffectedTests` is implemented and tested in `internal/decision/decider.go` and wired into the `/mindmap` TUI command, but during Step 5 `Loki` runs `go test ./...` via the `bash` tool rather than having the Go loop automatically rewrite the test command. |
| **Step 5: "`Loki` calls `EvaluateStopGate` (`internal/agent/rules.go`) to confirm 0 pending todos and 100% passing verification."** | **Go helper function, not an LLM-callable tool or active `OnStop` loop blocker yet.** `EvaluateStopGate(trace, todoLines)` is a Go function in `internal/agent/rules.go`, not a registered tool in `internal/tools/default.go`. Wiring it into `runLoop` / `RunStream` as an automatic `HookOnStop` blocker is **Task `2.1.d`** in Phase 2. |
| **Steps 1-7: "`Odin` / `Huginn` / `Thor` / `Loki` / `Heimdall` / `Muninn` calls `sdlc` (`save_deliverable`) to write `.mimir/sdlc/01-PLAN.md` .. `07-MAINTENANCE.md`."** | **Prompt-guided tool call in `agile` mode; strictly enforced gate only in `waterfall` mode.** In `agile` mode, the phase micro-prompt instructs the LLM to save the deliverable via the `sdlc` tool, but whether the model actually invokes `sdlc` depends on the LLM following instructions. Only `waterfall` mode (`mgr.SetMethodology("waterfall")`) deterministically blocks advancing to the next phase until `SaveDeliverable` or `SignOff` is called. |

# Mímir Testing Policy

**Standing rule (non-negotiable):** after every build and after every feature, run a
**live test** against a real model - not only unit tests. Unit tests prove the code is
correct in isolation; a live test proves the whole stack (provider wire format, streaming,
the recall -> infer -> remember loop) actually works end-to-end against a real backend.

## The three tiers

1. **Unit tests** - `go test ./...`. Always run, always green, offline. Includes a fake
   HTTP server that speaks the OpenAI-compatible wire format, so the provider + loop are
   tested without network or keys.
2. **Live test** - `go test ./internal/agent -run TestLiveRun -v` with the env vars below.
   Hits a real provider. **Skipped automatically** when `MIMIR_LIVE_BASE_URL` is unset, so
   it never breaks offline/CI runs.
3. **CLI smoke** - `go run ./cmd/mimir "prompt"` against a real provider; eyeball the reply.

## Running the live test

Local, free, no key (Ollama):

```powershell
$env:MIMIR_LIVE_BASE_URL = "http://localhost:11434/v1"
$env:MIMIR_LIVE_MODEL    = "qwen2.5:0.5b"   # or qwen3:8b, gemma4:e2b, etc.
go test ./internal/agent -run TestLiveRun -v
```

Cloud (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint):

```powershell
$env:MIMIR_LIVE_BASE_URL = "https://api.openai.com/v1"   # or OpenRouter, Groq, the Qwen compatible-mode, Mímir's own gateway
$env:MIMIR_LIVE_API_KEY  = $env:SOME_KEY                 # never echo the value
$env:MIMIR_LIVE_MODEL    = "gpt-5-nano"
go test ./internal/agent -run TestLiveRun -v
```

## Discipline

- A feature is **not done** until both `go test ./...` (green) and a live test (pass) have
  run. The live test does not need to be in CI (keys/cost), but it must be run by the
  developer/agent after the change.
- The live test must never print secrets: keys come from the environment and are never
  logged. Our provider's error path prints the server response body, never the request
  Authorization header.
- If the live test fails on a credential/401, that is a *credential* problem, not a code
  defect - but the network path still counts as "exercised." Fall back to a local Ollama
  model to get a clean pass that isolates the code from the credential.
- `go vet ./...` must also be clean after every change.

## Tool loop (when you add/change tools or the loop)

- **Deterministic (offline):** `go test ./internal/agent -run TestRunToolLoop -v` - a fake
  model asks to run `bash`, the loop runs the real tool, feeds the result back, and the
  model's final reply is returned. `TestRunUnknownTool` proves a bad tool name degrades
  gracefully. These never need network or keys.
- **Live:** `MIMIR_LIVE_TOOL=1 MIMIR_LIVE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1
  MIMIR_LIVE_MODEL=qwen3:8b go test ./internal/agent -run TestLiveToolCall -v` - a real
  model drives a real tool end-to-end. Needs a tool-capable model (qwen3:8b works; tiny
  models usually won't tool-call, so this is gated off by default).
- **CLI trace (watch it act):** `mimir trace "your prompt"` prints each tool call
  (name + args + result) then the final reply - the human-observable proof and a useful
  transparency/observability feature (F60).

A tool feature is not done until `TestRunToolLoop` passes (offline) AND a live tool test
or `mimir trace` shows a real model calling a real tool.

## Cross-run memory (the namesake feature)

- **Offline:** `go test ./internal/agent -run TestCrossRunMemory -v` - run 1 (fake model)
  writes a memory to a file-backed Cortex; a fresh store reopened from the same file
  (simulating a restart) recalls it on run 2. Proves memory survives across runs with no
  network. `go test ./internal/cortex/...` proves the store persists + the lexical recall.
- **Live:** `MIMIR_LIVE_MEMORY=1 MIMIR_LIVE_BASE_URL=... go test ./internal/agent -run TestLiveCrossRunMemory -v` - same, with a real model writing the memory.
- **CLI demo:** `demo.ps1` step 5 plants a code in run 1 and shows the `[memory]` recall
  line in run 2.
- Memory persists to `.mimir/cortex.json` (override with `MIMIR_CORTEX` / `MIMIR_HOME`).
  SurrealDB (E6.2) upgrades this to vector + graph recall; the file store is the base.

cloud data deleted Jul 15; repo read-only). Pre-acq: Solo free BYOK / Teams ~$10. Per-

**Gap: now defunct → 3.6M-install orphaned community needs a home (Apache 2.0 forkable but
unmaintained).** News: acquired by Cursor Jun 2026 (itself being bought by SpaceX/xAI).

---

## Updated White-Space Synthesis (after 29 competitors total)

The intersection **durable personal memory + guided gated SDLC + local-first sovereignty**
remains **completely unoccupied**. New strategic reads from batch 2:

1. **Three refugee pools just opened:** Continue (3.6M, shuttered by Cursor), Roo Code
   (3M, sunset), Aider (stalled). A maintained, memory-first, local-first successor can
   absorb them. Cline is the current magnet - Mímir competes with memory + SDLC + UI.
2. **Memory is heating up - move fast.** Codex shipped a "memory preview" (Apr 2026) -
   the first incumbent to touch it, but it's shallow preference recall, not a neural
   graph. Augment's Expert Registry is org-level, not personal. The personal-memory
   wedge is still open but closing.
3. **The prosumer/indie segment is being abandoned:** Tabnine killed free/individual
   tiers; Augment dropped its sub-$100 plan; Copilot's credit migration angered users.
   Mímir's free-self-hosted + cheap sync owns this.
4. **Cloud lock-in + billing opacity is the universal flank:** Replit ($9B), Lovable
   ($6.6-13B), Bolt ($700M) prove huge demand for "build with AI" but all have token
   anxiety + dual-layer billing + no data sovereignty. "Your models, your machine,
   cancel anytime" attacks them directly.
5. **Local sovereignty has a model ally:** Poolside's open-weight XS.2 (Apache 2.0, runs
   on a Mac) is a perfect local model to bundle/support - strengthens the no-cloud story.
6. **Computer use is table-stakes-soon:** Codex (Mac) + Factory Desktop (Apr 2026) +
   Replit self-test all have it. Mímir's F48 must match, not just claim.
7. **Autonomy vs guidance is the philosophical split:** the market races to "let go of
   the IDE" (Codex, Roomote, SOLO, Missions). Mímir's gated step-by-step is a deliberate
   contrarian bet for devs/teams who want control + auditability - and it's uncontested.

## Marketing / Positioning (refined)

- **Lead:** "the agent that remembers + walks the SDLC with you + you own it."
- **Recruit the refugees:** "your open, local, memory-first home" aimed at Continue/Roo/
  Aider orphans.
- **Attack billing opacity:** transparent, predictable, free self-hosted vs the credit/
  dual-layer chaos of Copilot/Cursor/Replit/Lovable.
- **Own the contrarian lane:** guided + human-in-the-loop, against the autonomy stampede.
- **Bundle a sovereign local model** (Poolside XS.2 / Qwen / nomic) to make "no cloud"
  real out of the box.

# Competitive Landscape - AI Coding Tools (July 2026)

**Analyst:** Mímir competitive-analysis workflow (F72)
**Date:** 2026-07-23
**Competitors analyzed:** OpenCode, Kiro, Devin, Cursor, Windsurf, CodeRabbit, Zencoder,
Mintlify, Paralect, Blitzy, Air (JetBrains), Merget, Qoder, Telerik
**Companion:** `opencode.md` (deep dive + authenticated dashboard),
`COMPETITIVE-LANDSCAPE-2.md` (16 more: Copilot, Codex, Cline, Roo, Q, Tabnine, Cody/Amp,
Replit, Augment, Trae, Factory, Poolside, Aider, Bolt, Lovable, Continue).

---

## Executive Summary - The White Space

Every competitor optimizes for **speed of code generation** and/or **autonomy**. **None**
owns the combination Mímir is built on:

> **Durable, user-owned memory + a guided, gated full-SDLC partnership + local-first
> sovereignty (your models, no lock-in).**

| Mímir differentiator | The gap across the field |
|---|---|
| **Neural knowledge graph (remembers everything)** | Everyone is stateless or session-scoped. Blitzy has a codebase graph (enterprise, $500K+/yr). Merget records context (team/cloud). Nobody has a *personal, persistent, growing* memory. |
| **Guided, user-gated SDLC** | Kiro/Zencoder/Qoder have specs but rigid/delegation-oriented. Devin/Cursor are autonomy-first. Nobody *walks with you* step-by-step, gated. |
| **Local-first / your models / no lock-in** | Kiro (AWS), Devin (cloud), Cursor (cloud + SpaceX), Qoder (Alibaba) are all locked. Mímir is sovereign. |
| **Computer use + futuristic UI** | Devin has desktop QA (cloud). Nobody combines coding agent + computer use in a distinctive, alive UI. |

**The two biggest competitive threats:** Cursor (DX leader, $4B ARR, but pricing-trust
deficit + SpaceX lock-in) and Qoder (price + distribution + spec-driven, but
Alibaba/privacy concerns). **Merget** validates the memory thesis from the team/cloud
angle - a potential ally or cautionary tale.

---

## Per-Competitor Summaries

### OpenCode (opencode.ai) - see `opencode.md`
Open-source AI coding agent (160K+ stars, 7.5M monthly devs). Free CLI + Zen
(pay-as-you-go, zero markup) + Go ($10/mo). **Gap: stateless, no memory, no guided
SDLC, cloud for the good stuff.**

### Kiro (kiro.dev) - AWS
Spec-driven IDE (successor to Amazon Q Developer, retires Apr 2027). Credit-based
(Free 50 / Pro $20 / Pro+ $40 / Pro Max $100 / Power $200). Generates
requirements/design/tasks before code; property-based testing; agent hooks.
**Gap: AWS/Bedrock lock-in, no BYOK, credit opacity, rigid specs, no memory.**
News: GA May 2026; replaces Amazon Q; Pro Max + iOS app Jun 2026.

### Devin (devin.ai) - Cognition
First-mover autonomous SWE agent. $1B+ Series D at **$26B** (May 2026); ~$492M
run-rate. Free / Pro $20 / Max $200 / Teams $80+ / Enterprise. Full autonomy,
dynamic re-planning, desktop QA via computer use, fleets of parallel Devins. Acquired
Windsurf (Jul 2025). **Gap: cloud-only, no BYOK, opaque metering, weak on ambiguous
work, no persistent memory.** 89% of Cognition's own code now committed by Devin.

### Cursor (cursor.com) - Anysphere
Dominant AI-native editor. **SpaceX/xAI $60B all-stock acquisition** announced Jun 2026;
$4B ARR. Hobby free / Pro $20 / Pro+ $60 / Ultra $200 / Teams. Best-in-class Tab
autocomplete, Composer 2.5, background/cloud agents, Bugbot. **Gap: no SDLC methodology,
no memory, metered-pricing trust deficit (Jul 2025 backlash), cloud + SpaceX lock-in.**

### Windsurf (windsurf.dev) - Cognition (acquired Dec 2025, ~$250M)
AI IDE, now Devin's front-end. Free / Pro $20 / Max $200 / Teams $40. Cascade agent,
SWE-1.6 (950 tok/s), Devin Cloud, Codemaps, Agent Command Center. **Gap: cloud-dependent,
session memory only, no guided SDLC, 3 owners in 18 months, proprietary model.**

### CodeRabbit (coderabbit.ai)
AI code review leader. $88M raised, **$550M** valuation, ~$40M ARR (700% YoY). Free /
Pro $24 / Pro Plus $48 / Enterprise. CodeGraph, 40+ linters, learnings, Slack/Discord
agent. **Gap: reactive (post-PR), not a builder, no memory graph, cloud, per-seat cost.**

### Zencoder (zencoder.ai)
Multi-model orchestration (Andrew Filev, ex-Wrike $2.25B exit). Free / Starter $19 /
Core $49 / Advanced $119 / Max $250. Multi-model cross-validation, spec-driven with
checkpoints, BYOK, Zenflow desktop app. **Gap: cloud SaaS, no memory, small/unfunded,
no computer use.** Closest to Mímir's gated-SDLC concept.

### Mintlify (mintlify.com)
Docs/knowledge platform pivoting to "AI knowledge infrastructure." $45M Series B at
**$500M** (Apr 2026, a16z). Free / Pro $250/mo / Enterprise. Docs-as-code, AI assistant,
auto MCP server, Agent Score. **Gap: cloud-only, $0→$250 cliff, documents not guides,
no memory/SDLC.**

### Paralect (paralect.com)
Product dev company / venture studio (not a product). Bootstrapped, services from
$2,500/bi-weekly. Full-SDLC services, "no lock-in" messaging, Ship boilerplate. **Gap:
it's a services business (time-for-money), not a scalable product; no memory product.**
Validates demand for a no-lock-in full-SDLC partner.

### Blitzy (blitzy.com)
Autonomous enterprise dev platform. $200M at **$1.4B** (May 2026, Northzone). Enterprise
only ($50K entry, $500K-$50M/yr). Reverse-engineers codebases into a knowledge graph,
orchestrates 3,000+ agents. 66.5% SWE-Bench Pro. **Gap: enterprise-only pricing,
batch/black-box non-cancellable runs, their infra, no personal memory.** Validates the
knowledge-graph thesis at enterprise scale.

### Air (air.dev) - JetBrains
Agentic Development Environment (ADE). Free preview (requires JetBrains AI sub or BYOK).
Parallel multi-agent (Claude/Codex/Gemini/Junie + ACP agents), isolated execution
(Docker/worktrees/cloud), co-developing ACP protocol. **Gap: no memory, no guided SDLC,
JetBrains-tied, utilitarian UI.** Local-friendly (partial overlap with Mímir).

### Merget (merget.ai)
"System of record for AI-native dev." $1M seed (IDrive), v0 Jul 2026. Auto-captures
prompts/diffs/goals across tools, D.O.M (Deep Organizational Memory), Merget Map/Stats.
**Gap: team-observability not an individual agent, cloud/GitHub-centric, very early.**
Closest conceptual cousin to Mímir's memory thesis - validates it from the team angle.

### Qoder (qoder.com) - Alibaba-backed
Agentic coding platform, 5M+ users. Free / Pro $20 / Pro+ $60 / Ultra $200 / Teams $40.
Quest Mode (spec-driven), RepoWiki, Knowledge Engine, QoderWork (local-first), Qwen3-Coder.
**Gap: Alibaba/China privacy concerns, cloud/credit-metered, per-repo knowledge, delegation
not guided.** Big threat on price + distribution.

### Telerik (telerik.com) - Progress Software
.NET/JS UI component library (1,250+ components), not an agent. $649-$1,649/dev/yr.
Now has AI Coding Assistant + Agentic UI Generator via MCP. **Not a direct rival - an
integration candidate (MCP).** Highlights Mímir's local-first/model-agnostic identity.

## 1. Overview

OpenCode is an open-source AI coding agent (terminal, IDE, desktop) by Anomaly.
160K-190K GitHub stars, 900 contributors, 7.5M monthly devs. Free CLI + two paid
products (Zen, Go). Positioning: "the open source AI coding agent" - privacy-first,
use any model, no lock-in.

## 2. Products & Pricing

| Product | What | Price | Models | Hook |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **CLI** | open-source agent (terminal/IDE/desktop) | free | any (75+ via Models.dev) | open source, privacy-first |
| **Zen** | curated model gateway | pay-as-you-go, add $20 (+$1.23 fee), per-request, **zero markup**, auto-top-up at $5→+$20 | curated/benchmarked models | "use with any agent, cancel anytime" |
| **Go** | low-cost subscription | **$10/mo ($5 first month)**, top-up credit | open-source models (Grok 4.5, GLM-5.2, Kimi K3, Qwen3.7, MiniMax, DeepSeek...) | "generous limits, $5 first month" |
| **Enterprise** | enterprise tier | custom | - | privacy, governance |

**Pricing model:** free CLI (top of funnel) → Zen (pay-as-you-go, power users) + Go
($10/mo, cost-conscious). Both: "use with any agent," cancel anytime, transparent
pricing, zero markups.

## 3. Features (from site)

- LSP enabled (auto-loads the right LSPs)
- Multi-session (parallel agents on the same project)
- Share links (share a session for reference/debug)
- GitHub Copilot login (use your Copilot account)
- ChatGPT Plus/Pro login (use your OpenAI account)
- Any model (75+ providers via Models.dev, incl. local)
- Any editor (terminal, desktop app, IDE extension)
- Privacy-first (no code/context stored)

**Nav (consistent):** GitHub · Docs · Data · Zen · Go · Enterprise · Login/Download

- **Core promise:** "the open source AI coding agent" - free, open, privacy-first.

# Mímir - Architecture Document

**BMAD Artifact - Phase 4 (Winston, System Architect)**
Date: 2026-07-23 | Status: Draft for implementation-readiness review
Inputs: `mimirmind-prd.md`, `PROJECT-MASTER-PLAN.md`
Feeds: `bmad-check-implementation-readiness`, then epics/stories + build.

---

## 1. Architecture Overview

Mímir is a **modular, local-first agentic coding framework**. A single Go binary runs a
long-lived **daemon** that owns the agent loop, tools, the Cortex (SurrealDB brain),
sandboxing, plugins, and a local server. A **web GUI** (Solid) is served by the daemon
(also packaged as a Wails desktop app); a **Bubble Tea TUI** and (later) mobile/chat
clients all talk to the same daemon over a local REST + WebSocket API.

**Style:** modular monolith (clean package boundaries + a typed plugin SDK) running as a
local service; plugin-extensible; provider-agnostic. Not microservices - one process,
many well-separated packages, with SurrealDB as the only external companion.

```
                 +--------------------------------------------------+
   GUI (Solid) --|                                                  |
   TUI (BubbleTea)|              MIMIR DAEMON (Go binary)           |
   Mobile/Chat ---|  +----------+  +--------+  +-----------------+  |
        |        |  | Agent    |  | Tools  |  | Cortex (SurrealDB)| |
   REST + WS ---->|  | Loop     |->| (native|->| neurons/synapses | |
                 |  | (state   |  | + MCP) |  | engrams + RAG    | |
                 |  |  machine)|  +--------+  +-----------------+  |
                 |  +----------+                                    |
                 |  +----------+  +--------+  +-----------------+  |
                 |  | Plugin   |  | Policy |  | Sandbox Manager |  |
                 |  | Registry |  | Gate   |  | (Docker/Firecr.)|  |
                 |  +----------+  +--------+  +-----------------+  |
                 |  +--------------------------------------------+ |
                 |  | LLM Provider Abstraction (OpenAI-compat HTTP)| |
                 |  +--------------------------------------------+ |
                 +--------------------------------------------------+
                                   |
                    +--------------+--------------+
                    |                             |
            Any cloud provider             Local model
            (OpenAI/Anthropic/...)        (Ollama/llama.cpp/vLLM)
```

---

## 2. Resolved Decisions (PRD open questions)

| # | Question | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | SurrealDB embedded vs sidecar | **Managed sidecar** (daemon auto-starts a local SurrealDB; Docker or bundled binary) | SurrealDB's Go support is client/server; a managed sidecar keeps the brain durable and upgradable. Embedded revisited later. |
| Q2 | GUI framework | **Solid** (SolidJS) | Fast, fine-grained reactivity, small bundles; matches the user's prior SolidJS experience (agence). React is an acceptable fallback. |
| Q3 | Default zero-config model | **Ollama** if detected locally; else prompt for a provider key | Ollama is the most common local runtime; gives a true "runs with no key" path. |
| Q4 | Telemetry | **On by default**; opt-out in privacy settings | Collect anonymized metrics to improve the system; users can disable any time. |

---

## 3. Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)

### ADR-001: Go for the core runtime
- **Context:** Need a cross-platform single binary, a home-server daemon, parallel
  agents, and mobile clients.
- **Decision:** Implement the daemon, agent loop, tools, sandbox, plugins, and server
  in Go. The GUI is a separate web frontend (TypeScript/Solid).
- **Consequences:** (+) single static binary per OS/arch, great concurrency, robust
  daemon. (-) thinner AI ecosystem than TS - mitigated because LLM access is plain
  OpenAI-compatible HTTP and a Go MCP SDK exists.

### ADR-002: SurrealDB as the Cortex store
- **Context:** The brain needs graph (relationships), vector (RAG), and document
  (content) queries in one store.
- **Decision:** Use SurrealDB (multi-model: graph + vector + document + KV).
- **Consequences:** (+) one store for neurons/synapses/engrams + sessions + audit;
  native `RELATE` graph + vector search. (-) a companion service to manage (see ADR-003).

### ADR-003: SurrealDB as a managed sidecar
- **Decision:** The daemon auto-starts/manages a local SurrealDB (Docker container or
  bundled binary) and connects over `ws://localhost:8000/rpc`.
- **Consequences:** (+) durable, upgradeable brain; consistent with Open Notebook. (-)
  one more process; the daemon must health-check/restart it.

### ADR-004: Multi-dialect provider abstraction (OpenAI + Anthropic native; no SDK lock-in)
- **Decision:** A provider abstraction with pluggable API **dialects/encoders**. Built
  in: **OpenAI-compatible** (`/v1/chat/completions`, streaming) and **Anthropic-native**
  (`/v1/messages`). Per-provider adapters set base URL, auth, dialect, and quirks. More
  dialects (e.g. Gemini) via plugins.
- **Consequences:** (+) both OpenAI and Anthropic endpoints work natively; any provider
  or local model via one code path; no vendor SDK dependency. (-) we own per-dialect
  request/response mapping + streaming/usage parsing (small, well-understood).

### ADR-005: Modular packages + typed plugin SDK + central registry
- **Decision:** Clean Go package boundaries; plugins register capabilities via a typed
  `MimirPluginApi` into a central `PluginRegistry`; plugins import only
  `@mimirmind/plugin-sdk` barrels, never core internals.
- **Consequences:** (+) extensible without forking; testable modules (the lesson from
  agence's fork debt). (-) requires a stable SDK contract + contract tests.

### ADR-006: Solid for the GUI
- **Decision:** Web GUI in SolidJS, served by the daemon; packaged as a desktop app via
  Wails.
- **Consequences:** (+) fast, small, fine-grained; user familiarity. (-) smaller
  ecosystem than React (acceptable).

### ADR-007: Tiered sandbox (containers + microVMs)
- **Decision:** Sandbox Manager offers containers (fast, trusted code) and
  Firecracker/gVisor microVMs (strong, untrusted code), with an in-guest agent exposing
  exec/files/PTY; the agent picks per task.
- **Consequences:** (+) strong isolation on demand; snapshot/fork; per-user isolation.
  (-) complexity; containers ship first, microVMs later.

### ADR-008: Neural data model (neurons / synapses / engrams)
- **Decision:** Model knowledge as a neural graph: neurons (nodes), synapses (edges),
  engrams (durable memories), stored in SurrealDB.
- **Consequences:** (+) associative, self-organizing memory; distinctive identity. (-)
  more schema design than flat rows (worth it).

### ADR-009: Fail-closed policy gate (deterministic governance)
- **Decision:** Every tool/plugin call passes a deterministic policy gate BEFORE
  execution; default-deny with allow/require_approval rules; unbypassable.
- **Consequences:** (+) misbehavior is structurally impossible, not prompt-discouraged.
  (-) policy authoring overhead (ship sensible defaults).

### ADR-010: Ollama default local model; telemetry on by default (opt-out)
- **Decision:** Zero-config path uses Ollama if present. Telemetry is **on by default**
  (anonymized usage metrics) with an opt-out in privacy settings.
- **Consequences:** (+) true "no key, no cloud" first run; we collect data to improve the
  system. (-) must be transparent, easy opt-out, and never collect code/content by default.

### ADR-011: Small-model-first structured workflow
- **Context:** A core goal is smooth coding on <=30B local models, which derail easily
  (too many tools, open-ended tasks, weak planning, poor self-verification).
- **Decision:** Enforce a structured protocol: mandatory game plan -> convert to an
  ordered to-do list -> work one item at a time (implement -> debug -> test -> done) ->
  verify each step. For small models, expose a lean tool set and focused context.
- **Consequences:** (+) small models stay on track and produce working code; the to-do
  list is the agent's working memory. (-) adds a planning step (worth it; large models
  can fast-path it).

---

## 5. Cortex Schema (SurrealDB / SurrealQL)

```sql
-- Neurons: the knowledge nodes (sources, notes, concepts, memories, skills)
DEFINE TABLE neuron SCHEMAFULL;
DEFINE FIELD kind        ON neuron TYPE string
  ASSERT $value IN ["source","note","concept","memory","skill"];
DEFINE FIELD layer       ON neuron TYPE string
  ASSERT $value IN ["activity","context","experience","identity","preference"];
DEFINE FIELD scope       ON neuron TYPE string DEFAULT "project";   -- or "__global__"
DEFINE FIELD title       ON neuron TYPE string;
DEFINE FIELD content     ON neuron TYPE string;
DEFINE FIELD summary     ON neuron TYPE option<string>;
DEFINE FIELD embedding   ON neuron FLEXIBLE TYPE option<array<float>>;  -- vector
DEFINE FIELD importance  ON neuron TYPE string DEFAULT "medium"
  ASSERT $value IN ["low","medium","high","critical"];
DEFINE FIELD decay_score ON neuron TYPE float DEFAULT 1.0;            -- forgetting curve
DEFINE FIELD access_count ON neuron TYPE int DEFAULT 0;               -- reinforcement
DEFINE FIELD last_accessed ON neuron TYPE option<datetime>;
DEFINE FIELD expires_at  ON neuron TYPE option<datetime>;
DEFINE FIELD provenance  ON neuron FLEXIBLE TYPE option<object>;      -- {docPath,docHash,url}
DEFINE FIELD confidence  ON neuron TYPE option<float>;
DEFINE FIELD created_at  ON neuron TYPE datetime DEFAULT time::now();
DEFINE FIELD updated_at  ON neuron TYPE datetime DEFAULT time::now();
DEFINE INDEX neuron_embedding ON neuron FIELDS embedding MTREE DIMENSION 1536;
DEFINE INDEX neuron_fts ON neuron FIELDS title, content SEARCH ANALYZER ascii BM25;

-- Synapses: typed relationships between neurons (graph edges)
DEFINE TABLE synapse SCHEMAFULL;
DEFINE FIELD in    ON synapse TYPE record<neuron>;
DEFINE FIELD out   ON synapse TYPE record<neuron>;
DEFINE FIELD kind  ON synapse TYPE string
  ASSERT $value IN ["references","derives_from","relates_to","contradicts","cross_layer_link"];
DEFINE FIELD weight ON synapse TYPE float DEFAULT 1.0;
DEFINE FIELD created_at ON synapse TYPE datetime DEFAULT time::now();
-- usage: RELATE neuron:a->synapse->neuron:b SET kind="relates_to", weight=0.8;

-- Engrams: durable memories (a neuron kind=memory promoted to long-term)
DEFINE TABLE engram SCHEMAFULL;
DEFINE FIELD neuron   ON engram TYPE record<neuron>;
DEFINE FIELD strength ON engram TYPE float DEFAULT 1.0;
DEFINE FIELD consolidated ON engram TYPE bool DEFAULT false;

-- Sessions / messages
DEFINE TABLE session SCHEMAFULL;
DEFINE FIELD project ON session TYPE string;
DEFINE FIELD agent   ON session TYPE string DEFAULT "default";
DEFINE FIELD created_at ON session TYPE datetime DEFAULT time::now();
DEFINE TABLE message SCHEMAFULL;
DEFINE FIELD session ON message TYPE record<session>;
DEFINE FIELD role    ON message TYPE string ASSERT $value IN ["user","assistant","tool","system"];
DEFINE FIELD content ON message TYPE string;
DEFINE FIELD tool_calls ON message FLEXIBLE TYPE option<array>;
DEFINE FIELD created_at ON message TYPE datetime DEFAULT time::now();

-- Audit: tamper-evident, hash-chained
DEFINE TABLE audit SCHEMAFULL;
DEFINE FIELD prev_hash ON audit TYPE string;
DEFINE FIELD hash      ON audit TYPE string;        -- hash(prev_hash + tool + args + decision)
DEFINE FIELD tool      ON audit TYPE string;
DEFINE FIELD args      ON audit FLEXIBLE TYPE object;
DEFINE FIELD policy_decision ON audit TYPE string ASSERT $value IN ["allow","deny","require_approval"];
DEFINE FIELD result_code ON audit TYPE option<int>;
DEFINE FIELD created_at ON audit TYPE datetime DEFAULT time::now();

-- Skills, tasks, sandboxes
DEFINE TABLE skill SCHEMAFULL;
DEFINE FIELD name ON skill TYPE string;
DEFINE FIELD content ON skill TYPE string;
DEFINE FIELD source ON skill TYPE string ASSERT $value IN ["reflected","quality_gate","manual"];
DEFINE TABLE task SCHEMAFULL;
DEFINE FIELD goal      ON task TYPE string;
DEFINE FIELD status    ON task TYPE string DEFAULT "pending"
  ASSERT $value IN ["pending","in_progress","completed","blocked"];
DEFINE FIELD plan      ON task FLEXIBLE TYPE option<object>;   -- the game plan
DEFINE FIELD session   ON task TYPE option<record<session>>;
DEFINE FIELD created_at ON task TYPE datetime DEFAULT time::now();
-- To-do items: the game plan broken into ordered, verifiable steps (small-model memory)
DEFINE TABLE todo SCHEMAFULL;
DEFINE FIELD task     ON todo TYPE record<task>;
DEFINE FIELD ord      ON todo TYPE int;                        -- order
DEFINE FIELD content  ON todo TYPE string;
DEFINE FIELD status   ON todo TYPE string DEFAULT "pending"
  ASSERT $value IN ["pending","in_progress","completed","blocked"];
DEFINE FIELD parent   ON todo TYPE option<record<todo>>;       -- subtasks
DEFINE FIELD depends  ON todo FLEXIBLE TYPE option<array<record<todo>>>;  -- dependencies
DEFINE FIELD tags     ON todo FLEXIBLE TYPE option<array<string>>;
DEFINE FIELD verified ON todo TYPE bool DEFAULT false;         -- debug/test passed
DEFINE TABLE sandbox SCHEMAFULL;
DEFINE FIELD backend ON sandbox TYPE string ASSERT $value IN ["container","microvm"];
DEFINE FIELD status ON sandbox TYPE string DEFAULT "creating";
DEFINE FIELD snapshot_id ON sandbox TYPE option<string>;
```

## 6. Agent-Loop State Machine

States: `idle -> running -> (awaiting_approval) -> running -> (compacting) -> done | error`.

```
run(sessionKey, prompt):
  1. INTAKE        - resolve session, persist user message
  2. ASSEMBLE      - build system prompt: AGENTS.md + active skills + recalled
                     engrams (<past_learnings>) + tool schemas
  3. INFER (stream)- call provider; stream tokens to UI
  4. ACT           - on tool_call: policy gate -> (approve?) -> execute in
                     sandbox/native -> persist result -> capture memory if outcome
  5. LOOP          - feed result back; goto 3 until model stops
  6. COMPACT       - if near limit, compact (re-inject memory + skills)
  7. DONE/ERROR    - persist final; emit lifecycle event
```
- Runs are serialized per session lane (no tool/session races); subagents run on their
  own goroutines with isolated context, returning only a summary.
- The policy gate (ADR-009) wraps every ACT step; a `require_approval` transitions to
  `awaiting_approval` and pauses until the user responds (GUI/TUI/mobile).

### Small-Model Mode (<=30B) - structured workflow
Small models derail easily (too many tools, open-ended tasks, weak planning). Mímir
keeps them on track with a forced structure (ADR-011):
1. **Game plan first** - before any code, produce a spec (requirements -> design ->
   tasks). Plan-before-code is enforced.
2. **Plan -> to-do list** - convert the plan into an ordered `todo` list (each item
   small + independently verifiable), persisted in SurrealDB.
3. **One item at a time** - work a single todo: implement -> debug -> test -> mark
   `completed` -> next. The to-do list is the model's working memory, re-injected each
   step so it stays oriented.
4. **Verify each step** - run tests/checks after each item; debug before advancing.
5. **Lean tools** - for small models, expose a focused set (read/write/edit/bash/
   todowrite) instead of all tools; focused context (only the current task).
6. **Anti-derailment** - doom-loop detection (F4.3), step budgets, "re-read the plan"
   re-orientation prompts.
- **Model-tier awareness:** detect small models (size/family) and auto-enable this mode
  + lean tools; large models get the full toolset (and may fast-path the plan).

### Agent personas (Norse)
Agent modes/subagents are named Norse figures (F33): **Odin** (orchestrator/planner),
**Thor** (builder), **Loki** (debugger/tester), **Heimdall** (reviewer + policy gate),
**Bragi** (docs/skald); subagents **Huginn & Muninn** (scouts - thought & memory) and
**Ratatoskr** (messenger); planning **Norns** (Urd/Verdandi/Skuld) + **Forseti**
(arbiter). Each persona bundles a prompt + tool allowlist + default model.

---

## 7. Plugin SDK Contract (Go)

```go
// MimirPluginApi is the only surface plugins use to extend Mimir.
type MimirPluginApi interface {
    RegisterProvider(p ProviderDef) error
    RegisterTool(t ToolDef) error
    RegisterHook(h HookDef) error
    RegisterChannel(c ChannelDef) error          // chat channels
    RegisterHarness(h HarnessDef) error          // pluggable agent runtimes
    RegisterCapability(c CapabilityDef) error    // embedding/speech/image/etc.
    RegisterCommand(cmd CommandDef) error
    Runtime() RuntimeHelpers                     // config, logger, cortex access
}

// A plugin exports a single registration entrypoint:
type Plugin interface {
    Manifest() Manifest                          // id, version, contracts
    Register(api MimirPluginApi) error
}
```
- Plugins import only `@mimirmind/plugin-sdk`; never `internal/**`.
- The `PluginRegistry` collects registrations; core reads the registry (one-way).
- **Contract tests** assert each plugin registers exactly what its manifest declares.
- Plugin runtimes (v1): in-process Go plugins; later: wasm / subprocess / MCP.

---

## 8. Provider Abstraction

```go
type Provider interface {
    ID() string
    Dialect() Dialect                            // openai_compat | anthropic | ...
    Generate(ctx, req GenerateRequest) (GenerateResponse, error)
    Stream(ctx, req GenerateRequest) (<-chan StreamEvent, error)  // deltas + usage
}

// Dialect encodes/decodes one API wire format.
type Dialect interface {
    EncodeRequest(req GenerateRequest) (httpRequest, error)
    DecodeStream(chunk []byte) (StreamEvent, error)
}
```
- Built-in dialects: `openaiCompatDialect` (`/v1/chat/completions`) and
  `anthropicDialect` (`/v1/messages`). More via plugins (e.g. Gemini).
- Provider registry routes by model string (`anthropic/claude-...`, `openai/...`,
  `ollama/...`) and selects the matching dialect.
- Base URL + API key from `mimir.json` / env / `auth.json` (encrypted).
- Default local: Ollama at `http://localhost:11434` (ADR-010).

---

## 9. GUI <-> Daemon Protocol

- **REST** (`/api/...`): CRUD for projects, sessions, cortex (neurons/search), config,
  auth, tasks, sandboxes. The GUI uses an **SWR-style** cache (keyed dedup +
  stale-while-revalidate + optimistic updates).
- **WebSocket** (`/ws`): push stream of typed events - `token` (model deltas),
  `tool` (start/update/end), `lifecycle` (start/end/error/awaiting_approval),
  `status` (sandbox/agent state). The GUI renders these live.
- **GUI serving:** the daemon serves the built Solid app at `http://localhost:<port>`;
  Wails wraps the same app for desktop.

---

## 10. Sandbox Architecture

- **Sandbox Manager** maintains a warm pool; `sandbox_create` boots a container (fast)
  or microVM (strong) in ~ms-s; `sandbox_exec` runs commands via the in-guest agent;
  `sandbox_destroy` reaps. Snapshots (container commit / Firecracker snapshot) stored
  with metadata in SurrealDB; `fork` clones from a snapshot.
- **In-guest agent:** a tiny daemon inside each sandbox exposing exec / file read-write
  / PTY over a socket - one protocol regardless of backend.
- **Port routing:** local reverse proxy maps `localhost:N` -> guest port; the GUI
  previews apps at `http://localhost:N`.
- **Per-user isolation:** one Linux user per agent; setgid shared group dirs.
- **Egress policy:** per-sandbox allow/deny via nftables or a userspace proxy.

---

## 11. Security Architecture

- **Policy gate (fail-closed):** every tool/plugin call -> evaluate rules (default-deny)
  -> allow / deny / require_approval. Unbypassable, even in bypass mode.
- **Privilege rings:** tools/plugins assigned to 4 tiers; higher tiers need more trust.
- **Audit:** hash-chained (Merkle) records of policy + request + decision (Decision BOM).
- **Secrets:** API keys encrypted at rest (MIMIR_ENCRYPTION_KEY); `.env` gitignored.
- **Sandboxing:** untrusted code runs in containers/microVMs (ADR-007).
- **MCP security gateway** (Tier 2): tool-poisoning/drift/hidden-instruction scanning.
- **Telemetry (on by default, opt-out):** anonymized usage metrics (counts, model/tool,
  success/error rates, latency) to improve the system. No code/content/prompts by
  default (separate explicit opt-in). Disabled in privacy settings; the only outbound
  call besides the chosen LLM provider; fully disable-able for air-gapped use.

---

## 12. Request Lifecycle (end to end)

1. User types in GUI -> POST `/api/sessions/:id/messages` + WS subscribe.
2. Daemon `run()`: intake -> assemble (AGENTS.md + skills + recalled engrams).
3. Provider.Stream() -> tokens pushed over WS -> GUI renders.
4. Tool call -> policy gate -> (approval?) -> execute (native or sandbox) -> result.
5. Outcome capture: correction/preference/failure -> engram in Cortex.
6. Loop until done -> persist -> lifecycle `end` over WS.

---

## 13. Deployment Architecture

- **Default (local-first):** one `mimir` binary + a managed SurrealDB sidecar (Docker or
  bundled). GUI at `localhost:<port>`. No cloud required.
- **Optional hosted layer (business):** gateway.mimirmind.com (model gateway),
  console.mimirmind.com (billing/keys), relay.mimirmind.com (mobile tunnel), hosted
  Cortex sync. All optional; the local install is fully functional without them.

---

## 14. Implementation Readiness Notes

- **Ready to build:** Go module skeleton (E1), provider abstraction + agent loop (E2),
  native tools (E3), policy gate (E4), plugin SDK + registry (E11), GUI shell (E12).
- **Spike first:** SurrealDB sidecar management (auto-start/health/restart) and the
  in-guest sandbox agent protocol - these are the two least-proven mechanisms.
- **De-risk:** the plugin SDK contract must freeze early (everything depends on it);
  write contract tests alongside E11.
- **Sequencing:** E1 -> E2 -> E3 -> E4 -> E11 -> E12 -> E5/E6/E7/E8/E9 -> E10/E14.

Next: `bmad-check-implementation-readiness` to gate the build, then John breaks the
Core epics into stories.
