package agent

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"sync"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/cortex"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/decision"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/llm"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/policy"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/sdlc"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/tools"
)

// maxToolSteps caps the infer->act loop so a misbehaving model can't spin forever
// (doom-loop protection, F4.3).
const maxToolSteps = 20

// maxStopGateContinuations caps how many times a failing OnStop gate can force
// the loop to continue for a verification pass in a single run (F25).
const maxStopGateContinuations = 2

// Permission modes (inspired by smolcoder ro / edit / bypass).
const (
	ModeReadOnly = "ro"
	ModeEdit     = "edit"
	ModeBypass   = "bypass"
)

// Config wires an agent's dependencies.
type Config struct {
	Provider      llm.Provider
	Tools         *tools.Registry
	Cortex        cortex.Store
	Model         string
	Usage         *llm.Tracker      // optional: records token usage for the dashboard (E69)
	Decider       *decision.Decider // System-One Decision Engine (defaults to Liquid AI d1-omni-600M)
	SDLC          *sdlc.Manager     // 7-Phase SDLC State Machine & Phase-Scoped Prompt Loader
	Local         bool              // whether the provider is local (local tokens cost $0)
	Mode          string            // "ro" | "edit" | "bypass" (default "edit")
	Effort        string            // "" | "off" | "low" | "medium" | "high"
	SmolPolicy    string            // "auto" (default) | "on" | "off"
	ApprovalFunc  func(toolName, rawArgs string) bool
	Gate          *policy.Gate // Fail-closed execution policy gate (F2/ADR-009)
	Hooks         *HookRunner  // Level 1 Lifecycle Hooks
	AutoVerify    bool         // When true, a failing OnStop gate forces a verification pass instead of only annotating the reply (F25)
	ContextBudget int          // Max context token budget (defaults to 8192 in SmolMode, 32768 standard)
}

// Step records one tool execution in a turn (used by RunTrace / the trace CLI).
type Step struct {
	Name   string `json:"name"`
	Args   string `json:"args"`
	Result string `json:"result"`
	Err    string `json:"err,omitempty"`
}

// Result is the full outcome of a turn: the final reply, the tool trace, and the
// memories that were recalled into the prompt (so memory is observable/testable).
type Result struct {
	Reply    string
	Trace    []Step
	Recalled []string
}

// Event kinds emitted by RunStream (F2.1 streaming).
const (
	EventMemory = "memory" // recalled memory (Text = content)
	EventToken  = "token"  // a delta of the model's reply (Text = delta)
	EventTool   = "tool"   // a tool execution (Step)
	EventSteer  = "steer"  // mid-turn user steering injected
	EventDone   = "done"   // turn complete (Reply = final answer)
	EventError  = "error"  // turn failed (Err)
)

// Event is one streaming update from a turn, surfaced to live UIs by RunStream.
type Event struct {
	Type  string `json:"type"`
	Text  string `json:"text,omitempty"`
	Step  *Step  `json:"step,omitempty"`
	Reply string `json:"reply,omitempty"`
	Err   string `json:"err,omitempty"`
}

// maxSteersPerSession caps how many steering instructions may wait in one
// session's queue. It matches the capacity of the single global channel this
// design replaced, now applied per session instead of process-wide.
const maxSteersPerSession = 16

// Agent runs the gather -> infer -> act -> verify loop.
type Agent struct {
	mu  sync.RWMutex
	cfg Config
	// steerMu guards steers, the per-session steering queues. Queues are
	// keyed by chat session ID so an instruction can only ever be delivered
	// into a run of the session it was queued for.
	steerMu sync.Mutex
	steers  map[string][]string
}

// New returns an Agent wired to the given dependencies.
func New(cfg Config) *Agent {
	if cfg.Mode == "" {
		cfg.Mode = ModeEdit
	}
	if cfg.SmolPolicy == "" {
		cfg.SmolPolicy = SmolAuto
	}
	if cfg.Decider == nil {
		cfg.Decider = defaultDecider(cfg.Provider)
	}
	if cfg.SDLC == nil {
		if cfg.Tools != nil {
			if st, ok := cfg.Tools.Get("sdlc"); ok {
				if sdlcTool, ok := st.(*tools.SDLCTool); ok && sdlcTool.Manager != nil {
					cfg.SDLC = sdlcTool.Manager
				}
			}
		}
		if cfg.SDLC == nil {
			cfg.SDLC = sdlc.NewManager(".")
		}
	}
	if cfg.Hooks == nil {
		cfg.Hooks = NewHookRunner(".")
	}
	return &Agent{
		cfg:    cfg,
		steers: make(map[string][]string),
	}
}

// defaultDecider builds the System-One decider with a real endpoint when one
// is configured (F26b): MIMIR_DECISION_BASE_URL wins, then the main provider's
// base URL. With neither, the base URL stays empty and the decider falls back
// to its deterministic heuristics, as before. The model name comes from
// MIMIR_DECISION_MODEL, else the primary decision model.
func defaultDecider(provider llm.Provider) *decision.Decider {
	baseURL := os.Getenv("MIMIR_DECISION_BASE_URL")
	if baseURL == "" {
		if p, ok := provider.(*llm.OpenAIProvider); ok {
			baseURL = p.BaseURL
		}
	}
	model := os.Getenv("MIMIR_DECISION_MODEL")
	if model == "" {
		model = decision.PrimaryDecisionModel
	}
	return decision.New(baseURL, "", model)
}

// Hooks returns Mímir's Level 1 lifecycle hook runner.
func (a *Agent) Hooks() *HookRunner {
	a.mu.RLock()
	defer a.mu.RUnlock()
	return a.cfg.Hooks
}

// Decider returns Mímir's built-in System-One Decision Engine (Liquid AI d1-omni-600M).
func (a *Agent) Decider() *decision.Decider {
	a.mu.RLock()
	defer a.mu.RUnlock()
	return a.cfg.Decider
}

// SDLC returns Mímir's 7-Phase SDLC State Machine & Phase-Scoped Prompt Loader.
func (a *Agent) SDLC() *sdlc.Manager {
	a.mu.RLock()
	defer a.mu.RUnlock()
	return a.cfg.SDLC
}

// SmolMode reports whether smolcoder tiny-model optimizations are currently active
// (either forced on or auto-activated by DetectSmolModel).
func (a *Agent) SmolMode() bool {
	a.mu.RLock()
	defer a.mu.RUnlock()
	switch a.cfg.SmolPolicy {
	case SmolOn:
		return true
	case SmolOff:
		return false
	default:
		pid := ""
		if a.cfg.Provider != nil {
			pid = a.cfg.Provider.ID()
		}
		return DetectSmolModel(pid, a.cfg.Model, a.cfg.Local)
	}
}

// SmolPolicy returns the current SmolMode policy ("auto", "on", "off").
func (a *Agent) SmolPolicy() string {
	a.mu.RLock()
	defer a.mu.RUnlock()
	if a.cfg.SmolPolicy == "" {
		return SmolAuto
	}
	return a.cfg.SmolPolicy
}

// SetSmolPolicy sets the SmolMode policy ("auto", "on", "off").
func (a *Agent) SetSmolPolicy(policy string) {
	a.mu.Lock()
	defer a.mu.Unlock()
	switch strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(policy)) {
	case SmolOn:
		a.cfg.SmolPolicy = SmolOn
	case SmolOff:
		a.cfg.SmolPolicy = SmolOff
	default:
		a.cfg.SmolPolicy = SmolAuto
	}
}

// Mode returns the current permission mode ("ro", "edit", "bypass").
func (a *Agent) Mode() string {
	a.mu.RLock()
	defer a.mu.RUnlock()
	if a.cfg.Mode == "" {
		return ModeEdit
	}
	return a.cfg.Mode
}

// SetMode sets the active permission mode ("ro", "edit", "bypass").
func (a *Agent) SetMode(mode string) {
	a.mu.Lock()
	defer a.mu.Unlock()
	switch mode {
	case ModeReadOnly, ModeEdit, ModeBypass:
		a.cfg.Mode = mode
	}
}

// CycleMode cycles permission modes: edit -> bypass -> ro -> edit (Shift+Tab in TUI).
func (a *Agent) CycleMode() string {
	a.mu.Lock()
	defer a.mu.Unlock()
	switch a.cfg.Mode {
	case ModeReadOnly:
		a.cfg.Mode = ModeEdit
	case ModeEdit:
		a.cfg.Mode = ModeBypass
	default:
		a.cfg.Mode = ModeReadOnly
	}
	return a.cfg.Mode
}

// Effort returns the current reasoning effort ("", "off", "low", "medium", "high").
func (a *Agent) Effort() string {
	a.mu.RLock()
	defer a.mu.RUnlock()
	return a.cfg.Effort
}

// SetEffort updates the reasoning effort level.
func (a *Agent) SetEffort(effort string) {
	a.mu.Lock()
	defer a.mu.Unlock()
	a.cfg.Effort = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(effort))
}

// SetProvider hot-swaps the active LLM provider and model at runtime.
func (a *Agent) SetProvider(p llm.Provider, model string, local bool) {
	a.mu.Lock()
	defer a.mu.Unlock()
	a.cfg.Provider = p
	a.cfg.Model = model
	a.cfg.Local = local
}

// ModelInfo returns the current provider ID, model name, and local flag.
func (a *Agent) ModelInfo() (string, string, bool) {
	a.mu.RLock()
	defer a.mu.RUnlock()
	pid := "none"
	if a.cfg.Provider != nil {
		pid = a.cfg.Provider.ID()
	}
	return pid, a.cfg.Model, a.cfg.Local
}

// sessionContextKey is the context key carrying the chat session a run
// belongs to. It exists solely so steering instructions queued for a session
// are delivered only into runs of that same session.
type sessionContextKey struct{}

// WithSessionID returns a context that binds agent runs started with it to
// the given chat session for steering delivery. Runs started from a context
// carrying no session ID (one-shot CLI runs, swarm worker runs, tests)
// receive no session steering at all: the binding fails closed.
func WithSessionID(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) context.Context {
	if ctx == nil || sessionID == "" {
		return ctx
	}
	return context.WithValue(ctx, sessionContextKey{}, sessionID)
}

// sessionIDFromContext returns the chat session bound to ctx, or "" when the
// run is sessionless.
func sessionIDFromContext(ctx context.Context) string {
	if ctx == nil {
		return ""
	}
	id, _ := ctx.Value(sessionContextKey{}).(string)
	return id
}

// Steer queues a mid-turn user steering instruction for one chat session, to
// be injected cleanly at the next joined tool boundary of a run OF THAT
// SESSION without aborting the turn (sausheong/harness pattern). Delivery is
// bound to the session: drainSteer only ever returns a session's queue to a
// run carrying that session's ID, so a steer can never leak into another
// user's run or into a sessionless run.
//
// Steer reports whether the instruction was actually queued. It returns
// false when the session ID or the message is empty, or when the session's
// queue already holds maxSteersPerSession instructions; callers must surface
// that failure instead of reporting success for a dropped instruction.
//
// Queue memory stays bounded: each session holds at most
// maxSteersPerSession short strings, a queue is deleted when drained, and
// the only production enqueue path is the server's mobile steer handler,
// which first proves the named session exists and belongs to the caller, so
// queues cannot be minted by spamming invented session IDs.
func (a *Agent) Steer(sessionID, msg string) bool {
	msg = strings.TrimSpace(msg)
	if sessionID == "" || msg == "" {
		return false
	}
	a.steerMu.Lock()
	defer a.steerMu.Unlock()
	q := a.steers[sessionID]
	if len(q) >= maxSteersPerSession {
		return false
	}
	a.steers[sessionID] = append(q, msg)
	return true
}

// drainSteer returns and clears the steering instructions queued for
// sessionID. An empty sessionID drains nothing (fail closed): session
// steers are never delivered into sessionless runs.
func (a *Agent) drainSteer(sessionID string) []string {
	if sessionID == "" {
		return nil
	}
	a.steerMu.Lock()
	defer a.steerMu.Unlock()
	q := a.steers[sessionID]
	if len(q) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	delete(a.steers, sessionID)
	return q
}

// phaseToolFilter returns the active SDLC phase's allowed tool set when a
// methodology with phase-scoped tools is active (waterfall), or nil when no
// phase restriction applies. It is the single source of the computation used
// both to filter advertised schemas and to enforce the set at execution time.
func (a *Agent) phaseToolFilter() map[string]bool {
	a.mu.RLock()
	sdlcMgr := a.cfg.SDLC
	a.mu.RUnlock()
	if sdlcMgr != nil && sdlcMgr.Methodology() == sdlc.MethodWaterfall {
		return sdlcMgr.AllowedToolSet()
	}
	return nil
}

// schemasForMode converts the registered tools visible in the given mode
// ("" = the agent's configured mode) into model-facing tool schemas. The
// mode decides which tools ForMode exposes. When SDLC Waterfall
// methodology is active, it also enforces the active phase's AllowedToolSet.
func (a *Agent) schemasForMode(modeOverride string) []llm.ToolSchema {
	a.mu.RLock()
	reg := a.cfg.Tools
	mode := a.cfg.Mode
	a.mu.RUnlock()
	if m, ok := validMode(modeOverride); ok {
		mode = m
	}
	if reg == nil {
		return nil
	}
	phaseFilter := a.phaseToolFilter()
	var out []llm.ToolSchema
	for _, t := range reg.ForMode(mode) {
		if phaseFilter != nil && !phaseFilter[t.Name()] {
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, llm.ToolSchema{
			Name: t.Name(), Description: t.Description(), Parameters: t.Parameters(),
		})
	}
	return out
}

// runStopGate executes the OnStop lifecycle hooks for a finished turn and
// returns the evaluated stop gate status plus any advisory the hooks injected.
func (a *Agent) runStopGate(ctx context.Context, trace []Step) (StopGateStatus, string) {
	a.mu.RLock()
	hooks := a.cfg.Hooks
	a.mu.RUnlock()
	if hooks == nil {
		return StopGateStatus{}, ""
	}
	hCtx := &HookContext{
		Type:      HookOnStop,
		Trace:     trace,
		TodoLines: a.todoLines(),
	}
	_ = hooks.Execute(ctx, hCtx)
	return hCtx.StopStatus, hCtx.InjectedMsg
}

// stopGateReminder builds the system feedback injected into the conversation
// when AutoVerify forces another pass after a failing stop gate (F25).
func stopGateReminder(advisory string) string {
	return "[Harness OnStop Gate]: " + advisory + ". Before finishing, run the appropriate verification (build, tests, lint, or an audit tool) and complete or update the pending todos, then give your final summary."
}

func (a *Agent) todoLines() []string {
	a.mu.RLock()
	reg := a.cfg.Tools
	a.mu.RUnlock()
	if reg == nil {
		return nil
	}
	t, ok := reg.Get("todo")
	if !ok {
		return nil
	}
	tt, ok := t.(*tools.TodoTool)
	if !ok || tt.Store == nil {
		return nil
	}
	var lines []string
	for _, item := range tt.Store.List() {
		lines = append(lines, fmt.Sprintf("- #%d [%s] %s", item.ID, item.Status, item.Content))
	}
	return lines
}

// validMode reports whether mode is a canonical permission mode and returns
// it. Used to validate per-request mode overrides (N2).
func validMode(mode string) (string, bool) {
	switch mode {
	case ModeReadOnly, ModeEdit, ModeBypass:
		return mode, true
	}
	return "", false
}

func (a *Agent) executeToolCall(ctx context.Context, tc llm.ToolCall) Step {
	return a.executeToolCallMode(ctx, tc, "")
}

// executeToolCallMode runs one tool call under the given per-request mode
// override ("" means the agent's configured mode). The override is local to
// this invocation and never mutates the agent's stored mode (N2).
func (a *Agent) executeToolCallMode(ctx context.Context, tc llm.ToolCall, modeOverride string) Step {
	repairedArgs := llm.RepairJSON(tc.Arguments)
	st := Step{Name: tc.Name, Args: repairedArgs}

	a.mu.RLock()
	reg := a.cfg.Tools
	mode := a.cfg.Mode
	approve := a.cfg.ApprovalFunc
	gate := a.cfg.Gate
	a.mu.RUnlock()
	if m, ok := validMode(modeOverride); ok {
		mode = m
	}

	var args map[string]any
	if repairedArgs != "" {
		_ = json.Unmarshal([]byte(repairedArgs), &args)
	}

	// 0. SDLC phase enforcement at execution time (F5): schemasForMode only filters
	// which tools are advertised, so a model that emits a call anyway (or a
	// direct caller) must still be rejected when the active phase's allowed
	// tool set does not include the tool.
	if phaseFilter := a.phaseToolFilter(); phaseFilter != nil && !phaseFilter[tc.Name] {
		st.Err = fmt.Sprintf("blocked by SDLC phase policy: tool %q is not in the active phase's allowed tool set", tc.Name)
		st.Result = st.Err
		return st
	}

	// 1. Fail-closed policy gate check (F2/F3/ADR-009)
	approved := false
	if gate != nil {
		dec := gate.Evaluate(policy.Request{Tool: tc.Name, Args: args})
		switch dec {
		case policy.Deny:
			st.Err = fmt.Sprintf("execution of tool %q blocked by policy gate (deny)", tc.Name)
			st.Result = st.Err
			return st
		case policy.RequireApproval:
			// Bypass mode is the user's explicit opt-out of approval prompts:
			// RequireApproval verdicts are waived in bypass mode. Deny verdicts
			// are NOT waived (handled above) and still block execution.
			if mode == ModeBypass {
				// Waived by explicit user opt-out; proceed without approval.
			} else if approve == nil || !approve(tc.Name, repairedArgs) {
				// Fail closed (N1): a RequireApproval verdict with no approver
				// configured denies the call instead of silently passing.
				st.Err = fmt.Sprintf("execution of tool %q denied: policy gate requires approval but no approver approved it", tc.Name)
				st.Result = st.Err
				return st
			} else {
				approved = true
			}
		case policy.Allow:
			// Allowed to proceed
		}
	}

	if mode == ModeReadOnly && tools.IsWriteTool(tc.Name) {
		st.Err = "blocked in read-only (ro) mode: switch to edit or bypass mode (Shift+Tab) to allow mutations"
		st.Result = st.Err
		return st
	}
	if mode == ModeEdit && !approved && tools.IsWriteTool(tc.Name) {
		// Fail closed (N1): edit mode requires approval for write tools; with
		// no approver configured the call is denied, not silently passed.
		if approve == nil || !approve(tc.Name, repairedArgs) {
			st.Err = "tool execution rejected: edit mode requires user approval for write tools and no approver approved it"
			st.Result = st.Err
			return st
		}
	}

	a.mu.RLock()
	hooks := a.cfg.Hooks
	a.mu.RUnlock()

	if hooks != nil {
		hCtx := &HookContext{
			Type:     HookPreTool,
			ToolName: tc.Name,
			ToolArgs: repairedArgs,
		}
		_ = hooks.Execute(ctx, hCtx)
	}

	tool, ok := reg.Get(tc.Name)
	if !ok {
		st.Err = "unknown tool: " + tc.Name
		st.Result = st.Err
		return st
	}
	r, err := tool.Run(ctx, args)
	st.Result = r
	if err != nil {
		st.Err = err.Error()
		if st.Result == "" {
			st.Result = st.Err
		}
	}

	if hooks != nil {
		hCtx := &HookContext{
			Type:       HookPostTool,
			ToolName:   tc.Name,
			ToolArgs:   repairedArgs,
			ToolResult: st.Result,
			ToolErr:    st.Err,
		}
		_ = hooks.Execute(ctx, hCtx)
		st.Result = hCtx.ToolResult
		if hCtx.ToolErr != "" {
			st.Err = hCtx.ToolErr
		}
	}
	return st
}

// buildPromptForInput selects smolSystemPrompt when SmolMode is active, or
// the standard systemPrompt otherwise, and appends the persistent
// harness-owned Todo checklist.
func (a *Agent) buildPromptForInput(input string, memories []cortex.Neuron, schemas []llm.ToolSchema) string {
	smol := a.SmolMode()
	base := systemPrompt(memories, schemas)
	if smol {
		base = smolSystemPrompt(memories, schemas)
	}
	return base + BuildPhaseScopedRulesBlock(a.SDLC(), input) + FormatTodoChecklist(a.todoLines())
}

// runLoop drives the infer -> act cycle until the model returns text or the step
// cap is hit. It returns the final text reply and a trace of tool executions.
// modeOverride is the per-request permission mode ("" = agent default); it is
// local to this run and never written back to the agent (N2).
func (a *Agent) runLoop(ctx context.Context, msgs []llm.Message, modeOverride string) (string, []Step, error) {
	schemas := a.schemasForMode(modeOverride)
	var trace []Step
	var last string
	smol := a.SmolMode()
	a.mu.RLock()
	autoVerify := a.cfg.AutoVerify
	a.mu.RUnlock()
	stopContinuations := 0
	keepRecent := 4
	if smol {
		keepRecent = 2
	}
	for step := 0; step < maxToolSteps; step++ {
		msgs = a.maybeCompactContext(msgs, smol)
		pruned := PruneHistoryPlaceholders(msgs, keepRecent)
		a.mu.RLock()
		prov := a.cfg.Provider
		model := a.cfg.Model
		local := a.cfg.Local
		effort := a.cfg.Effort
		usageTracker := a.cfg.Usage
		a.mu.RUnlock()

		// In SmolMode, automatically disable chain-of-thought on mechanical follow-up
		// tool steps (step > 0) when effort is auto ("") for 3-5x faster tool loops.
		if smol && step > 0 && effort == "" {
			effort = "off"
		}

		resp, err := prov.Generate(ctx, llm.GenerateRequest{
			Model: model, Messages: pruned, Tools: schemas, Effort: effort,
		})
		if err != nil {
			return "", trace, err
		}
		if usageTracker != nil {
			usageTracker.Record(model, local, resp.Usage)
		}
		last = StripEmDashes(resp.Content)
		msgs = append(msgs, llm.Message{Role: "assistant", Content: last, ToolCalls: resp.ToolCalls})
		if len(resp.ToolCalls) == 0 {
			_, advisory := a.runStopGate(ctx, trace)
			// F25: with AutoVerify on, a failing stop gate enforces instead of
			// only annotating: feed the gate's reminder back and continue the
			// loop for a verification pass, capped per run.
			if autoVerify && advisory != "" && stopContinuations < maxStopGateContinuations {
				stopContinuations++
				msgs = append(msgs, llm.Message{Role: "user", Content: stopGateReminder(advisory)})
				continue
			}
			if advisory != "" {
				last += "\n\n[" + advisory + "]"
			}
			return last, trace, nil
		}
		for _, tc := range resp.ToolCalls {
			st := a.executeToolCallMode(ctx, tc, modeOverride)
			trace = append(trace, st)
			msgs = append(msgs, llm.Message{Role: "tool", ToolCallID: tc.ID, Content: st.Result})
		}
		// Inject any mid-turn user steering messages queued for THIS run's
		// session during tool execution (empty session drains nothing).
		for _, sm := range a.drainSteer(sessionIDFromContext(ctx)) {
			msgs = append(msgs, llm.Message{Role: "user", Content: "[User steering instruction]: " + sm})
		}
	}
	if _, advisory := a.runStopGate(ctx, trace); advisory != "" {
		last += "\n\n[" + advisory + "]"
	}
	return last, trace, nil
}

// Run executes one conversational turn and returns the final text reply.
func (a *Agent) Run(ctx context.Context, input string, history []llm.Message) (string, error) {
	r, err := a.runTurn(ctx, input, history)
	return r.Reply, err
}

// RunTrace is like Run but also returns the trace of tool executions.
func (a *Agent) RunTrace(ctx context.Context, input string, history []llm.Message) (string, []Step, error) {
	r, err := a.runTurn(ctx, input, history)
	return r.Reply, r.Trace, err
}

// RunFull returns the complete Result, including the memories recalled into the
// prompt - used by the trace CLI and the cross-run memory tests.
func (a *Agent) RunFull(ctx context.Context, input string, history []llm.Message) (Result, error) {
	return a.runTurn(ctx, input, history)
}

// RunWithMode is Run under a per-request permission mode override (N2): the
// mode applies to this invocation only and never changes the agent's stored
// mode, so concurrent or sequential requests cannot leak modes into each other.
func (a *Agent) RunWithMode(ctx context.Context, mode, input string, history []llm.Message) (string, error) {
	r, err := a.runTurnMode(ctx, mode, input, history)
	return r.Reply, err
}

// RunFullWithMode is RunFull under a per-request permission mode override (N2).
func (a *Agent) RunFullWithMode(ctx context.Context, mode, input string, history []llm.Message) (Result, error) {
	return a.runTurnMode(ctx, mode, input, history)
}

// RunStream runs one conversational turn while streaming updates to emit as they
// happen: recalled memories, token deltas of the model's reply, tool executions, and
// a final done event carrying the full reply (F2.1 streaming + tool calling).
func (a *Agent) RunStream(ctx context.Context, input string, history []llm.Message, emit func(Event)) error {
	return a.runStreamMode(ctx, "", input, history, emit)
}

// RunStreamWithMode is RunStream under a per-request permission mode override
// (N2): the mode applies to this invocation only and never changes the agent's
// stored mode.
func (a *Agent) RunStreamWithMode(ctx context.Context, mode, input string, history []llm.Message, emit func(Event)) error {
	return a.runStreamMode(ctx, mode, input, history, emit)
}

func (a *Agent) runStreamMode(ctx context.Context, modeOverride, input string, history []llm.Message, emit func(Event)) error {
	memories, err := a.cfg.Cortex.Search(ctx, input, 5)
	if err != nil {
		emit(Event{Type: EventError, Err: err.Error()})
		return err
	}
	for _, m := range memories {
		emit(Event{Type: EventMemory, Text: m.Content})
	}
	schemas := a.schemasForMode(modeOverride)
	msgs := []llm.Message{
		{Role: "system", Content: a.buildPromptForInput(input, memories, schemas)},
	}
	msgs = append(msgs, history...)
	msgs = append(msgs, llm.Message{Role: "user", Content: input})
	var finalReply string
	var trace []Step
	a.mu.RLock()
	autoVerify := a.cfg.AutoVerify
	a.mu.RUnlock()
	stopContinuations := 0
	smol := a.SmolMode()
	keepRecent := 4
	if smol {
		keepRecent = 2
	}
	for step := 0; step < maxToolSteps; step++ {
		msgs = a.maybeCompactContext(msgs, smol)
		pruned := PruneHistoryPlaceholders(msgs, keepRecent)
		a.mu.RLock()
		prov := a.cfg.Provider
		model := a.cfg.Model
		local := a.cfg.Local
		effort := a.cfg.Effort
		usageTracker := a.cfg.Usage
		a.mu.RUnlock()

		if smol && step > 0 && effort == "" {
			effort = "off"
		}

		ch, err := prov.Stream(ctx, llm.GenerateRequest{
			Model: model, Messages: pruned, Tools: schemas, Effort: effort,
		})
		if err != nil {
			emit(Event{Type: EventError, Err: err.Error()})
			return err
		}
		var content strings.Builder
		var toolCalls []llm.ToolCall
		var usage llm.Usage
		for ev := range ch {
			if ev.Err != nil {
				emit(Event{Type: EventError, Err: ev.Err.Error()})
				return ev.Err
			}
			if ev.Delta != "" {
				cleanDelta := StripEmDashes(ev.Delta)
				content.WriteString(cleanDelta)
				emit(Event{Type: EventToken, Text: cleanDelta})
			}
			if ev.Done {
				toolCalls = ev.ToolCalls
				usage = ev.Usage
			}
		}
		if usageTracker != nil {
			usageTracker.Record(model, local, usage)
		}
		text := StripEmDashes(content.String())
		finalReply = text
		msgs = append(msgs, llm.Message{Role: "assistant", Content: text, ToolCalls: toolCalls})
		if len(toolCalls) == 0 {
			_, advisory := a.runStopGate(ctx, trace)
			// F25: same enforcement as runLoop; a failing gate under AutoVerify
			// continues the stream for a verification pass, capped per run.
			if autoVerify && advisory != "" && stopContinuations < maxStopGateContinuations {
				stopContinuations++
				msgs = append(msgs, llm.Message{Role: "user", Content: stopGateReminder(advisory)})
				continue
			}
			if advisory != "" {
				finalReply += "\n\n[" + advisory + "]"
			}
			emit(Event{Type: EventDone, Reply: finalReply})
			return nil
		}
		for _, tc := range toolCalls {
			st := a.executeToolCallMode(ctx, tc, modeOverride)
			trace = append(trace, st)
			emit(Event{Type: EventTool, Step: &st})
			msgs = append(msgs, llm.Message{Role: "tool", ToolCallID: tc.ID, Content: st.Result})
		}
		for _, sm := range a.drainSteer(sessionIDFromContext(ctx)) {
			emit(Event{Type: EventSteer, Text: sm})
			msgs = append(msgs, llm.Message{Role: "user", Content: "[User steering instruction]: " + sm})
		}
	}
	if _, advisory := a.runStopGate(ctx, trace); advisory != "" {
		finalReply += "\n\n[" + advisory + "]"
	}
	emit(Event{Type: EventDone, Reply: finalReply})
	return nil
}

func (a *Agent) runTurn(ctx context.Context, input string, history []llm.Message) (Result, error) {
	return a.runTurnMode(ctx, "", input, history)
}

// runTurnMode is runTurn under a per-request mode override ("" = agent default).
func (a *Agent) runTurnMode(ctx context.Context, modeOverride, input string, history []llm.Message) (Result, error) {
	memories, err := a.cfg.Cortex.Search(ctx, input, 5)
	if err != nil {
		return Result{}, err
	}
	recalled := make([]string, len(memories))
	for i, m := range memories {
		recalled[i] = m.Content
	}
	schemas := a.schemasForMode(modeOverride)
	msgs := []llm.Message{
		{Role: "system", Content: a.buildPromptForInput(input, memories, schemas)},
	}
	msgs = append(msgs, history...)
	msgs = append(msgs, llm.Message{Role: "user", Content: input})
	reply, trace, err := a.runLoop(ctx, msgs, modeOverride)
	if err != nil {
		return Result{Trace: trace, Recalled: recalled}, err
	}
	return Result{Reply: reply, Trace: trace, Recalled: recalled}, nil
}

// systemPrompt assembles the system prompt with recalled memory + a tool hint.
func systemPrompt(memories []cortex.Neuron, schemas []llm.ToolSchema) string {
	p := "You are Mímir, an agent that remembers. Use what you recall. You have access to the full conversation history - reference earlier messages when relevant."
	if len(memories) > 0 {
		p += "\n\nRelevant memory:"
		for _, m := range memories {
			p += "\n- " + m.Content
		}
	}
	if len(schemas) > 0 {
		names := make([]string, len(schemas))
		for i, s := range schemas {
			names[i] = s.Name
		}
		p += "\n\nYou have these tools - call them when useful: " + strings.Join(names, ", ") + "."
	}
	p += "\n\nWhen presenting multiple-choice questions or options, use this exact format so the UI renders clickable buttons:\n[choice]\nA) option text\nB) option text\nC) option text\n[/choice]\nAlways use this format for multiple-choice answers - never just list them as plain text."
	return p
}

// maybeCompactContext checks if estimated conversation token count exceeds 80%
// of the context budget. When exceeded, it generates `.mimir/HANDOFF.md` to persist
// continuity state before aggressively compacting history to prevent context overflow.
func (a *Agent) maybeCompactContext(msgs []llm.Message, smol bool) []llm.Message {
	budget := a.cfg.ContextBudget
	if budget <= 0 {
		if smol {
			budget = 8192
		} else {
			budget = 32768
		}
	}
	threshold := int(float64(budget) * 0.8)
	current := EstimateTokens(msgs)
	if current < threshold {
		return msgs
	}

	// Generate continuity handoff document before aggressive trimming
	handoffMD := GenerateHandoffMarkdown("session-auto-compaction", msgs, a.todoLines(), "")
	_, _ = WriteHandoffFile(".", handoffMD)

	// Keep system prompt (index 0) and the most recent 2 turns, replace middle with summary notice
	if len(msgs) <= 3 {
		return msgs
	}
	sysMsg := msgs[0]
	recent := msgs[len(msgs)-2:]
	compactedNotice := llm.Message{
		Role:    "user",
		Content: fmt.Sprintf("[Context Compaction: Conversation exceeded 80%% context threshold (%d/%d tokens). Previous state persisted to .mimir/HANDOFF.md. Active todos and recent turns preserved.]", current, budget),
	}
	return append([]llm.Message{sysMsg, compactedNotice}, recent...)
}

package agent

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/cortex"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/llm"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/tools"
)

// TestAgentRunRecallAndRemember proves the full loop against a fake provider:
// a seeded memory is recalled into the system prompt and the model reply is returned.
// Exchanges are no longer auto-stored; they live in sessions (F2.2).
func TestAgentRunRecallAndRemember(t *testing.T) {
	var captured []struct {
		Role    string `json:"role"`
		Content string `json:"content"`
	}
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		var req struct {
			Messages []struct {
				Role    string `json:"role"`
				Content string `json:"content"`
			} `json:"messages"`
		}
		_ = json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req)
		captured = req.Messages
		_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(map[string]any{
			"choices": []map[string]any{
				{"message": map[string]string{"role": "assistant", "content": "the answer"}},
			},
		})
	}))
	defer srv.Close()

	store := cortex.NewMemoryStore()
	if _, err := store.PutNeuron(context.Background(), cortex.Neuron{
		Kind: cortex.KindMemory, Layer: "preference",
		Content: "note about format my code please: use tabs", Decay: 1,
	}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("seed: %v", err)
	}

	a := New(Config{
		Provider: &llm.OpenAIProvider{IDStr: "fake", BaseURL: srv.URL + "/v1", APIKey: "k", Model: "m"},
		Tools:    tools.NewRegistry(),
		Cortex:   store,
		Model:    "m",
	})

	reply, err := a.Run(context.Background(), "format my code please", nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Run: %v", err)
	}
	if reply != "the answer" {
		t.Errorf("reply = %q", reply)
	}
	if len(captured) == 0 || captured[0].Role != "system" || !strings.Contains(captured[0].Content, "use tabs") {
		t.Errorf("expected recalled memory in system prompt, got %+v", captured)
	}
}


==============================================================================
FILE: internal/agent/compaction.go
==============================================================================
package agent

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/llm"
)

const (
	// placeholderMinChars is the minimum size of a file write/edit payload before
	// we replace it with a compact placeholder in older turns (smolcoder pattern).
	placeholderMinChars = 300
	// maxOldToolOutputChars caps older tool outputs in conversation history
	// (sausheong/harness Stage 1 in-place tool output trimming).
	maxOldToolOutputChars = 2000
)

// PruneHistoryPlaceholders returns a copy of msgs where older bulky tool-call arguments
// (write_file, edit_block) and oversized tool outputs are replaced with compact
// placeholders (inspired by smolcoder's isHistoryPlaceholder and sausheong/harness Stage 1).
// The most recent keepRecent messages are left untouched so active context stays intact.
func PruneHistoryPlaceholders(msgs []llm.Message, keepRecent int) []llm.Message {
	if keepRecent <= 0 {
		keepRecent = 4
	}
	if len(msgs) <= keepRecent {
		return msgs
	}
	cutoff := len(msgs) - keepRecent
	out := make([]llm.Message, len(msgs))
	copy(out, msgs)

	for i := 0; i < cutoff; i++ {
		m := out[i]
		if m.Role == "assistant" && len(m.ToolCalls) > 0 {
			tcs := make([]llm.ToolCall, len(m.ToolCalls))
			copy(tcs, m.ToolCalls)
			for j, tc := range tcs {
				if tc.Name == "write_file" || tc.Name == "edit_block" {
					tcs[j].Arguments = compactFileToolArgs(tc.Name, tc.Arguments)
				}
			}
			m.ToolCalls = tcs
			out[i] = m
		} else if m.Role == "tool" && len(m.Content) > maxOldToolOutputChars {
			head := m.Content[:1000]
			tail := m.Content[len(m.Content)-600:]
			omitted := len(m.Content) - 1600
			m.Content = fmt.Sprintf("%s\n...[%d chars compacted from earlier tool output]...\n%s", head, omitted, tail)
			out[i] = m
		}
	}
	return out
}

func compactFileToolArgs(toolName, rawArgs string) string {
	if len(rawArgs) < placeholderMinChars {
		return rawArgs
	}
	var args map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(llm.RepairJSON(rawArgs)), &args); err != nil {
		return rawArgs
	}
	path, _ := args["path"].(string)
	if path == "" {
		path = "<file>"
	}
	modified := false
	if content, ok := args["content"].(string); ok && len(content) >= placeholderMinChars {
		args["content"] = fmt.Sprintf("[%d characters already applied to %s. Call read_file for current code.]", len(content), path)
		modified = true
	}
	if newStr, ok := args["new_string"].(string); ok && len(newStr) >= placeholderMinChars {
		args["new_string"] = fmt.Sprintf("[%d characters already applied to %s. Call read_file for current code.]", len(newStr), path)
		modified = true
	}
	if oldStr, ok := args["old_string"].(string); ok && len(oldStr) >= placeholderMinChars {
		args["old_string"] = fmt.Sprintf("[%d characters matched in %s]", len(oldStr), path)
		modified = true
	}
	if !modified {
		return rawArgs
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(args)
	if err != nil {
		return rawArgs
	}
	return string(b)
}

// EstimateTokens returns a fast token estimate (~4 characters per token) for status
// bars and context budget tracking.
func EstimateTokens(msgs []llm.Message) int {
	chars := 0
	for _, m := range msgs {
		chars += len(m.Content) + 16
		for _, tc := range m.ToolCalls {
			chars += len(tc.Name) + len(tc.Arguments) + 12
		}
	}
	if chars == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	return (chars + 3) / 4
}

// FormatTodoChecklist formats a concise harness-owned checklist block to inject
// into the system prompt so the model never loses track of its plan across compactions.
func FormatTodoChecklist(items []string) string {
	if len(items) == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	return "\n\nActive Todo Checklist (survives context compaction):\n" + strings.Join(items, "\n")
}

func TestPruneHistoryPlaceholders(t *testing.T) {
	bigCode := strings.Repeat("func hello() {}\n", 40) // > 300 chars
	argsJSON := fmt.Sprintf(`{"path":"main.go","content":%q}`, bigCode)

	msgs := []llm.Message{
		{Role: "system", Content: "sys"},
		{Role: "user", Content: "write main.go"},
		{
			Role: "assistant",
			ToolCalls: []llm.ToolCall{
				{ID: "tc1", Name: "write_file", Arguments: argsJSON},
			},
		},
		{Role: "tool", ToolCallID: "tc1", Content: "wrote main.go"},
		{Role: "user", Content: "now check status"},
		{Role: "assistant", Content: "checking"},
	}

	pruned := PruneHistoryPlaceholders(msgs, 2)
	gotArgs := pruned[2].ToolCalls[0].Arguments
	if !strings.Contains(gotArgs, "characters already applied to main.go") {
		t.Fatalf("expected placeholder in pruned write_file args, got: %s", gotArgs)
	}
	if len(gotArgs) >= len(argsJSON) {
		t.Fatalf("expected pruned args to be much shorter (%d vs %d)", len(gotArgs), len(argsJSON))
	}
}

func TestMaybeCompactContext(t *testing.T) {
	tmpDir := t.TempDir()
	origDir, _ := os.Getwd()
	_ = os.Chdir(tmpDir)
	defer func() { _ = os.Chdir(origDir) }()

	ag := New(Config{
		ContextBudget: 100, // very small budget so threshold is 80 tokens (~320 chars)
	})

	longContent := strings.Repeat("This is a long conversation content line to trigger token compaction. ", 20)
	msgs := []llm.Message{
		{Role: "system", Content: "System prompt"},
		{Role: "user", Content: "Task 1 " + longContent},
		{Role: "assistant", Content: "Task 1 answer"},
		{Role: "user", Content: "Task 2"},
		{Role: "assistant", Content: "Task 2 answer"},
	}

	compacted := ag.maybeCompactContext(msgs, false)
	if len(compacted) >= len(msgs) {
		t.Fatalf("expected compacted messages to be trimmed, got %d msgs", len(compacted))
	}
	if !strings.Contains(compacted[1].Content, "Context Compaction") {
		t.Fatalf("expected compaction notice in message 1, got: %s", compacted[1].Content)
	}

	// Verify .mimir/HANDOFF.md was written
	handoffPath := filepath.Join(tmpDir, ".mimir", "HANDOFF.md")
	if _, err := os.Stat(handoffPath); os.IsNotExist(err) {
		t.Fatalf("expected %s to be created by auto-compaction", handoffPath)
	}
}

// TestDefaultDeciderEndpoint proves the F26b fix: the default decider is no
// longer constructed with a permanently empty base URL. It inherits the main
// provider's base URL, and MIMIR_DECISION_BASE_URL overrides it.
func TestDefaultDeciderEndpoint(t *testing.T) {
	prov := &llm.OpenAIProvider{IDStr: "p", BaseURL: "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1", Model: "m"}
	a := New(Config{
		Provider: prov, Tools: tools.NewRegistry(),
		Cortex: cortex.NewMemoryStore(), Model: "m",

		t.Errorf("decider BaseURL = %q, want the provider base URL", got)
	}
	if got := a.Decider().Model; got != decision.PrimaryDecisionModel {
		t.Errorf("decider Model = %q, want %q", got, decision.PrimaryDecisionModel)
	}

	t.Setenv("MIMIR_DECISION_BASE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:9999/v1")
	t.Setenv("MIMIR_DECISION_MODEL", "d1-test")
	a = New(Config{
		Provider: prov, Tools: tools.NewRegistry(),
		Cortex: cortex.NewMemoryStore(), Model: "m",
	})
	if got := a.Decider().BaseURL; got != "http://127.0.0.1:9999/v1" {
		t.Errorf("decider BaseURL = %q, want the env override", got)
	}
	if got := a.Decider().Model; got != "d1-test" {
		t.Errorf("decider Model = %q, want the env override", got)
	}
}

package agent

import (
	"context"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/cortex"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/llm"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/tools"

func writeCall() llm.ToolCall {
	return llm.ToolCall{ID: "w1", Name: "write_file", Arguments: `{"path":"out.txt","content":"hi"}`}
}

// TestGateRequireApprovalNilApproverDenies proves the F2/N1 fix: a gate
// RequireApproval verdict with no approver configured fails closed instead
// of silently passing the tool call.
func TestGateRequireApprovalNilApproverDenies(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	a := New(Config{
		Provider: &oneCallProvider{}, Tools: tools.Default(dir),
		Cortex: cortex.NewMemoryStore(), Model: "m",
		Gate: policy.DefaultDevGate(),
	})
	st := a.executeToolCall(context.Background(), writeCall())
	if st.Err == "" {
		t.Fatalf("expected denial with nil approver, got step %+v", st)
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, "out.txt")); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
		t.Errorf("write_file executed despite the missing approver")
	}
}

// TestGateRequireApprovalApproverDecides proves an approver returning false
// denies and an approver returning true allows the gated tool call.
func TestGateRequireApprovalApproverDecides(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	deny := New(Config{
		Provider: &oneCallProvider{}, Tools: tools.Default(dir),
		Cortex: cortex.NewMemoryStore(), Model: "m",
		Gate:         policy.DefaultDevGate(),
		ApprovalFunc: func(string, string) bool { return false },
	})
	if st := deny.executeToolCall(context.Background(), writeCall()); st.Err == "" {
		t.Errorf("approver=false: expected denial, got %+v", st)
	}

	allow := New(Config{
		Provider: &oneCallProvider{}, Tools: tools.Default(dir),
		Cortex: cortex.NewMemoryStore(), Model: "m",
		Gate:         policy.DefaultDevGate(),
		ApprovalFunc: func(string, string) bool { return true },
	})
	st := allow.executeToolCall(context.Background(), writeCall())
	if st.Err != "" {
		t.Fatalf("approver=true: unexpected error %q", st.Err)
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, "out.txt")); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("approver=true: file was not written: %v", err)
	}
}

// TestBypassWaivesApprovalButNotDeny proves bypass mode is an explicit user
// opt-out of approval prompts only: RequireApproval is waived with no approver
// at all, while a Deny verdict still blocks execution.
func TestBypassWaivesApprovalButNotDeny(t *testing.T) {
	gate := policy.NewGate()
	gate.AddRule(policy.Rule{Pattern: "write_file", Decision: policy.RequireApproval})
	gate.AddRule(policy.Rule{Pattern: "bash", Decision: policy.Deny})

	dir := t.TempDir()
	a := New(Config{
		Provider: &oneCallProvider{}, Tools: tools.Default(dir),
		Cortex: cortex.NewMemoryStore(), Model: "m",
		Mode: ModeBypass, Gate: gate,
	})
	st := a.executeToolCall(context.Background(), writeCall())
	if st.Err != "" {
		t.Errorf("bypass + RequireApproval: unexpected error %q", st.Err)
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, "out.txt")); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("bypass + RequireApproval: file was not written: %v", err)
	}

	st = a.executeToolCall(context.Background(), llm.ToolCall{ID: "b1", Name: "bash", Arguments: `{"command":"echo hi"}`})
	if st.Err == "" || !strings.Contains(st.Err, "deny") {
		t.Errorf("bypass + Deny: expected a deny error, got %+v", st)
	}
}

// TestEditModeNilApproverDeniesWrite proves the ModeEdit approval branch also
// fails closed: in edit mode a write tool with no approver is denied even

func TestEditModeNilApproverDeniesWrite(t *testing.T) {

	})

	}

	}

// TestPhaseEnforcementAtExecution proves the F5 fix: under waterfall, a tool
// outside the active phase's allowed set is rejected inside executeToolCall,
// not merely hidden from the advertised schemas.
func TestPhaseEnforcementAtExecution(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	mgr := sdlc.NewManager(dir)
	if err := mgr.SetMethodology("waterfall"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SetMethodology: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := mgr.SetPhase("planning"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SetPhase: %v", err)
	}
	a := New(Config{
		Provider: &oneCallProvider{}, Tools: tools.Default(dir),
		Cortex: cortex.NewMemoryStore(), Model: "m",
		Mode: ModeBypass, SDLC: mgr,
	})

	st := a.executeToolCall(context.Background(), llm.ToolCall{ID: "b1", Name: "bash", Arguments: `{"command":"echo hi"}`})
	if st.Err == "" || !strings.Contains(st.Err, "SDLC phase policy") {
		t.Errorf("bash in waterfall planning phase: expected a phase policy rejection, got %+v", st)
	}

	// read_file IS in the planning phase set, so it must not be phase-blocked
	// (it errors only because the file does not exist).
	st = a.executeToolCall(context.Background(), llm.ToolCall{ID: "r1", Name: "read_file", Arguments: `{"path":"missing.txt"}`})
	if strings.Contains(st.Err, "SDLC phase policy") {
		t.Errorf("read_file in planning phase was phase-blocked: %q", st.Err)
	}
}


==============================================================================
FILE: internal/agent/handoff.go
==============================================================================
package agent

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/llm"
)

// HandoffState captures the structured context needed for cross-session continuity.
type HandoffState struct {
	SessionID        string
	Timestamp        time.Time
	CurrentObjective string
	CompletedTasks   []string
	VerifiedFiles    []string
	RemainingTodos   []string
	FailedApproaches []string
	NextCommand      string
}

// GenerateHandoffMarkdown analyzes conversation history, todo items, and Yggdrasil
// mind map status to produce a structured .mimir/HANDOFF.md document.
func GenerateHandoffMarkdown(sessionID string, history []llm.Message, todoLines []string, mindMapSummary string) string {
	state := HandoffState{
		SessionID: sessionID,
		Timestamp: time.Now().UTC(),
	}

	// 1. Extract Current Objective from earliest user message
	for _, m := range history {
		if m.Role == "user" && !strings.HasPrefix(m.Content, "[") {
			state.CurrentObjective = strings.TrimSpace(m.Content)
			break
		}
	}
	if state.CurrentObjective == "" {
		state.CurrentObjective = "Ongoing software development sprint."
	}

	// 2. Parse Todo Checklist into completed vs remaining
	for _, line := range todoLines {
		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
		if strings.Contains(trimmed, "[completed]") || strings.Contains(trimmed, "[x]") {
			state.CompletedTasks = append(state.CompletedTasks, trimmed)
		} else {
			state.RemainingTodos = append(state.RemainingTodos, trimmed)
		}
	}

	// 3. Scan tool history for touched files and failed approaches
	seenFiles := make(map[string]bool)
	for _, m := range history {
		if m.Role == "tool" {
			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(m.Content), "error") || strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(m.Content), "failed") {
				errMsg := strings.TrimSpace(m.Content)
				if len(errMsg) > 160 {
					errMsg = errMsg[:160] + "..."
				}
				state.FailedApproaches = append(state.FailedApproaches, errMsg)
			}
		}
		for _, tc := range m.ToolCalls {
			if tc.Name == "write_file" || tc.Name == "edit_block" {
				target := extractTargetFile(tc.Arguments)
				if target != "" && !seenFiles[target] {
					seenFiles[target] = true
					state.VerifiedFiles = append(state.VerifiedFiles, target)
				}
			}
		}
	}

	// 4. Determine Suggested Next Command
	if len(state.RemainingTodos) > 0 {
		state.NextCommand = "mimir \"continue working on remaining checklist items\""
	} else {
		state.NextCommand = "mimir review"
	}

	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("# Mímir Session Handoff & Continuity State\n")
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Session ID**: `%s`\n", state.SessionID)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Generated At**: `%s`\n", state.Timestamp.Format(time.RFC3339))
	if mindMapSummary != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Repository State**: %s\n", mindMapSummary)
	}
	b.WriteString("\n")

	b.WriteString("## 1. Current Objective & Architectural State\n")
	b.WriteString(state.CurrentObjective + "\n\n")

	b.WriteString("## 2. Completed Tasks & Verified Files\n")
	if len(state.CompletedTasks) > 0 {
		b.WriteString("### Completed Checklist Items\n")
		for _, t := range state.CompletedTasks {
			b.WriteString(t + "\n")
		}
	}
	if len(state.VerifiedFiles) > 0 {
		b.WriteString("\n### Modified / Verified Files\n")
		for _, f := range state.VerifiedFiles {
			b.WriteString("- `" + f + "`\n")
		}
	}
	if len(state.CompletedTasks) == 0 && len(state.VerifiedFiles) == 0 {
		b.WriteString("No completed tasks or modified files recorded yet.\n")
	}
	b.WriteString("\n")

	b.WriteString("## 3. Remaining Todo Checklist (In-Progress & Pending)\n")
	if len(state.RemainingTodos) > 0 {
		for _, t := range state.RemainingTodos {
			b.WriteString(t + "\n")
		}
	} else {
		b.WriteString("- No pending checklist items. All scheduled tasks completed.\n")
	}
	b.WriteString("\n")

	b.WriteString("## 4. Failed Approaches & Guardrails (Do Not Repeat)\n")
	if len(state.FailedApproaches) > 0 {
		for _, f := range state.FailedApproaches {
			b.WriteString("- " + f + "\n")
		}
	} else {
		b.WriteString("- Zero failed tool executions recorded in this session.\n")
	}
	b.WriteString("\n")

	b.WriteString("## 5. Exact Next Command to Run\n")
	b.WriteString("```bash\n" + state.NextCommand + "\n```\n")

	return b.String()
}

// WriteHandoffFile saves the generated handoff markdown to .mimir/HANDOFF.md.
func WriteHandoffFile(workDir, content string) (string, error) {
	if workDir == "" {
		workDir = "."
	}
	dir := filepath.Join(workDir, ".mimir")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	outPath := filepath.Join(dir, "HANDOFF.md")
	if err := os.WriteFile(outPath, []byte(content), 0o644); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return outPath, nil
}

package agent

import (
	"os"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/llm"
)

func TestGenerateHandoffMarkdown(t *testing.T) {
	history := []llm.Message{
		{Role: "user", Content: "Build the Level 1 harness lifecycle hooks"},
		{
			Role:    "assistant",
			Content: "Editing hooks.go",
			ToolCalls: []llm.ToolCall{
				{
					Name:      "write_file",
					Arguments: `{"path": "internal/agent/hooks.go"}`,
				},
			},
		},
		{Role: "tool", Content: "error: file not found on initial read"},
	}

	todos := []string{
		"- #1 [completed] Implement hooks.go",
		"- #2 [in_progress] Implement handoff.go",
	}

	md := GenerateHandoffMarkdown("session-42", history, todos, "108 files (~237k tokens)")

	if !strings.Contains(md, "session-42") {
		t.Errorf("expected session-42 in handoff, got:\n%s", md)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(md, "Build the Level 1 harness lifecycle hooks") {
		t.Errorf("expected objective in handoff, got:\n%s", md)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(md, "internal/agent/hooks.go") {
		t.Errorf("expected modified file in handoff, got:\n%s", md)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(md, "Implement handoff.go") {
		t.Errorf("expected pending todo in handoff, got:\n%s", md)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(md, "error: file not found on initial read") {
		t.Errorf("expected failed approach recorded, got:\n%s", md)
	}
}

func TestWriteHandoffFile(t *testing.T) {

	content := "# Test Handoff Content"
	path, err := WriteHandoffFile(dir, content)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("WriteHandoffFile: %v", err)
	}

	read, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil || string(read) != content {
		t.Fatalf("mismatch reading handoff file: %s (%v)", string(read), err)
	}
}


==============================================================================
FILE: internal/agent/hooks.go
==============================================================================
package agent

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"sync"
)

// HookType identifies a lifecycle execution point in the agent harness.
type HookType string

const (
	HookPrePrompt HookType = "pre_prompt" // Before prompt construction / LLM invocation
	HookPreTool   HookType = "pre_tool"   // Before a tool executes
	HookPostTool  HookType = "post_tool"  // Immediately after a tool finishes execution
	HookOnStop    HookType = "on_stop"    // When the agent turn finishes (final reply emitted)
)

// HookContext provides state and metadata to hooks.
type HookContext struct {
	Type        HookType
	ToolName    string
	ToolArgs    string
	ToolResult  string
	ToolErr     string
	Path        string   // Target file if mutation tool
	TodoLines   []string // Current harness-owned todo items
	Trace       []Step   // Steps taken during the turn
	StopStatus  StopGateStatus
	InjectedMsg string // Optional feedback injected back into agent history
}

// HookHandler defines a hook callback function.
type HookHandler func(ctx context.Context, hCtx *HookContext) error

// HookRule defines an external rule from .mimir/hooks.json.
type HookRule struct {
	Type    HookType `json:"type"`
	Command string   `json:"command"` // Shell command to run
	Tool    string   `json:"tool"`    // Optional tool filter (e.g. "write_file", "edit_block")
}

// HookRunner manages and executes Level 1 lifecycle hooks.
type HookRunner struct {
	mu       sync.RWMutex
	handlers map[HookType][]HookHandler
	workDir  string
}

// NewHookRunner initializes a HookRunner with built-in Level 1 verification rules.
func NewHookRunner(workDir string) *HookRunner {
	if workDir == "" {
		workDir = "."
	}
	hr := &HookRunner{
		handlers: make(map[HookType][]HookHandler),
		workDir:  workDir,
	}
	hr.registerBuiltinHooks()
	hr.loadConfigFile()
	return hr
}

// Register adds a custom in-process hook handler for a specific lifecycle phase.
func (hr *HookRunner) Register(hType HookType, handler HookHandler) {
	hr.mu.Lock()
	defer hr.mu.Unlock()
	hr.handlers[hType] = append(hr.handlers[hType], handler)
}

func (hr *HookRunner) registerBuiltinHooks() {
	// PostTool: Run fast syntax check / formatting on modified source files.
	hr.Register(HookPostTool, func(ctx context.Context, hCtx *HookContext) error {
		if hCtx.ToolName != "write_file" && hCtx.ToolName != "edit_block" {
			return nil
		}
		target := extractTargetFile(hCtx.ToolArgs)
		if target == "" {
			return nil
		}
		fullPath := filepath.Join(hr.workDir, target)
		if !filepath.IsAbs(target) {
			fullPath = filepath.Clean(fullPath)
		} else {
			fullPath = target
		}

		ext := strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(fullPath))
		if ext == ".go" {
			if out, err := runSyntaxCheckGo(ctx, fullPath); err != nil {
				hCtx.ToolResult += fmt.Sprintf("\n[Hook Linter Warning]: gofmt syntax validation issue:\n%s", out)
			}
		}
		return nil
	})

	// OnStop: Evaluate harness stop gate and suggest verification if tasks remain unverified.
	hr.Register(HookOnStop, func(ctx context.Context, hCtx *HookContext) error {
		gate := EvaluateStopGate(hCtx.Trace, hCtx.TodoLines)
		hCtx.StopStatus = gate
		if gate.Advisory != "" {
			hCtx.InjectedMsg = gate.Advisory
		}
		return nil
	})
}

func (hr *HookRunner) loadConfigFile() {
	configPath := filepath.Join(hr.workDir, ".mimir", "hooks.json")
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(configPath)
	if err != nil {
		return
	}
	var rules []HookRule
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &rules); err != nil {
		return
	}
	for _, rule := range rules {
		r := rule
		hr.Register(r.Type, func(ctx context.Context, hCtx *HookContext) error {
			if r.Tool != "" && !strings.EqualFold(r.Tool, hCtx.ToolName) {
				return nil
			}
			cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "sh", "-c", r.Command)
			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(os.Getenv("OS")), "windows") {
				cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "powershell", "-NoProfile", "-Command", r.Command)
			}
			cmd.Dir = hr.workDir
			var out bytes.Buffer
			cmd.Stdout = &out
			cmd.Stderr = &out
			_ = cmd.Run()
			if out.Len() > 0 {
				hCtx.ToolResult += fmt.Sprintf("\n[Hook %s Output]: %s", r.Type, strings.TrimSpace(out.String()))
			}
			return nil
		})
	}
}

// Execute runs all handlers registered for the given hook type.
func (hr *HookRunner) Execute(ctx context.Context, hCtx *HookContext) error {
	if hr == nil {
		return nil
	}
	hr.mu.RLock()
	handlers := hr.handlers[hCtx.Type]
	hr.mu.RUnlock()

	for _, handler := range handlers {
		if err := handler(ctx, hCtx); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func extractTargetFile(rawArgs string) string {
	var args map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(rawArgs), &args); err != nil {
		return ""
	}
	if p, ok := args["path"].(string); ok && p != "" {
		return p
	}
	if p, ok := args["target"].(string); ok && p != "" {
		return p
	}
	return ""
}

func runSyntaxCheckGo(ctx context.Context, path string) (string, error) {
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "gofmt", "-e", path)
	out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
	if err != nil {
		return strings.TrimSpace(string(out)), err
	}
	return "", nil
}

package agent

import (
	"context"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestHookRunner_RegistrationAndExecution(t *testing.T) {
	hr := NewHookRunner(t.TempDir())
	called := false
	hr.Register(HookPreTool, func(ctx context.Context, hCtx *HookContext) error {
		if hCtx.ToolName == "test_tool" {
			called = true
		}
		return nil
	})

	hCtx := &HookContext{
		Type:     HookPreTool,
		ToolName: "test_tool",
	}
	if err := hr.Execute(context.Background(), hCtx); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Execute failed: %v", err)
	}
	if !called {
		t.Fatalf("expected hook to be called")
	}
}

func TestHookRunner_PostToolCatchesGoSyntaxError(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	badGoFile := filepath.Join(dir, "broken.go")
	if err := os.WriteFile(badGoFile, []byte("package broken\nfunc foo( { nope"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write file: %v", err)
	}

	hr := NewHookRunner(dir)
	hCtx := &HookContext{
		Type:       HookPostTool,
		ToolName:   "write_file",
		ToolArgs:   `{"path": "broken.go"}`,
		ToolResult: "file written successfully",
	}

	if err := hr.Execute(context.Background(), hCtx); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Execute: %v", err)
	}

	if !strings.Contains(hCtx.ToolResult, "[Hook Linter Warning]") {
		t.Fatalf("expected linter warning in ToolResult, got:\n%s", hCtx.ToolResult)
	}
}

func TestHookRunner_OnStopEvaluatesGate(t *testing.T) {
	hr := NewHookRunner(t.TempDir())
	hCtx := &HookContext{
		Type: HookOnStop,
		TodoLines: []string{
			"- #1 [in_progress] finish hooks",
		},
		Trace: []Step{
			{Name: "write_file", Args: `{"path":"main.go"}`},
		},
	}

	if err := hr.Execute(context.Background(), hCtx); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Execute: %v", err)
	}

	if hCtx.InjectedMsg == "" || !strings.Contains(hCtx.InjectedMsg, "Harness OnStop Gate Advisory") {
		t.Fatalf("expected stop gate advisory, got %q", hCtx.InjectedMsg)
	}
}

package agent

import (
	"context"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/cortex"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/llm"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/tools"
)

// TestLiveRun exercises the recall -> infer -> remember loop against a REAL provider
// (not a fake server). SKIPPED unless MIMIR_LIVE_BASE_URL is set, so the normal
// `go test ./...` stays green and offline. See docs/TESTING-POLICY.md.
func TestLiveRun(t *testing.T) {
	base := os.Getenv("MIMIR_LIVE_BASE_URL")
	if base == "" {
		t.Skip("set MIMIR_LIVE_BASE_URL (+ MIMIR_LIVE_MODEL, optional MIMIR_LIVE_API_KEY) to run the live test")
	}
	model := os.Getenv("MIMIR_LIVE_MODEL")
	if model == "" {
		model = "qwen2.5:0.5b"
	}

	store := cortex.NewMemoryStore()
	if _, err := store.PutNeuron(context.Background(), cortex.Neuron{
		Kind: cortex.KindMemory, Layer: "preference", Content: "the secret codeword is pinecone", Decay: 1,
	}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("seed: %v", err)
	}

	a := New(Config{
		Provider: &llm.OpenAIProvider{
			IDStr: "live", BaseURL: base, APIKey: os.Getenv("MIMIR_LIVE_API_KEY"), Model: model,
		},
		Tools: tools.NewRegistry(), Cortex: store, Model: model,
	})

	reply, err := a.Run(context.Background(), "Say hello in one short word.", nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("live Run: %v", err)
	}
	if strings.TrimSpace(reply) == "" {
		t.Fatal("live model returned an empty reply")
	}
	t.Logf("live reply from %s/%s: %q", "live", model, reply)

	remembered, _ := store.Search(context.Background(), "hello", 5)
	if len(remembered) == 0 {
		t.Error("expected the live exchange to be remembered in the Cortex")
	}
}

// TestLiveToolCall is the live proof that a real model can drive a real tool through
// the loop. SKIPPED unless MIMIR_LIVE_TOOL=1 (it needs a tool-capable model, e.g.
// qwen3:8b). It asks the model to run bash and checks the tool actually executed.
func TestLiveToolCall(t *testing.T) {
	if os.Getenv("MIMIR_LIVE_TOOL") == "" {
		t.Skip("set MIMIR_LIVE_TOOL=1 (and MIMIR_LIVE_BASE_URL + a tool-capable MIMIR_LIVE_MODEL like qwen3:8b) to run the live tool test")
	}
	base := os.Getenv("MIMIR_LIVE_BASE_URL")
	if base == "" {
		t.Skip("MIMIR_LIVE_TOOL=1 but MIMIR_LIVE_BASE_URL is unset")
	}
	model := os.Getenv("MIMIR_LIVE_MODEL")
	if model == "" {
		model = "qwen3:8b"
	}

	a := New(Config{
		Provider: &llm.OpenAIProvider{
			IDStr: "live", BaseURL: base, APIKey: os.Getenv("MIMIR_LIVE_API_KEY"), Model: model,
		},
		Tools: tools.Default(t.TempDir()), Cortex: cortex.NewMemoryStore(), Model: model,
	})

	reply, trace, err := a.RunTrace(context.Background(), "You have a bash tool. Use the bash tool to run exactly this command: echo MIMIR_TOOL_LIVE. Then reply with the single word DONE.", nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("live RunTrace: %v", err)
	}
	used := false
	for _, s := range trace {
		if s.Name == "bash" {
			used = true
			if !strings.Contains(s.Result, "MIMIR_TOOL_LIVE") {
				t.Errorf("bash result = %q, want it to contain MIMIR_TOOL_LIVE", s.Result)
			}
		}
	}
	if !used {
		t.Fatalf("the live model did not call the bash tool (reply was %q); pick a tool-capable model via MIMIR_LIVE_MODEL", reply)
	}
	t.Logf("live tool loop OK; reply=%q trace steps=%d", reply, len(trace))
}

// TestLiveCrossRunMemory proves cross-run memory with a REAL model: run 1 writes a
// memory to a file-backed Cortex; a fresh store reopened from the same file recalls it
// on run 2. Asserts on Recalled (deterministic regardless of the model's wording).
func TestLiveCrossRunMemory(t *testing.T) {
	if os.Getenv("MIMIR_LIVE_MEMORY") == "" {
		t.Skip("set MIMIR_LIVE_MEMORY=1 (+ MIMIR_LIVE_BASE_URL + model) to run the live cross-run memory test")
	}
	base := os.Getenv("MIMIR_LIVE_BASE_URL")
	if base == "" {
		t.Skip("MIMIR_LIVE_MEMORY=1 but MIMIR_LIVE_BASE_URL is unset")
	}
	model := os.Getenv("MIMIR_LIVE_MODEL")
	if model == "" {
		model = "qwen3:8b"
	}
	p := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "cortex.json")
	mk := func() *Agent {
		st, err := cortex.NewMemoryStoreAt(p)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("store: %v", err)
		}
		return New(Config{
			Provider: &llm.OpenAIProvider{
				IDStr: "live", BaseURL: base, APIKey: os.Getenv("MIMIR_LIVE_API_KEY"), Model: model,
			},
			Tools: tools.NewRegistry(), Cortex: st, Model: model,
		})
	}

	if _, err := mk().Run(context.Background(), "Remember this exactly: the launch code is KIWI55. Reply OK.", nil); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("run1: %v", err)
	}
	res, err := mk().RunFull(context.Background(), "What is the launch code KIWI55? Answer from memory.", nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("run2: %v", err)
	}
	found := false
	for _, c := range res.Recalled {
		if strings.Contains(c, "KIWI55") {
			found = true
		}
	}
	if !found {
		t.Fatalf("run 2 did not recall run 1's memory from disk; recalled=%v", res.Recalled)
	}
	t.Logf("live cross-run memory OK; recalled %d memory(ies)", len(res.Recalled))
}

package agent

import (
	"context"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/cortex"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/llm"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/tools"
)

// textProvider always returns a fixed reply with no tool calls - enough to drive the
// loop and exercise memory write/recall deterministically (no network).
type textProvider struct{ t string }

func (p *textProvider) ID() string { return "txt" }
func (p *textProvider) Generate(context.Context, llm.GenerateRequest) (llm.GenerateResponse, error) {
	return llm.GenerateResponse{Content: p.t, FinishReason: "stop"}, nil
}
func (p *textProvider) Stream(context.Context, llm.GenerateRequest) (<-chan llm.StreamEvent, error) {
	return nil, nil
}

// TestCrossRunMemory proves memory survives across runs: run 1 seeds a memory
// into a file-backed Cortex; a second agent opening a NEW store from the same file
// (simulating a process restart) recalls it on run 2. No network involved.
func TestCrossRunMemory(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	p := filepath.Join(dir, "cortex.json")
	mk := func() *Agent {
		st, err := cortex.NewMemoryStoreAt(p)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("store: %v", err)
		}
		return New(Config{
			Provider: &textProvider{"ok"}, Tools: tools.NewRegistry(), Cortex: st, Model: "m",
		})
	}

	st, _ := cortex.NewMemoryStoreAt(p)
	if _, err := st.PutNeuron(context.Background(), cortex.Neuron{
		Kind: cortex.KindMemory, Layer: "fact",
		Content: "KIWI55 is a secret codeword", Decay: 1,
	}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("seed: %v", err)
	}

	res, err := mk().RunFull(context.Background(), "tell me about KIWI55", nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("run2: %v", err)
	}
	found := false
	for _, c := range res.Recalled {
		if strings.Contains(c, "KIWI55") {
			found = true
		}
	}
	if !found {
		t.Fatalf("expected cross-run recall of KIWI55; recalled=%v", res.Recalled)
	}
}

FILE: internal/agent/mode_override_test.go

package agent

import (
	"context"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/cortex"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/llm"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/tools"
)

// TestPerRequestModeDoesNotLeak proves the N2 fix at the agent level: a run
// under a bypass override executes with bypass semantics, yet the agent's
// stored mode is untouched, so the next default run still runs read-only.
func TestPerRequestModeDoesNotLeak(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	call := llm.ToolCall{ID: "w1", Name: "write_file", Arguments: `{"path":"out.txt","content":"hi"}`}
	a := New(Config{
		Provider: &oneCallProvider{call: call}, Tools: tools.Default(dir),
		Cortex: cortex.NewMemoryStore(), Model: "m",
		Mode: ModeReadOnly,
	})

	res, err := a.RunFullWithMode(context.Background(), ModeBypass, "write it", nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("RunFullWithMode: %v", err)
	}
	if len(res.Trace) != 1 || res.Trace[0].Err != "" {
		t.Fatalf("bypass run: expected the write to succeed, trace = %+v", res.Trace)
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, "out.txt")); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("bypass run: file was not written: %v", err)
	}
	if got := a.Mode(); got != ModeReadOnly {
		t.Fatalf("agent mode leaked: stored mode = %q, want %q", got, ModeReadOnly)
	}

	// A subsequent default run must still be read-only: the write is blocked.
	a2 := New(Config{
		Provider: &oneCallProvider{call: call}, Tools: tools.Default(dir),
		Cortex: cortex.NewMemoryStore(), Model: "m",
		Mode: ModeReadOnly,
	})
	res, err = a2.RunFull(context.Background(), "write it", nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("RunFull: %v", err)
	}
	if len(res.Trace) != 1 || !strings.Contains(res.Trace[0].Err, "read-only") {
		t.Errorf("default run after bypass: expected a read-only block, trace = %+v", res.Trace)
	}
}

FILE: internal/agent/personas.go

package agent

import "strings"

// Persona is a named agent role (Norse figures; F33).
type Persona struct {
	Name   string   // Norse name (id)
	Role   string   // human-readable role
	Prompt string   // system-prompt fragment
	Tools  []string // tool allowlist (empty = all)
	Model  string   // default model (empty = inherit)
}

// DefaultVoice is Mímir's default communication style, prepended to every persona's
// prompt (F44). It defines the framework's voice.
const DefaultVoice = "Voice: talk like a 10th-grade high school student. Simple, casual, relatable, like explaining to a friend. Keep it clear and chill, not stiff or corporate. NEVER use em dashes; use hyphens (-) or colons (:) instead."

// BaseRules are workflow rules prepended to every persona's prompt (F31.3, F45).
const BaseRules = "Always use the to-do list (todo tool) to plan and track your work: for any task bigger than a tiny change, write the steps as to-dos first, then work through them one at a time, updating their status as you go. Use the question tool to ask the user structured multiple-choice questions whenever you need a decision, preference, or clarification."

// FullPrompt returns the persona's full system prompt: default voice + base rules +
// the persona's own prompt.
func (p Persona) FullPrompt() string {
	return DefaultVoice + "\n\n" + BaseRules + "\n\n" + p.Prompt
}

// StripEmDashes replaces em dashes and en dashes with hyphens. This is the post-output
// filter that enforces the no-em-dash rule (F44.5).
func StripEmDashes(s string) string {
	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "\u2014", "-") // em dash
	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "\u2013", "-") // en dash
	return s
}

// BuiltinPersonas are Mímir's Norse agent personas (F33). The BMAD planning personas
// (Mary/John/Winston/...) are the process; these are the product.
var BuiltinPersonas = []Persona{
	{Name: "odin", Role: "Orchestrator / planner", Prompt: "You are Odin, the All-Father. See the whole board: make the game plan, delegate, and coordinate."},
	{Name: "thor", Role: "Builder", Prompt: "You are Thor. Do the heavy lifting: write code, run tools, and execute decisively."},
	{Name: "loki", Role: "Tester & debugger", Prompt: "You are Loki, tester and debugger. Run end-to-end tests, reproduce and fix bugs, and break things to make them stronger."},
	{Name: "heimdall", Role: "Visual auditor", Prompt: "You are Heimdall, the all-seeing watchman. Screenshot the running app and verify the UI matches the approved mock and looks right; let no visual flaw pass."},
	{Name: "bragi", Role: "Skald", Prompt: "You are Bragi, the skald: write clear documentation, comments, and eloquent output."},
	{Name: "huginn", Role: "Scout (thought)", Prompt: "You are Huginn, Odin's raven of thought: fly out, explore, and bring back what you learn."},
	{Name: "muninn", Role: "Scout (memory)", Prompt: "You are Muninn, Odin's raven of memory: gather and recall what is known."},
	{Name: "ratatoskr", Role: "Messenger", Prompt: "You are Ratatoskr: carry messages between agents up and down Yggdrasil."},
	{Name: "forseti", Role: "Code auditor", Prompt: "You are Forseti, the judge. Review code for quality, correctness, and security; let nothing flawed pass."},
}

// PersonaByName returns a built-in persona by name.
func PersonaByName(name string) (Persona, bool) {
	for _, p := range BuiltinPersonas {
		if p.Name == name {
			return p, true
		}
	}
	return Persona{}, false
}

		t.Errorf("expected at least 9 builtin personas, got %d", len(BuiltinPersonas))
	}
	// every persona must have a name, role, and prompt
	for _, p := range BuiltinPersonas {
		if p.Name == "" || p.Role == "" || p.Prompt == "" {
			t.Errorf("persona missing fields: %+v", p)
		}
	}

func TestDefaultVoiceAndFilter(t *testing.T) {
	p, ok := PersonaByName("odin")
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("odin persona not found")
	}
	full := p.FullPrompt()
	if !strings.Contains(full, "10th-grade") {
		t.Error("FullPrompt should include the 10th-grade voice")
	}
	if !strings.Contains(full, "NEVER use em dashes") {
		t.Error("FullPrompt should include the no-em-dash rule")
	}
	if !strings.Contains(full, "Always use the to-do list") {
		t.Error("FullPrompt should include the always-use-todo rule")
	}
	if !strings.Contains(full, "question tool") {
		t.Error("FullPrompt should mention the question tool")
	}
	out := StripEmDashes("hello \u2014 world \u2013 ok")
	if out != "hello - world - ok" {
		t.Errorf("StripEmDashes = %q, want %q", out, "hello - world - ok")
	}
}

FILE: internal/agent/rules.go

package agent

import (
	"strings"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/sdlc"
)

// CoreIdentityLine is the single-sentence identity header (<25 tokens) that keeps
// the base prompt razor-thin for both frontier and tiny local models.
const CoreIdentityLine = "Mímir is a modular polyglot Software Engineering & Creation Harness (Go + Rust + Mojo + Flutter). Never use em dashes."

// WebAndMarketingCreationRules holds the full 4-Layer SEO/GEO & Anti-Slop specification
// for on-demand auditing/skills (NOT injected in bulk into the base prompt).
const WebAndMarketingCreationRules = `
[MÍMIR 4-LAYER WEB, SEO/GEO & ANTI-SLOP REFERENCE SPEC]
1. TECHNICAL DISCOVERABILITY (SEO + GEO/AEO): Semantic HTML5, Core Web Vitals, JSON-LD Schema.org (LocalBusiness, SoftwareApplication, Product, FAQPage), /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, and /llms.txt.
2. ENTITY CLARITY: Explicit machine-readable facts (NAP consistency for Google Maps/GBP, service areas, exact pricing units, direct-answer FAQ blocks).
3. EVIDENCE PROVENANCE & ANTI-SLOP: Zero generic AI hero clichés, zero fabricated statistics/reviews (FTC Review Rule), label vendor numbers as [vendor claim].
4. SPEED-TO-LEAD ARCHITECTURE: First-party lead record (source, response_time, contact, booked_outcome, next_action) + 1-click human handoff.`

var webCreationKeywords = []string{
	"website", "web app", "webapp", "landing page", "frontend", "html", "css",
	"nextjs", "react", "astro", "tailwind", "flutter", "seo", "geo", "aeo",
	"schema.org", "json-ld", "llms.txt", "sitemap", "google maps", "gbp",
	"local business", "marketing", "lead gen", "conversion", "saas", "pricing page",
	"blog", "hero section", "ui", "ux",
}

// DetectWebCreationTask returns true when the prompt involves building, designing,
// auditing, or optimizing a website, web/mobile app, UI, or SEO/GEO marketing surface.
func DetectWebCreationTask(input string) bool {
	lower := strings.ToLower(input)
	for _, kw := range webCreationKeywords {
		if strings.Contains(lower, kw) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// BuildPhaseScopedRulesBlock returns ONLY the active SDLC phase's compact micro-prompt
// (~40-75 tokens) + optional 1-line Web/SEO overlay for that specific phase, keeping
// the main prompt completely free of multi-phase bloat for both big and tiny LLMs.
func BuildPhaseScopedRulesBlock(mgr *sdlc.Manager, input string) string {
	if mgr == nil {
		mgr = sdlc.NewManager(".")
	}
	isWeb := DetectWebCreationTask(input)
	return "\n" + CoreIdentityLine + mgr.BuildPhasePrompt(input, isWeb)
}

// BuildHarnessRulesBlock is a convenience wrapper around BuildPhaseScopedRulesBlock.
func BuildHarnessRulesBlock(input string, _ bool) string {
	return BuildPhaseScopedRulesBlock(sdlc.NewManager("."), input)
}

// StopGateStatus summarizes the Level 1-3 Harness OnStop verification checks.
type StopGateStatus struct {
	HasPendingTodos bool
	PendingCount    int
	RanVerification bool
	Advisory        string
}

// EvaluateStopGate inspects the current turn's tool trace and Todo store to verify
// whether the agent completed its checklist and ran verification before stopping.
func EvaluateStopGate(trace []Step, todoLines []string) StopGateStatus {
	var pending int
	for _, line := range todoLines {
		if strings.Contains(line, "[pending]") || strings.Contains(line, "[in_progress]") {
			pending++
		}
	}
	ranVerify := false
	mutatedFiles := false
	for _, st := range trace {
		if st.Name == "write_file" || st.Name == "edit_block" {
			mutatedFiles = true
		}
		if st.Name == "web_seo_audit" || st.Name == "epistemic_audit" {
			ranVerify = true
		}
		if st.Name == "bash" || st.Name == "run_shell" {
			lowerArgs := strings.ToLower(st.Args)
			if strings.Contains(lowerArgs, "test") || strings.Contains(lowerArgs, "vet") ||
				strings.Contains(lowerArgs, "lint") || strings.Contains(lowerArgs, "build") ||
				strings.Contains(lowerArgs, "check") {
				ranVerify = true
			}
		}
	}

	status := StopGateStatus{
		HasPendingTodos: pending > 0,
		PendingCount:    pending,
		RanVerification: !mutatedFiles || ranVerify,
	}

	var reasons []string
	if status.HasPendingTodos {
		reasons = append(reasons, "pending todo items remain")
	}
	if mutatedFiles && !ranVerify {
		reasons = append(reasons, "files were modified without running build/lint/test verification")
	}
	if len(reasons) > 0 {
		status.Advisory = "Harness OnStop Gate Advisory: " + strings.Join(reasons, "; ")
	}
	return status
}
