package agent

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestDetectWebCreationTask(t *testing.T) {
	if !DetectWebCreationTask("Build a Next.js landing page for a local business with Google Maps SEO") {
		t.Fatal("expected DetectWebCreationTask to return true for web/SEO task")
	}
	if !DetectWebCreationTask("Create a Flutter UI dashboard and add llms.txt + JSON-LD Schema.org") {
		t.Fatal("expected DetectWebCreationTask to return true for Flutter/Schema.org task")
	}
	if DetectWebCreationTask("Refactor the mutex lock in internal/cortex/sqlite.go") {
		t.Fatal("expected DetectWebCreationTask to return false for pure backend mutex task")
	}
}

func TestBuildHarnessRulesBlockZeroBloat(t *testing.T) {
	// 1. Backend Implementation task: loads ONLY Step 4 Implementation micro-prompt (<350 chars), NO Web/SEO bloat.
	backendRules := BuildHarnessRulesBlock("Fix a race condition in the Go channel worker", false)
	if !strings.Contains(backendRules, "SDLC 4/7: IMPLEMENTATION") {
		t.Errorf("expected Step 4 IMPLEMENTATION micro-prompt, got: %s", backendRules)
	}
	if strings.Contains(backendRules, "Web/SEO") || strings.Contains(backendRules, "SDLC 1/7") {
		t.Errorf("did not expect Web/SEO or other SDLC phases in backend prompt, got: %s", backendRules)
	}
	if len(backendRules) > 400 {
		t.Errorf("expected compact phase-scoped prompt (<400 chars), got %d chars: %s", len(backendRules), backendRules)
	}

	// 2. Web Implementation task: loads Step 4 Implementation micro-prompt + compact 1-line Web/SEO Build overlay.
	webRules := BuildHarnessRulesBlock("Build a SaaS landing page with local SEO and Google Maps GBP schema", false)
	if !strings.Contains(webRules, "SDLC 4/7: IMPLEMENTATION") {
		t.Errorf("expected Step 4 IMPLEMENTATION in web build prompt, got: %s", webRules)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(webRules, "[Web/SEO Build]") || !strings.Contains(webRules, "llms.txt") || !strings.Contains(webRules, "[vendor claim]") {
		t.Errorf("expected compact [Web/SEO Build] overlay in web prompt, got: %s", webRules)
	}

	// 3. Planning task: loads ONLY Step 1 Planning micro-prompt.
	planRules := BuildHarnessRulesBlock("Define the project plan and scope charter", true)
	if !strings.Contains(planRules, "SDLC 1/7: PLANNING") {
		t.Errorf("expected Step 1 PLANNING micro-prompt, got: %s", planRules)
	}
}

func TestEvaluateStopGate(t *testing.T) {
	trace := []Step{
		{Name: "edit_block", Args: `{"path":"main.go"}`},
	}
	todos := []string{"- #1 [pending] Run unit tests"}
	gate := EvaluateStopGate(trace, todos)
	if !gate.HasPendingTodos || gate.PendingCount != 1 {
		t.Errorf("expected 1 pending todo, got %+v", gate)
	}
	if gate.RanVerification {
		t.Errorf("expected RanVerification=false when edit_block ran without run_shell test/vet")
	}
	if !strings.Contains(gate.Advisory, "pending todo") || !strings.Contains(gate.Advisory, "verification") {
		t.Errorf("unexpected advisory: %s", gate.Advisory)
	}

	traceVerified := []Step{
		{Name: "edit_block", Args: `{"path":"main.go"}`},
		{Name: "run_shell", Args: `{"command":"go test ./..."}`},
	}
	todosDone := []string{"- #1 [completed] Run unit tests"}
	gateOk := EvaluateStopGate(traceVerified, todosDone)
	if gateOk.HasPendingTodos || !gateOk.RanVerification || gateOk.Advisory != "" {
		t.Errorf("expected clean StopGateStatus, got %+v", gateOk)
	}
}


==============================================================================
FILE: internal/agent/smolmode.go
==============================================================================
package agent

import (
	"strings"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/cortex"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/llm"
)

// SmolPolicy controls whether SmolMode is auto-activated ("auto"), forced on ("on"),
// or forced off ("off"). Default is "auto".
const (
	SmolAuto = "auto"
	SmolOn   = "on"
	SmolOff  = "off"
)

var smolTokens = []string{
	"0.5b", "600m", "1b", "1.5b", "1.7b", "2b", "3b", "4b", "6.7b", "7b", "8b", "9b",
	"12b", "13b", "14b", "16b", "22b", "24b", "27b", "30b", "32b",
	"mini", "flash", "smol", "nano", "haiku", "small", "phi-", "gemma",
	"muse-glimmer", "d1-", "clef-flash",
}

var largeLocalTokens = []string{
	"70b", "72b", "110b", "120b", "123b", "235b", "405b", "671b",
}

// DetectSmolModel returns true when the active model is a small/local model (<=32B)
// or a fast/compact cloud tier (flash/mini/nano/haiku), triggering automatic
// smolcoder optimizations (lean 2-paragraph system prompt, aggressive 2-turn
// history placeholder pruning, and automatic /no_think on mechanical tool steps).
func DetectSmolModel(providerID, model string, local bool) bool {
	m := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(model))
	p := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(providerID))

	for _, tok := range smolTokens {
		if strings.Contains(m, tok) {
			return true
		}
	}
	if local || p == "ollama" || p == "lmstudio" || p == "llamacpp" {
		for _, big := range largeLocalTokens {
			if strings.Contains(m, big) {
				return false
			}
		}
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// smolSystemPrompt is the ultra-compact 2-paragraph system prompt (inspired by
// smolcoder.dev) designed specifically for 7B-32B local models and small context windows.
func smolSystemPrompt(memories []cortex.Neuron, schemas []llm.ToolSchema) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("You are Mímir (⚡SmolMode), a fast, precise coding agent with persistent memory. ")
	b.WriteString("Act directly using your tools: read files before editing, keep edit_block old_string snippets small (under 15 lines), and track multi-step tasks with the todo tool. Never use em dashes.\n\n")

	if len(schemas) > 0 {
		names := make([]string, len(schemas))
		for i, s := range schemas {
			names[i] = s.Name
		}
		b.WriteString("Available tools: " + strings.Join(names, ", ") + ". ")
		b.WriteString("Example tool usage: `read_file` with `{\"path\":\"main.go\"}`, `edit_block` with `{\"path\":\"main.go\",\"old_string\":\"old\",\"new_string\":\"new\"}`, `todo` with `{\"action\":\"add\",\"content\":\"step 1\"}`.")
	}

	if len(memories) > 0 {
		b.WriteString("\n\nRelevant memory:")
		for _, m := range memories {
			b.WriteString("\n- " + m.Content)
		}
	}

	b.WriteString("\n\nWhen asking multiple-choice questions, use:\n[choice]\nA) option\nB) option\n[/choice]")
	return b.String()
}

package agent

func TestDetectSmolModel(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		provider string
		model    string
		local    bool
		want     bool
	}{
		{"ollama", "qwen3:8b", true, true},
		{"lmstudio", "deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-14b", true, true},
		{"ollama", "llama3.3:70b", true, false},
		{"mimo", "mimo-v2-flash", false, true},
		{"openai", "gpt-4o-mini", false, true},
		{"mimo", "mimo-v2-pro", false, false},
		{"anthropic", "claude-3-7-sonnet", false, false},
	}

	for _, tc := range cases {
		got := DetectSmolModel(tc.provider, tc.model, tc.local)
		if got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("DetectSmolModel(%q, %q, local=%v) = %v, want %v",
				tc.provider, tc.model, tc.local, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestAgentAutoActivatesSmolMode(t *testing.T) {
	ag := New(Config{
		Model: "qwen3:8b",
		Local: true,

		t.Fatal("expected SmolMode() to auto-activate for local qwen3:8b")

	ag.SetSmolPolicy(SmolOff)

		t.Fatal("expected SmolMode() to be false when policy is SmolOff")
	}
	ag.SetSmolPolicy(SmolOn)
	if !ag.SmolMode() {
		t.Fatal("expected SmolMode() to be true when policy is SmolOn")

FILE: internal/agent/steer_test.go

package agent

import (
	"context"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/cortex"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/llm"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/tools"
)

// TestSteerQueuesArePerSession proves the queue is keyed by session: a steer
// queued for one session is invisible to every other session, a sessionless
// drain gets nothing, and a drain consumes the queue exactly once.
func TestSteerQueuesArePerSession(t *testing.T) {
	a := New(Config{Provider: &fakeProvider{}, Tools: tools.NewRegistry(), Cortex: cortex.NewMemoryStore(), Model: "m"})

	if !a.Steer("sess-a", "for a only") {
		t.Fatal("Steer for sess-a was rejected")
	}
	if got := a.drainSteer("sess-b"); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("drainSteer(sess-b) = %v, want empty (per-session isolation)", got)
	}
	if got := a.drainSteer(""); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("drainSteer(\"\") = %v, want empty (sessionless runs drain nothing)", got)
	}
	got := a.drainSteer("sess-a")
	if len(got) != 1 || got[0] != "for a only" {
		t.Fatalf("drainSteer(sess-a) = %v, want [for a only]", got)
	}
	if got := a.drainSteer("sess-a"); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("second drainSteer(sess-a) = %v, want empty (queue consumed)", got)
	}
}

// TestSteerReportsRejection proves Steer never silently drops: empty session
// IDs and empty messages are rejected, a full per-session queue rejects, and
// the queue accepts again after a drain. (Pre-fix, Steer returned nothing
// and a non-blocking channel send dropped overflow without a trace.)
func TestSteerReportsRejection(t *testing.T) {
	a := New(Config{Provider: &fakeProvider{}, Tools: tools.NewRegistry(), Cortex: cortex.NewMemoryStore(), Model: "m"})

	if a.Steer("", "no session") {
		t.Error("Steer with empty session ID reported success")
	}
	if a.Steer("sess", "") {
		t.Error("Steer with empty message reported success")
	}
	if a.Steer("sess", "   ") {
		t.Error("Steer with whitespace-only message reported success")
	}
	for i := 0; i < maxSteersPerSession; i++ {
		if !a.Steer("sess", "queued") {
			t.Fatalf("Steer %d of %d reported failure below the cap", i+1, maxSteersPerSession)
		}
	}
	if a.Steer("sess", "one too many") {
		t.Error("Steer beyond the per-session cap reported success")
	}
	// A different session has its own queue and is unaffected by the full one.
	if !a.Steer("other", "still fine") {
		t.Error("Steer for a different session was rejected by another session's full queue")
	}
	if got := a.drainSteer("sess"); len(got) != maxSteersPerSession {
		t.Fatalf("drainSteer(sess) returned %d messages, want %d", len(got), maxSteersPerSession)
	}
	if !a.Steer("sess", "after drain") {
		t.Error("Steer after drain reported failure")
	}
}

// steerLoopProvider is run-aware like the server probe: it returns one tool
// call when the request does not yet end with a tool result, then final text,
// and records every message across all runs.
type steerLoopProvider struct {
	seen [][]llm.Message
}

func (p *steerLoopProvider) ID() string { return "steerloop" }
func (p *steerLoopProvider) Generate(_ context.Context, req llm.GenerateRequest) (llm.GenerateResponse, error) {
	p.seen = append(p.seen, req.Messages)
	if n := len(req.Messages); n == 0 || req.Messages[n-1].Role != "tool" {
		return llm.GenerateResponse{
			ToolCalls:    []llm.ToolCall{{ID: "s1", Name: "todo", Arguments: "{}"}},
			FinishReason: "tool_calls",
		}, nil
	}
	return llm.GenerateResponse{Content: "done", FinishReason: "stop"}, nil
}
func (p *steerLoopProvider) Stream(context.Context, llm.GenerateRequest) (<-chan llm.StreamEvent, error) {
	return nil, nil
}
func (p *steerLoopProvider) sawSteering(msg string) bool {
	for _, call := range p.seen {
		for _, m := range call {
			if strings.Contains(m.Content, "[User steering instruction]: "+msg) {
				return true
			}
		}
	}
	return false
}

// TestRunDeliversSteerOnlyToBoundSession proves the end-to-end binding at
// the agent level: a steer queued for session X is delivered only into a run
// whose context carries session X (WithSessionID). A run bound to another
// session and a sessionless run receive nothing, and delivery happens once.
func TestRunDeliversSteerOnlyToBoundSession(t *testing.T) {
	prov := &steerLoopProvider{}
	a := New(Config{
		Provider: prov, Tools: tools.NewRegistry(), Cortex: cortex.NewMemoryStore(), Model: "m",
		ApprovalFunc: func(string, string) bool { return true },
	})
	if !a.Steer("sess-x", "bound steer") {
		t.Fatal("Steer for sess-x was rejected")
	}
	run := func(ctx context.Context) {
		t.Helper()
		if _, err := a.Run(ctx, "go", nil); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("Run: %v", err)
		}
	}

	run(WithSessionID(context.Background(), "sess-y"))
	if prov.sawSteering("bound steer") {
		t.Fatal("steer for sess-x leaked into a run bound to sess-y")
	}
	run(context.Background())
	if prov.sawSteering("bound steer") {
		t.Fatal("steer for sess-x leaked into a sessionless run")
	}
	run(WithSessionID(context.Background(), "sess-x"))
	if !prov.sawSteering("bound steer") {
		t.Fatal("steer for sess-x was not delivered into the sess-x run")
	}
}

FILE: internal/agent/stopgate_test.go

package agent

import (
	"context"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/cortex"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/llm"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/tools"
)

// scriptProvider replays a fixed script of Generate responses in order.
type scriptProvider struct {
	responses []llm.GenerateResponse
	calls     int
}

func (p *scriptProvider) ID() string { return "script" }
func (p *scriptProvider) Generate(context.Context, llm.GenerateRequest) (llm.GenerateResponse, error) {
	p.calls++
	if p.calls <= len(p.responses) {
		return p.responses[p.calls-1], nil
	}
	return llm.GenerateResponse{Content: "script exhausted", FinishReason: "stop"}, nil
}
func (p *scriptProvider) Stream(context.Context, llm.GenerateRequest) (<-chan llm.StreamEvent, error) {
	return nil, nil
}

func toolResp(name, args string) llm.GenerateResponse {
	return llm.GenerateResponse{
		ToolCalls:    []llm.ToolCall{{ID: "s1", Name: name, Arguments: args}},
		FinishReason: "tool_calls",
	}
}

func textResp(text string) llm.GenerateResponse {
	return llm.GenerateResponse{Content: text, FinishReason: "stop"}
}

// TestAutoVerifyForcesVerificationPass proves the F25 fix: with AutoVerify on,
// a turn that mutates a file and stops without verification is not finished;
// the loop continues, and once the model runs a verification command the turn
// completes without an advisory.
func TestAutoVerifyForcesVerificationPass(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	prov := &scriptProvider{responses: []llm.GenerateResponse{
		toolResp("write_file", `{"path":"out.txt","content":"hi"}`),
		textResp("done, trust me"),
		toolResp("bash", `{"command":"echo check"}`),
		textResp("verified and done"),
	}}
	a := New(Config{
		Provider: prov, Tools: tools.Default(dir),
		Cortex: cortex.NewMemoryStore(), Model: "m",
		Mode: ModeBypass, AutoVerify: true,
	})
	reply, _, err := a.RunTrace(context.Background(), "build it", nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("RunTrace: %v", err)
	}
	if prov.calls != 4 {
		t.Errorf("provider calls = %d, want 4 (the unverified stop must be forced to continue)", prov.calls)
	}
	if reply != "verified and done" {
		t.Errorf("reply = %q, want the post-verification reply with no advisory", reply)
	}
}

// TestAutoVerifyContinuationCap proves the forced continuations are capped at
// 2 per run: a model that never verifies still finishes, with the advisory
// attached, instead of looping forever.
func TestAutoVerifyContinuationCap(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	prov := &scriptProvider{responses: []llm.GenerateResponse{
		toolResp("write_file", `{"path":"out.txt","content":"hi"}`),
		textResp("done"),
		textResp("still done"),
		textResp("really done"),
	}}
	a := New(Config{
		Provider: prov, Tools: tools.Default(dir),
		Cortex: cortex.NewMemoryStore(), Model: "m",
		Mode: ModeBypass, AutoVerify: true,
	})
	reply, _, err := a.RunTrace(context.Background(), "build it", nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("RunTrace: %v", err)
	}
	// 1 tool turn + 1 stop + 2 forced continuations = 4 Generate calls.
	if prov.calls != 4 {
		t.Errorf("provider calls = %d, want 4 (cap of 2 forced continuations)", prov.calls)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(reply, "Harness OnStop Gate Advisory") {
		t.Errorf("reply = %q, want the advisory attached after the cap", reply)
	}
}

// TestAutoVerifyOffKeepsAdvisoryOnly proves the pre-F25 behavior is preserved
// when AutoVerify is disabled: the gate annotates and the turn ends.
func TestAutoVerifyOffKeepsAdvisoryOnly(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	prov := &scriptProvider{responses: []llm.GenerateResponse{
		toolResp("write_file", `{"path":"out.txt","content":"hi"}`),
		textResp("done"),
	}}
	a := New(Config{
		Provider: prov, Tools: tools.Default(dir),
		Cortex: cortex.NewMemoryStore(), Model: "m",
		Mode: ModeBypass, AutoVerify: false,
	})
	reply, _, err := a.RunTrace(context.Background(), "build it", nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("RunTrace: %v", err)
	}
	if prov.calls != 2 {
		t.Errorf("provider calls = %d, want 2 (no forced continuation when AutoVerify is off)", prov.calls)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(reply, "Harness OnStop Gate Advisory") {
		t.Errorf("reply = %q, want the advisory attached", reply)
	}
}

FILE: internal/agent/stream_test.go

package agent

import (
	"context"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/cortex"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/llm"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/tools"
)

// fakeStreamProvider streams: turn 1 issues a bash tool call, turn 2 streams the
// final answer in two deltas. It exercises RunStream's stream -> act -> stream loop.
type fakeStreamProvider struct {
	calls int
}

func (f *fakeStreamProvider) ID() string { return "fakestream" }
func (f *fakeStreamProvider) Generate(context.Context, llm.GenerateRequest) (llm.GenerateResponse, error) {
	return llm.GenerateResponse{}, nil
}
func (f *fakeStreamProvider) Stream(context.Context, llm.GenerateRequest) (<-chan llm.StreamEvent, error) {
	f.calls++
	out := make(chan llm.StreamEvent)
	go func() {
		defer close(out)
		if f.calls == 1 {
			out <- llm.StreamEvent{Done: true, ToolCalls: []llm.ToolCall{
				{ID: "c1", Name: "bash", Arguments: `{"command":"echo MIMIRX"}`},
			}}
			return
		}
		out <- llm.StreamEvent{Delta: "all "}
		out <- llm.StreamEvent{Delta: "done"}
		out <- llm.StreamEvent{Done: true}
	}()
	return out, nil
}

// TestRunStream proves the streaming turn end to end: a seeded memory is recalled,
// the model's tool call is executed and surfaced, the final answer streams token by
// token, the done event carries the full reply, and the exchange is persisted.
func TestRunStream(t *testing.T) {
	store := cortex.NewMemoryStore()
	if _, err := store.PutNeuron(context.Background(), cortex.Neuron{
		Kind: cortex.KindMemory, Content: "the codeword is MANGO77", Decay: 1,
	}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("seed: %v", err)
	}
	a := New(Config{
		Provider: &fakeStreamProvider{}, Tools: tools.Default(t.TempDir()),
		Cortex: store, Model: "m",
		// Edit mode now fails closed without an approver (F2/N1); this test
		// exercises the stream loop, so it approves tool calls explicitly.
		ApprovalFunc: func(string, string) bool { return true },
	})

	var events []Event
	if err := a.RunStream(context.Background(), "tell me about MANGO77 please", nil, func(e Event) {
		events = append(events, e)
	}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("RunStream: %v", err)
	}

	var (
		sawMemory, sawTool, sawDone bool
		tokens, doneReply           string
		toolStep                    *Step
	)
	for _, e := range events {
		switch e.Type {
		case EventMemory:
			if strings.Contains(e.Text, "MANGO77") {
				sawMemory = true
			}
		case EventToken:
			tokens += e.Text
		case EventTool:
			sawTool = true
			toolStep = e.Step
		case EventDone:
			sawDone = true
			doneReply = e.Reply
		case EventError:
			t.Fatalf("unexpected error event: %s", e.Err)
		}
	}
	if !sawMemory {
		t.Error("expected a recalled-memory event for MANGO77")
	}
	if !sawTool || toolStep == nil || toolStep.Name != "bash" || !strings.Contains(toolStep.Result, "MIMIRX") {
		t.Errorf("expected a bash tool event whose result contains MIMIRX, got %+v", toolStep)
	}
	if tokens != "all done" {
		t.Errorf("streamed tokens = %q, want %q", tokens, "all done")
	}
	if !sawDone || doneReply != "all done" {
		t.Errorf("done reply = %q, want %q", doneReply, "all done")
	}
}

FILE: internal/agent/toolloop_test.go

package agent

import (
	"context"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/cortex"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/llm"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/tools"
)

// fakeProvider is a deterministic llm.Provider: first call returns a tool call,
// the second returns final text. It records the messages it sees each call so the
// test can prove the tool result was fed back into the loop.
type fakeProvider struct {
	calls int
	seen  [][]llm.Message
}

func (f *fakeProvider) ID() string { return "fake" }

func (f *fakeProvider) Generate(_ context.Context, req llm.GenerateRequest) (llm.GenerateResponse, error) {
	f.seen = append(f.seen, req.Messages)
	f.calls++
	if f.calls == 1 {
		return llm.GenerateResponse{
			ToolCalls:    []llm.ToolCall{{ID: "c1", Name: "bash", Arguments: `{"command":"echo MIMIRX"}`}},
			FinishReason: "tool_calls",
		}, nil
	}
	return llm.GenerateResponse{Content: "all done", FinishReason: "stop"}, nil
}

func (f *fakeProvider) Stream(context.Context, llm.GenerateRequest) (<-chan llm.StreamEvent, error) {
	return nil, nil
}

// TestRunToolLoop proves the infer -> act -> feed-back cycle end to end with a real
// tool (bash) and a deterministic model: the model asks to run bash, the loop runs it,
// feeds the output back, and the model's final reply is returned.
func TestRunToolLoop(t *testing.T) {
	fp := &fakeProvider{}
	a := New(Config{
		Provider: fp, Tools: tools.Default(t.TempDir()),
		Cortex: cortex.NewMemoryStore(), Model: "m",
		// Edit mode now fails closed without an approver (F2/N1); this test
		// exercises the tool loop, so it approves tool calls explicitly.
		ApprovalFunc: func(string, string) bool { return true },
	})

	reply, trace, err := a.RunTrace(context.Background(), "do it", nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("RunTrace: %v", err)
	}
	if reply != "all done" {
		t.Errorf("reply = %q, want %q", reply, "all done")
	}
	if len(trace) != 1 || trace[0].Name != "bash" {
		t.Fatalf("trace = %+v", trace)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(trace[0].Result, "MIMIRX") {
		t.Errorf("bash result = %q, want it to contain MIMIRX", trace[0].Result)
	}
	if trace[0].Err != "" {
		t.Errorf("unexpected tool error: %q", trace[0].Err)
	}
	// The second model call must include the tool result message.
	if len(fp.seen) < 2 {
		t.Fatalf("expected 2 model calls, got %d", len(fp.seen))
	}
	found := false
	for _, m := range fp.seen[1] {
		if m.Role == "tool" && strings.Contains(m.Content, "MIMIRX") {
			found = true
		}
	}
	if !found {
		t.Errorf("tool result was not fed back to the model: %+v", fp.seen[1])
	}
}

// TestRunUnknownTool proves an unknown tool call returns an error result to the
// model instead of crashing the loop.
func TestRunUnknownTool(t *testing.T) {
	fp := &fakeProvider{}
	fp.calls = 0
	// Override: make the first call ask for a tool that isn't registered.
	a := New(Config{
		Provider: &oneCallProvider{call: llm.ToolCall{ID: "x", Name: "nope", Arguments: `{}`}},
		Tools:    tools.Default(t.TempDir()), Cortex: cortex.NewMemoryStore(), Model: "m",
	})
	reply, trace, err := a.RunTrace(context.Background(), "go", nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("RunTrace: %v", err)
	}
	if reply != "final" {
		t.Errorf("reply = %q", reply)
	}
	if len(trace) != 1 || trace[0].Err == "" {
		t.Errorf("expected an error step for unknown tool, got %+v", trace)
	}
	_ = fp
}

// oneCallProvider returns one tool call then final text.
type oneCallProvider struct {
	call  llm.ToolCall
	calls int
}

func (p *oneCallProvider) ID() string { return "one" }
func (p *oneCallProvider) Generate(context.Context, llm.GenerateRequest) (llm.GenerateResponse, error) {
	p.calls++
	if p.calls == 1 {
		return llm.GenerateResponse{ToolCalls: []llm.ToolCall{p.call}, FinishReason: "tool_calls"}, nil
	}
	return llm.GenerateResponse{Content: "final", FinishReason: "stop"}, nil
}
func (p *oneCallProvider) Stream(context.Context, llm.GenerateRequest) (<-chan llm.StreamEvent, error) {
	return nil, nil
}

package config

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
)

// Config is the top-level mimir.json configuration.
type Config struct {
	Port      int                  `json:"port"`
	LogLevel  string               `json:"log_level"`
	Home      string               `json:"home"`
	Telemetry bool                 `json:"telemetry"`
	Providers map[string]Provider  `json:"providers"`
	MCP       map[string]MCPServer `json:"mcp"`
}

// Provider configures one model backend.
type Provider struct {
	Name    string `json:"name"`
	BaseURL string `json:"base_url"`
	APIKey  string `json:"api_key"` // supports {env:VAR} / {file:path}
	Dialect string `json:"dialect"` // openai_compat | anthropic
}

// MCPServer configures an external MCP tool server.
type MCPServer struct {
	Command []string          `json:"command"`
	URL     string            `json:"url"`
	Env     map[string]string `json:"env"`
	Enabled bool              `json:"enabled"`
}

// Default returns a config with sane defaults.
func Default() *Config {
	home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
	return &Config{
		Port:      8420,
		LogLevel:  "info",
		Home:      filepath.Join(home, ".mimir"),
		Telemetry: true, // on by default; opt-out in privacy settings (F32)
		Providers: map[string]Provider{},
		MCP:       map[string]MCPServer{},
	}
}

// Load reads mimir.json (or the opencode-compatible fallback) and applies defaults.
func Load(path string) (*Config, error) {
	cfg := Default()
	if path == "" {
		path = "mimir.json"
		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err != nil {
			path = "opencode.json" // import opencode-style config
		}
	}
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
			return cfg, nil // no config file: run with defaults
		}
		return nil, err
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, cfg); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	cfg.interpolate()
	return cfg, nil
}

func (c *Config) interpolate() {
	for id, p := range c.Providers {
		p.APIKey = Interpolate(p.APIKey)
		c.Providers[id] = p
	}
}

// Interpolate replaces {env:VAR} and {file:path} tokens in s.
func Interpolate(s string) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	for i := 0; i < len(s); {
		if strings.HasPrefix(s[i:], "{env:") {
			end := strings.Index(s[i:], "}")
			if end < 0 {
				b.WriteString(s[i:])
				break
			}
			b.WriteString(os.Getenv(s[i+5 : i+end]))
			i += end + 1
			continue
		}
		if strings.HasPrefix(s[i:], "{file:") {
			end := strings.Index(s[i:], "}")
			if end < 0 {
				b.WriteString(s[i:])
				break
			}
			if data, err := os.ReadFile(s[i+6 : i+end]); err == nil {
				b.WriteString(strings.TrimSpace(string(data)))
			}
			i += end + 1
			continue
		}
		b.WriteByte(s[i])
		i++
	}
	return b.String()
}

package config

import (
	"os"
	"testing"
)

func TestInterpolateEnv(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv("MIMIR_TEST_KEY", "secret123")
	if got, want := Interpolate("key={env:MIMIR_TEST_KEY}"), "key=secret123"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("Interpolate env = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}

func TestInterpolateMissingEnvIsEmpty(t *testing.T) {
	if got, want := Interpolate("key={env:MIMIR_DOES_NOT_EXIST}"), "key="; got != want {
		t.Errorf("Interpolate missing env = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}

func TestInterpolateFile(t *testing.T) {
	f, err := os.CreateTemp(t.TempDir(), "secret")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := f.WriteString("file-secret\n"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := f.Close(); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := Interpolate("{file:"+f.Name()+"}"), "file-secret"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("Interpolate file = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}

func TestDefault(t *testing.T) {
	cfg := Default()
	if cfg.Port != 8420 {
		t.Errorf("default port = %d, want 8420", cfg.Port)
	}
	if !cfg.Telemetry {
		t.Error("telemetry should default to true (opt-out)")
	}
}

package config

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

// DiscoveredModel represents a model found via local port probing or cloud env vars.
type DiscoveredModel struct {
	ProviderID string `json:"provider_id"`
	BaseURL    string `json:"base_url"`
	APIKey     string `json:"api_key,omitempty"`
	Model      string `json:"model"`
	Local      bool   `json:"local"`
}

// AutoDiscoverProvider resolves a provider in priority order (inspired by smolcoder):
// 1. Explicit MIMIR_BASE_URL environment variable.
// 2. Cloud API keys (MIMO_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY).
// 3. Local Ollama (:11434) and LM Studio (:1234) port probing.
func AutoDiscoverProvider(ctx context.Context) (EnvProvider, bool) {
	if ep, ok := ProviderFromEnv(); ok {
		return ep, true
	}

	// Check Mímir Well Subscription Gateway (OpenCode Zen-style unified subscription)
	if key := os.Getenv("MIMIR_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY"); key != "" {
		return EnvProvider{
			ID:      "mimir-well",
			BaseURL: envOr("MIMIR_WELL_URL", "https://api.mimirmind.com/v1"),
			APIKey:  key,
			Model:   envOr("MIMIR_MODEL", "muse-wonder-1.0"),
		}, true
	}

	// Check Meta Model API (Muse Wonder / Muse Spark / Muse Glimmer)
	if key := firstEnv("META_API_KEY", "MUSE_API_KEY"); key != "" {
		return EnvProvider{
			ID:      "meta",
			BaseURL: envOr("META_BASE_URL", "https://api.meta.ai/v1"),
			APIKey:  key,
			Model:   firstEnvDefault("muse-wonder-1.0", "MIMIR_MODEL", "META_MODEL"),
		}, true
	}

	// Check Xiaomi MiMo / OpenRouter / OpenAI / DeepSeek / Gemini / xAI / Groq keys
	if key := os.Getenv("MIMO_API_KEY"); key != "" {
		return EnvProvider{
			ID:      "mimo",
			BaseURL: envOr("MIMO_BASE_URL", "https://api.xiaomimimo.com/v1"),
			APIKey:  key,
			Model:   envOr("MIMIR_MODEL", "mimo-v2-pro"),
		}, true
	}
	if key := os.Getenv("OPENROUTER_API_KEY"); key != "" {
		return EnvProvider{
			ID:      "openrouter",
			BaseURL: "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1",
			APIKey:  key,
			Model:   envOr("MIMIR_MODEL", "xiaomi/mimo-v2-pro"),
		}, true
	}
	if key := os.Getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"); key != "" {
		return EnvProvider{
			ID:      "openai",
			BaseURL: "https://api.openai.com/v1",
			APIKey:  key,
			Model:   envOr("MIMIR_MODEL", "gpt-4o-mini"),
		}, true
	}
	if key := os.Getenv("DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"); key != "" {
		return EnvProvider{
			ID:      "deepseek",
			BaseURL: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1",
			APIKey:  key,
			Model:   envOr("MIMIR_MODEL", "deepseek-chat"),
		}, true
	}
	if key := os.Getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"); key != "" {
		return EnvProvider{
			ID:      "gemini",
			BaseURL: "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai",
			APIKey:  key,
			Model:   envOr("MIMIR_MODEL", "gemini-2.5-flash"),
		}, true
	}
	if key := os.Getenv("XAI_API_KEY"); key != "" {
		return EnvProvider{
			ID:      "xai",
			BaseURL: "https://api.x.ai/v1",
			APIKey:  key,
			Model:   envOr("MIMIR_MODEL", "grok-4-fast"),
		}, true
	}
	if key := os.Getenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"); key != "" {
		return EnvProvider{
			ID:      "anthropic",
			BaseURL: envOr("ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL", "https://api.anthropic.com/v1"),
			APIKey:  key,
			Model:   envOr("MIMIR_MODEL", "claude-sonnet-4-6"),
		}, true
	}
	if key := os.Getenv("GROQ_API_KEY"); key != "" {
		return EnvProvider{
			ID:      "groq",
			BaseURL: "https://api.groq.com/openai/v1",
			APIKey:  key,
			Model:   envOr("MIMIR_MODEL", "llama-3.3-70b-versatile"),
		}, true
	}

	// Probe local Ollama and LM Studio servers
	models := DiscoverLocalModels(ctx, 350*time.Millisecond)
	if len(models) > 0 {
		m := models[0]
		if pref := os.Getenv("MIMIR_MODEL"); pref != "" {
			for _, cand := range models {
				if strings.EqualFold(cand.Model, pref) {
					m = cand
					break
				}
			}
		}
		return EnvProvider{
			ID:      m.ProviderID,
			BaseURL: m.BaseURL,
			APIKey:  m.APIKey,
			Model:   m.Model,
		}, true
	}

	return EnvProvider{}, false
}

// DiscoverLocalModels probes local Ollama (127.0.0.1:11434) and LM Studio (127.0.0.1:1234)
// and returns all available chat/coding models (filtering out pure embedding models).
func DiscoverLocalModels(ctx context.Context, timeout time.Duration) []DiscoveredModel {
	if timeout <= 0 {
		timeout = 350 * time.Millisecond
	}
	ollamaURL := envOr("MIMIR_OLLAMA_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:11434")
	lmStudioURL := envOr("MIMIR_LMSTUDIO_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:1234")

	var out []DiscoveredModel
	out = append(out, probeOllama(ctx, ollamaURL, timeout)...)
	out = append(out, probeOpenAIModels(ctx, "lmstudio", lmStudioURL, timeout)...)
	return out
}

func probeOllama(ctx context.Context, base string, timeout time.Duration) []DiscoveredModel {
	base = strings.TrimRight(base, "/")
	cctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
	defer cancel()

	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(cctx, http.MethodGet, base+"/api/tags", nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		return nil
	}

	var payload struct {
		Models []struct {
			Name string `json:"name"`
		} `json:"models"`
	}
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&payload); err != nil {
		return nil
	}

	var out []DiscoveredModel
	for _, m := range payload.Models {
		if isEmbeddingModel(m.Name) {
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, DiscoveredModel{
			ProviderID: "ollama",
			BaseURL:    base + "/v1",
			APIKey:     "ollama",
			Model:      m.Name,
			Local:      true,
		})
	}
	return out
}

func probeOpenAIModels(ctx context.Context, providerID, base string, timeout time.Duration) []DiscoveredModel {
	base = strings.TrimRight(base, "/")
	cctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
	defer cancel()

	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(cctx, http.MethodGet, base+"/v1/models", nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		return nil
	}

	var payload struct {
		Data []struct {
			ID string `json:"id"`
		} `json:"data"`
	}
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&payload); err != nil {
		return nil
	}

	var out []DiscoveredModel
	for _, m := range payload.Data {
		if isEmbeddingModel(m.ID) {
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, DiscoveredModel{
			ProviderID: providerID,
			BaseURL:    base + "/v1",
			APIKey:     providerID,
			Model:      m.ID,
			Local:      true,
		})
	}
	return out
}

func isEmbeddingModel(name string) bool {
	lower := strings.ToLower(name)
	return strings.Contains(lower, "embed") || strings.Contains(lower, "bge-")
}

// MetaModelSpec describes a model from the Meta Model API (https://dev.meta.ai/docs/overview).
type MetaModelSpec struct {

func firstEnv(keys ...string) string {
	for _, k := range keys {
		if v := os.Getenv(k); v != "" {
			return v
		}
	}
	return ""
}

func firstEnvDefault(def string, keys ...string) string {
	if v := firstEnv(keys...); v != "" {
		return v
	}
	return def
}

import (

func TestProbeOllamaFiltersEmbeddings(t *testing.T) {
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		if r.URL.Path != "/api/tags" {
			http.NotFound(w, r)
			return
		}
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"models":[{"name":"nomic-embed-text:latest"},{"name":"qwen3:8b"},{"name":"deepseek-coder:6.7b"}]}`))
	}))
	defer srv.Close()

	models := probeOllama(context.Background(), srv.URL, time.Second)
	if len(models) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("got %d models, want 2: %+v", len(models), models)
	}
	if models[0].Model != "qwen3:8b" || !models[0].Local || models[0].ProviderID != "ollama" {
		t.Errorf("unexpected first model: %+v", models[0])
	}
}

func TestMetaModelAPIDiscovery(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv("MIMIR_BASE_URL", "")
	t.Setenv("META_API_KEY", "meta-test-key")
	t.Setenv("MIMIR_MODEL", "")
	t.Setenv("META_MODEL", "")

	ep, ok := AutoDiscoverProvider(context.Background())
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("expected AutoDiscoverProvider to succeed with META_API_KEY")
	}
	if ep.ID != "meta" || ep.BaseURL != "https://api.meta.ai/v1" || ep.Model != "muse-wonder-1.0" {
		t.Errorf("unexpected Meta provider: %+v", ep)
	}

	cat := MetaMuseCatalog()
	if len(cat) < 7 {
		t.Errorf("expected at least 7 Meta Muse models in catalog, got %d", len(cat))
	}
}

package config

import "os"

// EnvProvider holds provider settings read from the environment, so Mímir can run
// a turn with no config file - just MIMIR_BASE_URL (+ key + model).
type EnvProvider struct {
	ID      string
	BaseURL string
	APIKey  string
	Model   string
}

// ProviderFromEnv returns provider settings from the environment. ok is false when
// MIMIR_BASE_URL is unset (no provider configured).
func ProviderFromEnv() (EnvProvider, bool) {
	base := os.Getenv("MIMIR_BASE_URL")
	if base == "" {
		return EnvProvider{}, false
	}
	return EnvProvider{
		ID:      envOr("MIMIR_PROVIDER_ID", "openai-compatible"),
		BaseURL: base,
		APIKey:  os.Getenv("MIMIR_API_KEY"),
		Model:   os.Getenv("MIMIR_MODEL"),
	}, true
}

func envOr(key, def string) string {
	if v := os.Getenv(key); v != "" {
		return v
	}
	return def
}

package cortex

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"crypto/tls"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"math/big"
	"net"
	"net/smtp"
	"os"
	"sync"
	"time"
)

type User struct {
	ID        string    `json:"id"`
	Email     string    `json:"email"`
	CreatedAt time.Time `json:"created_at"`
}

type AuthToken struct {
	ID        string    `json:"id"`
	UserID    string    `json:"user_id"`
	Token     string    `json:"token"`
	CreatedAt time.Time `json:"created_at"`
	ExpiresAt time.Time `json:"expires_at"`
}

type OTP struct {
	ID        string    `json:"id"`
	Email     string    `json:"email"`
	Code      string    `json:"code"`
	CreatedAt time.Time `json:"created_at"`
	ExpiresAt time.Time `json:"expires_at"`
	Used      bool      `json:"used"`
}

type rateLimitEntry struct {
	sendCount   int
	lastSend    time.Time
	verifyFails int
	lockedUntil time.Time
}

type AuthStore struct {
	cli        *surrealClient
	ns         string
	db         string
	rateLimits map[string]*rateLimitEntry
	mu         sync.Mutex
}

func NewAuthStore(cli *surrealClient) *AuthStore {
	return &AuthStore{
		cli:        cli,
		ns:         "mimir",
		db:         "mimir",
		rateLimits: make(map[string]*rateLimitEntry),
	}
}

func (a *AuthStore) Exec(ctx context.Context, sql string) error {
	results, err := a.cli.exec(ctx, a.ns, a.db, sql)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	for _, r := range results {
		if r.Status == "ERR" {
			return fmt.Errorf("surreal: %s", string(r.Result))
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func (a *AuthStore) Query(ctx context.Context, sql string) ([]map[string]any, error) {
	results, err := a.cli.exec(ctx, a.ns, a.db, sql)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var rows []map[string]any
	for _, r := range results {
		if r.Status == "ERR" {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("surreal: %s", string(r.Result))
		}
		var arr []map[string]any
		if err := json.Unmarshal(r.Result, &arr); err != nil {
			continue
		}
		rows = append(rows, arr...)
	}
	return rows, nil
}

func (a *AuthStore) EnsureAuthTables(ctx context.Context) error {
	// Remove legacy fields from earlier password-based schema
	_ = a.Exec(ctx, `REMOVE FIELD password_hash ON user`)
	_ = a.Exec(ctx, `REMOVE FIELD password ON user`)
	stmts := []string{
		`DEFINE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user SCHEMAFULL`,
		`DEFINE FIELD IF NOT EXISTS email ON user TYPE string`,
		`DEFINE FIELD IF NOT EXISTS created_at ON user TYPE datetime`,
		`DEFINE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS user_email ON user FIELDS email UNIQUE`,
		`DEFINE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS auth_token SCHEMAFULL`,
		`DEFINE FIELD IF NOT EXISTS user_id ON auth_token TYPE record<user>`,
		`DEFINE FIELD IF NOT EXISTS token ON auth_token TYPE string`,
		`DEFINE FIELD IF NOT EXISTS created_at ON auth_token TYPE datetime`,
		`DEFINE FIELD IF NOT EXISTS expires_at ON auth_token TYPE datetime`,
		`DEFINE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS auth_token_value ON auth_token FIELDS token UNIQUE`,
		`DEFINE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS otp SCHEMAFULL`,
		`DEFINE FIELD IF NOT EXISTS email ON otp TYPE string`,
		`DEFINE FIELD IF NOT EXISTS code ON otp TYPE string`,
		`DEFINE FIELD IF NOT EXISTS created_at ON otp TYPE datetime`,
		`DEFINE FIELD IF NOT EXISTS expires_at ON otp TYPE datetime`,
		`DEFINE FIELD IF NOT EXISTS used ON otp TYPE bool`,
	}
	for _, s := range stmts {
		if err := a.Exec(ctx, s); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("auth schema: %s: %w", s[:50], err)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// SendOTP generates a 6-digit code, stores it in SurrealDB, and emails it.
func (a *AuthStore) SendOTP(ctx context.Context, email string) error {
	now := time.Now().UTC()

	// Rate limit check: maximum 3 requests within 2 minutes; lockout if triggered
	a.mu.Lock()
	entry, ok := a.rateLimits[email]
	if !ok {
		entry = &rateLimitEntry{}
		a.rateLimits[email] = entry
	}
	if entry.lockedUntil.After(now) {
		a.mu.Unlock()
		return fmt.Errorf("too many attempts: account locked until %s", entry.lockedUntil.Format("15:04:05"))
	}
	if now.Sub(entry.lastSend) < 2*time.Minute {
		if entry.sendCount >= 3 {
			entry.lockedUntil = now.Add(15 * time.Minute)
			a.mu.Unlock()
			return fmt.Errorf("rate limit exceeded: too many login codes requested, please wait 15 minutes")
		}
		entry.sendCount++
	} else {
		entry.sendCount = 1
		entry.verifyFails = 0
	}
	entry.lastSend = now
	a.mu.Unlock()

	// Invalidate any existing unused OTPs for this email
	_ = a.Exec(ctx, fmt.Sprintf(
		`UPDATE otp SET used = true WHERE email = %s AND used = false`,
		escapeStringForSurreal(email),
	))

	code := generateOTPCode()
	otpID := "o" + now.Format("20060102150405") + fmt.Sprintf("%09d", now.Nanosecond())
	q := fmt.Sprintf(
		`CREATE otp:%s SET email = %s, code = %s, created_at = time::now(), expires_at = time::now() + 5m, used = false`,
		otpID, escapeStringForSurreal(email), escapeStringForSurreal(code),
	)
	if err := a.Exec(ctx, q); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("create otp: %w", err)
	}

	// Send email (best-effort, log failure)
	if err := sendOTPEmail(email, code); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "auth: send OTP email to %s: %v\n", email, err)
	} else {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "auth: OTP sent to %s\n", email)
	}
	return nil
}

// VerifyOTP validates a code and returns an auth token (creates user on first login).
func (a *AuthStore) VerifyOTP(ctx context.Context, email, code string) (*User, *AuthToken, error) {
	now := time.Now().UTC()

	a.mu.Lock()
	entry, ok := a.rateLimits[email]
	if !ok {
		entry = &rateLimitEntry{}
		a.rateLimits[email] = entry
	}
	if entry.lockedUntil.After(now) {
		a.mu.Unlock()
		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("account temporarily locked due to too many failed attempts, please retry later")
	}
	a.mu.Unlock()

	rows, err := a.Query(ctx, fmt.Sprintf(
		`SELECT * FROM otp WHERE email = %s AND code = %s AND used = false AND expires_at > time::now() ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1`,
		escapeStringForSurreal(email), escapeStringForSurreal(code),
	))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("query otp: %w", err)
	}
	if len(rows) == 0 {
		a.mu.Lock()
		entry.verifyFails++
		if entry.verifyFails >= 5 {
			entry.lockedUntil = now.Add(15 * time.Minute)
		}
		a.mu.Unlock()
		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid or expired code")
	}

	b, _ := json.Marshal(rows[0])
	var raw struct {
		ID string `json:"id"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &raw); err != nil {
		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("decode otp row: %w", err)
	}
	otpID := StripRecordID(raw.ID)

	// Mark OTP as used
	if err := a.Exec(ctx, fmt.Sprintf(`UPDATE otp:%s SET used = true`, otpID)); err != nil {
		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("mark otp used: %w", err)
	}

	// Reset failure count on success
	a.mu.Lock()
	entry.verifyFails = 0
	a.mu.Unlock()

	// Find or create user
	user, err := a.findOrCreateUser(ctx, email)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, nil, err
	}

	tok, err := a.createToken(ctx, user.ID)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, nil, err
	}
	return user, tok, nil
}

func (a *AuthStore) findOrCreateUser(ctx context.Context, email string) (*User, error) {
	rows, err := a.Query(ctx, fmt.Sprintf(
		`SELECT * FROM user WHERE email = %s`, escapeStringForSurreal(email),
	))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if len(rows) > 0 {
		b, _ := json.Marshal(rows[0])
		var raw struct {
			ID        string `json:"id"`
			Email     string `json:"email"`
			CreatedAt string `json:"created_at"`
		}
		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &raw); err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode user row: %w", err)
		}
		return &User{
			ID:        StripRecordID(raw.ID),
			Email:     raw.Email,
			CreatedAt: parseTime(raw.CreatedAt),
		}, nil
	}

	now := time.Now().UTC()
	userID := "u" + now.Format("20060102150405") + fmt.Sprintf("%09d", now.Nanosecond())
	q := fmt.Sprintf(
		`CREATE user:%s SET email = %s, created_at = time::now()`,
		userID, escapeStringForSurreal(email),
	)
	if err := a.Exec(ctx, q); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("create user: %w", err)
	}
	return &User{ID: userID, Email: email, CreatedAt: now}, nil
}

// SeedAdmin ensures the super admin account exists.
func (a *AuthStore) SeedAdmin(ctx context.Context, email string) error {
	rows, err := a.Query(ctx, fmt.Sprintf(
		`SELECT * FROM user WHERE email = %s`, escapeStringForSurreal(email),
	))
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if len(rows) > 0 {
		return nil // already exists
	}
	now := time.Now().UTC()
	q := fmt.Sprintf(
		`CREATE user:%s SET email = %s, created_at = time::now()`,
		"u"+now.Format("20060102150405")+fmt.Sprintf("%09d", now.Nanosecond()),
		escapeStringForSurreal(email),
	)
	return a.Exec(ctx, q)
}

func hashToken(token string) string {
	h := sha256.Sum256([]byte(token))
	return hex.EncodeToString(h[:])
}

func (a *AuthStore) ValidateToken(ctx context.Context, token string) (string, error) {
	// Look up by token hash only (F17: prevent plaintext bearer tokens at rest).
	// Legacy tokens stored in plaintext before hashing was introduced are
	// intentionally no longer accepted: their owners must sign in again to
	// receive a hashed token.
	tokenHash := hashToken(token)
	rows, err := a.Query(ctx, fmt.Sprintf(
		`SELECT * FROM auth_token WHERE token = %s AND expires_at > time::now()`,
		escapeStringForSurreal(tokenHash),
	))
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("query token: %w", err)
	}
	if len(rows) == 0 {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid or expired token")
	}
	b, _ := json.Marshal(rows[0])
	var raw struct {
		ID     string `json:"id"`
		UserID string `json:"user_id"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &raw); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("decode token row: %w", err)
	}
	return StripRecordID(raw.UserID), nil
}

func (a *AuthStore) createToken(ctx context.Context, userID string) (*AuthToken, error) {
	now := time.Now().UTC()
	tokID := "t" + now.Format("20060102150405") + fmt.Sprintf("%09d", now.Nanosecond())
	token := generateToken()
	tokenHash := hashToken(token)
	q := fmt.Sprintf(
		`CREATE auth_token:%s SET token = %s, user_id = user:%s, created_at = time::now(), expires_at = time::now() + 30d`,
		tokID, escapeStringForSurreal(tokenHash), userID,
	)
	if err := a.Exec(ctx, q); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("create token: %w", err)
	}
	// Return the plaintext token to the user for HTTP Authorization Bearer headers
	return &AuthToken{ID: tokID, UserID: userID, Token: token, CreatedAt: now, ExpiresAt: now.Add(30 * 24 * time.Hour)}, nil
}

func generateToken() string {
	b := make([]byte, 32)
	rand.Read(b)
	h := sha256.Sum256(b)
	return hex.EncodeToString(h[:])
}

func generateOTPCode() string {
	n, _ := rand.Int(rand.Reader, big.NewInt(1000000))
	return fmt.Sprintf("%06d", n.Int64())
}

func sendOTPEmail(to, code string) error {
	host := os.Getenv("MIMIR_SMTP_HOST")
	if host == "" {
		host = "smtp.titan.email"
	}
	port := os.Getenv("MIMIR_SMTP_PORT")
	if port == "" {
		port = "465"
	}
	user := os.Getenv("MIMIR_SMTP_USER")
	if user == "" {
		user = "mimir@itak.live"
	}
	pass := os.Getenv("MIMIR_SMTP_PASS")
	if pass == "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("MIMIR_SMTP_PASS environment variable is unset: refusing to send OTP email without configured credentials")
	}
	fromName := os.Getenv("MIMIR_SMTP_FROM_NAME")
	if fromName == "" {
		fromName = "Mímir"
	}
	fromAddr := os.Getenv("MIMIR_SMTP_FROM")
	if fromAddr == "" {
		fromAddr = user
	}

	msg := fmt.Sprintf("From: %s <%s>\r\nTo: %s\r\nSubject: Your Mímir login code\r\n\r\nYour Mímir login code is: %s\r\n\r\nThis code expires in 5 minutes.\r\n", fromName, fromAddr, to, code)

	addr := net.JoinHostPort(host, port)
	tc, err := tls.Dial("tcp", addr, &tls.Config{ServerName: host})
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("tls dial: %w", err)
	}
	defer tc.Close()

	c, err := smtp.NewClient(tc, host)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("smtp client: %w", err)
	}
	defer c.Quit()

	auth := smtp.PlainAuth("", user, pass, host)
	if err := c.Auth(auth); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("auth: %w", err)
	}
	if err := c.Mail(fromAddr); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("mail from: %w", err)
	}
	if err := c.Rcpt(to); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("rcpt: %w", err)
	}
	w, err := c.Data()
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("data: %w", err)
	}
	_, err = w.Write([]byte(msg))
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("write: %w", err)
	}
	return w.Close()
}

func parseTime(s string) time.Time {
	t, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, s)
	return t
}


==============================================================================
FILE: internal/cortex/auth_test.go

package cortex

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"regexp"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// fakeTokenDB emulates the SurrealDB /sql endpoint for auth_token statements.
// It models a table holding exactly one stored token value: a SELECT matches
// only when one of the queried token values equals the stored value, like a
// real equality lookup against the stored column.
type fakeTokenDB struct {
	stored     string   // the token column value present in the table
	createSQL  []string // captured CREATE statements
	tokenQuery []string // token values seen in SELECT token = '...' clauses

	// numericUserID makes the matched row carry a JSON number in user_id
	// instead of a string, so decoding the row into the auth structs fails.
	numericUserID bool
}

var tokenEqRe = regexp.MustCompile(`token = '([^']*)'`)

func (f *fakeTokenDB) handler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	body, _ := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
	sql := string(body)
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	switch {
	case strings.Contains(sql, "CREATE auth_token"):
		f.createSQL = append(f.createSQL, sql)
		_, _ = fmt.Fprint(w, `[{"result":[],"status":"OK"}]`)
	case strings.Contains(sql, "SELECT * FROM auth_token"):
		var rows []map[string]any
		for _, m := range tokenEqRe.FindAllStringSubmatch(sql, -1) {
			f.tokenQuery = append(f.tokenQuery, m[1])
			if m[1] == f.stored {
				row := map[string]any{
					"id":      "auth_token:t1",
					"user_id": "user:u42",
					"token":   f.stored,
				}
				if f.numericUserID {
					row["user_id"] = 12345
				}
				rows = []map[string]any{row}
			}
		}
		if rows == nil {
			rows = []map[string]any{}
		}
		out, _ := json.Marshal([]map[string]any{{"result": rows, "status": "OK"}})
		_, _ = w.Write(out)
	default:
		_, _ = fmt.Fprint(w, `[{"result":[],"status":"OK"}]`)
	}
}

func newFakeAuthStore(t *testing.T, db *fakeTokenDB) *AuthStore {
	t.Helper()
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(db.handler))
	t.Cleanup(srv.Close)
	return NewAuthStore(&surrealClient{addr: srv.URL, auth: "Basic dGVzdDp0ZXN0"})
}

// A legacy row storing the bearer token in plaintext must no longer validate
// (F17 sunset): ValidateToken looks up the token hash only.
func TestValidateTokenRejectsPlaintextStoredToken(t *testing.T) {
	plaintext := generateToken()
	db := &fakeTokenDB{stored: plaintext}
	a := newFakeAuthStore(t, db)

	if _, err := a.ValidateToken(context.Background(), plaintext); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("plaintext-stored token validated; the plaintext fallback is still active")
	}
	for _, q := range db.tokenQuery {
		if q == plaintext {
			t.Fatal("ValidateToken queried the database with the plaintext token")
		}
	}
}

// A token stored as its SHA-256 hash (what createToken writes) must validate.
func TestValidateTokenAcceptsHashedStoredToken(t *testing.T) {
	plaintext := generateToken()
	db := &fakeTokenDB{stored: hashToken(plaintext)}
	a := newFakeAuthStore(t, db)

	userID, err := a.ValidateToken(context.Background(), plaintext)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("hashed token rejected: %v", err)
	}
	if userID != "u42" {
		t.Fatalf("userID = %q, want u42", userID)
	}
}

// A stored token row whose fields do not decode (here user_id is a JSON
// number, not a string) must fail closed: ValidateToken returns an error
// instead of a session for an empty user.
func TestValidateTokenRejectsMalformedRow(t *testing.T) {
	plaintext := generateToken()
	db := &fakeTokenDB{stored: hashToken(plaintext), numericUserID: true}
	a := newFakeAuthStore(t, db)

	userID, err := a.ValidateToken(context.Background(), plaintext)
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("malformed token row validated as user %q; want a decode error", userID)
	}
	if userID != "" {
		t.Fatalf("userID = %q, want empty on decode failure", userID)
	}
}

// createToken must persist the hash, never the plaintext bearer token.
func TestCreateTokenStoresHashOnly(t *testing.T) {
	db := &fakeTokenDB{}
	a := newFakeAuthStore(t, db)

	tok, err := a.createToken(context.Background(), "u42")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("createToken: %v", err)
	}
	if len(db.createSQL) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("captured %d CREATE statements, want 1", len(db.createSQL))
	}
	sql := db.createSQL[0]
	if !strings.Contains(sql, "'"+hashToken(tok.Token)+"'") {
		t.Fatal("CREATE does not store the token hash")
	}
	if strings.Contains(sql, "'"+tok.Token+"'") {
		t.Fatal("CREATE stores the plaintext token")
	}
}

FILE: internal/cortex/cortex.go
==============================================================================
// Package cortex is Mímir's brain (F6): a neural knowledge graph of neurons
// (knowledge nodes), synapses (relationships), and engrams (durable memories).
// This is the namesake feature - the memory that makes Mímir Mímir.
package cortex

import "context"

// NeuronKind classifies a knowledge neuron.
type NeuronKind string

const (
	KindSource  NeuronKind = "source"  // ingested content (docs, web, video)
	KindNote    NeuronKind = "note"    // a note the agent or user wrote
	KindConcept NeuronKind = "concept" // an abstracted concept
	KindMemory  NeuronKind = "memory"  // a learned preference/lesson
	KindSkill   NeuronKind = "skill"   // a reusable skill
)

// Neuron is one node in the knowledge graph.
type Neuron struct {
	ID          string     `json:"id"`
	Kind        NeuronKind `json:"kind"`
	Layer       string     `json:"layer,omitempty"` // activity | context | experience | identity | preference
	Title       string     `json:"title,omitempty"`
	Content     string     `json:"content"`
	Embedding   []float64  `json:"embedding,omitempty"`    // vector for RAG
	Decay       float64    `json:"decay"`                  // forgetting-curve weight (F6)
	AccessCount int        `json:"access_count,omitempty"` // reinforcement: times recalled (F6)
}

// Synapse is a relationship between two neurons.
type Synapse struct {
	From string
	To   string
	Kind string // references | derives_from | relates_to | contradicts
}

// Engram is a durable memory - a neuron hardened so it won't be forgotten.
type Engram struct {
	NeuronID string
	Strength float64
}

// Store is the persistence interface for the Cortex. The real implementation
// uses SurrealDB (graph + vector + document); tests can use an in-memory store.
type Store interface {
	PutNeuron(ctx context.Context, n Neuron) (string, error)
	GetNeuron(ctx context.Context, id string) (Neuron, error)
	Search(ctx context.Context, query string, limit int) ([]Neuron, error)
	Relate(ctx context.Context, s Synapse) error
	Remember(ctx context.Context, e Engram) error
	All() []Neuron
}

FILE: internal/cortex/credentials.go
==============================================================================
package cortex

import (
	"crypto/rand"
	"encoding/hex"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"sync"
)

// SurrealDB credential resolution (F19). There is deliberately no built-in
// default password: the previous root/root fallback meant every default
// install shared one publicly known credential.
//
// Resolution order for NewSurrealStore and the managed Sidecar:
//  1. credentials supplied by the caller (SurrealConfig / Sidecar fields)
//  2. MIMIR_SURREAL_USER / MIMIR_SURREAL_PASS environment variables
//  3. for a store connecting to a managed sidecar address, the per-run
//     password the Sidecar generated at launch (resolveSidecarCreds)
//  4. otherwise an error: the caller must configure credentials
//
// defaultSurrealUser is a username only (the conventional name of the
// SurrealDB root account). It is never used as a password.
const defaultSurrealUser = "root"

const (
	envSurrealUser = "MIMIR_SURREAL_USER"
	envSurrealPass = "MIMIR_SURREAL_PASS"
)

// sidecarCreds maps a managed sidecar's HTTP base URL to the credentials it
// was launched with, so a SurrealStore created later in the same process can
// authenticate to it. Values live only in process memory and are never
// logged or persisted.
var sidecarCreds sync.Map // string addr -> [2]string{user, pass}

func registerSidecarCreds(httpAddr, user, pass string) {
	sidecarCreds.Store(strings.TrimRight(httpAddr, "/"), [2]string{user, pass})
}

func lookupSidecarCreds(httpAddr string) (user, pass string, ok bool) {
	v, found := sidecarCreds.Load(strings.TrimRight(httpAddr, "/"))
	if !found {
		return "", "", false
	}
	c := v.([2]string)
	return c[0], c[1], true
}

// generateSurrealPassword returns a random per-run password for a managed
// sidecar. It is shared with the in-process client via registerSidecarCreds,
// so a zero-config local install works without any known credential existing.
func generateSurrealPassword() (string, error) {
	b := make([]byte, 32)
	if _, err := rand.Read(b); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("generate password: %w", err)
	}
	return hex.EncodeToString(b), nil
}

// resolveSurrealCreds applies the resolution order above for a direct store
// connection to addr. It returns an error rather than inventing a credential.
func resolveSurrealCreds(user, pass, addr string) (string, string, error) {
	if user == "" {
		user = os.Getenv(envSurrealUser)
	}
	if pass == "" {
		pass = os.Getenv(envSurrealPass)
	}
	if pass == "" {
		if su, sp, ok := lookupSidecarCreds(addr); ok {
			if user == "" {
				user = su
			}
			pass = sp
		}
	}
	if pass == "" {
		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("surreal: no credentials for %s: set %s and %s, pass credentials in the config, or connect to a managed sidecar", addr, envSurrealUser, envSurrealPass)
	}
	if user == "" {
		user = defaultSurrealUser
	}
	return user, pass, nil
}

package cortex

// F19: no source file in this package may assign the literal "root" as a
// password ever again. Usernames may default to the root account name; a
// known default password may not exist.
func TestNoRootPasswordLiteral(t *testing.T) {
	_, thisFile, _, ok := runtime.Caller(0)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("runtime.Caller failed")
	}
	dir := filepath.Dir(thisFile)
	passRoot := regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)\bpass\w*\s*[:=]\s*"root"`)
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read package dir: %v", err)
	}
	for _, e := range entries {
		name := e.Name()
		if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".go") || strings.HasSuffix(name, "_test.go") {
			continue
		}
		b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, name))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", name, err)
		}
		if loc := passRoot.FindIndex(b); loc != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s assigns \"root\" as a password near byte %d", name, loc[0])
		}
	}
}

func clearSurrealEnv(t *testing.T) {
	t.Helper()
	t.Setenv(envSurrealUser, "")
	t.Setenv(envSurrealPass, "")
}

func TestResolveSurrealCredsExplicitWins(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv(envSurrealUser, "envuser")
	t.Setenv(envSurrealPass, "envpass")
	user, pass, err := resolveSurrealCreds("cfguser", "cfgpass", "http://127.0.0.1:9")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("resolve: %v", err)
	}
	if user != "cfguser" || pass != "cfgpass" {
		t.Fatalf("got %q/%q, want cfguser/cfgpass", user, pass)
	}
}

	t.Setenv(envSurrealUser, "envuser")
	t.Setenv(envSurrealPass, "envpass")
	user, pass, err := resolveSurrealCreds("", "", "http://127.0.0.1:9")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("resolve: %v", err)
	}
	if user != "envuser" || pass != "envpass" {
		t.Fatalf("got %q/%q, want envuser/envpass", user, pass)
	}
}

	clearSurrealEnv(t)

	registerSidecarCreds(addr, "sidecaruser", "sidecarpass")

	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("resolve: %v", err)

		t.Fatalf("got %q/%q, want the registered sidecar credentials", user, pass)
	}
}

		t.Fatal("expected an error when no credentials are available")

	if err == nil {

		t.Fatalf("unexpected error: %v", err)
	}
}

// A zero-config Sidecar generates a per-run password and registers it, so
// the credential the client resolves for the sidecar address matches the
// one the sidecar will launch with.
func TestSidecarGeneratesMatchingPassword(t *testing.T) {
	clearSurrealEnv(t)
	sc := &Sidecar{
		Addr:     fmt.Sprintf("127.0.0.1:%d", freePort(t)),
		BinPath:  filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "no-such-surreal-binary"),
		DataPath: "memory",
	}
	// No binary exists, so Start must fail; the password is generated and
	// registered before the launch attempt, which is what this test checks.
	if err := sc.Start(context.Background()); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected Start to fail with a nonexistent binary")
	}
	if sc.Pass == "" {
		t.Fatal("sidecar did not generate a password")
	}
	if len(sc.Pass) != 64 {
		t.Fatalf("generated password length = %d, want 64 hex chars", len(sc.Pass))
	}
	if _, err := hex.DecodeString(sc.Pass); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("generated password is not hex: %v", err)
	}
	user, pass, err := resolveSurrealCreds("", "", sc.HTTPAddr())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("client cannot resolve sidecar credentials: %v", err)
	}
	if pass != sc.Pass || user != sc.User {
		t.Fatal("client-resolved credentials do not match the sidecar credentials")
	}
}

func TestGenerateSurrealPasswordRandom(t *testing.T) {
	a, err := generateSurrealPassword()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("generate: %v", err)
	}
	b, err := generateSurrealPassword()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("generate: %v", err)
	}
	if a == b {
		t.Fatal("two generated passwords are identical")
	}
	if len(a) != 64 {
		t.Fatalf("password length = %d, want 64", len(a))
	}
}

FILE: internal/cortex/embed.go
==============================================================================
package cortex

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
)

// Embedder turns text into a vector for semantic (vector) recall. The Cortex uses it
// to embed neuron content and queries so Search can rank by meaning, not just shared
// words (F41 / E58). Implementations wrap a local model (Ollama) or a cloud provider.
type Embedder interface {
	Embed(ctx context.Context, text string) ([]float64, error)
}

// OllamaEmbedder embeds text via a local Ollama server's /api/embed endpoint (default
// model nomic-embed-text, 768-dim). Dependency-free: we own the wire format.
type OllamaEmbedder struct {
	BaseURL string // e.g. http://localhost:11434 (default)
	Model   string // e.g. nomic-embed-text (default)
	Client  *http.Client
}

func (e *OllamaEmbedder) client() *http.Client {
	if e.Client != nil {
		return e.Client
	}
	return http.DefaultClient
}

func (e *OllamaEmbedder) model() string {
	if e.Model != "" {
		return e.Model
	}
	return "nomic-embed-text"
}

// Embed returns the embedding vector for text.
func (e *OllamaEmbedder) Embed(ctx context.Context, text string) ([]float64, error) {
	base := e.BaseURL
	if base == "" {
		base = "http://localhost:11434"
	}
	body, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"model": e.model(), "input": text})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, strings.TrimRight(base, "/")+"/api/embed", bytes.NewReader(body))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	resp, err := e.client().Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("embed: HTTP %d from %s", resp.StatusCode, base)
	}
	var out struct {
		Embeddings [][]float64 `json:"embeddings"`
	}
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&out); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if len(out.Embeddings) == 0 || len(out.Embeddings[0]) == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("embed: no embedding returned by %s", e.model())
	}
	return out.Embeddings[0], nil
}

FILE: internal/cortex/memory.go
==============================================================================
package cortex

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"unicode"
)

// MemoryStore is a Cortex store. With an empty path it is purely in-memory (tests);
// with a path it persists neurons to a JSON file so memory survives across runs - the
// dependency-free base that SurrealDB (E6.2) later upgrades to vector + graph recall.
type MemoryStore struct {
	mu      sync.Mutex
	path    string
	neurons map[string]Neuron
	nextID  int
}

// NewMemoryStore returns an in-memory store (no persistence).
func NewMemoryStore() *MemoryStore {
	return &MemoryStore{neurons: map[string]Neuron{}, nextID: 1}
}

// NewMemoryStoreAt returns a store backed by path, loading any existing neurons.
// A missing file is not an error (the store starts empty and is created on first write).
func NewMemoryStoreAt(path string) (*MemoryStore, error) {
	s := &MemoryStore{path: path, neurons: map[string]Neuron{}, nextID: 1}
	if err := s.load(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return s, nil
}

func (m *MemoryStore) load() error {
	if m.path == "" {
		return nil
	}
	data, err := os.ReadFile(m.path)
	if err != nil {
		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
			return nil
		}
		return err
	}
	if len(strings.TrimSpace(string(data))) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	var ns []Neuron
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &ns); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("cortex: corrupt memory file %s: %w", m.path, err)
	}
	for _, n := range ns {
		m.neurons[n.ID] = n
		if id := parseID(n.ID); id >= m.nextID {
			m.nextID = id + 1
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func (m *MemoryStore) save() error {
	if m.path == "" {
		return nil
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(m.path), 0o755); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	ns := make([]Neuron, 0, len(m.neurons))
	for _, n := range m.neurons {
		ns = append(ns, n)
	}
	sort.Slice(ns, func(i, j int) bool { return ns[i].ID < ns[j].ID })
	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(ns, "", "  ")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.WriteFile(m.path, data, 0o644)
}

func parseID(id string) int {
	i := strings.LastIndex(id, "-")
	if i < 0 || i == len(id)-1 {
		return 0
	}
	var n int
	if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(id[i+1:], "%d", &n); err != nil {
		return 0
	}
	return n
}

// PutNeuron stores a neuron, assigning an id if it has none, and persists.
func (m *MemoryStore) PutNeuron(ctx context.Context, n Neuron) (string, error) {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	if n.ID == "" {
		n.ID = fmt.Sprintf("n-%d", m.nextID)
		m.nextID++
	}
	m.neurons[n.ID] = n
	return n.ID, m.save()
}

// GetNeuron returns a neuron by id.
func (m *MemoryStore) GetNeuron(ctx context.Context, id string) (Neuron, error) {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	return m.neurons[id], nil
}

// Search returns neurons whose content shares a word (>=4 chars) with the query,
// ranked by the number of matching words. This is a basic lexical recall; vector +
// graph recall replace it once SurrealDB lands.
func (m *MemoryStore) Search(ctx context.Context, query string, limit int) ([]Neuron, error) {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	qt := tokens(query)
	type scored struct {
		n     Neuron
		score int
	}
	var hits []scored
	for _, n := range m.neurons {
		hay := strings.ToLower(n.Content + " " + n.Title)
		sc := 0
		for _, t := range qt {
			if strings.Contains(hay, t) {
				sc++
			}
		}
		if sc > 0 {
			hits = append(hits, scored{n, sc})
		}
	}
	sort.Slice(hits, func(i, j int) bool {
		if hits[i].score != hits[j].score {
			return hits[i].score > hits[j].score
		}
		return hits[i].n.ID < hits[j].n.ID
	})
	out := make([]Neuron, 0, limit)
	for i, h := range hits {
		if i >= limit {
			break
		}
		out = append(out, h.n)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// Relate records a synapse (no-op until the graph store lands).
func (m *MemoryStore) Relate(ctx context.Context, s Synapse) error { return nil }

// Remember hardens an engram (no-op until the graph store lands).
func (m *MemoryStore) Remember(ctx context.Context, e Engram) error { return nil }

// All returns every neuron (for the /memory endpoint + tests).
func (m *MemoryStore) All() []Neuron {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	out := make([]Neuron, 0, len(m.neurons))
	for _, n := range m.neurons {
		out = append(out, n)
	}
	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].ID < out[j].ID })
	return out
}

// tokens extracts lowercase alphanumeric words of length >= 4 for lexical recall.
func tokens(s string) []string {
	var out []string
	var cur strings.Builder
	flush := func() {
		if cur.Len() >= 4 {
			out = append(out, cur.String())
		}
		cur.Reset()
	}
	for _, r := range strings.ToLower(s) {
		if unicode.IsLetter(r) || unicode.IsDigit(r) {
			cur.WriteRune(r)
		} else {
			flush()
		}
	}
	flush()
	return out
}

package cortex

import (
	"context"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

func TestMemoryPersistsToDisk(t *testing.T) {
	p := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "cortex.json")
	s1, err := NewMemoryStoreAt(p)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("new: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := s1.PutNeuron(context.Background(), Neuron{
		Kind: KindMemory, Content: "the codeword is MANGO77", Decay: 1,
	}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("put: %v", err)
	}

	// A brand-new store opened from the same file (a restart) must see the neuron.
	s2, err := NewMemoryStoreAt(p)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("reopen: %v", err)
	}
	got, _ := s2.Search(context.Background(), "MANGO77", 5)
	if len(got) != 1 || got[0].Content != "the codeword is MANGO77" {
		t.Fatalf("persisted search = %+v", got)
	}
}

func TestMemoryTokenSearch(t *testing.T) {
	s := NewMemoryStore()
	_, _ = s.PutNeuron(context.Background(), Neuron{Content: "alpha beta gamma delta", Decay: 1})
	if got, _ := s.Search(context.Background(), "gamma zzzz", 5); len(got) != 1 {
		t.Errorf("expected match on shared token gamma, got %d", len(got))
	}
	if got, _ := s.Search(context.Background(), "zzzz qq", 5); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("expected no match, got %d", len(got))
	}
}

FILE: internal/cortex/sessions.go
