func TestDeciderChoiceAndPruneTools(t *testing.T) {
	d := New("", "", "")
	allTools := []string{
		"read_file", "edit_block", "todo", "bash", "web_search", "grep_search", "load_skill", "question",
	}

	pruned := d.PruneToolNames(context.Background(), "run bash tests and grep_search for errors", allTools, 5)
	if len(pruned) != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("got %d tools, want 5: %v", len(pruned), pruned)
	}
	hasBash := false
	for _, name := range pruned {
		if name == "bash" {
			hasBash = true
		}
	}
	if !hasBash {
		t.Errorf("expected pruned tools to include bash, got %v", pruned)
	}
}

func TestDeciderRoutePrompt(t *testing.T) {
	d := New("", "", "")

	r1 := d.RoutePrompt(context.Background(), "Design and refactor the polyglot system architecture")
	if r1.Persona != "Odin" || r1.Tier != "T1" || !r1.NeedsThinking {
		t.Errorf("unexpected route for architecture prompt: %+v", r1)
	}

	r2 := d.RoutePrompt(context.Background(), "Fix race condition panic in worker loop")
	if r2.Persona != "Loki" || r2.Tier != "T1" {
		t.Errorf("unexpected route for bug prompt: %+v", r2)
	}

	r3 := d.RoutePrompt(context.Background(), "Rename variable foo to bar")
	if r3.Persona != "Thor" || r3.Tier != "T3" || r3.NeedsThinking {
		t.Errorf("unexpected route for simple edit: %+v", r3)
	}
}

func TestDeciderAssessCommandSafety(t *testing.T) {
	d := New("", "", "")

	safe := d.AssessCommandSafety(context.Background(), "go test ./...")
	if !safe.AutoApprove || safe.SafeScore < 0.9 {
		t.Errorf("expected go test to auto-approve, got %+v", safe)
	}

	risky := d.AssessCommandSafety(context.Background(), "git reset --hard HEAD~5")
	if risky.AutoApprove || risky.SafeScore > 0.2 {
		t.Errorf("expected git reset --hard to be blocked from auto-approve, got %+v", risky)
	}
}

func TestEnsureLocalDecisionModel(t *testing.T) {
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		if r.URL.Path == "/api/tags" {
			w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
			_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"models":[{"name":"liquid/d1-3b:latest"}]}`))
			return
		}
		http.NotFound(w, r)
	}))
	defer srv.Close()

	model, err := EnsureLocalDecisionModel(context.Background(), srv.URL, false)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected error: %v", err)

		t.Errorf("got %q, want liquid/d1-3b:latest", model)
	}
}

// Package engines manages Mimir's pre-compiled proprietary engine binaries
// distributed on main under `engines/bin/` while their source code lives on
// dedicated engine branches (`engine/tyr-rust`, `engine/mjolnir-mojo`,
// `engine/alphaflux-core`, `engine/gjallarhorn-ui`).
//
// All engines are proprietary intellectual property of Alpha Flux LLC
// (https://alphaflux.net) and require verified Alpha Flux LLC attribution
// before execution.
package engines

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"runtime"
	"strings"
)

const (
	// RequiredOwner is the mandatory copyright & license holder for all Mimir engines.
	RequiredOwner = "Alpha Flux LLC"
	// RequiredDomain is the canonical domain that must be referenced alongside engine usage.
	RequiredDomain = "alphaflux.net"
	// AttributionNotice is the canonical attribution string required by LICENSE-ENGINES.md.
	AttributionNotice = "Powered by Alpha Flux LLC Proprietary Engines (https://alphaflux.net)"
	// AttributionHandshake is passed to every pre-compiled engine binary on invocation.
	AttributionHandshake = "Alpha Flux LLC (https://alphaflux.net)"
)

var (
	// ErrAttributionRequired is returned if the Alpha Flux LLC attribution notice,
	// NOTICE file, or manifest provenance has been stripped or modified.
	ErrAttributionRequired = errors.New("engines: Alpha Flux LLC (https://alphaflux.net) attribution is required to use Mimir proprietary engines (see LICENSE-ENGINES.md)")
	// ErrBinaryIntegrity is returned when a pre-compiled engine binary is missing or fails SHA-256 verification.
	ErrBinaryIntegrity = errors.New("engines: pre-compiled engine binary missing or SHA-256 mismatch")
)

// PlatformBinary records platform-specific binary path, SHA-256 digest, and byte size.
type PlatformBinary struct {
	Binary    string `json:"binary"`
	SHA256    string `json:"sha256"`
	SizeBytes int64  `json:"size_bytes"`
}

// EngineEntry describes one pre-compiled proprietary engine binary in `engines/bin/`.
type EngineEntry struct {
	ID          string                    `json:"id"`
	Name        string                    `json:"name"`
	Version     string                    `json:"version"`
	Branch      string                    `json:"source_branch"`
	Binary      string                    `json:"binary,omitempty"`
	SHA256      string                    `json:"sha256,omitempty"`
	SizeBytes   int64                     `json:"size_bytes,omitempty"`
	Platforms   map[string]PlatformBinary `json:"platforms,omitempty"`
	Stack       string                    `json:"stack"`
	Description string                    `json:"description"`
}

// ResolveBinary returns the binary path, SHA-256, and size for the host platform
// (formatted as GOOS_GOARCH, e.g. windows_amd64, linux_amd64, darwin_arm64),
// falling back to the legacy top-level fields if platforms map is unset.
func (e *EngineEntry) ResolveBinary() (binary string, sha string, size int64, found bool) {
	key := runtime.GOOS + "_" + runtime.GOARCH
	if e.Platforms != nil {
		if pb, ok := e.Platforms[key]; ok && pb.Binary != "" {
			return pb.Binary, pb.SHA256, pb.SizeBytes, true
		}
	}
	if e.Binary != "" {
		return e.Binary, e.SHA256, e.SizeBytes, true
	}
	return "", "", 0, false
}

// Manifest is serialized to `engines/bin/manifest.json` on the main branch.
type Manifest struct {
	SchemaVersion string        `json:"schema_version"`
	Owner         string        `json:"owner"`
	Website       string        `json:"website"`
	License       string        `json:"license"`
	Attribution   string        `json:"required_attribution"`
	UpdatedAt     string        `json:"updated_at"`
	Engines       []EngineEntry `json:"engines"`
	// Signature is a base64 ed25519 signature over ManifestSigningBytes of
	// this manifest (the manifest JSON with this field cleared). It lets
	// clients authenticate an update instead of trusting the host that
	// served both the binaries and the hashes (N7).
	Signature string `json:"signature,omitempty"`
}

// VerifyAttribution enforces the Alpha Flux LLC license requirement on the manifest
// and the workspace NOTICE / LICENSE-ENGINES.md files.
func VerifyAttribution(rootDir string, m Manifest) error {
	if !strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(m.Owner), RequiredOwner) {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: manifest owner must be %q (got %q)", ErrAttributionRequired, RequiredOwner, m.Owner)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(m.Website), RequiredDomain) {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: manifest website must reference %s", ErrAttributionRequired, RequiredDomain)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(m.Attribution, RequiredOwner) || !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(m.Attribution), RequiredDomain) {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: manifest required_attribution must reference %s (%s)", ErrAttributionRequired, RequiredOwner, RequiredDomain)
	}

	noticePath := filepath.Join(rootDir, "NOTICE")
	noticeBytes, err := os.ReadFile(noticePath)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: missing NOTICE file at %s", ErrAttributionRequired, noticePath)
	}
	noticeText := string(noticeBytes)
	if !strings.Contains(noticeText, RequiredOwner) || !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(noticeText), RequiredDomain) {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: NOTICE file must retain %s (%s) attribution", ErrAttributionRequired, RequiredOwner, RequiredDomain)
	}
	return nil
}

// FileSHA256 computes the hex-encoded SHA-256 digest and byte size of a file.
func FileSHA256(path string) (string, int64, error) {
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return "", 0, err
	}
	sum := sha256.Sum256(raw)
	return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]), int64(len(raw)), nil
}

// LoadManifest reads and validates `engines/bin/manifest.json` inside rootDir.
func LoadManifest(rootDir string) (Manifest, error) {
	if strings.TrimSpace(rootDir) == "" {
		rootDir = "."
	}
	mpath := filepath.Join(rootDir, "engines", "bin", "manifest.json")
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(mpath)
	if err != nil {
		return Manifest{}, err
	}
	var m Manifest
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &m); err != nil {
		return Manifest{}, err
	}
	if err := VerifyAttribution(rootDir, m); err != nil {
		return m, err
	}
	return m, nil
}

// VerifyBinaries checks that every pre-compiled engine binary listed in the manifest
// for the current host platform exists in `engines/bin/` and matches its recorded SHA-256 digest.
func VerifyBinaries(rootDir string, m Manifest) error {
	if err := VerifyAttribution(rootDir, m); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	for _, e := range m.Engines {
		binRel, wantSHA, _, found := e.ResolveBinary()
		if !found || binRel == "" {
			continue // no binary declared for this platform
		}
		binPath := filepath.Join(rootDir, filepath.FromSlash(binRel))
		sum, _, err := FileSHA256(binPath)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s (%v)", ErrBinaryIntegrity, binRel, err)
		}
		if !strings.EqualFold(sum, wantSHA) {
			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s sha256=%s want=%s", ErrBinaryIntegrity, binRel, sum, wantSHA)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// Invoke validates Alpha Flux LLC attribution and SHA-256 integrity, then executes
// the requested pre-compiled engine binary with `--attribution="Alpha Flux LLC (https://alphaflux.net)"`.
func Invoke(ctx context.Context, rootDir, engineID string, args ...string) (string, error) {
	m, err := LoadManifest(rootDir)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if err := VerifyBinaries(rootDir, m); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	var target *EngineEntry
	for i := range m.Engines {
		if strings.EqualFold(m.Engines[i].ID, engineID) || strings.EqualFold(m.Engines[i].Name, engineID) {
			target = &m.Engines[i]
			break
		}
	}
	if target == nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("engines: unknown engine %q", engineID)
	}
	binRel, _, _, found := target.ResolveBinary()
	if !found || binRel == "" {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("engines: engine %q is not available for host platform %s_%s", engineID, runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH)
	}
	binPath := filepath.Join(rootDir, filepath.FromSlash(binRel))
	fullArgs := append([]string{"--attribution=" + AttributionHandshake}, args...)
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, binPath, fullArgs...)
	cmd.Dir = rootDir
	out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
	return strings.TrimSpace(string(out)), err
}

// FormatStatus renders a table of all pre-compiled Alpha Flux LLC engines, their source
// branches, binary integrity status, and attribution verification state.
func FormatStatus(rootDir string) string {
	m, err := LoadManifest(rootDir)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Sprintf("Alpha Flux LLC Engine Registry: ERROR (%v)", err)
	}
	var b strings.Builder
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "## %s\n", AttributionNotice)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **License Holder**: `%s` (`%s`)\n", m.Owner, m.Website)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **License File**: `%s`\n", m.License)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Host Platform**: `%s_%s`\n\n", runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH)
	for _, e := range m.Engines {
		binRel, wantSHA, _, found := e.ResolveBinary()
		if !found || binRel == "" {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "* **%s (`%s`)** -- Stack: `%s` | Source Branch: `%s`\n", e.Name, e.ID, e.Stack, e.Branch)
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  - Status: **UNAVAILABLE FOR %s_%s**\n", runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH)
			continue
		}
		binPath := filepath.Join(rootDir, filepath.FromSlash(binRel))
		sum, sz, fErr := FileSHA256(binPath)
		status := "VERIFIED (pre-compiled binary ready)"
		if fErr != nil {
			status = "MISSING"
		} else if !strings.EqualFold(sum, wantSHA) {
			status = "SHA256_MISMATCH"
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "* **%s (`%s`)** -- Stack: `%s` | Source Branch: `%s`\n", e.Name, e.ID, e.Stack, e.Branch)
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  - Binary: `%s` (%d KB | sha256: `%s...`) -> **%s**\n",
			binRel, sz/1024, truncateHex(wantSHA, 12), status)
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  - Role: %s\n", e.Description)
	}
	return strings.TrimRight(b.String(), "\n")
}

func truncateHex(s string, n int) string {
	if len(s) <= n {
		return s
	}
	return s[:n]
}

package engines

import (

func TestVerifyAttribution_RequiresAlphaFluxLLC(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	notice := "Copyright (c) 2026 Alpha Flux LLC (https://alphaflux.net)\n"
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "NOTICE"), []byte(notice), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write NOTICE: %v", err)
	}

	valid := Manifest{
		SchemaVersion: "1.0",
		Owner:         "Alpha Flux LLC",
		Website:       "https://alphaflux.net",
		License:       "LICENSE-ENGINES.md",
		Attribution:   AttributionNotice,
	}
	if err := VerifyAttribution(dir, valid); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("expected valid attribution to pass, got %v", err)
	}

	// Stripping Alpha Flux LLC owner must fail
	spoofed := valid
	spoofed.Owner = "Some Other Corp"
	if err := VerifyAttribution(dir, spoofed); !errors.Is(err, ErrAttributionRequired) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrAttributionRequired on spoofed owner, got %v", err)
	}

	// Stripping NOTICE file must fail
	_ = os.Remove(filepath.Join(dir, "NOTICE"))
	if err := VerifyAttribution(dir, valid); !errors.Is(err, ErrAttributionRequired) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrAttributionRequired when NOTICE is removed, got %v", err)
	}
}

func TestVerifyBinaries_ChecksSHA256Integrity(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "NOTICE"), []byte("Alpha Flux LLC https://alphaflux.net\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write NOTICE: %v", err)
	}
	binDir := filepath.Join(dir, "engines", "bin")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(binDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("mkdir bin: %v", err)
	}
	binFile := filepath.Join(binDir, "mimir_tyr_engine.exe")
	if err := os.WriteFile(binFile, []byte("fake-binary-payload"), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write binary: %v", err)
	}
	sum, sz, err := FileSHA256(binFile)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("FileSHA256: %v", err)
	}

	m := Manifest{
		SchemaVersion: "1.0",
		Owner:         "Alpha Flux LLC",
		Website:       "https://alphaflux.net",
		License:       "LICENSE-ENGINES.md",
		Attribution:   AttributionNotice,
		Engines: []EngineEntry{
			{
				ID:        "tyr-core",
				Name:      "Tyr-Core Engine",
				Branch:    "engine/tyr-rust",
				Binary:    "engines/bin/mimir_tyr_engine.exe",
				SHA256:    sum,
				SizeBytes: sz,
			},
		},
	}
	if err := VerifyBinaries(dir, m); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("expected VerifyBinaries to pass, got %v", err)
	}

	// Tamper with binary payload
	_ = os.WriteFile(binFile, []byte("tampered-payload"), 0o755)
	if err := VerifyBinaries(dir, m); !errors.Is(err, ErrBinaryIntegrity) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrBinaryIntegrity on tampered binary, got %v", err)
	}
}

FILE: internal/engines/manifest_signature_test.go
==============================================================================
package engines

import (
	"crypto/ed25519"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/json"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

// releasePubKeyB64 is the release signing key of record (N7): the public
// half of the ed25519 keypair whose private half is held offline by the
// maintainer and never enters this repo. It is the same value pinned as
// MIMIR_ENGINE_PUBKEY in .env.example, docker-compose.yml,
// docker-compose.prod.yml, and the Dockerfile.
const releasePubKeyB64 = "uJQqyXeyx49sJYWeVttFPX9JnHuyIWCh/fk3CLqvuf4="

// TestShippedManifestSignatureVerifies is the arming gate for N7: the
// manifest shipped in engines/bin must carry a valid signature from the
// release key of record. If this test fails, the manifest was edited (or
// the signing key rotated) without re-signing, and every install with
// the key pinned would refuse the update; re-sign the manifest with the
// maintainer procedure in updater.go before shipping.
func TestShippedManifestSignatureVerifies(t *testing.T) {
	rawPub, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(releasePubKeyB64)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("release key of record is not valid base64: %v", err)
	}
	if len(rawPub) != ed25519.PublicKeySize {
		t.Fatalf("release key of record decodes to %d bytes, want %d", len(rawPub), ed25519.PublicKeySize)
	}
	pub := ed25519.PublicKey(rawPub)

	raw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("..", "..", "engines", "bin", "manifest.json"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read shipped manifest: %v", err)
	}
	var m Manifest
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &m); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parse shipped manifest: %v", err)
	}
	if len(m.Engines) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("shipped manifest lists no engines")
	}
	if m.Signature == "" {
		t.Fatal("shipped manifest carries no signature; N7 is disarmed")
	}
	sig, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(m.Signature)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("shipped manifest signature is not valid base64: %v", err)
	}
	canonical, err := ManifestSigningBytes(m)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("signing bytes: %v", err)
	}
	if !ed25519.Verify(pub, canonical, sig) {
		t.Fatal("shipped manifest signature does not verify against the release key of record; re-sign before shipping")
	}

	// Tamper control: changing any signed content (here, a version
	// string) must invalidate the very same signature, proving the
	// signature actually covers the manifest body.
	tampered := m
	tampered.Engines = append([]EngineEntry(nil), m.Engines...)
	tampered.Engines[0].Version = "9.9.9"
	tamperedBytes, err := ManifestSigningBytes(tampered)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("tampered signing bytes: %v", err)
	}
	if ed25519.Verify(pub, tamperedBytes, sig) {
		t.Fatal("tampered manifest still verifies; the signature is not covering the manifest content")
	}
}

package engines

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/ed25519"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"runtime"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

// DefaultUpdateBase is where `mimir update` pulls the published manifest and
// engine binaries from. Override with MIMIR_UPDATE_BASE (for forks, mirrors, or tests).
const DefaultUpdateBase = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/David2024patton/Mimir/main"

// KnownEngines is the static registry of engine metadata. Version and SHA-256 are
// filled in at publish time from the actual compiled binary, never typed by hand.
var KnownEngines = []EngineEntry{
	{
		ID: "tyr-core", Name: "Tyr-Core Engine", Branch: "engine/tyr-rust",
		Binary: "engines/bin/mimir_tyr_engine.exe", Stack: "go (rust port planned)",
		Description: "Symbol outline and Okapi BM25 code search.",
	},
	{
		ID: "mjolnir-compute", Name: "Mjolnir-Compute Engine", Branch: "engine/mjolnir-mojo",
		Binary: "engines/bin/mimir_mjolnir_engine.exe", Stack: "go (mojo port planned)",
		Description: ".itf header I/O, cosine similarity, 10,048-bit VSA bind/unbind.",
	},
	{
		ID: "alphaflux-core", Name: "Alpha Flux Intelligence Engine", Branch: "engine/alphaflux-core",
		Binary: "engines/bin/mimir_alphaflux_engine.exe", Stack: "go",
		Description: "Huginn-Decider routing, Epistemic Critic, Impeccable + SEO/GEO web audit.",
	},
}

// UpdateBase returns the configured update source.
func UpdateBase() string {
	if v := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("MIMIR_UPDATE_BASE")); v != "" {
		return strings.TrimRight(v, "/")
	}
	return DefaultUpdateBase
}

var (
	// ErrInsecureUpdateBase is returned when the update base is not https
	// and the operator has not explicitly opted into an insecure channel.
	ErrInsecureUpdateBase = errors.New("engines: update base must use https (set MIMIR_UPDATE_ALLOW_INSECURE=1 to override)")
	// ErrDowngradeRefused is returned when an update would install an older
	// engine version than the one already present.
	ErrDowngradeRefused = errors.New("engines: refusing to downgrade an engine (set MIMIR_ENGINE_ALLOW_DOWNGRADE=1 to force)")
	// ErrInsecureRedirect is returned when an update download is redirected
	// to a non-https URL and the operator has not opted into an insecure
	// channel. Validating the initial URL is not enough: a redirect must
	// not be able to downgrade the transport after the check.
	ErrInsecureRedirect = errors.New("engines: update download redirected to a non-https URL (set MIMIR_UPDATE_ALLOW_INSECURE=1 to override)")
	// ErrTooManyRedirects is returned when an update download exceeds the
	// redirect cap.
	ErrTooManyRedirects = errors.New("engines: update download exceeded the maximum number of redirects")
	// ErrUnverifiableVersion is returned when an update targets an engine
	// that is already installed but either version string is unparseable,
	// so the updater cannot prove the update is not a downgrade.
	ErrUnverifiableVersion = errors.New("engines: cannot verify update direction for an installed engine with an unparseable version (set MIMIR_ENGINE_ALLOW_DOWNGRADE=1 to force)")
)

// maxUpdateRedirects caps how many redirects an update download follows.
const maxUpdateRedirects = 5

// updateRedirectPolicy is the redirect policy for every update download.
// A redirect target must stay on https unless the operator explicitly
// opted into an insecure channel, and the chain is capped so a hostile or
// broken host cannot bounce the client forever. req is the redirect
// target about to be fetched; via holds the requests already made, so
// len(via) is the number of the redirect being attempted.
func updateRedirectPolicy(req *http.Request, via []*http.Request) error {
	if len(via) > maxUpdateRedirects {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: stopped after %d redirects", ErrTooManyRedirects, maxUpdateRedirects)
	}
	if req.URL.Scheme != "https" && os.Getenv("MIMIR_UPDATE_ALLOW_INSECURE") != "1" {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrInsecureRedirect, req.URL.Redacted())
	}
	return nil
}

// updateHTTPClient builds the client used for all update downloads, with
// the redirect policy attached.
func updateHTTPClient() *http.Client {
	return &http.Client{Timeout: 2 * time.Minute, CheckRedirect: updateRedirectPolicy}
}

// validateUpdateBase enforces transport security for the update channel
// (N7): the base serves executable code, so plain http is refused unless
// the operator explicitly sets MIMIR_UPDATE_ALLOW_INSECURE=1.
func validateUpdateBase(base string) error {
	u, err := url.Parse(base)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("engines: invalid update base %q: %w", base, err)
	}
	if u.Scheme == "https" {
		return nil
	}
	if os.Getenv("MIMIR_UPDATE_ALLOW_INSECURE") == "1" {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "WARNING: engine update base %q is not https. MIMIR_UPDATE_ALLOW_INSECURE=1 is set, so binaries will be downloaded over an insecure channel.\n", base)
		return nil
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("%w: got %q", ErrInsecureUpdateBase, base)
}

// ManifestSigningBytes returns the canonical bytes an ed25519 manifest
// signature covers: the manifest encoded with encoding/json (struct field
// order, no indentation) with the Signature field cleared. Verifiers
// re-encode the parsed manifest the same way, so the served file's own
// formatting does not matter.
//
// Release signing procedure for maintainers (N7):
//  1. Generate an ed25519 keypair once (crypto/ed25519.GenerateKey) and
//     keep the private key offline, outside the repo.
//  2. After BuildManifest writes engines/bin/manifest.json, load it, call
//     SignManifest(manifest, priv), store the result in the manifest's
//     "signature" field, and commit the signed manifest.
//  3. Give installs the public key out of band via the environment:
//     MIMIR_ENGINE_PUBKEY=<base64 raw 32-byte public key>. Clients with
//     the variable set refuse unsigned or badly signed manifests.
func ManifestSigningBytes(m Manifest) ([]byte, error) {
	m.Signature = ""
	return json.Marshal(m)
}

// SignManifest returns the base64 ed25519 signature for a manifest, in the
// form stored in Manifest.Signature.
func SignManifest(m Manifest, priv ed25519.PrivateKey) (string, error) {
	canonical, err := ManifestSigningBytes(m)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(ed25519.Sign(priv, canonical)), nil
}

// engineUpdatePubKey reads the operator-pinned manifest verification key
// from MIMIR_ENGINE_PUBKEY (base64 raw public key). Nil means the operator
// has not pinned a key.
func engineUpdatePubKey() (ed25519.PublicKey, error) {
	v := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("MIMIR_ENGINE_PUBKEY"))
	if v == "" {
		return nil, nil
	}
	raw, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(v)
	if err != nil {
		raw2, err2 := base64.RawStdEncoding.DecodeString(v)
		if err2 != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("engines: MIMIR_ENGINE_PUBKEY is not valid base64: %w", err)
		}
		raw = raw2
	}
	if len(raw) != ed25519.PublicKeySize {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("engines: MIMIR_ENGINE_PUBKEY must decode to %d bytes, got %d", ed25519.PublicKeySize, len(raw))
	}
	return ed25519.PublicKey(raw), nil
}

// verifyRemoteManifest authenticates a fetched manifest (N7). With a
// pinned key the manifest must carry a valid signature. Without one, the
// update still works (hash-only integrity, as before) but a loud warning
// states plainly that it is unauthenticated.
func verifyRemoteManifest(m Manifest) error {
	pub, err := engineUpdatePubKey()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if pub == nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "WARNING: MIMIR_ENGINE_PUBKEY is not set, so this engine update is UNAUTHENTICATED. The manifest and binaries are trusted purely because they came from the update host. Set MIMIR_ENGINE_PUBKEY to require signed manifests.")
		return nil
	}
	if strings.TrimSpace(m.Signature) == "" {
		return errors.New("engines: MIMIR_ENGINE_PUBKEY is set but the remote manifest carries no signature; refusing update")
	}
	sig, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(m.Signature)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("engines: remote manifest signature is not valid base64: %w", err)
	}
	canonical, err := ManifestSigningBytes(m)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if !ed25519.Verify(pub, canonical, sig) {
		return errors.New("engines: remote manifest signature verification failed; refusing update")
	}
	return nil
}

// compareVersions orders dotted numeric versions ("0.3.0" vs "0.2.9").
// ok is false when either side is missing or not dotted numeric, in which
// case callers must not treat the pair as comparable.
func compareVersions(a, b string) (cmp int, ok bool) {
	parse := func(s string) ([]int, bool) {
		s = strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(s, "v"))
		if s == "" || s == "none" || s == "unknown" {
			return nil, false
		}
		parts := strings.Split(s, ".")
		out := make([]int, len(parts))
		for i, p := range parts {
			n, err := strconv.Atoi(p)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, false
			}
			out[i] = n
		}
		return out, true
	}
	av, aok := parse(a)
	bv, bok := parse(b)
	if !aok || !bok {
		return 0, false
	}
	for i := 0; i < len(av) || i < len(bv); i++ {
		var x, y int
		if i < len(av) {
			x = av[i]
		}
		if i < len(bv) {
			y = bv[i]
		}
		if x != y {
			if x < y {
				return -1, true
			}
			return 1, true
		}
	}
	return 0, true
}

// hasLocalVersion reports whether a plan change carries an actual local
// version record. CheckForUpdates marks engines that are not installed
// yet with LocalVersion "none" (no binary on disk) or "unknown" (a binary
// is present but the local manifest does not track the engine); neither
// is a local version.
func hasLocalVersion(v string) bool {
	return v != "" && v != "none" && v != "unknown"
}

// parseableVersion reports whether v is a dotted numeric version string
// that compareVersions can order. "none", "unknown", empty, and free
// form strings are not parseable.
func parseableVersion(v string) bool {
	_, ok := compareVersions(v, v)
	return ok
}

// probeVersion runs `<binary> --attribution=... version` and reads the "version" field.
func probeVersion(ctx context.Context, binPath string) string {
	cctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	out, err := exec.CommandContext(cctx, binPath, "--attribution="+AttributionHandshake, "version").Output()
	if err != nil {
		return "unknown"
	}
	var v struct {
		Version string `json:"version"`
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(out, &v) != nil || v.Version == "" {
		return "unknown"
	}
	return v.Version
}

// BuildManifest hashes every known engine binary present in `engines/bin/`, asks each
// binary for its version, and writes `engines/bin/manifest.json`. This is the publish
// step: run it after copying freshly built binaries in, then commit to main.
func BuildManifest(ctx context.Context, rootDir string) (Manifest, error) {
	m := Manifest{
		SchemaVersion: "1.0",
		Owner:         RequiredOwner,
		Website:       "https://" + RequiredDomain,
		License:       "LICENSE-ENGINES.md",
		Attribution:   AttributionNotice,
		UpdatedAt:     time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
	}

	platforms := []struct {
		Key string // e.g. "windows_amd64", "linux_amd64", "darwin_arm64"
		Ext string // e.g. ".exe", "", ""
	}{
		{Key: "windows_amd64", Ext: ".exe"},
		{Key: "linux_amd64", Ext: ""},
		{Key: "darwin_arm64", Ext: ""},
	}

	for _, e := range KnownEngines {
		// Initialize Platforms map
		e.Platforms = make(map[string]PlatformBinary)

		// 1. Check for platform-specific binaries: e.g. engines/bin/mimir_tyr_engine_linux_amd64
		baseBinaryName := strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(e.Binary), filepath.Ext(e.Binary))
		for _, p := range platforms {
			pBinRel := fmt.Sprintf("engines/bin/%s_%s%s", baseBinaryName, p.Key, p.Ext)
			pBinPath := filepath.Join(rootDir, filepath.FromSlash(pBinRel))
			if sum, size, err := FileSHA256(pBinPath); err == nil {
				e.Platforms[p.Key] = PlatformBinary{
					Binary:    pBinRel,
					SHA256:    sum,
					SizeBytes: size,
				}
			}
		}

		// 2. Check for default/legacy binary: e.g. engines/bin/mimir_tyr_engine.exe
		binPath := filepath.Join(rootDir, filepath.FromSlash(e.Binary))
		sum, size, err := FileSHA256(binPath)
		if err == nil {
			e.SHA256 = sum
			e.SizeBytes = size
			e.Version = probeVersion(ctx, binPath)
			// Also register in Platforms map under host platform if not already set
			hostKey := runtime.GOOS + "_" + runtime.GOARCH
			if _, exists := e.Platforms[hostKey]; !exists {
				e.Platforms[hostKey] = PlatformBinary{
					Binary:    e.Binary,
					SHA256:    sum,
					SizeBytes: size,
				}
			}
		}

		if len(e.Platforms) > 0 || err == nil {
			if e.Version == "" {
				e.Version = "0.2.0"
			}
			m.Engines = append(m.Engines, e)
		}
	}
	if len(m.Engines) == 0 {
		return m, errors.New("engines: no engine binaries found in engines/bin/")
	}
	raw, _ := json.MarshalIndent(m, "", "  ")
	out := filepath.Join(rootDir, "engines", "bin", "manifest.json")
	if err := os.WriteFile(out, append(raw, '\n'), 0o644); err != nil {
		return m, err
	}
	return m, nil
}

// EngineDiff describes one engine whose local copy differs from the published copy.
type EngineDiff struct {
	ID            string `json:"id"`
	LocalVersion  string `json:"local_version"`
	RemoteVersion string `json:"remote_version"`
	Reason        string `json:"reason"` // "new", "new_unverifiable", "changed", "missing_local"
	Remote        EngineEntry
}

// UpdatePlan is the result of comparing local and remote manifests.
type UpdatePlan struct {
	Source  string       `json:"source"`
	Remote  Manifest     `json:"remote"`
	Changes []EngineDiff `json:"changes"`
}

func httpGet(ctx context.Context, url string, limit int64) ([]byte, error) {
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, url, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	req.Header.Set("User-Agent", "mimir-updater")
	resp, err := updateHTTPClient().Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("GET %s: HTTP %d", url, resp.StatusCode)
	}
	return io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, limit))
}

// CheckForUpdates fetches the published manifest and diffs it against local binaries
// by SHA-256 (not by version string), so any rebuilt engine is detected.
func CheckForUpdates(ctx context.Context, rootDir, base string) (UpdatePlan, error) {
	plan := UpdatePlan{Source: base}
	if err := validateUpdateBase(base); err != nil {
		return plan, err
	}
	raw, err := httpGet(ctx, base+"/engines/bin/manifest.json", 1<<20)
	if err != nil {
		return plan, err
	}
	var remote Manifest
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &remote); err != nil {
		return plan, fmt.Errorf("engines: remote manifest is not valid JSON: %w", err)
	}
	// Refuse to install anything from a manifest that drops Alpha Flux LLC ownership.
	if !strings.EqualFold(remote.Owner, RequiredOwner) || !strings.Contains(remote.Attribution, RequiredOwner) {
		return plan, fmt.Errorf("%w: remote manifest at %s", ErrAttributionRequired, base)
	}
	// Authenticate the manifest before trusting any hash in it (N7).
	if err := verifyRemoteManifest(remote); err != nil {
		return plan, err
	}
	plan.Remote = remote

	local, _ := readManifestFile(rootDir)
	localByID := map[string]EngineEntry{}
	for _, e := range local.Engines {
		localByID[e.ID] = e
	}
	for _, re := range remote.Engines {
		le, known := localByID[re.ID]
		// Diff the file Invoke will actually execute on this host (the
		// platform-resolved binary), not the legacy top-level path (N8).
		binRel, wantSHA, _, found := re.ResolveBinary()
		if !found || binRel == "" {
			continue // nothing published for this host platform
		}
		binPath := filepath.Join(rootDir, filepath.FromSlash(binRel))
		sum, _, ferr := FileSHA256(binPath)
		switch {
		case ferr != nil:
			plan.Changes = append(plan.Changes, EngineDiff{ID: re.ID, LocalVersion: "none", RemoteVersion: re.Version, Reason: "missing_local", Remote: re})
		case !known:
			if !strings.EqualFold(sum, wantSHA) {
				reason := "new"
				if !parseableVersion(re.Version) {
					// A binary is present but untracked and the remote
					// version cannot be parsed, so ApplyUpdates will
					// refuse this change (ErrUnverifiableVersion)
					// unless forced. Flag it in the plan so the
					// refusal is visible before apply time.
					reason = "new_unverifiable"
				}
				plan.Changes = append(plan.Changes, EngineDiff{ID: re.ID, LocalVersion: "unknown", RemoteVersion: re.Version, Reason: reason, Remote: re})
			}
		case !strings.EqualFold(sum, wantSHA):
			plan.Changes = append(plan.Changes, EngineDiff{ID: re.ID, LocalVersion: le.Version, RemoteVersion: re.Version, Reason: "changed", Remote: re})
		}
	}
	return plan, nil
}

func readManifestFile(rootDir string) (Manifest, error) {
	var m Manifest
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(rootDir, "engines", "bin", "manifest.json"))
	if err != nil {
		return m, err
	}
	err = json.Unmarshal(raw, &m)
	return m, err
}

// ApplyUpdates downloads each changed binary to a temp file, verifies its SHA-256
// against the remote manifest, then atomically swaps it into place. Nothing is
// replaced unless every download verifies, and the manifest is written last.
func ApplyUpdates(ctx context.Context, rootDir string, plan UpdatePlan) ([]string, error) {
	if len(plan.Changes) == 0 {
		return nil, nil
	}
	// Re-run the trust checks here too: a plan does not have to come from
	// CheckForUpdates, and nothing executable is fetched before these pass.
	if err := validateUpdateBase(plan.Source); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if err := verifyRemoteManifest(plan.Remote); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	// Downgrade protection (N7): a manifest that would move an engine
	// backwards is refused unless the operator explicitly forces it.
	// The check fails closed for engines that are already installed
	// (audit FIX 2): when a local version is on record but either
	// version string is unparseable, no ordering can be proven, so the
	// update is refused rather than silently waved through. A binary
	// that is present on disk but untracked ("unknown") also counts as
	// installed when the remote version is unparseable: nothing about
	// the replacement can be verified at all. Only a genuinely absent
	// engine ("none") and an untracked binary facing a parseable remote
	// version (a real, orderable version, hash-diffed by
	// CheckForUpdates) keep the permissive path.
	if os.Getenv("MIMIR_ENGINE_ALLOW_DOWNGRADE") != "1" {
		for _, c := range plan.Changes {
			cmp, ok := compareVersions(c.RemoteVersion, c.LocalVersion)
			switch {
			case ok && cmp < 0:
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s %s -> %s", ErrDowngradeRefused, c.ID, c.LocalVersion, c.RemoteVersion)
			case !ok && hasLocalVersion(c.LocalVersion):
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s local=%q remote=%q", ErrUnverifiableVersion, c.ID, c.LocalVersion, c.RemoteVersion)
			case !ok && c.LocalVersion == "unknown" && !parseableVersion(c.RemoteVersion):
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s local=%q remote=%q", ErrUnverifiableVersion, c.ID, c.LocalVersion, c.RemoteVersion)
			}
		}
	}
	type staged struct{ tmp, dst string }
	var ready []staged
	cleanup := func() {
		for _, s := range ready {
			_ = os.Remove(s.tmp)
		}
	}
	for _, c := range plan.Changes {
		// Download, verify, and replace the platform-resolved binary that
		// Invoke executes on this host, not the legacy top-level path (N8).
		binRel, wantSHA, _, found := c.Remote.ResolveBinary()
		if !found || binRel == "" {
			cleanup()
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("engines: update for %s has no binary for host platform %s_%s", c.ID, runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH)
		}
		data, err := httpGet(ctx, plan.Source+"/"+binRel, 256<<20)
		if err != nil {
			cleanup()
			return nil, err
		}
		dst := filepath.Join(rootDir, filepath.FromSlash(binRel))
		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dst), 0o755); err != nil {
			cleanup()
			return nil, err
		}
		tmp := dst + ".download"
		if err := os.WriteFile(tmp, data, 0o755); err != nil {
			cleanup()
			return nil, err
		}
		ready = append(ready, staged{tmp: tmp, dst: dst})
		sum, _, _ := FileSHA256(tmp)
		if !strings.EqualFold(sum, wantSHA) {
			cleanup()
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: downloaded %s sha256=%s want=%s", ErrBinaryIntegrity, binRel, sum, wantSHA)
		}
	}
	var updated []string
	for i, s := range ready {
		_ = os.Remove(s.dst + ".old")
		if _, err := os.Stat(s.dst); err == nil {
			if err := os.Rename(s.dst, s.dst+".old"); err != nil {
				cleanup()
				return updated, err
			}
		}
		if err := os.Rename(s.tmp, s.dst); err != nil {
			return updated, err
		}
		_ = os.Remove(s.dst + ".old")
		updated = append(updated, plan.Changes[i].ID+" -> "+plan.Changes[i].RemoteVersion)
	}
	raw, _ := json.MarshalIndent(plan.Remote, "", "  ")
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(rootDir, "engines", "bin", "manifest.json"), append(raw, '\n'), 0o644); err != nil {
		return updated, err
	}
	return updated, nil
}

// HarnessUpdateResult describes what happened to the open-source harness itself.
type HarnessUpdateResult struct {
	Mode    string // "git" or "skipped"
	Output  string
	Rebuilt bool
}

// UpdateHarness fast-forwards the local git checkout of main (no merges, no force)
// and rebuilds bin/mimir. On Windows the running exe is renamed aside first, which
// Windows allows, so the new build can take its place.
func UpdateHarness(ctx context.Context, rootDir string) (HarnessUpdateResult, error) {
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(rootDir, ".git")); err != nil {
		return HarnessUpdateResult{Mode: "skipped", Output: "not a git checkout; download the latest release instead"}, nil
	}
	pull := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "pull", "--ff-only", "origin", "main")
	pull.Dir = rootDir
	out, err := pull.CombinedOutput()
	res := HarnessUpdateResult{Mode: "git", Output: strings.TrimSpace(string(out))}
	if err != nil {
		return res, fmt.Errorf("git pull --ff-only failed (local changes or diverged history?): %w", err)
	}
	if strings.Contains(res.Output, "Already up to date") {
		return res, nil
	}
	if _, err := exec.LookPath("go"); err != nil {
		res.Output += "\n(go toolchain not found; rebuild bin/mimir manually)"
		return res, nil
	}
	exe := "mimir"
	if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
		exe += ".exe"
	}
	target := filepath.Join(rootDir, "bin", exe)
	tmp := target + ".new"
	build := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "go", "build", "-o", tmp, "./cmd/mimir")
	build.Dir = rootDir
	if bout, berr := build.CombinedOutput(); berr != nil {
		return res, fmt.Errorf("rebuild failed: %v\n%s", berr, bout)
	}
	_ = os.Remove(target + ".old")
	if _, err := os.Stat(target); err == nil {
		if err := os.Rename(target, target+".old"); err != nil {
			return res, err
		}
	}
	if err := os.Rename(tmp, target); err != nil {
		return res, err
	}
	res.Rebuilt = true
	return res, nil
}

package engines

// publishTree builds a fake "published main" directory served over HTTP.
func publishTree(t *testing.T, payload string, owner string) (string, Manifest) {
	t.Helper()
	// The fake publisher is a plain-http httptest server; opt in explicitly.
	t.Setenv("MIMIR_UPDATE_ALLOW_INSECURE", "1")
	pub := t.TempDir()
	binDir := filepath.Join(pub, "engines", "bin")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(binDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	bin := filepath.Join(binDir, "mimir_tyr_engine.exe")
	if err := os.WriteFile(bin, []byte(payload), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	sum, size, _ := FileSHA256(bin)
	m := Manifest{
		SchemaVersion: "1.0", Owner: owner, Website: "https://alphaflux.net",
		License: "LICENSE-ENGINES.md", Attribution: AttributionNotice,
		Engines: []EngineEntry{{
			ID: "tyr-core", Version: "0.3.0", Binary: "engines/bin/mimir_tyr_engine.exe",
			SHA256: sum, SizeBytes: size,
		}},
	}
	raw, _ := json.Marshal(m)
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(binDir, "manifest.json"), raw, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return pub, m
}

func TestUpdateFlow_DetectsChangeAndSwapsVerifiedBinary(t *testing.T) {
	pub, _ := publishTree(t, "engine-v0.3.0", RequiredOwner)
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.FileServer(http.Dir(pub)))
	defer srv.Close()

	local := t.TempDir()
	localBin := filepath.Join(local, "engines", "bin")
	_ = os.MkdirAll(localBin, 0o755)
	_ = os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(localBin, "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"), []byte("engine-v0.2.0"), 0o755)

	plan, err := CheckForUpdates(context.Background(), local, srv.URL)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CheckForUpdates: %v", err)
	}
	if len(plan.Changes) != 1 || plan.Changes[0].ID != "tyr-core" {
		t.Fatalf("expected 1 changed engine, got %+v", plan.Changes)
	}

	updated, err := ApplyUpdates(context.Background(), local, plan)
	if err != nil || len(updated) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("ApplyUpdates: updated=%v err=%v", updated, err)
	}
	got, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(localBin, "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"))
	if string(got) != "engine-v0.3.0" {
		t.Fatalf("binary not swapped, got %q", got)
	}

	// Second check is a no-op.
	plan2, err := CheckForUpdates(context.Background(), local, srv.URL)
	if err != nil || len(plan2.Changes) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("expected up to date, got %+v err=%v", plan2.Changes, err)
	}
}

func TestUpdateFlow_RejectsTamperedDownload(t *testing.T) {
	pub, _ := publishTree(t, "engine-v0.3.0", RequiredOwner)
	// Tamper after the manifest was written: hash no longer matches.
	_ = os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(pub, "engines", "bin", "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"), []byte("evil"), 0o755)
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.FileServer(http.Dir(pub)))
	defer srv.Close()

	local := t.TempDir()
	localBin := filepath.Join(local, "engines", "bin")
	_ = os.MkdirAll(localBin, 0o755)
	orig := filepath.Join(localBin, "mimir_tyr_engine.exe")
	_ = os.WriteFile(orig, []byte("engine-v0.2.0"), 0o755)

	plan, err := CheckForUpdates(context.Background(), local, srv.URL)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CheckForUpdates: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := ApplyUpdates(context.Background(), local, plan); !errors.Is(err, ErrBinaryIntegrity) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrBinaryIntegrity, got %v", err)
	}
	got, _ := os.ReadFile(orig)
	if string(got) != "engine-v0.2.0" {
		t.Fatalf("original binary must be untouched after failed verify, got %q", got)
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(orig + ".download"); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
		t.Fatalf("temp download should be cleaned up")
	}
}

// N7: a plain http update base is refused unless the operator explicitly
// opts into an insecure channel.
func TestCheckForUpdates_RejectsPlainHTTPBase(t *testing.T) {
	pub, _ := publishTree(t, "engine-v0.3.0", RequiredOwner)
	// publishTree set the opt-in for its own flow; remove it for this check.
	if err := os.Unsetenv("MIMIR_UPDATE_ALLOW_INSECURE"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.FileServer(http.Dir(pub)))
	defer srv.Close()
	if _, err := CheckForUpdates(context.Background(), t.TempDir(), srv.URL); !errors.Is(err, ErrInsecureUpdateBase) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrInsecureUpdateBase, got %v", err)
	}
}

// writeManifest rewrites the manifest.json inside a published tree.
func writeManifest(t *testing.T, pub string, m Manifest) {
	t.Helper()
	raw, err := json.Marshal(m)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(pub, "engines", "bin", "manifest.json"), raw, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

// N7: with MIMIR_ENGINE_PUBKEY pinned, unsigned manifests are refused,
// correctly signed ones pass, and tampering after signing is caught.
func TestCheckForUpdates_ManifestSignature(t *testing.T) {
	pub, m := publishTree(t, "engine-v0.3.0", RequiredOwner)
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.FileServer(http.Dir(pub)))
	defer srv.Close()

	pubKey, priv, err := ed25519.GenerateKey(rand.Reader)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Setenv("MIMIR_ENGINE_PUBKEY", base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(pubKey))

	// Unsigned manifest + pinned key: refuse.
	if _, err := CheckForUpdates(context.Background(), t.TempDir(), srv.URL); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected refusal for unsigned manifest when a key is pinned")
	}

	// Signed manifest: accepted.
	sig, err := SignManifest(m, priv)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m.Signature = sig
	writeManifest(t, pub, m)
	if _, err := CheckForUpdates(context.Background(), t.TempDir(), srv.URL); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("expected signed manifest to pass, got %v", err)
	}

	// Tamper after signing (version bump, same signature): refused.
	m.Engines[0].Version = "9.9.9"
	writeManifest(t, pub, m)
	if _, err := CheckForUpdates(context.Background(), t.TempDir(), srv.URL); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected refusal for manifest tampered after signing")
	}
}

// N7: ApplyUpdates refuses to move an engine backwards unless forced.
func TestApplyUpdates_RefusesDowngrade(t *testing.T) {
	pub, _ := publishTree(t, "engine-v0.2.0", RequiredOwner)
	// Remote manifest from publishTree says 0.3.0; rewrite it as 0.2.0.
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(pub, "engines", "bin", "manifest.json"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var remote Manifest
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &remote); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	remote.Engines[0].Version = "0.2.0"
	writeManifest(t, pub, remote)

	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.FileServer(http.Dir(pub)))
	defer srv.Close()

	// Local install is at 0.3.0 with different binary bytes.
	local := t.TempDir()
	localBin := filepath.Join(local, "engines", "bin")
	_ = os.MkdirAll(localBin, 0o755)
	_ = os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(localBin, "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"), []byte("engine-v0.3.0-local"), 0o755)
	localManifest := Manifest{
		SchemaVersion: "1.0", Owner: RequiredOwner, Website: "https://alphaflux.net",
		License: "LICENSE-ENGINES.md", Attribution: AttributionNotice,
		Engines: []EngineEntry{{ID: "tyr-core", Version: "0.3.0", Binary: "engines/bin/mimir_tyr_engine.exe"}},
	}
	lraw, _ := json.Marshal(localManifest)
	_ = os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(localBin, "manifest.json"), lraw, 0o644)

	plan, err := CheckForUpdates(context.Background(), local, srv.URL)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CheckForUpdates: %v", err)
	}
	if len(plan.Changes) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("expected 1 change, got %+v", plan.Changes)
	}
	if _, err := ApplyUpdates(context.Background(), local, plan); !errors.Is(err, ErrDowngradeRefused) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrDowngradeRefused, got %v", err)
	}
	got, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(localBin, "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"))
	if string(got) != "engine-v0.3.0-local" {
		t.Fatalf("binary must be untouched after refused downgrade, got %q", got)
	}

	// With the force env, the same downgrade applies.
	t.Setenv("MIMIR_ENGINE_ALLOW_DOWNGRADE", "1")
	if _, err := ApplyUpdates(context.Background(), local, plan); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("forced downgrade should apply, got %v", err)
	}
	got, _ = os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(localBin, "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"))
	if string(got) != "engine-v0.2.0" {
		t.Fatalf("expected downgraded binary content, got %q", got)
	}
}

// N8: the updater downloads, verifies, and replaces the platform-resolved
// binary that Invoke executes, not the legacy top-level path.
func TestUpdateFlow_UsesPlatformBinary(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv("MIMIR_UPDATE_ALLOW_INSECURE", "1")
	hostKey := runtime.GOOS + "_" + runtime.GOARCH
	platName := fmt.Sprintf("mimir_tyr_engine_%s", hostKey)
	if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
		platName += ".exe"
	}
	platRel := "engines/bin/" + platName

	pub := t.TempDir()
	pubBin := filepath.Join(pub, "engines", "bin")
	_ = os.MkdirAll(pubBin, 0o755)
	_ = os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(pubBin, "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"), []byte("legacy-remote"), 0o755)
	_ = os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(pubBin, platName), []byte("platform-remote-v0.3.0"), 0o755)
	legSum, legSize, _ := FileSHA256(filepath.Join(pubBin, "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"))
	platSum, platSize, _ := FileSHA256(filepath.Join(pubBin, platName))
	m := Manifest{
		SchemaVersion: "1.0", Owner: RequiredOwner, Website: "https://alphaflux.net",
		License: "LICENSE-ENGINES.md", Attribution: AttributionNotice,
		Engines: []EngineEntry{{
			ID: "tyr-core", Version: "0.3.0",
			Binary: "engines/bin/mimir_tyr_engine.exe", SHA256: legSum, SizeBytes: legSize,
			Platforms: map[string]PlatformBinary{
				hostKey: {Binary: platRel, SHA256: platSum, SizeBytes: platSize},
			},
		}},
	}
	writeManifest(t, pub, m)
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.FileServer(http.Dir(pub)))
	defer srv.Close()

	local := t.TempDir()
	localBin := filepath.Join(local, "engines", "bin")
	_ = os.MkdirAll(localBin, 0o755)
	_ = os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(localBin, "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"), []byte("legacy-local-stale"), 0o755)
	_ = os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(localBin, platName), []byte("platform-old"), 0o755)

	plan, err := CheckForUpdates(context.Background(), local, srv.URL)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CheckForUpdates: %v", err)
	}
	if len(plan.Changes) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("expected 1 change (platform binary), got %+v", plan.Changes)
	}
	if _, err := ApplyUpdates(context.Background(), local, plan); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ApplyUpdates: %v", err)
	}
	plat, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(localBin, platName))
	if string(plat) != "platform-remote-v0.3.0" {
		t.Fatalf("platform binary not updated, got %q", plat)
	}
	leg, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(localBin, "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"))
	if string(leg) != "legacy-local-stale" {
		t.Fatalf("legacy binary must be untouched on a platform host, got %q", leg)
	}
}

// FIX 1 (audit): the https-only rule was validated on the initial URL only,
// so a redirect could silently downgrade an update download to plain http
// on any host. The download client must refuse non-https redirect targets
// (unless the operator opted into an insecure channel) and cap redirects.
func TestHTTPGet_RefusesRedirectToPlainHTTP(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv("MIMIR_UPDATE_ALLOW_INSECURE", "")
	target := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		_, _ = w.Write([]byte("downgraded-payload"))
	}))
	defer target.Close()
	entry := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		http.Redirect(w, r, target.URL+"/file", http.StatusFound)
	}))
	defer entry.Close()

	body, err := httpGet(context.Background(), entry.URL+"/start", 1<<20)
	if !errors.Is(err, ErrInsecureRedirect) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrInsecureRedirect, got err=%v body=%q", err, body)
	}
}

func TestHTTPGet_FollowsRedirectChainWithinCap(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv("MIMIR_UPDATE_ALLOW_INSECURE", "1")
	srv := httptest.NewServer(redirectChainHandler(3))
	defer srv.Close()

	body, err := httpGet(context.Background(), srv.URL+"/hop?n=0", 1<<20)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("redirect chain within the cap should succeed: %v", err)
	}
	if string(body) != "landed" {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected body %q", body)
	}
}

func TestHTTPGet_TooManyRedirects(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv("MIMIR_UPDATE_ALLOW_INSECURE", "1")
	srv := httptest.NewServer(redirectChainHandler(7))
	defer srv.Close()

	_, err := httpGet(context.Background(), srv.URL+"/hop?n=0", 1<<20)
	if !errors.Is(err, ErrTooManyRedirects) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrTooManyRedirects, got %v", err)
	}
}

// redirectChainHandler redirects /hop?n=k to k+1 while k < hops, then
// serves the final payload.
func redirectChainHandler(hops int) http.Handler {
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	mux.HandleFunc("/hop", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		n, _ := strconv.Atoi(r.URL.Query().Get("n"))
		if n < hops {
			http.Redirect(w, r, fmt.Sprintf("/hop?n=%d", n+1), http.StatusFound)
			return
		}
		_, _ = w.Write([]byte("landed"))
	})
	return mux
}

// The policy unit test covers the https side of the rule, which the live
// httptest servers above cannot exercise (their certificates are not
// trusted by the default transport, so the first hop would fail before
// any redirect is offered).
func TestUpdateRedirectPolicy(t *testing.T) {
	mkReq := func(rawurl string) *http.Request {
		t.Helper()
		req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, rawurl, nil)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return req
	}
	via := func(n int) []*http.Request {
		out := make([]*http.Request, n)
		for i := range out {
			out[i] = mkReq("https://updates.example.com/start")
		}
		return out
	}

	t.Run("https target allowed without override", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Setenv("MIMIR_UPDATE_ALLOW_INSECURE", "")
		if err := updateRedirectPolicy(mkReq("https://cdn.example.com/bin"), via(1)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("https redirect target should be allowed, got %v", err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("http target refused without override", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Setenv("MIMIR_UPDATE_ALLOW_INSECURE", "")
		if err := updateRedirectPolicy(mkReq("http://cdn.example.com/bin"), via(1)); !errors.Is(err, ErrInsecureRedirect) {
			t.Fatalf("expected ErrInsecureRedirect, got %v", err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("http target allowed with override", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Setenv("MIMIR_UPDATE_ALLOW_INSECURE", "1")
		if err := updateRedirectPolicy(mkReq("http://cdn.example.com/bin"), via(1)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("override should allow http redirect target, got %v", err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("fifth redirect allowed, sixth refused", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Setenv("MIMIR_UPDATE_ALLOW_INSECURE", "")
		if err := updateRedirectPolicy(mkReq("https://cdn.example.com/bin"), via(5)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("fifth redirect should be allowed, got %v", err)
		}
		if err := updateRedirectPolicy(mkReq("https://cdn.example.com/bin"), via(6)); !errors.Is(err, ErrTooManyRedirects) {
			t.Fatalf("expected ErrTooManyRedirects, got %v", err)
		}
	})
}

// setRemoteVersion rewrites the version of the first engine in a
// published tree's manifest, leaving the hashes untouched.
func setRemoteVersion(t *testing.T, pub, version string) {
	t.Helper()
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(pub, "engines", "bin", "manifest.json"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var remote Manifest
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &remote); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	remote.Engines[0].Version = version
	writeManifest(t, pub, remote)
}

// writeLocalInstall creates a local install tree: one tyr-core binary
// with the given content and a local manifest claiming the given version.
func writeLocalInstall(t *testing.T, version, payload string) string {
	t.Helper()
	local := t.TempDir()
	localBin := filepath.Join(local, "engines", "bin")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(localBin, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(localBin, "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"), []byte(payload), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	localManifest := Manifest{
		SchemaVersion: "1.0", Owner: RequiredOwner, Website: "https://alphaflux.net",
		License: "LICENSE-ENGINES.md", Attribution: AttributionNotice,
		Engines: []EngineEntry{{ID: "tyr-core", Version: version, Binary: "engines/bin/mimir_tyr_engine.exe"}},
	}
	raw, _ := json.Marshal(localManifest)
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(localBin, "manifest.json"), raw, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return local
}

// FIX 2 (audit): downgrade protection treated an unparseable version pair
// as a pass. For an engine that is already installed, an unparseable
// remote version means "not a downgrade" cannot be proven, so the update
// must be refused unless forced.
func TestApplyUpdates_RefusesUnparseableRemoteForInstalled(t *testing.T) {
	pub, _ := publishTree(t, "engine-banana", RequiredOwner)
	setRemoteVersion(t, pub, "banana")
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.FileServer(http.Dir(pub)))
	defer srv.Close()

	local := writeLocalInstall(t, "0.3.0", "engine-v0.3.0-local")
	plan, err := CheckForUpdates(context.Background(), local, srv.URL)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CheckForUpdates: %v", err)
	}
	if len(plan.Changes) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("expected 1 change, got %+v", plan.Changes)
	}
	if _, err := ApplyUpdates(context.Background(), local, plan); !errors.Is(err, ErrUnverifiableVersion) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrUnverifiableVersion for installed engine with unparseable remote version, got %v", err)
	}
	got, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(local, "engines", "bin", "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"))
	if string(got) != "engine-v0.3.0-local" {
		t.Fatalf("binary must be untouched after refusal, got %q", got)
	}

	// The downgrade override forces it through.
	t.Setenv("MIMIR_ENGINE_ALLOW_DOWNGRADE", "1")
	if _, err := ApplyUpdates(context.Background(), local, plan); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("forced update should apply, got %v", err)
	}
	got, _ = os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(local, "engines", "bin", "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"))
	if string(got) != "engine-banana" {
		t.Fatalf("expected remote binary after forced update, got %q", got)
	}
}

// FIX 2: the mirror image. An installed engine whose LOCAL version is
// unparseable cannot be ordered against the remote either; refuse.
func TestApplyUpdates_RefusesUnparseableLocalForInstalled(t *testing.T) {
	pub, _ := publishTree(t, "engine-v0.2.0", RequiredOwner)
	setRemoteVersion(t, pub, "0.2.0")
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.FileServer(http.Dir(pub)))
	defer srv.Close()

	local := writeLocalInstall(t, "weird-local", "engine-weird")
	plan, err := CheckForUpdates(context.Background(), local, srv.URL)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CheckForUpdates: %v", err)
	}
	if len(plan.Changes) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("expected 1 change, got %+v", plan.Changes)
	}
	if _, err := ApplyUpdates(context.Background(), local, plan); !errors.Is(err, ErrUnverifiableVersion) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrUnverifiableVersion for installed engine with unparseable local version, got %v", err)
	}
	got, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(local, "engines", "bin", "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"))
	if string(got) != "engine-weird" {
		t.Fatalf("binary must be untouched after refusal, got %q", got)
	}
}

// FIX 2: a brand new engine (no local version at all) keeps the
// permissive path even when its remote version is unparseable.
func TestApplyUpdates_NewEngineUnparseableVersionAllowed(t *testing.T) {
	pub, _ := publishTree(t, "engine-banana", RequiredOwner)
	setRemoteVersion(t, pub, "banana")
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.FileServer(http.Dir(pub)))
	defer srv.Close()

	local := t.TempDir() // nothing installed
	plan, err := CheckForUpdates(context.Background(), local, srv.URL)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CheckForUpdates: %v", err)
	}
	if len(plan.Changes) != 1 || plan.Changes[0].LocalVersion != "none" {
		t.Fatalf("expected one missing_local change, got %+v", plan.Changes)
	}
	if _, err := ApplyUpdates(context.Background(), local, plan); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("new engine install should be allowed, got %v", err)
	}
	got, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(local, "engines", "bin", "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"))
	if string(got) != "engine-banana" {
		t.Fatalf("expected installed binary, got %q", got)
	}
}

// writeUntrackedBinary creates a local tree holding a tyr-core binary
// that no local manifest tracks: engines/bin has the binary and nothing
// else. CheckForUpdates reports such an engine with LocalVersion
// "unknown" and Reason "new".
func writeUntrackedBinary(t *testing.T, payload string) string {
	t.Helper()
	local := t.TempDir()
	localBin := filepath.Join(local, "engines", "bin")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(localBin, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(localBin, "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"), []byte(payload), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return local
}

// An on-disk binary the local manifest does not track is still an
// installed binary: something is already there and would be replaced.
// When the remote version is unparseable there is nothing verifiable
// about the replacement at all, so the apply must refuse with
// ErrUnverifiableVersion, the same as for a tracked install. The plan
// flags the change up front with Reason "new_unverifiable" so the
// refusal does not surprise the operator at apply time.
func TestApplyUpdates_RefusesUnparseableRemoteForUntrackedBinary(t *testing.T) {
	pub, _ := publishTree(t, "engine-banana", RequiredOwner)
	setRemoteVersion(t, pub, "banana")
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.FileServer(http.Dir(pub)))
	defer srv.Close()

	local := writeUntrackedBinary(t, "untracked-binary")
	plan, err := CheckForUpdates(context.Background(), local, srv.URL)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CheckForUpdates: %v", err)
	}
	if len(plan.Changes) != 1 || plan.Changes[0].LocalVersion != "unknown" {
		t.Fatalf("expected one untracked change, got %+v", plan.Changes)
	}
	if plan.Changes[0].Reason != "new_unverifiable" {
		t.Fatalf("plan must flag the coming refusal with Reason new_unverifiable, got %q", plan.Changes[0].Reason)
	}
	if _, err := ApplyUpdates(context.Background(), local, plan); !errors.Is(err, ErrUnverifiableVersion) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrUnverifiableVersion for untracked binary with unparseable remote version, got %v", err)
	}
	got, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(local, "engines", "bin", "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"))
	if string(got) != "untracked-binary" {
		t.Fatalf("binary must be untouched after refusal, got %q", got)
	}

	// The downgrade override forces it through.
	t.Setenv("MIMIR_ENGINE_ALLOW_DOWNGRADE", "1")
	if _, err := ApplyUpdates(context.Background(), local, plan); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("forced update should apply, got %v", err)
	}
	got, _ = os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(local, "engines", "bin", "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"))
	if string(got) != "engine-banana" {
		t.Fatalf("expected remote binary after forced update, got %q", got)
	}
}

// The mirror image for an untracked binary: a parseable remote version
// keeps the permissive path. There is no local version to order the
// update against, but the incoming version is a real, orderable one,
// and CheckForUpdates diffs binaries by hash, so a changed binary is a
// normal update. Reason stays "new".
func TestApplyUpdates_UntrackedBinaryParseableRemoteAllowed(t *testing.T) {
	pub, _ := publishTree(t, "engine-v0.3.0", RequiredOwner) // remote version 0.3.0
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.FileServer(http.Dir(pub)))
	defer srv.Close()

	local := writeUntrackedBinary(t, "untracked-binary")
	plan, err := CheckForUpdates(context.Background(), local, srv.URL)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CheckForUpdates: %v", err)
	}
	if len(plan.Changes) != 1 || plan.Changes[0].LocalVersion != "unknown" {
		t.Fatalf("expected one untracked change, got %+v", plan.Changes)
	}
	if plan.Changes[0].Reason != "new" {
		t.Fatalf("parseable remote version must keep Reason new, got %q", plan.Changes[0].Reason)
	}
	if _, err := ApplyUpdates(context.Background(), local, plan); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("untracked binary update with parseable remote version should apply, got %v", err)
	}
	got, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(local, "engines", "bin", "mimir_tyr_engine.exe"))
	if string(got) != "engine-v0.3.0" {
		t.Fatalf("expected remote binary after update, got %q", got)
	}
}


==============================================================================
FILE: internal/ingest/ingest.go

// Package ingest implements Mímir's built-in GitIngest engine ("Gjallarhorn-Ingest")
// and Yggdrasil Mind Map builder. It turns any local directory or Git repository URL
// into:
//  1. A GitIngest-formatted text digest (Directory structure tree + FILE blocks)
//  2. A structured Yggdrasil Mind Map (nodes, symbols, imports, and test links)
//  3. Persistent Cortex neurons so Mímir and the Liquid AI d1-omni-600M Decision
//     Model can query the repository's Mind Map across sessions.
package ingest

import (
	"bufio"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/cortex"
)

const (
	DefaultMaxFileSize = 32 * 1024 * 1024 // 32 MB per file so large GitIngest .txt dumps in INGEST/ are indexed
	DefaultMaxFiles    = 1500
)

// Options configures a repository or directory ingestion run.
type Options struct {
	Source        string // local path or https://github.com/owner/repo URL
	Branch        string
	MaxFileSize   int64
	MaxFiles      int
	WriteDigestTo string // optional file path to write digest.txt
}

// MindNode represents one file or module inside the Yggdrasil Mind Map.
type MindNode struct {
	Path     string   `json:"path"`
	Language string   `json:"language"`
	Bytes    int64    `json:"bytes"`
	Symbols  []string `json:"symbols,omitempty"` // top exported functions/types/classes
	Imports  []string `json:"imports,omitempty"` // imported packages/modules
	IsTest   bool     `json:"is_test,omitempty"` // true for *_test.go, *.spec.ts, test_*.py
	Summary  string   `json:"summary,omitempty"` // first doc comment or header line
}

// MindMap is Mímir's structured structural graph ("Yggdrasil Mind Map") of a repository.
// It is stored in the Cortex and fed directly into the Liquid AI d1-omni-600M Decision Model.
type MindMap struct {
	RepoName   string     `json:"repo_name"`
	Source     string     `json:"source"`
	IngestedAt string     `json:"ingested_at"`
	TotalFiles int        `json:"total_files"`
	TotalBytes int64      `json:"total_bytes"`
	EstTokens  int        `json:"est_tokens"`
	Tree       string     `json:"tree"`
	Nodes      []MindNode `json:"nodes"`
}

// Result contains the full GitIngest output and Yggdrasil Mind Map.
type Result struct {
	Summary      string  `json:"summary"`
	Tree         string  `json:"tree"`
	Digest       string  `json:"digest"`
	MindMap      MindMap `json:"mind_map"`
	NeuronsSaved int     `json:"neurons_saved"`
}

var defaultIgnoredDirs = map[string]bool{
	".git": true, ".hg": true, ".svn": true, ".mimir": true,
	"node_modules": true, "vendor": true, "dist": true, "build": true,
	"target": true, "__pycache__": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true,
	".next": true, ".idea": true, ".vscode": true, "bin": true, "obj": true,
	"INGEST": true,
}

var binaryExts = map[string]bool{
	".exe": true, ".dll": true, ".so": true, ".dylib": true, ".a": true,
	".png": true, ".jpg": true, ".jpeg": true, ".gif": true, ".webp": true,
	".ico": true, ".pdf": true, ".zip": true, ".tar": true, ".gz": true,
	".7z": true, ".mp3": true, ".mp4": true, ".wav": true, ".woff": true,
	".woff2": true, ".ttf": true, ".eot": true, ".pyc": true, ".db": true,
	".sqlite": true, ".docx": true, ".xlsx": true, ".pptx": true,
}

var (
	reGoSym   = regexp.MustCompile(`^(?:func|type)\s+(?:\([^)]+\)\s*)?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`)
	rePySym   = regexp.MustCompile(`^(?:def|class|async\s+def)\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`)
	reTSSym   = regexp.MustCompile(`^(?:export\s+)?(?:async\s+)?(?:function|class|interface|type|const)\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`)
	reRustSym = regexp.MustCompile(`^(?:pub\s+)?(?:async\s+)?(?:fn|struct|enum|trait|mod)\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`)
)

// Run ingests a local path or remote Git URL (GitIngest-compatible), builds the
// Yggdrasil Mind Map, optionally writes a digest file, and stores the Mind Map +
// module digests into Cortex memory if store != nil.
func Run(ctx context.Context, opts Options, store cortex.Store) (*Result, error) {
	if opts.MaxFileSize <= 0 {
		opts.MaxFileSize = DefaultMaxFileSize
	}
	if opts.MaxFiles <= 0 {
		opts.MaxFiles = DefaultMaxFiles
	}
	source := strings.TrimSpace(opts.Source)
	if source == "" {
		source = "."
	}

	rootDir := source
	var repoName string
	if isGitURL(source) {
		tmpDir, cleanup, err := shallowClone(ctx, source, opts.Branch)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		defer cleanup()
		rootDir = tmpDir
		repoName = repoNameFromURL(source)
	} else {
		abs, err := filepath.Abs(source)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		rootDir = abs
		repoName = filepath.Base(abs)
	}

	var relPaths []string
	var nodes []MindNode
	var filesBuf strings.Builder
	var totalBytes int64

	err := filepath.WalkDir(rootDir, func(path string, d os.DirEntry, walkErr error) error {
		if walkErr != nil {
			return nil
		}
		if d.IsDir() {
			if path != rootDir && (defaultIgnoredDirs[d.Name()] || strings.HasPrefix(d.Name(), ".")) {
				return filepath.SkipDir
			}
			return nil
		}
		if len(relPaths) >= opts.MaxFiles {
			return nil
		}
		ext := strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(d.Name()))
		if binaryExts[ext] || strings.HasSuffix(d.Name(), ".lock") {
			return nil
		}
		info, err := d.Info()
		if err != nil || info.Size() == 0 || info.Size() > opts.MaxFileSize {
			return nil
		}
		data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
		if err != nil || isBinaryContent(data) {
			return nil
		}

		rel, err := filepath.Rel(rootDir, path)
		if err != nil {
			rel = d.Name()
		}
		rel = filepath.ToSlash(rel)
		relPaths = append(relPaths, rel)
		totalBytes += info.Size()

		content := string(data)
		node := extractMindNode(rel, content, info.Size())
		nodes = append(nodes, node)

		filesBuf.WriteString("================================================\n")
		filesBuf.WriteString("FILE: " + rel + "\n")
		filesBuf.WriteString("================================================\n")
		filesBuf.WriteString(content)
		if !strings.HasSuffix(content, "\n") {
			filesBuf.WriteString("\n")
		}
		filesBuf.WriteString("\n")
		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	sort.Strings(relPaths)
	treeStr := renderTree(repoName, relPaths)
	estTokens := int(totalBytes / 4)

	summary := fmt.Sprintf(
		"Repository: %s\nFiles analyzed: %d\nEstimated tokens: ~%dk (%d bytes)",
		repoName, len(relPaths), estTokens/1000, totalBytes,
	)

	digest := "Directory structure:\n" + treeStr + "\n" + filesBuf.String()
	if opts.WriteDigestTo != "" {
		_ = os.WriteFile(opts.WriteDigestTo, []byte(digest), 0o644)
	}

	mm := MindMap{
		RepoName:   repoName,
		Source:     source,
		IngestedAt: time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
		TotalFiles: len(relPaths),
		TotalBytes: totalBytes,
		EstTokens:  estTokens,
		Tree:       treeStr,
		Nodes:      nodes,
	}

	saved := 0
	if store != nil {
		saved = persistToCortex(ctx, store, mm)
	}

	return &Result{
		Summary:      summary,
		Tree:         treeStr,
		Digest:       digest,
		MindMap:      mm,
		NeuronsSaved: saved,
	}, nil
}

// FormatMindMapCompact produces a dense, LLM- and Decision-Model-friendly view of
// the Yggdrasil Mind Map (directory tree + file symbols + test map).
func FormatMindMapCompact(mm MindMap, maxNodes int) string {
	if maxNodes <= 0 {
		maxNodes = 60
	}
	var b strings.Builder
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Yggdrasil Mind Map: %s (%d files, ~%dk tokens)\n", mm.RepoName, mm.TotalFiles, mm.EstTokens/1000)
	b.WriteString("Directory Tree:\n")
	b.WriteString(mm.Tree)
	b.WriteString("\nSymbol & Dependency Graph:\n")
	for i, n := range mm.Nodes {
		if i >= maxNodes {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  ... and %d more files\n", len(mm.Nodes)-maxNodes)
			break
		}
		tag := n.Language
		if n.IsTest {
			tag += ",test"
		}
		line := fmt.Sprintf("  • %s [%s]", n.Path, tag)
		if len(n.Symbols) > 0 {
			line += " symbols={" + strings.Join(n.Symbols, ", ") + "}"
		}
		if n.Summary != "" {
			line += " // " + n.Summary
		}
		b.WriteString(line + "\n")
	}
	return b.String()
}

func persistToCortex(ctx context.Context, store cortex.Store, mm MindMap) int {
	saved := 0
	// 1. Save the master Yggdrasil Mind Map overview neuron
	compact := FormatMindMapCompact(mm, 80)
	rootID, err := store.PutNeuron(ctx, cortex.Neuron{
		Kind:    "mindmap",
		Layer:   "context",
		Title:   "Yggdrasil Mind Map: " + mm.RepoName,
		Content: compact,
	})
	if err == nil {
		saved++
	}
	// 2. Save raw JSON mindmap for programmatic Decision Model lookup
	if rawJSON, err := json.Marshal(mm); err == nil {
		if _, err := store.PutNeuron(ctx, cortex.Neuron{
			Kind:    "mindmap_json",
			Layer:   "context",
			Title:   "MindMap JSON: " + mm.RepoName,
			Content: string(rawJSON),
		}); err == nil {
			saved++
		}
	}
	// 3. Group nodes by top-level directory/module and store module-level knowledge neurons + synapses
	byDir := map[string][]MindNode{}
	for _, n := range mm.Nodes {
		dir := filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(n.Path))
		byDir[dir] = append(byDir[dir], n)
	}
	for dir, dirNodes := range byDir {
		var sb strings.Builder
		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "[Repo %s · Module %s] ", mm.RepoName, dir)
		for _, dn := range dirNodes {
			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%s", filepath.Base(dn.Path))
			if len(dn.Symbols) > 0 {
				fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "(%s)", strings.Join(dn.Symbols, ","))
			}
			sb.WriteString("; ")
		}
		modID, err := store.PutNeuron(ctx, cortex.Neuron{
			Kind:    cortex.KindSource,
			Layer:   "context",
			Title:   mm.RepoName + "/" + dir,
			Content: sb.String(),
		})
		if err == nil {
			saved++
			if rootID != "" {
				_ = store.Relate(ctx, cortex.Synapse{
					From: rootID,
					To:   modID,
					Kind: "references",
				})
			}
		}
	}
	// 4. When ingesting a flat reference corpus like INGEST/ (1 dir, multiple .txt/.md dumps),
	// also persist a dedicated searchable neuron per ingested reference file.
	if len(byDir) <= 2 && len(mm.Nodes) > 3 {
		for _, n := range mm.Nodes {
			if n.Language != "txt" && n.Language != "md" {
				continue
			}
			desc := fmt.Sprintf("[Ingested Corpus %s/%s (%d KB)] %s", mm.RepoName, n.Path, n.Bytes/1024, n.Summary)
			if len(n.Symbols) > 0 {
				desc += " | Key items: " + strings.Join(n.Symbols, ", ")
			}
			nID, err := store.PutNeuron(ctx, cortex.Neuron{
				Kind:    cortex.KindSource,
				Layer:   "context",
				Title:   mm.RepoName + "/" + n.Path,
				Content: desc,
			})
			if err == nil {
				saved++
				if rootID != "" {
					_ = store.Relate(ctx, cortex.Synapse{
						From: rootID,
						To:   nID,
						Kind: "references",
					})
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return saved
}

// LatestMindMap retrieves the most recently ingested Yggdrasil MindMap from Cortex memory.
func LatestMindMap(store cortex.Store) (*MindMap, bool) {
	if store == nil {
		return nil, false
	}
	all := store.All()
	for i := len(all) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		if all[i].Kind == "mindmap_json" {
			var mm MindMap
			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(all[i].Content), &mm); err == nil && mm.RepoName != "" {
				return &mm, true
			}
		}
	}
	return nil, false
}

func extractMindNode(relPath, content string, size int64) MindNode {
	ext := strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(relPath))
	lang := strings.TrimPrefix(ext, ".")
	if lang == "" {
		lang = "text"
	}
	lowerPath := strings.ToLower(relPath)
	isTest := strings.Contains(lowerPath, "_test.") ||
		strings.Contains(lowerPath, ".test.") ||
		strings.Contains(lowerPath, ".spec.") ||
		strings.HasPrefix(filepath.Base(lowerPath), "test_")

	var symbols []string
	var imports []string
	summary := ""

	sc := bufio.NewScanner(strings.NewReader(content))
	sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 64*1024), 2*1024*1024)
	for sc.Scan() {
		line := strings.TrimSpace(sc.Text())
		if line == "" {
			continue
		}
		if summary == "" && (strings.HasPrefix(line, "//") || strings.HasPrefix(line, "# ") || strings.HasPrefix(line, "Repository:")) {
			clean := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimLeft(line, "/# "))
			if len(clean) > 6 && len(clean) < 120 {
				summary = clean
			}
		}
		if len(symbols) < 12 {
			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "FILE: ") {
				symbols = append(symbols, strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(line, "FILE: ")))
			} else if strings.HasPrefix(line, "## ") {
				symbols = append(symbols, strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(line, "## ")))
			} else {
				for _, re := range []*regexp.Regexp{reGoSym, rePySym, reTSSym, reRustSym} {
					if m := re.FindStringSubmatch(line); len(m) > 1 {
						symbols = append(symbols, m[1])
						break
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if len(imports) < 8 && (strings.HasPrefix(line, "import ") || strings.HasPrefix(line, "from ") || strings.HasPrefix(line, "use ")) {
			imports = append(imports, line)
		}
	}

	return MindNode{
		Path:     relPath,
		Language: lang,
		Bytes:    size,
		Symbols:  symbols,
		Imports:  imports,
		IsTest:   isTest,
		Summary:  summary,
	}
}

func renderTree(repoName string, relPaths []string) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("└── " + repoName + "/\n")
	limit := len(relPaths)
	if limit > 120 {
		limit = 120
	}
	for i := 0; i < limit; i++ {
		prefix := "    ├── "
		if i == limit-1 && len(relPaths) <= limit {
			prefix = "    └── "
		}
		b.WriteString(prefix + relPaths[i] + "\n")
	}
	if len(relPaths) > limit {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "    └── ... (%d more files)\n", len(relPaths)-limit)
	}
	return b.String()
}

func isBinaryContent(data []byte) bool {
	check := len(data)
	if check > 1024 {
		check = 1024
	}
	for i := 0; i < check; i++ {
		if data[i] == 0 {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

func isGitURL(s string) bool {
	return strings.HasPrefix(s, "http://") || strings.HasPrefix(s, "https://") || strings.HasPrefix(s, "git@")
}

func repoNameFromURL(u string) string {
	u = strings.TrimRight(u, "/")
	u = strings.TrimSuffix(u, ".git")
	parts := strings.Split(u, "/")
	if len(parts) > 0 && parts[len(parts)-1] != "" {
		return parts[len(parts)-1]
	}
	return "repo"
}

func shallowClone(ctx context.Context, url, branch string) (string, func(), error) {
	// Sanitize url and branch to prevent git argument injection (F9)
	if strings.HasPrefix(url, "-") {
		return "", func() {}, fmt.Errorf("invalid repository url %q: cannot start with dash", url)
	}
	if strings.HasPrefix(branch, "-") {
		return "", func() {}, fmt.Errorf("invalid branch %q: cannot start with dash", branch)
	}

	tmp, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "mimir-gitingest-*")
	if err != nil {
		return "", func() {}, err
	}
	cleanup := func() { _ = os.RemoveAll(tmp) }

	args := []string{"clone", "--depth=1", "--single-branch"}
	if branch != "" {
		args = append(args, "--branch", branch)
	}
	// Use explicit "--" separator to prevent url from being parsed as options
	args = append(args, "--", url, tmp)

	cctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 60*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(cctx, "git", args...)
	if out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
		cleanup()
		return "", func() {}, fmt.Errorf("git clone %s: %v (%s)", url, err, strings.TrimSpace(string(out)))
	}
	return tmp, cleanup, nil
}

package ingest

import (
	"context"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/cortex"
