func TestIngestLocalDirAndPersistMindMapToCortex(t *testing.T) {
	tmp := t.TempDir()
	srcDir := filepath.Join(tmp, "sample-repo")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(srcDir, "pkg"), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	goFile := `// Package pkg provides sample math helpers.
package pkg

import "fmt"

func ComputeHash(input string) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("%x", input)
}

type Engine struct {
	Name string
}
`
	testFile := `package pkg

import "testing"

func TestComputeHash(t *testing.T) {
	if ComputeHash("a") == "" {
		t.Fatal("empty")
	}
}
`
	_ = os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(srcDir, "pkg", "engine.go"), []byte(goFile), 0o644)
	_ = os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(srcDir, "pkg", "engine_test.go"), []byte(testFile), 0o644)

	store, err := cortex.NewMemoryStoreAt(filepath.Join(tmp, "cortex.json"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	digestPath := filepath.Join(tmp, "digest.txt")
	res, err := Run(context.Background(), Options{
		Source:        srcDir,
		WriteDigestTo: digestPath,
	}, store)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ingest.Run failed: %v", err)
	}
	if res.MindMap.TotalFiles != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("got %d files, want 2", res.MindMap.TotalFiles)
	}
	if res.NeuronsSaved < 2 {
		t.Errorf("expected at least 2 neurons saved to Cortex, got %d", res.NeuronsSaved)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(res.Digest, "FILE: pkg/engine.go") {
		t.Errorf("digest missing FILE header:\n%s", res.Digest)
	}

	mm, ok := LatestMindMap(store)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("expected LatestMindMap to recover MindMap from Cortex")
	}
	compact := FormatMindMapCompact(*mm, 20)
	if !strings.Contains(compact, "ComputeHash") || !strings.Contains(compact, "Engine") {
		t.Errorf("expected MindMap compact output to include extracted symbols, got:\n%s", compact)
	}
}

==============================================================================
package llm

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"strings"
)

// RepairJSON repairs common malformed JSON emitted by smaller local models (7B-32B)
// and fast streaming tool calls (inspired by charmbracelet/fantasy jsonrepair).
// It strips markdown code fences, removes trailing commas before '}' or ']',
// and balances unclosed quotes, brackets, and braces.
func RepairJSON(raw string) string {
	s := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
	if s == "" {
		return "{}"
	}

	// Fast path: already valid JSON.
	if json.Valid([]byte(s)) {
		return s
	}

	// 1. Strip markdown code fences (e.g. ```json ... ```)
	if strings.HasPrefix(s, "```") {
		if nl := strings.IndexByte(s, '\n'); nl >= 0 {
			s = s[nl+1:]
		} else {
			s = strings.TrimPrefix(s, "```json")
			s = strings.TrimPrefix(s, "```")
		}
		if end := strings.LastIndex(s, "```"); end >= 0 {
			s = s[:end]
		}
		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
		if json.Valid([]byte(s)) {
			return s
		}
	}

	// 2. Scan character by character to remove trailing commas and track open delimiters.
	var out strings.Builder
	out.Grow(len(s) + 8)

	var stack []byte
	inString := false
	escaped := false

	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		ch := s[i]
		if inString {
			out.WriteByte(ch)
			if escaped {
				escaped = false
			} else if ch == '\\' {
				escaped = true
			} else if ch == '"' {
				inString = false
			}
			continue
		}

		switch ch {
		case '"':
			inString = true
			out.WriteByte(ch)
		case '{':
			stack = append(stack, '}')
			out.WriteByte(ch)
		case '[':
			stack = append(stack, ']')
			out.WriteByte(ch)
		case '}', ']':
			if len(stack) > 0 && stack[len(stack)-1] == ch {
				stack = stack[:len(stack)-1]
			}
			out.WriteByte(ch)
		case ',':
			// Skip trailing comma if the next non-whitespace character closes an object/array
			// or if we are at the end of the string.
			j := i + 1
			for j < len(s) && (s[j] == ' ' || s[j] == '\t' || s[j] == '\n' || s[j] == '\r') {
				j++
			}
			if j >= len(s) || s[j] == '}' || s[j] == ']' {
				continue
			}
			out.WriteByte(ch)
		default:
			out.WriteByte(ch)
		}
	}

	// 3. Close dangling escape or string quote.
	if inString {
		if escaped {
			out.WriteByte('\\')
		}
		out.WriteByte('"')
	}

	// 4. Close any unclosed objects or arrays in reverse order.
	for i := len(stack) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		out.WriteByte(stack[i])
	}

	repaired := out.String()
	if json.Valid([]byte(repaired)) {
		return repaired
	}
	return s
}


==============================================================================
FILE: internal/llm/jsonrepair_test.go
==============================================================================
package llm

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"testing"
)

func TestRepairJSON(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		in   string
		want string
	}{
		{
			name: "empty string becomes empty object",
			in:   "   ",
			want: "path",
		},
		{
			name: "strips markdown code fence",
			in:   "```json\n{\"path\": \"main.go\"}\n```",
			want: "main.go",
		},
		{
			name: "removes trailing comma in object",
			in:   `{"path": "foo.go", "content": "bar", }`,
			want: "foo.go",
		},
		{
			name: "closes truncated string and object",
			in:   `{"path": "internal/agent/agent.go`,
			want: "internal/agent/agent.go",
		},
		{
			name: "closes nested array and object",
			in:   `{"questions": [{"question": "Which mode?", "header": "Mode", "options": [{"label": "Fast", "description": "Low latency"}`,
			want: "",
		},
	}

	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			got := RepairJSON(tc.in)
			if !json.Valid([]byte(got)) {
				t.Fatalf("RepairJSON(%q) produced invalid JSON: %q", tc.in, got)
			}
			var m map[string]any
			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(got), &m); err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("Unmarshal(%q) failed: %v", got, err)
			}
			if tc.name != "empty string becomes empty object" && tc.want != "" {
				if p, _ := m["path"].(string); p != tc.want {
					t.Fatalf("got path=%q, want %q", p, tc.want)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

package llm

import (
	"bufio"
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"sort"
	"strings"
)

// OpenAIProvider talks to any OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint with
// zero external dependencies - we own the wire format. This single client covers
// OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, Mistral, Cerebras, DeepInfra, Together, the Alibaba /
// Qwen compatible-mode, Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio, and Mímir's own gateway (F1).
type OpenAIProvider struct {
	IDStr   string
	BaseURL string // e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1 (trailing slash optional)
	APIKey  string // bearer token; may be empty for local servers
	Model   string // default model when a request leaves Model blank
	Client  *http.Client
}

func (p *OpenAIProvider) ID() string { return p.IDStr }

type oaFunction struct {
	Name        string `json:"name"`
	Arguments   string `json:"arguments"`
	Description string `json:"description,omitempty"`
	Parameters  any    `json:"parameters,omitempty"`
}

type oaToolCall struct {
	Index    int        `json:"index,omitempty"` // streaming only: which call a delta belongs to
	ID       string     `json:"id"`
	Type     string     `json:"type"`
	Function oaFunction `json:"function"`
}

type oaTool struct {
	Type     string     `json:"type"`
	Function oaFunction `json:"function"`
}

type oaMessage struct {
	Role       string       `json:"role"`
	Content    string       `json:"content"`
	ToolCalls  []oaToolCall `json:"tool_calls,omitempty"`
	ToolCallID string       `json:"tool_call_id,omitempty"`
}

type oaChoice struct {
	Message      oaMessage `json:"message"`
	Delta        oaMessage `json:"delta"`
	FinishReason string    `json:"finish_reason"`
}

type oaRequest struct {
	Model           string           `json:"model"`
	Messages        []oaMessage      `json:"messages"`
	Tools           []oaTool         `json:"tools,omitempty"`
	Stream          bool             `json:"stream"`
	StreamOptions   *oaStreamOptions `json:"stream_options,omitempty"`
	ReasoningEffort string           `json:"reasoning_effort,omitempty"`
}

type oaStreamOptions struct {
	IncludeUsage bool `json:"include_usage"`
}

type oaResponse struct {
	Choices []oaChoice `json:"choices"`
	Usage   *oaUsage   `json:"usage"`
}

type oaUsage struct {
	PromptTokens     int `json:"prompt_tokens"`
	CompletionTokens int `json:"completion_tokens"`
	TotalTokens      int `json:"total_tokens"`
}

func (u *oaUsage) toUsage() Usage {
	if u == nil {
		return Usage{}
	}
	return Usage{PromptTokens: u.PromptTokens, CompletionTokens: u.CompletionTokens}
}

func (p *OpenAIProvider) httpClient() *http.Client {
	if p.Client != nil {
		return p.Client
	}
	return http.DefaultClient
}

func (p *OpenAIProvider) baseURL() string { return strings.TrimRight(p.BaseURL, "/") }

func (p *OpenAIProvider) model(m string) string {
	if m != "" {
		return m
	}
	if p.Model != "" {
		return p.Model
	}
	return "default"
}

func toOpenAI(messages []Message) []oaMessage {
	out := make([]oaMessage, len(messages))
	for i, m := range messages {
		om := oaMessage{Role: m.Role, Content: m.Content, ToolCallID: m.ToolCallID}
		for _, tc := range m.ToolCalls {
			om.ToolCalls = append(om.ToolCalls, oaToolCall{
				ID: tc.ID, Type: "function",
				Function: oaFunction{Name: tc.Name, Arguments: tc.Arguments},
			})
		}
		out[i] = om
	}
	return out
}

func toOATools(schemas []ToolSchema) []oaTool {
	if len(schemas) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	out := make([]oaTool, len(schemas))
	for i, s := range schemas {
		params := s.Parameters
		if params == nil {
			params = map[string]any{"type": "object"}
		}
		out[i] = oaTool{Type: "function", Function: oaFunction{
			Name: s.Name, Description: s.Description, Parameters: params,
		}}
	}
	return out
}

// thinkOpen / thinkClose are the reasoning-model chain-of-thought delimiters. They
// are built by concatenation so the literal tag tokens never appear in this source
// file (which keeps tooling that scans for thinking blocks from mis-parsing it).
const (
	thinkOpen  = "<" + "think>"
	thinkClose = "<" + "/think>"
)

// stripThink removes a reasoning chain-of-thought block (the think delimiters) from
// a model reply so the visible answer (and stored memory) is clean. Reasoning models
// (e.g. Qwen3) wrap their thinking in these tags; the answer follows the closing tag.
func stripThink(s string) string {
	if i := strings.Index(s, thinkOpen); i >= 0 {
		if j := strings.Index(s[i:], thinkClose); j >= 0 {
			return strings.TrimSpace(s[i+j+len(thinkClose):])
		}
		return strings.TrimSpace(s[:i])
	}
	return s
}

// thinkStripper removes reasoning chain-of-thought blocks (the think delimiters)
// from a stream of text deltas - the streaming counterpart of stripThink. Reasoning
// models emit their thinking first; only the answer after the closing tag should
// reach the user. It buffers a few bytes at chunk boundaries so a delimiter split
// across two deltas is still detected.
type thinkStripper struct {
	buf     string
	inThink bool
}

// feed adds a delta and returns the visible text to emit now.
func (t *thinkStripper) feed(d string) string {
	t.buf += d
	var out strings.Builder
	for {
		if t.inThink {
			if i := strings.Index(t.buf, thinkClose); i >= 0 {
				t.buf = t.buf[i+len(thinkClose):]
				t.inThink = false
				continue
			}
			t.buf = tail(t.buf, len(thinkClose)-1)
			return out.String()
		}
		if i := strings.Index(t.buf, thinkOpen); i >= 0 {
			out.WriteString(t.buf[:i])
			t.buf = t.buf[i+len(thinkOpen):]
			t.inThink = true
			continue
		}
		keep := len(thinkOpen) - 1
		if keep > len(t.buf) {
			keep = len(t.buf)
		}
		out.WriteString(t.buf[:len(t.buf)-keep])
		t.buf = t.buf[len(t.buf)-keep:]
		return out.String()
	}
}

// flush returns any remaining visible text at end of stream (suppressing it if the
// stream ended mid-think, matching stripThink's behavior).
func (t *thinkStripper) flush() string {
	if t.inThink {
		t.buf = ""
		return ""
	}
	out := t.buf
	t.buf = ""
	return out
}

func tail(s string, n int) string {
	if len(s) <= n {
		return s
	}
	return s[len(s)-n:]
}

func (p *OpenAIProvider) post(ctx context.Context, req GenerateRequest) (*http.Response, error) {
	msgs := toOpenAI(req.Messages)
	if req.Effort == "off" && len(msgs) > 0 && msgs[0].Role == "system" {
		// Qwen3 / Ollama / local reasoning models honor /no_think in the system prompt
		// to skip chain-of-thought during fast mechanical tool loops (smolcoder pattern).
		if !strings.Contains(msgs[0].Content, "/no_think") {
			msgs[0].Content = "/no_think\n" + msgs[0].Content
		}
	}
	oReq := oaRequest{
		Model:    p.model(req.Model),
		Messages: msgs,
		Tools:    toOATools(req.Tools),
		Stream:   req.Stream,
	}
	if req.Effort == "low" || req.Effort == "medium" || req.Effort == "high" {
		oReq.ReasoningEffort = req.Effort
	}
	if req.Stream {
		oReq.StreamOptions = &oaStreamOptions{IncludeUsage: true}
	}
	body, err := json.Marshal(oReq)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	httpReq, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, p.baseURL()+"/chat/completions", bytes.NewReader(body))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	httpReq.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	if p.APIKey != "" {
		httpReq.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+p.APIKey)
	}
	return p.httpClient().Do(httpReq)
}

// Generate returns a complete (non-streamed) reply, including any tool calls.
func (p *OpenAIProvider) Generate(ctx context.Context, req GenerateRequest) (GenerateResponse, error) {
	req.Stream = false
	resp, err := p.post(ctx, req)
	if err != nil {
		return GenerateResponse{}, err
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		b, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
		return GenerateResponse{}, fmt.Errorf("provider %s: HTTP %d: %s", p.IDStr, resp.StatusCode, string(b))
	}
	var r oaResponse
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&r); err != nil {
		return GenerateResponse{}, err
	}
	if len(r.Choices) == 0 {
		return GenerateResponse{}, fmt.Errorf("provider %s: empty choices", p.IDStr)
	}
	ch := r.Choices[0]
	var calls []ToolCall
	for _, tc := range ch.Message.ToolCalls {
		calls = append(calls, ToolCall{ID: tc.ID, Name: tc.Function.Name, Arguments: tc.Function.Arguments})
	}
	return GenerateResponse{Content: stripThink(ch.Message.Content), ToolCalls: calls, FinishReason: ch.FinishReason, Usage: r.Usage.toUsage()}, nil
}

// Stream returns a channel of streamed events: text deltas (with reasoning
// think-blocks stripped), ending with a Done event that carries any tool calls the
// model issued (accumulated across the stream's fragmented tool-call deltas).
func (p *OpenAIProvider) Stream(ctx context.Context, req GenerateRequest) (<-chan StreamEvent, error) {
	req.Stream = true
	resp, err := p.post(ctx, req)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		b, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
		resp.Body.Close()
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("provider %s: HTTP %d: %s", p.IDStr, resp.StatusCode, string(b))
	}
	out := make(chan StreamEvent)
	go func() {
		defer close(out)
		defer resp.Body.Close()
		var ts thinkStripper
		toolAcc := map[int]*ToolCall{}
		var lastUsage Usage
		finish := func() {
			if vis := ts.flush(); vis != "" {
				out <- StreamEvent{Delta: vis}
			}
			var tcs []ToolCall
			if len(toolAcc) > 0 {
				idxs := make([]int, 0, len(toolAcc))
				for i := range toolAcc {
					idxs = append(idxs, i)
				}
				sort.Ints(idxs)
				for _, i := range idxs {
					tcs = append(tcs, *toolAcc[i])
				}
			}
			out <- StreamEvent{Done: true, ToolCalls: tcs, Usage: lastUsage}
		}
		scanner := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)
		for scanner.Scan() {
			line := scanner.Text()
			if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "data:") {
				continue
			}
			data := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(line, "data:"))
			if data == "" {
				continue
			}
			if data == "[DONE]" {
				finish()
				return
			}
			var r oaResponse
			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(data), &r); err != nil {
				continue
			}
			if r.Usage != nil {
				lastUsage = r.Usage.toUsage()
			}
			if len(r.Choices) == 0 {
				continue
			}
			ch := r.Choices[0]
			if d := ch.Delta.Content; d != "" {
				if vis := ts.feed(d); vis != "" {
					out <- StreamEvent{Delta: vis}
				}
			}
			for _, tc := range ch.Delta.ToolCalls {
				cur, ok := toolAcc[tc.Index]
				if !ok {
					cur = &ToolCall{}
					toolAcc[tc.Index] = cur
				}
				if tc.ID != "" {
					cur.ID = tc.ID
				}
				if tc.Function.Name != "" {
					cur.Name = tc.Function.Name
				}
				cur.Arguments += tc.Function.Arguments
			}
			if ch.FinishReason != "" {
				finish()
				return
			}
		}
		if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
			out <- StreamEvent{Err: err}
			return
		}
		finish()
	}()
	return out, nil
}

func TestOpenAIProviderStream(t *testing.T) {
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
		flusher, _ := w.(http.Flusher)
		writeDelta := func(delta string) {
			b, _ := json.Marshal(oaResponse{Choices: []oaChoice{{Delta: oaMessage{Content: delta}}}})
			_, _ = w.Write([]byte("data: " + string(b) + "\n\n"))
			flusher.Flush()
		}
		writeDelta("hel")
		writeDelta("lo")
		_, _ = w.Write([]byte("data: [DONE]\n\n"))
		flusher.Flush()
	}))
	defer srv.Close()

	p := &OpenAIProvider{IDStr: "fake", BaseURL: srv.URL + "/v1", APIKey: "k", Model: "m"}
	ch, err := p.Stream(context.Background(), GenerateRequest{
		Messages: []Message{{Role: "user", Content: "hi"}},
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Stream: %v", err)
	}
	var got string
	for ev := range ch {
		if ev.Err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("stream error: %v", ev.Err)
		}
		got += ev.Delta
		if ev.Done {
			break
		}
	}
	if got != "hello" {
		t.Errorf("streamed %q, want %q", got, "hello")
	}
}

// TestOpenAIProviderStreamToolCalls proves Stream accumulates tool calls that arrive
// fragmented across many deltas (id + name once, arguments in pieces) and surfaces
// them on the final Done event.
func TestOpenAIProviderStreamToolCalls(t *testing.T) {
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
		flusher, _ := w.(http.Flusher)
		write := func(v any) {
			b, _ := json.Marshal(v)
			_, _ = w.Write([]byte("data: " + string(b) + "\n\n"))
			flusher.Flush()
		}
		tc := func(id, name, args string) oaResponse {
			return oaResponse{Choices: []oaChoice{{Delta: oaMessage{ToolCalls: []oaToolCall{
				{Type: "function", ID: id, Function: oaFunction{Name: name, Arguments: args}},
			}}}}}
		}
		write(tc("call_1", "bash", ""))
		write(tc("", "", `{"command":`))
		write(tc("", "", `"echo hi"}`))
		write(oaResponse{Choices: []oaChoice{{FinishReason: "tool_calls"}}})
		_, _ = w.Write([]byte("data: [DONE]\n\n"))
		flusher.Flush()
	}))
	defer srv.Close()

	p := &OpenAIProvider{IDStr: "fake", BaseURL: srv.URL + "/v1", APIKey: "k", Model: "m"}
	ch, err := p.Stream(context.Background(), GenerateRequest{Messages: []Message{{Role: "user", Content: "run echo"}}})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Stream: %v", err)
	}
	var got []ToolCall
	var done bool
	for ev := range ch {
		if ev.Err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("stream error: %v", ev.Err)
		}
		if ev.Done {
			done = true
			got = ev.ToolCalls
			break
		}
	}
	if !done {
		t.Fatal("stream did not signal Done")
	}
	if len(got) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("tool calls = %d, want 1 (%+v)", len(got), got)
	}
	if got[0].ID != "call_1" || got[0].Name != "bash" || got[0].Arguments != `{"command":"echo hi"}` {
		t.Errorf("accumulated tool call = %+v", got[0])
	}
}

		flusher.Flush()

		t.Fatalf("Stream: %v", err)
	}
	var got string

			t.Fatalf("stream error: %v", ev.Err)
		}
		got += ev.Delta
		if ev.Done {
			break
		}
	}
	if got != "The answer is 42." {
		t.Errorf("streamed %q, want %q (think block must be stripped)", got, "The answer is 42.")
	}
}

// Package llm defines the model provider abstraction. Mímir talks to any model
// (cloud or local) through this interface - BYOK or Ollama (F1).
package llm

import "context"

// Message is one turn in a conversation.
type Message struct {
	Role       string // system | user | assistant | tool
	Content    string
	ToolCalls  []ToolCall // assistant messages may carry tool calls
	ToolCallID string     // tool-role messages reference the call id
}

// ToolCall is a model-issued tool invocation.
type ToolCall struct {
	ID        string
	Name      string
	Arguments string // raw JSON object string
}

// ToolSchema describes a tool to the model.
type ToolSchema struct {
	Name        string
	Description string
	Parameters  any // a JSON Schema object
}

// GenerateRequest is a provider-agnostic completion request.
type GenerateRequest struct {
	Model    string
	Messages []Message
	Tools    []ToolSchema
	Stream   bool
	Effort   string // optional reasoning effort: off | low | medium | high (smolcoder /effort pattern)
}

// GenerateResponse is a provider-agnostic completion response.
type GenerateResponse struct {
	Content      string
	ToolCalls    []ToolCall
	FinishReason string
	Usage        Usage
}

// StreamEvent is one chunk of a streamed response. Text arrives as Delta events;
// the final event has Done set and carries any ToolCalls the model issued
// (accumulated across the stream's fragmented tool-call deltas) and the token Usage.
type StreamEvent struct {
	Delta     string
	ToolCalls []ToolCall
	Usage     Usage
	Done      bool
	Err       error
}

// Provider talks to one model backend. Implementations wrap OpenAI-compatible
// APIs (cloud) or Ollama (local).
type Provider interface {
	// ID returns the provider id (e.g. "ollama", "openai").
	ID() string
	// Generate returns a full (non-streamed) completion, including any tool calls.
	Generate(ctx context.Context, req GenerateRequest) (GenerateResponse, error)
	// Stream returns a channel of streamed chunks.
	Stream(ctx context.Context, req GenerateRequest) (<-chan StreamEvent, error)
}

// Registry maps provider ids to Providers.
type Registry struct {
	providers map[string]Provider
}

// NewRegistry returns an empty provider registry.
func NewRegistry() *Registry {
	return &Registry{providers: map[string]Provider{}}
}

// Register adds a provider to the registry.
func (r *Registry) Register(p Provider) {
	r.providers[p.ID()] = p
}

// Get returns a provider by id.
func (r *Registry) Get(id string) (Provider, bool) {
	p, ok := r.providers[id]
	return p, ok
}

FILE: internal/llm/usage.go
==============================================================================
package llm

import (
	"sort"
	"sync"
)

// Usage is the token accounting for one completion (F37.1).
type Usage struct {
	PromptTokens     int
	CompletionTokens int
}

// Total returns prompt + completion tokens.
func (u Usage) Total() int { return u.PromptTokens + u.CompletionTokens }

// IsZero reports whether no usage was recorded.
func (u Usage) IsZero() bool { return u.PromptTokens == 0 && u.CompletionTokens == 0 }

// ModelUsage is the accumulated usage for one model.
type ModelUsage struct {
	Model            string `json:"model"`
	Local            bool   `json:"local"`
	Requests         int    `json:"requests"`
	PromptTokens     int    `json:"prompt_tokens"`
	CompletionTokens int    `json:"completion_tokens"`
	TotalTokens      int    `json:"total_tokens"`
}

// Tracker accumulates token usage per model. It is safe for concurrent use (the
// streaming server handles many turns at once). It feeds the per-project dashboard
// (E69 / F52): total + per-model tokens, sorted most-to-least, local vs cloud.
type Tracker struct {
	mu      sync.Mutex
	byModel map[string]*ModelUsage
}

// NewTracker returns an empty usage tracker.
func NewTracker() *Tracker { return &Tracker{byModel: map[string]*ModelUsage{}} }

// Record adds one completion's usage to the model's totals. Zero usage is ignored.
func (t *Tracker) Record(model string, local bool, u Usage) {
	if u.IsZero() {
		return
	}
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	mu, ok := t.byModel[model]
	if !ok {
		mu = &ModelUsage{Model: model, Local: local}
		t.byModel[model] = mu
	}
	mu.Requests++
	mu.PromptTokens += u.PromptTokens
	mu.CompletionTokens += u.CompletionTokens
	mu.TotalTokens += u.Total()
}

// Snapshot returns per-model usage sorted most-tokens to least (F52.3).
func (t *Tracker) Snapshot() []ModelUsage {
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	out := make([]ModelUsage, 0, len(t.byModel))
	for _, mu := range t.byModel {
		out = append(out, *mu)
	}
	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].TotalTokens > out[j].TotalTokens })
	return out
}

// TotalTokens returns the sum of all tokens across every model.
func (t *Tracker) TotalTokens() int {
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	total := 0
	for _, mu := range t.byModel {
		total += mu.TotalTokens
	}
	return total
}

// Package plugins holds a draft Go-native plugin API contract.
//
// Status: this package is an unwired draft. Nothing in the Mimir binary
// imports it, no loader reads it at runtime, and no plugin can register
// with the shipped agent through it today. It is kept as a design sketch
// only. The planned plugin system is the Wasm plugin host (capability
// granted, sandboxed, hot swappable), which supersedes this contract;
// see the design-law notes in the project blueprint.
package plugins

// Manifest declares a plugin's identity + contracts.
type Manifest struct {
	ID        string
	Version   string
	Contracts []string // capabilities this plugin registers
}

// Plugin is the single entrypoint a plugin exports.
type Plugin interface {
	Manifest() Manifest
	Register(api API) error
}

// API is the only surface plugins use to extend Mimir (draft contract, see package status above).
// Plugins import this package only; never core internals.
type API interface {
	RegisterProvider(def ProviderDef) error
	RegisterTool(def ToolDef) error
	RegisterHook(def HookDef) error
	RegisterChannel(def ChannelDef) error
	RegisterHarness(def HarnessDef) error
	RegisterCapability(def CapabilityDef) error
	RegisterCommand(def CommandDef) error
}

// Def types are intentionally minimal here; fleshed out per capability epic.
type ProviderDef struct{ ID, Dialect, BaseURL string }
type ToolDef struct{ Name, Description string }
type HookDef struct{ Event string }
type ChannelDef struct{ ID string }
type HarnessDef struct{ ID string }
type CapabilityDef struct{ Kind string }
type CommandDef struct{ Name string }

// Registry collects plugin registrations (one-way: plugins register, core reads).
type Registry struct {
	plugins   map[string]Manifest
	tools     []ToolDef
	providers []ProviderDef
	hooks     []HookDef
}

func NewRegistry() *Registry {
	return &Registry{plugins: map[string]Manifest{}}
}

// Load registers a plugin and records its manifest.
func (r *Registry) Load(p Plugin) error {
	m := p.Manifest()
	if err := p.Register(r); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	r.plugins[m.ID] = m
	return nil
}

func (r *Registry) RegisterProvider(d ProviderDef) error {
	r.providers = append(r.providers, d)
	return nil
}
func (r *Registry) RegisterTool(d ToolDef) error             { r.tools = append(r.tools, d); return nil }
func (r *Registry) RegisterHook(d HookDef) error             { r.hooks = append(r.hooks, d); return nil }
func (r *Registry) RegisterChannel(d ChannelDef) error       { return nil }
func (r *Registry) RegisterHarness(d HarnessDef) error       { return nil }
func (r *Registry) RegisterCapability(d CapabilityDef) error { return nil }
func (r *Registry) RegisterCommand(d CommandDef) error       { return nil }

FILE: internal/policy/gate.go

package policy

import "strings"

// Decision is the result of evaluating a tool call against policy.
type Decision string

const (
	Allow           Decision = "allow"
	Deny            Decision = "deny"
	RequireApproval Decision = "require_approval"
)

// Request is a tool call to evaluate.
type Request struct {
	Tool string
	Args map[string]any
}

// Rule is one allow/deny/require_approval rule (pattern on tool/command).
type Rule struct {
	Pattern  string // tool name pattern or wildcard "*"
	Command  string // optional command pattern for shell/bash tools
	Decision Decision
}

// Gate is the fail-closed policy gate (E4.1, ADR-009).
type Gate struct {
	rules      []Rule
	defaultDec Decision
}

// NewGate returns a fail-closed gate (default-deny).
func NewGate() *Gate {
	return &Gate{defaultDec: Deny}
}

// DefaultDevGate returns a standard developer policy gate:
// read-only tools and harmless ops are Allowed; mutations & shell require approval or specific allow.
func DefaultDevGate() *Gate {
	g := NewGate()
	// Safe read-only inspections
	g.AddRule(Rule{Pattern: "read_file", Decision: Allow})
	g.AddRule(Rule{Pattern: "list_directory", Decision: Allow})
	g.AddRule(Rule{Pattern: "todo", Decision: Allow})
	g.AddRule(Rule{Pattern: "question", Decision: Allow})
	g.AddRule(Rule{Pattern: "load_skill", Decision: Allow})
	g.AddRule(Rule{Pattern: "epistemic_audit", Decision: Allow})
	g.AddRule(Rule{Pattern: "web_seo_audit", Decision: Allow})
	// SDLC self-guards sign_off/set_method in waterfall mode, and ingest_repo
	// only reads a source into the Cortex digest; both must be reachable or
	// default-deny silently blocks headline features (gate regression).
	g.AddRule(Rule{Pattern: "sdlc", Decision: Allow})
	g.AddRule(Rule{Pattern: "ingest_repo", Decision: Allow})

	// Modifications require approval unless bypass mode or explicit rule
	g.AddRule(Rule{Pattern: "write_file", Decision: RequireApproval})
	g.AddRule(Rule{Pattern: "edit_block", Decision: RequireApproval})
	g.AddRule(Rule{Pattern: "bash", Decision: RequireApproval})
	g.AddRule(Rule{Pattern: "shell", Decision: RequireApproval})
	return g
}

func (g *Gate) AddRule(r Rule) {
	g.rules = append(g.rules, r)
}

// Evaluate returns the decision for a request (default-deny; last matching rule wins).
func (g *Gate) Evaluate(req Request) Decision {
	decision := g.defaultDec
	for _, r := range g.rules {
		if match(r.Pattern, req.Tool) {
			if r.Command != "" && (req.Tool == "bash" || req.Tool == "shell") {
				cmd, _ := req.Args["command"].(string)
				if match(r.Command, cmd) {
					decision = r.Decision
				}
			} else {
				decision = r.Decision
			}
		}
	}
	return decision
}

func match(pattern, s string) bool {
	if pattern == "*" || pattern == s {
		return true
	}
	// Case-insensitive substring match when pattern starts with contains:
	if len(pattern) > 9 && pattern[:9] == "contains:" {
		return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(s), strings.ToLower(pattern[9:]))
	}
	return false
}

package policy

import "testing"

func TestGateFailClosedByDefault(t *testing.T) {
	g := NewGate()
	if d := g.Evaluate(Request{Tool: "bash"}); d != Deny {
		t.Errorf("default decision = %q, want deny (fail-closed)", d)
	}
}

func TestGateAllowRule(t *testing.T) {
	g := NewGate()
	g.AddRule(Rule{Pattern: "read_file", Decision: Allow})
	if d := g.Evaluate(Request{Tool: "read_file"}); d != Allow {
		t.Errorf("decision = %q, want allow", d)
	}
	if d := g.Evaluate(Request{Tool: "bash"}); d != Deny {
		t.Errorf("unmatched decision = %q, want deny", d)
	}
}

func TestGateWildcard(t *testing.T) {
	g := NewGate()
	g.AddRule(Rule{Pattern: "*", Decision: RequireApproval})
	if d := g.Evaluate(Request{Tool: "anything"}); d != RequireApproval {
		t.Errorf("wildcard decision = %q, want require_approval", d)
	}
}

func TestGateCommandContentMatching(t *testing.T) {
	g := NewGate()
	// Disallow rm -rf or destructive commands
	g.AddRule(Rule{Pattern: "bash", Command: "contains:rm -rf", Decision: Deny})
	// Allow safe test commands
	g.AddRule(Rule{Pattern: "bash", Command: "contains:go test", Decision: Allow})

	if d := g.Evaluate(Request{Tool: "bash", Args: map[string]any{"command": "go test ./..."}}); d != Allow {
		t.Errorf("safe command decision = %q, want allow", d)
	}
	if d := g.Evaluate(Request{Tool: "bash", Args: map[string]any{"command": "rm -rf /"}}); d != Deny {
		t.Errorf("destructive command decision = %q, want deny", d)
	}
}

func TestDefaultDevGate(t *testing.T) {
	g := DefaultDevGate()
	if d := g.Evaluate(Request{Tool: "read_file"}); d != Allow {
		t.Errorf("read_file decision = %q, want allow", d)
	}
	if d := g.Evaluate(Request{Tool: "write_file"}); d != RequireApproval {
		t.Errorf("write_file decision = %q, want require_approval", d)
	}
	if d := g.Evaluate(Request{Tool: "bash"}); d != RequireApproval {
		t.Errorf("bash decision = %q, want require_approval", d)
	}
	if d := g.Evaluate(Request{Tool: "unknown_dangerous"}); d != Deny {
		t.Errorf("unregistered tool decision = %q, want deny (fail-closed)", d)
	}
}

// TestDefaultDevGateCoversRegisteredTools proves the gate regression is fixed:
// the sdlc and ingest_repo tools (registered in tools.Default) must not fall
// through to default-deny in the shipped gate.
func TestDefaultDevGateCoversRegisteredTools(t *testing.T) {
	g := DefaultDevGate()
	for _, tool := range []string{"sdlc", "ingest_repo"} {
		if d := g.Evaluate(Request{Tool: tool}); d == Deny {
			t.Errorf("%s decision = deny, want non-deny (tool must stay reachable)", tool)
		}
	}
}


==============================================================================

// Package relay implements the encrypted mobile companion relay.
//
// Direction convention for frame nonces: the desktop host and the phone
// share ONE AEAD key, so the 8-byte counter field inside each frame nonce
// is partitioned by direction. Frames encrypted by the host (this
// package) always carry the TOP BIT of the counter set; frames sent by
// the phone client must carry it clear. Each side tracks replay only in
// the partition it receives. Without this partition, host frame 1 and
// phone frame 1 would reuse the identical (key, nonce) pair and break
// ChaCha20-Poly1305 confidentiality. This package is the host side: it
// sets the bit when encrypting and requires it clear when decrypting.
// Phone clients must do the mirror image.
package relay

import (
	"crypto/cipher"
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/subtle"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/binary"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/skip2/go-qrcode"
	"golang.org/x/crypto/chacha20poly1305"
	"golang.org/x/crypto/curve25519"
)

const (
	// UnpairedSessionTTL bounds how long an unpaired pairing session stays
	// valid. The QR code is a bearer credential until pairing completes, so
	// the window to use it is short.
	UnpairedSessionTTL = 10 * time.Minute
	// MaxLiveSessions caps the number of pairing sessions a Manager holds at
	// once, so the unauthenticated session-creation endpoint cannot be used
	// to grow memory without bound.
	MaxLiveSessions = 64
	// DefaultPairedSessionTTL bounds how long a paired session stays live,
	// measured from the moment pairing completes. Without it, paired
	// sessions would occupy the MaxLiveSessions cap forever. A Manager can
	// override it via its PairedSessionTTL field.
	DefaultPairedSessionTTL = 24 * time.Hour
	// nonceDirectionBit partitions the frame counter field of the AEAD
	// nonce by direction: the host (this package) sets it on frames it
	// encrypts, the phone clears it on frames it sends. See the package
	// documentation.
	nonceDirectionBit = uint64(1) << 63
)

// Session represents an end-to-end encrypted mobile companion pairing session.
// Powered by Alpha Flux LLC Proprietary Engines (https://alphaflux.net).
type Session struct {
	ID        string    `json:"id"`
	Host      string    `json:"host"`
	PublicKey string    `json:"public_key"`
	Nonce     string    `json:"nonce"`
	CreatedAt time.Time `json:"created_at"`

	privateKey [32]byte
	publicKey  [32]byte
	sharedKey  [32]byte
	paired     bool
	pairedAt   time.Time // when pairing completed; paired expiry is measured from here
	aead       cipher.AEAD
	sendSeq    uint64 // last counter used by EncryptFrame, before the direction bit is applied
	recvSeq    uint64 // highest counter accepted by DecryptFrame, in the phone (bit-clear) partition
	mu         sync.RWMutex
	listeners  map[chan []byte]struct{}
}

// PairURI generates the mimir:// URL format for QR-code pairing.
func (s *Session) PairURI() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("mimir://pair?id=%s&host=%s&pubkey=%s&nonce=%s",
		s.ID, s.Host, s.PublicKey, s.Nonce)
}

// GenerateQRCodeASCII generates a human-readable ASCII QR code for terminal pairing.
func (s *Session) GenerateQRCodeASCII() (string, error) {
	qr, err := qrcode.New(s.PairURI(), qrcode.Medium)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to generate qr code: %w", err)
	}
	return qr.ToSmallString(false), nil
}

// Manager coordinates mobile pairing sessions and encrypted relays.
type Manager struct {
	sessions map[string]*Session
	mu       sync.RWMutex
	// PairedSessionTTL bounds the lifetime of a paired session, measured
	// from pairing. Zero means DefaultPairedSessionTTL.
	PairedSessionTTL time.Duration
}

// NewManager creates a thread-safe relay session manager.
func NewManager() *Manager {
	return &Manager{
		sessions:         make(map[string]*Session),
		PairedSessionTTL: DefaultPairedSessionTTL,
	}
}

// pairedTTL resolves the effective paired-session lifetime.
func (m *Manager) pairedTTL() time.Duration {
	if m.PairedSessionTTL > 0 {
		return m.PairedSessionTTL
	}
	return DefaultPairedSessionTTL
}

// CreateSession generates a new X25519 ephemeral keypair and session tokens.
// Expired sessions (unpaired or paired) are purged first, so the cap counts
// live sessions only, and creation fails once MaxLiveSessions live sessions
// exist.
func (m *Manager) CreateSession(host string) (*Session, error) {
	var privKey [32]byte
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, privKey[:]); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to generate private key: %w", err)
	}

	var pubKey [32]byte
	curve25519.ScalarBaseMult(&pubKey, &privKey)

	nonceBytes := make([]byte, 16)
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, nonceBytes); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to generate nonce: %w", err)
	}

	// 128-bit session ID: the ID alone must not be guessable, because it is
	// the only handle needed to reach the pairing endpoints.
	sessIDBytes := make([]byte, 16)
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, sessIDBytes); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to generate session id: %w", err)
	}

	sessID := fmt.Sprintf("pair_%s", base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(sessIDBytes))
	pubKeyB64 := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(pubKey[:])
	nonceB64 := base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(nonceBytes)

	sess := &Session{
		ID:         sessID,
		Host:       host,
		PublicKey:  pubKeyB64,
		Nonce:      nonceB64,
		CreatedAt:  time.Now(),
		privateKey: privKey,
		publicKey:  pubKey,
		listeners:  make(map[chan []byte]struct{}),
	}

	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	m.purgeExpiredLocked(time.Now())
	if len(m.sessions) >= MaxLiveSessions {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("relay: too many live pairing sessions (max %d), try again later", MaxLiveSessions)
	}
	m.sessions[sessID] = sess
	slog.Info("relay session created", "session_id", sessID, "host", host)

	return sess, nil
}

// purgeExpiredLocked deletes sessions past their TTL: unpaired sessions
// past UnpairedSessionTTL from creation, paired sessions past the
// Manager's paired TTL from pairing. Callers must hold m.mu.
func (m *Manager) purgeExpiredLocked(now time.Time) {
	for id, s := range m.sessions {
		if m.expiredLocked(s, now) {
			m.expireLocked(id, s)
		}
	}
}

// expireLocked deletes an expired session and tears it down, so expiry
// terminates the session exactly the way RemoveSession does: the keys
// are wiped, the session unpairs, and listener channels are closed,
// which is what ends any live StreamHandler's loop. Callers must hold
// m.mu. teardown acquires only the session's own lock; the manager lock
// is always taken before the session lock (expiredLocked already reads
// session state under m.mu), so the ordering stays consistent and
// teardown cannot deadlock here. Its channel closes cannot race
// Broadcast sends either, because both happen under the session lock.
func (m *Manager) expireLocked(id string, s *Session) {
	delete(m.sessions, id)
	paired := s.IsPaired()
	s.teardown()
	slog.Info("relay session expired", "session_id", id, "paired", paired)
}

// expiredLocked reports whether s has outlived its TTL at now. Callers
// must hold m.mu.
func (m *Manager) expiredLocked(s *Session, now time.Time) bool {
	if s.IsPaired() {
		pairedAt := s.pairedAtTime()
		return !pairedAt.IsZero() && now.Sub(pairedAt) > m.pairedTTL()
	}
	return now.Sub(s.CreatedAt) > UnpairedSessionTTL
}

// pairedAtTime returns when pairing completed (zero if unpaired).
func (s *Session) pairedAtTime() time.Time {
	s.mu.RLock()
	defer s.mu.RUnlock()
	return s.pairedAt
}

// GetSession returns a session by ID if found. Sessions past their TTL
// (unpaired or paired) are treated as gone and removed lazily.
func (m *Manager) GetSession(id string) (*Session, bool) {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	s, ok := m.sessions[id]
	if !ok {
		return nil, false
	}
	if m.expiredLocked(s, time.Now()) {
		m.expireLocked(id, s)
		return nil, false
	}
	return s, true
}

// RemoveSession ends a pairing immediately: the session is dropped from
// the Manager, its keys are wiped, its listeners are closed, and it can
// no longer encrypt or decrypt. It returns true if a session with that
// ID existed; an unknown ID is a no-op and returns false.
func (m *Manager) RemoveSession(id string) bool {
	m.mu.Lock()
	s, ok := m.sessions[id]
	if ok {
		delete(m.sessions, id)
	}
	m.mu.Unlock()
	if !ok {
		return false
	}
	s.teardown()
	slog.Info("relay session removed", "session_id", id)
	return true
}

// teardown wipes a session's key material and closes its listeners, so a
// removed or expired session fails closed instead of silently continuing.
func (s *Session) teardown() {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	for ch := range s.listeners {
		close(ch)
	}
	s.listeners = make(map[chan []byte]struct{})
	s.aead = nil
	s.paired = false
	s.sharedKey = [32]byte{}
}

// CompletePairing performs the X25519 Diffie-Hellman exchange with the
// client public key. The caller must present the pairing token carried in
// the QR code (the session Nonce): without it, anyone who learns the
// session ID could pair their own key and hijack the session. The token is
// compared in constant time. Pairing is one-shot: an already paired
// session rejects further attempts instead of silently replacing its keys.
func (s *Session) CompletePairing(pairingToken, clientPubKeyB64 string) error {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()

	// Pairing is a trust boundary: failures are logged with a static
	// reason only. The token, the keys, and the shared secret are never
	// logged.
	fail := func(reason string, err error) error {
		slog.Warn("relay pairing failed", "session_id", s.ID, "reason", reason)
		return err
	}

	if s.paired {
		return fail("already paired", errors.New("session is already paired"))
	}
	if time.Since(s.CreatedAt) > UnpairedSessionTTL {
		return fail("session expired", errors.New("pairing session has expired"))
	}

	presented, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(strings.TrimSpace(pairingToken))
	if err != nil {
		return fail("invalid pairing token", errors.New("invalid pairing token"))
	}
	expected, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(s.Nonce)
	if err != nil {
		return fail("invalid pairing token", errors.New("invalid pairing token"))
	}
	if subtle.ConstantTimeCompare(presented, expected) != 1 {
		return fail("invalid pairing token", errors.New("invalid pairing token"))
	}

	clientPubBytes, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(clientPubKeyB64)
	if err != nil || len(clientPubBytes) != 32 {
		return fail("invalid client public key", errors.New("invalid client public key: must be 32 bytes base64"))
	}

	// X25519 (unlike ScalarMult) rejects low-order client public keys: it
	// errors when the resulting shared secret is all zeros, which is what
	// a low-order point forces. Without this, an attacker could pair with
	// a known, all-zero session key.
	shared, err := curve25519.X25519(s.privateKey[:], clientPubBytes)
	if err != nil {
		return fail("key agreement failed", errors.New("invalid client public key: key agreement failed"))
	}
	var sharedKey [32]byte
	copy(sharedKey[:], shared)

	aead, err := chacha20poly1305.New(sharedKey[:])
	if err != nil {
		return fail("aead init failed", fmt.Errorf("failed to initialize chacha20poly1305 aead: %w", err))
	}

	s.sharedKey = sharedKey
	s.aead = aead
	s.paired = true
	s.pairedAt = time.Now()
	slog.Info("relay session paired", "session_id", s.ID)
	return nil
}

// IsPaired checks if the session has established shared secret.
func (s *Session) IsPaired() bool {
	s.mu.RLock()
	defer s.mu.RUnlock()
	return s.paired
}

// EncryptFrame seals arbitrary data using ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD. The AEAD
// nonce is derived from a per-session monotonic counter (stored in the last
// 8 bytes of the nonce, big endian), never random, so a nonce can never
// repeat under the session key. Host frames carry the counter's top bit set
// (the host direction partition), so they can never collide with a phone
// frame at the same counter value. The wire format stays nonce || ciphertext.
func (s *Session) EncryptFrame(plaintext []byte) ([]byte, error) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return s.encryptFrameLocked(plaintext)
}

// encryptFrameLocked seals plaintext. Callers must hold s.mu.
func (s *Session) encryptFrameLocked(plaintext []byte) ([]byte, error) {
	if !s.paired || s.aead == nil {
		return nil, errors.New("session is not paired yet")
	}

	s.sendSeq++
	nonce := make([]byte, s.aead.NonceSize())
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(nonce[len(nonce)-8:], s.sendSeq|nonceDirectionBit)

	ciphertext := s.aead.Seal(nonce, nonce, plaintext, nil)
	return ciphertext, nil
}

// DecryptFrame decrypts and verifies a sealed ciphertext frame sent by
// the phone. Frames whose counter is at or below the highest counter
// already accepted are rejected, so a captured frame cannot be replayed.
// Frames carrying the host direction bit are also rejected: they belong
// to the partition this side encrypts into, so one arriving here is a
// reflection, not a phone frame.
func (s *Session) DecryptFrame(ciphertext []byte) ([]byte, error) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if !s.paired || s.aead == nil {
		return nil, errors.New("session is not paired yet")
	}

	nonceSize := s.aead.NonceSize()
	if len(ciphertext) < nonceSize {
		return nil, errors.New("ciphertext too short: missing nonce")
	}

	nonce := ciphertext[:nonceSize]
	sealed := ciphertext[nonceSize:]

	counter := binary.BigEndian.Uint64(nonce[len(nonce)-8:])
	if counter&nonceDirectionBit != 0 {
		return nil, errors.New("frame carries the host direction bit; reflected frames are rejected")
	}
	if counter <= s.recvSeq {
		return nil, errors.New("replayed or out-of-order frame rejected")
	}

	plaintext, err := s.aead.Open(nil, nonce, sealed, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("authentication error: %w", err)
	}
	s.recvSeq = counter
	return plaintext, nil
}

// Broadcast sends an encrypted JSON message to all connected SSE/WS mobile
// listeners. There is deliberately no plaintext path: broadcasting on an
// unpaired session is an error, never a cleartext send.
func (s *Session) Broadcast(msgType string, payload any) error {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()

	if !s.paired || s.aead == nil {
		return errors.New("session is not paired; refusing to broadcast without encryption")
	}

	raw, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
		"type":      msgType,
		"payload":   payload,
		"timestamp": time.Now().Unix(),
	})
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	data, err := s.encryptFrameLocked(raw)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	for ch := range s.listeners {
		select {
		case ch <- data:
		default:
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// RegisterListener adds a listener channel.
func (s *Session) RegisterListener(ch chan []byte) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.listeners[ch] = struct{}{}
}

// UnregisterListener removes a listener channel, closing it if it was
// registered. The membership check keeps a teardown that already closed
// the channel from causing a double close here.
func (s *Session) UnregisterListener(ch chan []byte) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if _, ok := s.listeners[ch]; ok {
		delete(s.listeners, ch)
		close(ch)
	}
}

// StreamHandler exposes Server-Sent Events (SSE) for the mobile app stream.
// The stream carries encrypted frames for the paired phone only, so it
// refuses unpaired sessions and sends no wildcard CORS header.
func (s *Session) StreamHandler() http.HandlerFunc {
	return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		if !s.IsPaired() {
			http.Error(w, "session is not paired", http.StatusForbidden)
			return
		}

		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
		w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
		w.Header().Set("Connection", "keep-alive")

		flusher, ok := w.(http.Flusher)
		if !ok {
			http.Error(w, "Streaming unsupported", http.StatusInternalServerError)
			return
		}

		ch := make(chan []byte, 32)
		s.RegisterListener(ch)
		defer s.UnregisterListener(ch)

		// Initial connection frame
		if _, err := fmt.Fprintf(w, "event: connected\ndata: %s\n\n", s.ID); err != nil {
			return
		}
		flusher.Flush()

		ctx := r.Context()
		for {
			select {
			case <-ctx.Done():
				return
			case msg, ok := <-ch:
				if !ok {
					return
				}
				b64 := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(msg)
				if _, err := fmt.Fprintf(w, "data: %s\n\n", b64); err != nil {
					return
				}
				flusher.Flush()
			}
		}
	}
}

FILE: internal/relay/happy_e2ee_test.go

package relay

import (
	"bytes"
	"crypto/cipher"
	"crypto/rand"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/binary"
	"io"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"golang.org/x/crypto/chacha20poly1305"
	"golang.org/x/crypto/curve25519"
)

func TestHappyE2EESessionFlow(t *testing.T) {
	mgr := NewManager()

	// 1. Host creates pairing session
	sess, err := mgr.CreateSession("192.168.0.83:8080")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to create session: %v", err)
	}
	if sess.ID == "" || sess.PublicKey == "" || sess.Nonce == "" {
		t.Fatalf("invalid session properties: %+v", sess)
	}

	// 2. Verify QR URI format
	uri := sess.PairURI()
	if !strings.HasPrefix(uri, "mimir://pair?") {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected pair URI: %s", uri)
	}

	// 3. Verify terminal ASCII QR code generation
	asciiQR, err := sess.GenerateQRCodeASCII()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to generate ascii qr: %v", err)
	}
	if len(asciiQR) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("empty ascii qr output")
	}

	// 4. Simulate client (phone) generating its own ephemeral X25519 keypair
	var clientPriv [32]byte
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, clientPriv[:]); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var clientPub [32]byte
	curve25519.ScalarBaseMult(&clientPub, &clientPriv)
	clientPubB64 := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(clientPub[:])

	// 5. Complete handshake pairing (requires the QR pairing token)
	if err := sess.CompletePairing(sess.Nonce, clientPubB64); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to complete pairing: %v", err)
	}
	if !sess.IsPaired() {
		t.Fatal("session expected to be paired")
	}

	// 6. Test Encrypt & Decrypt Frame in both directions. The host side
	// (this package) and the phone side use the same shared key but
	// disjoint nonce partitions, so each direction is exercised through
	// its own endpoint: the host seals and the phone opens, then the
	// phone seals and the host opens.
	msg := []byte("ApprovalRequest: Thor wants to write to internal/relay/relay.go")
	sealed, err := sess.EncryptFrame(msg)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to encrypt frame: %v", err)
	}

	phone := peerAEAD(t, sess, clientPriv)
	nonceSize := phone.NonceSize()
	plaintext, err := phone.Open(nil, sealed[:nonceSize], sealed[nonceSize:], nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("phone failed to decrypt host frame: %v", err)
	}
	if string(plaintext) != string(msg) {
		t.Fatalf("plaintext mismatch: expected %q, got %q", string(msg), string(plaintext))
	}

	reply := peerSeal(phone, 1, []byte("Approved"))
	got, err := sess.DecryptFrame(reply)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("host failed to decrypt phone frame: %v", err)
	}
	if string(got) != "Approved" {
		t.Fatalf("reply mismatch: got %q", string(got))
	}
}

func clientKeypair(t *testing.T) (priv [32]byte, pubB64 string) {
	t.Helper()
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, priv[:]); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var pub [32]byte
	curve25519.ScalarBaseMult(&pub, &priv)
	return priv, base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(pub[:])
}

func clientKeyB64(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	_, pubB64 := clientKeypair(t)
	return pubB64
}

// peerAEAD builds the phone side's AEAD for a paired session: the phone
// derives the same shared secret from its private key and the host public
// key carried in the pair URI.
func peerAEAD(t *testing.T, sess *Session, clientPriv [32]byte) cipher.AEAD {
	t.Helper()
	hostPub, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(sess.PublicKey)
	if err != nil || len(hostPub) != 32 {
		t.Fatalf("bad host public key: %v", err)
	}
	shared, err := curve25519.X25519(clientPriv[:], hostPub)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("phone key agreement: %v", err)
	}
	aead, err := chacha20poly1305.New(shared)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("phone aead: %v", err)
	}
	return aead
}

// peerSeal seals a phone-to-host frame the way a conforming phone client
// must: the counter lives in the last 8 bytes of the nonce with the
// direction bit CLEAR (the phone partition).
func peerSeal(aead cipher.AEAD, counter uint64, plaintext []byte) []byte {
	nonce := make([]byte, aead.NonceSize())
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(nonce[len(nonce)-8:], counter)
	return aead.Seal(nonce, nonce, plaintext, nil)
}

func pairedSessionWithClient(t *testing.T) (*Session, [32]byte) {
	t.Helper()
	mgr := NewManager()
	sess, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CreateSession: %v", err)
	}
	priv, pubB64 := clientKeypair(t)
	if err := sess.CompletePairing(sess.Nonce, pubB64); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CompletePairing: %v", err)
	}
	return sess, priv
}

func pairedSession(t *testing.T) *Session {
	t.Helper()
	mgr := NewManager()
	sess, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CreateSession: %v", err)
	}
	if err := sess.CompletePairing(sess.Nonce, clientKeyB64(t)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CompletePairing: %v", err)
	}
	return sess
}

// N3: pairing without the QR token (or with a wrong one) must fail, so
// knowing the session ID alone is not enough to hijack a session.
func TestCompletePairingRequiresToken(t *testing.T) {
	mgr := NewManager()
	sess, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CreateSession: %v", err)
	}
	pub := clientKeyB64(t)

	if err := sess.CompletePairing("", pub); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected error for empty pairing token")
	}
	if err := sess.CompletePairing("AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA", pub); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected error for wrong pairing token")
	}
	if sess.IsPaired() {
		t.Fatal("session must not be paired after failed attempts")
	}
	if err := sess.CompletePairing(sess.Nonce, pub); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("expected correct token to pair, got %v", err)
	}
}

// N3: a paired session must reject re-pairing instead of silently
// overwriting the established keys.
func TestCompletePairingRejectsRePairing(t *testing.T) {
	sess := pairedSession(t)
	if err := sess.CompletePairing(sess.Nonce, clientKeyB64(t)); err == nil {

	}
}

// N3: session IDs carry 128 bits of randomness.
func TestSessionIDIs128Bit(t *testing.T) {
	mgr := NewManager()
	sess, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CreateSession: %v", err)
	}
	raw, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(strings.TrimPrefix(sess.ID, "pair_"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("session id is not raw-url base64: %v", err)
	}
	if len(raw) != 16 {
		t.Fatalf("expected 16-byte (128-bit) session id, got %d bytes", len(raw))
	}
}

// N3: unpaired sessions expire after the TTL, for both lookup and pairing.
func TestUnpairedSessionExpires(t *testing.T) {
	mgr := NewManager()
	sess, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CreateSession: %v", err)
	}
	sess.CreatedAt = sess.CreatedAt.Add(-UnpairedSessionTTL - time.Minute)

	if _, ok := mgr.GetSession(sess.ID); ok {
		t.Fatal("expected expired session to be gone from GetSession")
	}
	if err := sess.CompletePairing(sess.Nonce, clientKeyB64(t)); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected pairing an expired session to fail")
	}
}

// N3: live sessions are capped so session creation cannot grow unbounded.
func TestSessionCap(t *testing.T) {
	mgr := NewManager()
	for i := 0; i < MaxLiveSessions; i++ {
		if _, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420"); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("CreateSession %d: %v", i, err)
		}
	}
	if _, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420"); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected error beyond the live session cap")
	}
}

// N5: Broadcast on an unpaired session must error, never send plaintext.
func TestBroadcastUnpairedFails(t *testing.T) {
	mgr := NewManager()
	sess, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CreateSession: %v", err)
	}
	if err := sess.Broadcast("ping", map[string]any{"x": 1}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected broadcast on unpaired session to fail")
	}
}

// N5: a captured phone frame cannot be replayed, and an older frame is
// rejected once a newer one has been accepted. Frames arrive from the
// phone partition (direction bit clear).
func TestDecryptRejectsReplay(t *testing.T) {
	sess, clientPriv := pairedSessionWithClient(t)
	phone := peerAEAD(t, sess, clientPriv)

	f1 := peerSeal(phone, 1, []byte("one"))
	f2 := peerSeal(phone, 2, []byte("two"))

	if _, err := sess.DecryptFrame(f2); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("DecryptFrame(f2): %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := sess.DecryptFrame(f1); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected older frame to be rejected after newer frame accepted")
	}
	if _, err := sess.DecryptFrame(f2); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected replayed frame to be rejected")
	}
}

// FIX 2: the two directions share one AEAD key, so the counter field of
// the nonce is partitioned by direction. Host frames (encrypted by this
// package) carry the top bit of the 8-byte counter SET; phone frames must
// carry it CLEAR. Without the partition, host frame 1 and phone frame 1
// would use the identical (key, nonce) pair.
func TestNonceDirectionPartitions(t *testing.T) {
	sess, clientPriv := pairedSessionWithClient(t)
	phone := peerAEAD(t, sess, clientPriv)
	nonceSize := phone.NonceSize()

	hostFrame, err := sess.EncryptFrame([]byte("host one"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("EncryptFrame: %v", err)
	}
	hostCounter := binary.BigEndian.Uint64(hostFrame[nonceSize-8 : nonceSize])
	if hostCounter>>63 != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("host frame counter %#x is missing the direction bit", hostCounter)
	}

	// A phone frame with the same numeric counter (1) must still have
	// different nonce bytes, because it lives in the other partition.
	phoneFrame := peerSeal(phone, 1, []byte("phone one"))
	if bytes.Equal(phoneFrame[:nonceSize], hostFrame[:nonceSize]) {
		t.Fatal("host and phone frames with the same counter share a nonce")
	}
	phoneCounter := binary.BigEndian.Uint64(phoneFrame[nonceSize-8 : nonceSize])
	if phoneCounter>>63 != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("test bug: phone frame counter %#x has the direction bit set", phoneCounter)
	}

	// Both directions decrypt at their own endpoint.
	got, err := sess.DecryptFrame(phoneFrame)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("host DecryptFrame(phone frame): %v", err)
	}
	if string(got) != "phone one" {
		t.Fatalf("phone frame mismatch: got %q", string(got))
	}
	opened, err := phone.Open(nil, hostFrame[:nonceSize], hostFrame[nonceSize:], nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("phone Open(host frame): %v", err)
	}
	if string(opened) != "host one" {
		t.Fatalf("host frame mismatch: got %q", string(opened))
	}

	// A host frame reflected back at the host sits in the wrong partition
	// and must be rejected, not decrypted.
	if _, err := sess.DecryptFrame(hostFrame); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected host frame to be rejected by host DecryptFrame (wrong partition)")
	}
}

// FIX 3: a low-order client public key must be rejected. The all-zero point
// forces an all-zero shared secret, which would hand anyone a known session
// key. Pairing with it must fail.
func TestCompletePairingRejectsLowOrderKey(t *testing.T) {
	mgr := NewManager()
	sess, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CreateSession: %v", err)
	}
	zeroPub := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(make([]byte, 32))
	if err := sess.CompletePairing(sess.Nonce, zeroPub); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected pairing with the all-zero (low-order) public key to fail")
	}
	if sess.IsPaired() {
		t.Fatal("session must not be paired after a low-order key attempt")
	}
}

// FIX 1: paired sessions must expire too. Before this fix they lived in
// the Manager forever, so 64 pairings permanently exhausted the session
// cap (a pairing DoS). Expiry is measured from the pairing time with the
// Manager's PairedSessionTTL.
func TestPairedSessionExpires(t *testing.T) {
	mgr := NewManager()
	mgr.PairedSessionTTL = time.Minute
	sess, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CreateSession: %v", err)
	}
	if err := sess.CompletePairing(sess.Nonce, clientKeyB64(t)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CompletePairing: %v", err)
	}
	if _, ok := mgr.GetSession(sess.ID); !ok {
		t.Fatal("a freshly paired session must be live")
	}

	sess.mu.Lock()
	sess.pairedAt = time.Now().Add(-2 * time.Minute)
	sess.mu.Unlock()

	if _, ok := mgr.GetSession(sess.ID); ok {
		t.Fatal("expected paired session past its TTL to be gone from GetSession")
	}
}

// FIX 1: the CreateSession cap must count live sessions only. Once paired
// sessions expire, capacity frees up and creation succeeds again.
func TestPairedExpiryFreesCapacity(t *testing.T) {
	mgr := NewManager()
	mgr.PairedSessionTTL = time.Minute
	live := make([]*Session, 0, MaxLiveSessions)
	for i := 0; i < MaxLiveSessions; i++ {
		sess, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("CreateSession %d: %v", i, err)
		}
		if err := sess.CompletePairing(sess.Nonce, clientKeyB64(t)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("CompletePairing %d: %v", i, err)
		}
		live = append(live, sess)
	}
	if _, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420"); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected error beyond the live session cap")
	}

	for _, sess := range live {
		sess.mu.Lock()
		sess.pairedAt = time.Now().Add(-2 * time.Minute)
		sess.mu.Unlock()
	}
	if _, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("expected creation to succeed after paired sessions expired, got %v", err)
	}
}

// FIX 1: RemoveSession ends a pairing on demand. It reports whether a
// session existed; unknown IDs are a no-op reporting false.
func TestRemoveSession(t *testing.T) {
	mgr := NewManager()
	sess, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CreateSession: %v", err)
	}
	if err := sess.CompletePairing(sess.Nonce, clientKeyB64(t)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CompletePairing: %v", err)
	}

	if !mgr.RemoveSession(sess.ID) {
		t.Fatal("RemoveSession must report true for a live session")
	}
	if _, ok := mgr.GetSession(sess.ID); ok {
		t.Fatal("removed session must not be returned by GetSession")
	}
	if sess.IsPaired() {
		t.Fatal("removed session must be torn down (no longer paired)")
	}
	if _, err := sess.EncryptFrame([]byte("x")); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("removed session must not encrypt frames")
	}
	if mgr.RemoveSession(sess.ID) {
		t.Fatal("second RemoveSession must report false")
	}
	if mgr.RemoveSession("pair_no-such-session") {
		t.Fatal("RemoveSession of an unknown ID must report false")
	}
}

// FIX 5: trust-boundary events are logged via slog: session creation,
// pairing success, pairing failure (reason only), expiry, and removal.
// The pairing token must never appear in the log output.
func TestRelayLifecycleLogging(t *testing.T) {
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	old := slog.Default()
	slog.SetDefault(slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(&buf, nil)))
	defer slog.SetDefault(old)

	mgr := NewManager()
	sess, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CreateSession: %v", err)
	}
	if err := sess.CompletePairing("AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA", clientKeyB64(t)); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected wrong-token pairing to fail")
	}
	if err := sess.CompletePairing(sess.Nonce, clientKeyB64(t)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CompletePairing: %v", err)
	}
	if !mgr.RemoveSession(sess.ID) {
		t.Fatal("RemoveSession must succeed")
	}

	// An expired session purged during a later CreateSession is logged too.
	stale, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CreateSession: %v", err)
	}
	stale.CreatedAt = stale.CreatedAt.Add(-UnpairedSessionTTL - time.Minute)
	if _, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CreateSession: %v", err)
	}

	out := buf.String()
	for _, want := range []string{
		"relay session created",
		"relay pairing failed",
		"relay session paired",
		"relay session removed",
		"relay session expired",
	} {
		if !strings.Contains(out, want) {
			t.Errorf("log output missing %q; got:\n%s", want, out)
		}
	}
	if strings.Contains(out, sess.Nonce) {
		t.Error("log output must never contain the pairing token")
	}
}

// Expiry must TERMINATE a paired session, not just drop it from the
// Manager's map. Before this fix, expireLocked only deleted the map
// entry: the session object kept its keys and AEAD, could still encrypt
// frames, and Broadcast still delivered to registered listeners, so a
// "gone" session kept working for anyone holding the object.
func TestExpiredPairedSessionIsTornDown(t *testing.T) {
	mgr := NewManager()
	mgr.PairedSessionTTL = time.Minute
	sess, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CreateSession: %v", err)
	}
	if err := sess.CompletePairing(sess.Nonce, clientKeyB64(t)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CompletePairing: %v", err)
	}

	ch := make(chan []byte, 4)
	sess.RegisterListener(ch)

	// Sanity: the live session encrypts and broadcasts to the listener.
	if _, err := sess.EncryptFrame([]byte("before")); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("live session must encrypt: %v", err)
	}
	if err := sess.Broadcast("ping", map[string]any{"x": 1}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("live session must broadcast: %v", err)
	}
	select {
	case <-ch:
	default:
		t.Fatal("expected the broadcast to reach the registered listener")
	}

	// Backdate past the paired TTL and trigger expiry via GetSession.
	sess.mu.Lock()
	sess.pairedAt = time.Now().Add(-2 * time.Minute)
	sess.mu.Unlock()
	if _, ok := mgr.GetSession(sess.ID); ok {
		t.Fatal("expected expired session to be gone from GetSession")
	}

	if sess.IsPaired() {
		t.Fatal("expired session must be unpaired by expiry teardown")
	}
	if _, err := sess.EncryptFrame([]byte("after")); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expired session must not encrypt frames")
	}
	if _, err := sess.DecryptFrame([]byte("0123456789abcdef0123")); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expired session must not decrypt frames")
	}
	if err := sess.Broadcast("ping", map[string]any{"x": 2}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expired session must not broadcast")
	}
	// The registered listener channel must be closed by the teardown.
	select {
	case _, ok := <-ch:
		if ok {
			t.Fatal("listener channel must be closed by expiry teardown, got a frame instead")
		}
	case <-time.After(2 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("listener channel was not closed by expiry teardown")
	}
}

// A StreamHandler connected before expiry must end when the session
// expires: teardown closes its listener channel, which is the handler's
// signal to return. Before the fix, expiry never closed the channel, so
// the handler hung until the client disconnected.
func TestStreamHandlerEndsOnSessionExpiry(t *testing.T) {
	mgr := NewManager()
	mgr.PairedSessionTTL = time.Minute
	sess, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CreateSession: %v", err)
	}
	if err := sess.CompletePairing(sess.Nonce, clientKeyB64(t)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CompletePairing: %v", err)
	}

	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/stream", nil)
	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		defer close(done)
		sess.StreamHandler()(rec, req)
	}()

	// Wait until the handler has registered its listener channel.
	deadline := time.Now().Add(2 * time.Second)
	for {
		sess.mu.RLock()
		n := len(sess.listeners)
		sess.mu.RUnlock()
		if n == 1 {
			break
		}
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			t.Fatal("stream handler never registered a listener")
		}
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
	}

	// Expire the session through the CreateSession purge path.
	sess.mu.Lock()
	sess.pairedAt = time.Now().Add(-2 * time.Minute)
	sess.mu.Unlock()
	if _, err := mgr.CreateSession("127.0.0.1:8420"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CreateSession (purge trigger): %v", err)
	}

	select {
	case <-done:
	case <-time.After(3 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("stream handler did not return after the session expired")
	}
	if sess.IsPaired() {
		t.Fatal("expired session must be unpaired by expiry teardown")
	}
}

FILE: internal/runengine/runengine.go
