// Package runengine implements Mimir's unattended execution engine:
//   - Shell-less workspace file jail (prevents path traversal, symlink escapes, and .git tampering)
//   - Single-run lockfile (.mimir/run.lock) with stale lock detection
//   - Configurable execution limits (MaxSteps, MaxTokens, Timeout)
//   - Executor seam interface for deterministic testing and shell-free argv execution
//   - Explicit Two-Tier Testing Law:
//   - Tier 1 (Inner Edit Loop, SDLC Steps 4-5): Huginn-Decider selects affected tests for fast feedback.
//   - Tier 2 (Outer Ship Gate, mimir review / mimir ship): Always runs the full test suite + Checklist Gate + Epistemic Critic.
package runengine

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/critic"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/decision"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/sdlc"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/tools"
)

var (
	// ErrJailEscape is returned when a path resolves outside the workspace root.
	ErrJailEscape = errors.New("runengine: path escapes workspace jail")
	// ErrProtectedPath is returned when an unattended write targets .git or .mimir/run.lock.
	ErrProtectedPath = errors.New("runengine: write to protected path denied")
	// ErrRunLocked is returned when another unattended run holds .mimir/run.lock.
	ErrRunLocked = errors.New("runengine: another run is already active (.mimir/run.lock)")
	// ErrStepLimitExceeded is returned when an unattended run exceeds Limits.MaxSteps.
	ErrStepLimitExceeded = errors.New("runengine: max step limit exceeded")
	// ErrTokenLimitExceeded is returned when an unattended run exceeds Limits.MaxTokens.
	ErrTokenLimitExceeded = errors.New("runengine: max token budget exceeded")
)

// Limits defines the hard resource and verification bounds for an unattended run.
type Limits struct {
	MaxSteps               int           `json:"max_steps"`
	MaxTokens              int           `json:"max_tokens"`
	Timeout                time.Duration `json:"timeout"`
	StaleLockAfter         time.Duration `json:"stale_lock_after"`
	RequireFullSuiteAtGate bool          `json:"require_full_suite_at_gate"`
	RequireEpistemicPass   bool          `json:"require_epistemic_pass"`
}

// DefaultLimits returns production-safe defaults for unattended execution.
func DefaultLimits() Limits {
	return Limits{
		MaxSteps:               16,
		MaxTokens:              120000,
		Timeout:                10 * time.Minute,
		StaleLockAfter:         30 * time.Minute,
		RequireFullSuiteAtGate: true,
		RequireEpistemicPass:   true,
	}
}

// Jail enforces a shell-less workspace boundary rooted at RootDir.
type Jail struct {
	root string
}

// NewJail creates a workspace file jail rooted at rootDir.
func NewJail(rootDir string) (*Jail, error) {
	if strings.TrimSpace(rootDir) == "" {
		rootDir = "."
	}
	abs, err := filepath.Abs(rootDir)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs); err == nil {
		abs = resolved
	}
	return &Jail{root: filepath.Clean(abs)}, nil
}

// Root returns the canonical workspace root directory.
func (j *Jail) Root() string {
	return j.root
}

// Resolve validates that targetPath (relative or absolute) stays strictly inside
// the workspace root, resolving any existing parent symlinks.
func (j *Jail) Resolve(targetPath string) (string, error) {
	if strings.TrimSpace(targetPath) == "" {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: empty path", ErrJailEscape)
	}
	var candidate string
	if filepath.IsAbs(targetPath) {
		candidate = filepath.Clean(targetPath)
	} else {
		candidate = filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(j.root, targetPath))
	}

	// Resolve symlinks on the deepest existing ancestor to catch symlink escapes.
	checkPath := candidate
	for {
		if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(checkPath); err == nil {
			suffix, relErr := filepath.Rel(checkPath, candidate)
			if relErr == nil && suffix != "." {
				candidate = filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(resolved, suffix))
			} else {
				candidate = filepath.Clean(resolved)
			}
			break
		}
		parent := filepath.Dir(checkPath)
		if parent == checkPath {
			break
		}
		checkPath = parent
	}

	rel, err := filepath.Rel(j.root, candidate)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrJailEscape, err)
	}
	relSlash := filepath.ToSlash(rel)
	if relSlash == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(relSlash, "../") || filepath.IsAbs(rel) {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: %s resolves outside %s", ErrJailEscape, targetPath, j.root)
	}
	return candidate, nil
}

// CheckWrite validates that targetPath is inside the jail and does not mutate
// protected VCS metadata (.git/) or the active run lock (.mimir/run.lock).
func (j *Jail) CheckWrite(targetPath string) (string, error) {
	resolved, err := j.Resolve(targetPath)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	rel, err := filepath.Rel(j.root, resolved)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	relSlash := strings.ToLower(filepath.ToSlash(rel))
	if relSlash == ".git" || strings.HasPrefix(relSlash, ".git/") {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrProtectedPath, relSlash)
	}
	if relSlash == ".mimir/run.lock" {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrProtectedPath, relSlash)
	}
	return resolved, nil
}

// ReadFile reads a file strictly inside the workspace jail without invoking a shell.
func (j *Jail) ReadFile(targetPath string) ([]byte, error) {
	resolved, err := j.Resolve(targetPath)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return os.ReadFile(resolved)
}

// WriteFile writes content strictly inside the workspace jail without invoking a shell.
func (j *Jail) WriteFile(targetPath string, data []byte, perm os.FileMode) error {
	resolved, err := j.CheckWrite(targetPath)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if perm == 0 {
		perm = 0o644
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(resolved), 0o755); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.WriteFile(resolved, data, perm)
}

// ListDir lists entries in a directory strictly inside the workspace jail.
func (j *Jail) ListDir(targetPath string) ([]string, error) {
	if strings.TrimSpace(targetPath) == "" {
		targetPath = "."
	}
	resolved, err := j.Resolve(targetPath)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(resolved)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	out := make([]string, 0, len(entries))
	for _, e := range entries {
		name := e.Name()
		if e.IsDir() {
			name += "/"
		}
		out = append(out, name)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// LockMetadata is serialized into .mimir/run.lock while a run is active.
type LockMetadata struct {
	PID       int       `json:"pid"`
	Task      string    `json:"task"`
	StartedAt time.Time `json:"started_at"`
}

// RunLock represents an acquired single-run lockfile (.mimir/run.lock).
type RunLock struct {
	path string
	meta LockMetadata
}

// AcquireLock atomically creates .mimir/run.lock inside rootDir. If an existing
// lockfile is older than staleAfter (and staleAfter > 0), it is treated as stale
// and replaced; otherwise ErrRunLocked is returned.
func AcquireLock(rootDir, task string, staleAfter time.Duration) (*RunLock, error) {
	lockDir := filepath.Join(rootDir, ".mimir")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(lockDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	lockPath := filepath.Join(lockDir, "run.lock")

	tryCreate := func() (*RunLock, error) {
		f, err := os.OpenFile(lockPath, os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL|os.O_WRONLY, 0o600)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		defer f.Close()
		meta := LockMetadata{
			PID:       os.Getpid(),
			Task:      task,
			StartedAt: time.Now().UTC(),
		}
		raw, _ := json.MarshalIndent(meta, "", "  ")
		if _, err := f.Write(raw); err != nil {
			_ = os.Remove(lockPath)
			return nil, err
		}
		return &RunLock{path: lockPath, meta: meta}, nil
	}

	lock, err := tryCreate()
	if err == nil {
		return lock, nil
	}
	if !errors.Is(err, os.ErrExist) {
		return nil, err
	}

	// Inspect existing lock for staleness.
	if staleAfter > 0 {
		if raw, readErr := os.ReadFile(lockPath); readErr == nil {
			var existing LockMetadata
			if jsonErr := json.Unmarshal(raw, &existing); jsonErr == nil && !existing.StartedAt.IsZero() {
				if time.Since(existing.StartedAt) > staleAfter {
					_ = os.Remove(lockPath)
					if retryLock, retryErr := tryCreate(); retryErr == nil {
						return retryLock, nil
					}
				}
			}
		} else if fi, statErr := os.Stat(lockPath); statErr == nil {
			if time.Since(fi.ModTime()) > staleAfter {
				_ = os.Remove(lockPath)
				if retryLock, retryErr := tryCreate(); retryErr == nil {
					return retryLock, nil
				}
			}
		}
	}

	return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w at %s", ErrRunLocked, lockPath)
}

// Release removes the .mimir/run.lock file.
func (l *RunLock) Release() error {
	if l == nil || l.path == "" {
		return nil
	}
	err := os.Remove(l.path)
	l.path = ""
	if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
		return nil
	}
	return err
}

// StepResult captures the outcome of a single unattended step via the Executor seam.
type StepResult struct {
	Reply       string   `json:"reply"`
	TokensUsed  int      `json:"tokens_used"`
	EditedFiles []string `json:"edited_files,omitempty"`
	Done        bool     `json:"done"`
}

// TestRunResult captures the outcome of either Tier-1 targeted tests or Tier-2 full-suite tests.
type TestRunResult struct {
	Tier    string        `json:"tier"` // "targeted_inner_loop" or "full_suite_gate"
	Passed  bool          `json:"passed"`
	Targets []string      `json:"targets"`
	Output  string        `json:"output"`
	Elapsed time.Duration `json:"elapsed"`
}

// Executor is the seam between the run engine and actual LLM/test execution.
// Implementations never invoke an interpolated shell; process execution uses discrete argv.
type Executor interface {
	RunStep(ctx context.Context, prompt string) (StepResult, error)
	RunTargetedTests(ctx context.Context, targets []string) (TestRunResult, error)
	RunFullSuite(ctx context.Context) (TestRunResult, error)
}

// GoTestExecutor implements the test-running side of Executor using direct `go test` argv calls
// (no cmd.exe / powershell / bash shell interpolation) plus an optional step callback.
type GoTestExecutor struct {
	WorkDir string
	StepFn  func(ctx context.Context, prompt string) (StepResult, error)
}

// RunStep delegates to StepFn when configured.
func (g *GoTestExecutor) RunStep(ctx context.Context, prompt string) (StepResult, error) {
	if g.StepFn == nil {
		return StepResult{Reply: "no step runner configured", Done: true}, nil
	}
	return g.StepFn(ctx, prompt)
}

// RunTargetedTests executes `go test` on specific packages or test files (Tier 1 Inner Loop).
func (g *GoTestExecutor) RunTargetedTests(ctx context.Context, targets []string) (TestRunResult, error) {
	start := time.Now()
	pkgs := normalizeGoTargets(g.WorkDir, targets)
	args := append([]string{"test", "-count=1"}, pkgs...)
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "go", args...)
	cmd.Dir = g.WorkDir
	out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
	return TestRunResult{
		Tier:    "targeted_inner_loop",
		Passed:  err == nil,
		Targets: pkgs,
		Output:  strings.TrimSpace(string(out)),
		Elapsed: time.Since(start),
	}, err
}

// RunFullSuite executes `go test -count=1 ./...` across the entire repository (Tier 2 Outer Gate).
func (g *GoTestExecutor) RunFullSuite(ctx context.Context) (TestRunResult, error) {
	start := time.Now()
	args := []string{"test", "-count=1", "./..."}
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "go", args...)
	cmd.Dir = g.WorkDir
	out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
	return TestRunResult{
		Tier:    "full_suite_gate",
		Passed:  err == nil,
		Targets: []string{"./..."},
		Output:  strings.TrimSpace(string(out)),
		Elapsed: time.Since(start),
	}, err
}

func normalizeGoTargets(workDir string, targets []string) []string {
	if len(targets) == 0 {
		return []string{"./..."}
	}
	seen := make(map[string]bool)
	var pkgs []string
	for _, t := range targets {
		t = strings.TrimSpace(t)
		if t == "" {
			continue
		}
		if strings.HasPrefix(t, "./") && !strings.HasSuffix(t, ".go") {
			if !seen[t] {
				seen[t] = true
				pkgs = append(pkgs, t)
			}
			continue
		}
		// Convert file path like "internal/sdlc/sdlc_test.go" to package "./internal/sdlc"
		dir := filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(t))
		if filepath.IsAbs(t) && workDir != "" {
			if rel, err := filepath.Rel(workDir, filepath.Dir(t)); err == nil {
				dir = filepath.ToSlash(rel)
			}
		}
		dir = strings.TrimPrefix(dir, "./")
		pkg := "./" + dir
		if dir == "." || dir == "" {
			pkg = "."
		}
		if !seen[pkg] {
			seen[pkg] = true
			pkgs = append(pkgs, pkg)
		}
	}
	if len(pkgs) == 0 {
		return []string{"./..."}
	}
	return pkgs
}

// GateReport summarizes the deterministic Checklist Gate, Two-Tier Test Gate,
// SDLC Deliverable Gate, and Epistemic Critic Gate for `mimir review` and `mimir ship`.
type GateReport struct {
	Mode             string              `json:"mode"` // "review" or "ship"
	Passed           bool                `json:"passed"`
	ChecklistPassed  bool                `json:"checklist_passed"`
	PendingTodos     int                 `json:"pending_todos"`
	SDLCPassed       bool                `json:"sdlc_passed"`
	SDLCPhase        string              `json:"sdlc_phase"`
	MissingArtifacts []string            `json:"missing_artifacts,omitempty"`
	FullSuiteResult  TestRunResult       `json:"full_suite_result"`
	EpistemicPassed  bool                `json:"epistemic_passed"`
	EpistemicReport  *critic.AuditReport `json:"epistemic_report,omitempty"`
	BlockingReasons  []string            `json:"blocking_reasons,omitempty"`
}

// FormatMarkdown renders a human- and CI-readable summary of the Review/Ship Gate.
func (r GateReport) FormatMarkdown() string {
	var b strings.Builder
	verdict := "PASS"
	if !r.Passed {
		verdict = "FAIL (BLOCKED)"
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "## Mimir Deterministic %s Gate: `%s`\n", strings.ToUpper(r.Mode), verdict)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Checklist Gate**: `pass=%v` (`pending_todos=%d`)\n", r.ChecklistPassed, r.PendingTodos)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **SDLC Deliverable Gate**: `pass=%v` (`phase=%s`, `missing=%d`)\n", r.SDLCPassed, r.SDLCPhase, len(r.MissingArtifacts))
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Tier-2 Full Test Suite (`./...`)**: `pass=%v` (`elapsed=%s`)\n",
		r.FullSuiteResult.Passed, r.FullSuiteResult.Elapsed.Round(time.Millisecond))
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Epistemic Critic Gate**: `pass=%v`\n", r.EpistemicPassed)
	if len(r.BlockingReasons) > 0 {
		b.WriteString("\n### Blocking Reasons\n")
		for _, reason := range r.BlockingReasons {
			b.WriteString("- " + reason + "\n")
		}
	}
	return strings.TrimRight(b.String(), "\n")
}

// Engine coordinates unattended runs, the shell-less file jail, the single-run lock,
// and the Two-Tier Testing Law across inner edit loops and outer review/ship gates.
type Engine struct {
	Jail     *Jail
	Limits   Limits
	Executor Executor
	Decider  *decision.Decider
	SDLC     *sdlc.Manager
	Todos    *tools.TodoStore
}

// New creates a new Engine rooted at workDir.
func New(workDir string, exec Executor, limits Limits) (*Engine, error) {
	jail, err := NewJail(workDir)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if limits.MaxSteps <= 0 {
		limits = DefaultLimits()
	}
	if exec == nil {
		exec = &GoTestExecutor{WorkDir: jail.Root()}
	}
	return &Engine{
		Jail:     jail,
		Limits:   limits,
		Executor: exec,
		Decider:  decision.New("", "", ""),
		SDLC:     sdlc.NewManager(jail.Root()),
		Todos:    tools.NewTodoStore(),
	}, nil
}

// RunInnerLoopTests implements Tier 1 of Mimir's Two-Tier Testing Law:
// During SDLC Steps 4-5 (Implementation & Inner Testing), Huginn-Decider selects
// the affected test files from the Yggdrasil Mind Map so inner edit loops get fast feedback.
func (e *Engine) RunInnerLoopTests(ctx context.Context, editedFiles, candidateTestFiles []string, maxTests int) (TestRunResult, error) {
	if maxTests <= 0 {
		maxTests = 3
	}
	dec := e.Decider
	if dec == nil {
		dec = decision.New("", "", "")
	}
	selected := dec.SelectAffectedTests(ctx, editedFiles, candidateTestFiles, maxTests)
	if len(selected) == 0 {
		selected = editedFiles
	}
	return e.Executor.RunTargetedTests(ctx, selected)
}

// GateOptions provides optional draft/context inputs for the Review and Ship gates.
type GateOptions struct {
	DraftReport      string
	RetrievedContext string
	RequiredPhases   []sdlc.PhaseID
}

// ReviewGate runs the deterministic pre-ship review gate (Tier 2 of the Two-Tier Testing Law):
//  1. Checklist Gate: zero pending/in_progress/blocked todo items.
//  2. SDLC Gate: required phase deliverables exist on disk if specified (or if Waterfall mode is active).
//  3. Full Suite Gate: runs `Executor.RunFullSuite` (`go test ./...`), never just affected tests.
//  4. Epistemic Critic Gate: audits DraftReport against RetrievedContext when provided.
func (e *Engine) ReviewGate(ctx context.Context, opts GateOptions) GateReport {
	return e.evaluateGate(ctx, "review", opts)
}

// ShipGate runs the mandatory production release gate (`mimir ship`).
// In addition to all ReviewGate checks, if passed it signs off SDLC Step 5 (Testing)
// and advances the SDLC state machine to Step 6 (Deployment).
func (e *Engine) ShipGate(ctx context.Context, opts GateOptions) GateReport {
	rep := e.evaluateGate(ctx, "ship", opts)
	if rep.Passed && e.SDLC != nil {
		e.SDLC.SignOff(sdlc.PhaseTesting)
		_, _ = e.SDLC.SetPhase(string(sdlc.PhaseDeployment))
		rep.SDLCPhase = string(e.SDLC.CurrentPhase().ID)
	}
	return rep
}

func (e *Engine) evaluateGate(ctx context.Context, mode string, opts GateOptions) GateReport {
	rep := GateReport{
		Mode:            mode,
		ChecklistPassed: true,
		SDLCPassed:      true,
		EpistemicPassed: true,
	}

	// 1. Checklist Gate
	if e.Todos != nil {
		for _, item := range e.Todos.List() {
			if item.Status != tools.TodoCompleted {
				rep.PendingTodos++
			}
		}
		if rep.PendingTodos > 0 {
			rep.ChecklistPassed = false
			rep.BlockingReasons = append(rep.BlockingReasons,
				fmt.Sprintf("checklist gate failed: %d todo item(s) are not marked completed", rep.PendingTodos))
		}
	}

	// 2. SDLC Deliverable Gate
	if e.SDLC != nil {
		cur := e.SDLC.CurrentPhase()
		rep.SDLCPhase = string(cur.ID)
		required := opts.RequiredPhases
		if len(required) == 0 && e.SDLC.Methodology() == sdlc.MethodWaterfall {
			// In Waterfall mode, all phases up to the current step must have deliverables on disk.
			for _, p := range sdlc.AllPhases() {
				if p.Step <= cur.Step {
					required = append(required, p.ID)
				}
			}
		}
		for _, pid := range required {
			if spec, ok := sdlc.LookupPhase(string(pid)); ok {
				full := filepath.Join(e.Jail.Root(), filepath.FromSlash(spec.ArtifactFile))
				if _, err := os.Stat(full); err != nil {
					rep.MissingArtifacts = append(rep.MissingArtifacts, spec.ArtifactFile)
				}
			}
		}
		if len(rep.MissingArtifacts) > 0 {
			rep.SDLCPassed = false
			rep.BlockingReasons = append(rep.BlockingReasons,
				"missing required SDLC deliverable(s): "+strings.Join(rep.MissingArtifacts, ", "))
		}
	}

	// 3. Tier-2 Full Test Suite Gate (Law: always run full suite at the gate)
	if e.Limits.RequireFullSuiteAtGate {
		res, err := e.Executor.RunFullSuite(ctx)
		rep.FullSuiteResult = res
		if err != nil || !res.Passed {
			rep.FullSuiteResult.Passed = false
			rep.BlockingReasons = append(rep.BlockingReasons,
				"full test suite failed at outer gate (`go test ./...` must be 100% green)")
		}
	} else {
		rep.FullSuiteResult = TestRunResult{Tier: "full_suite_gate", Passed: true}
	}

	// 4. Epistemic Critic Gate
	if e.Limits.RequireEpistemicPass && strings.TrimSpace(opts.DraftReport) != "" {
		audit := critic.AuditDeterministic(opts.RetrievedContext, opts.DraftReport)
		rep.EpistemicReport = &audit
		if !audit.PassAudit {
			rep.EpistemicPassed = false
			rep.BlockingReasons = append(rep.BlockingReasons,
				"epistemic critic rejected draft report ("+audit.RoutingReason+")")
		}
	}

	rep.Passed = rep.ChecklistPassed && rep.SDLCPassed && rep.FullSuiteResult.Passed && rep.EpistemicPassed
	return rep
}

// UnattendedRunSummary records the trace and gate verdict of an unattended run.
type UnattendedRunSummary struct {
	Task       string          `json:"task"`
	Steps      int             `json:"steps"`
	TokensUsed int             `json:"tokens_used"`
	InnerTests []TestRunResult `json:"inner_tests,omitempty"`
	FinalReply string          `json:"final_reply"`
	Gate       GateReport      `json:"gate"`
}

// RunUnattended executes an unattended task inside the single-run lockfile (.mimir/run.lock),
// enforcing Limits (MaxSteps, MaxTokens, Timeout), running Tier-1 targeted tests whenever
// files are edited, and enforcing the Tier-2 ReviewGate before finishing.
func (e *Engine) RunUnattended(ctx context.Context, task string, candidateTestFiles []string) (*UnattendedRunSummary, error) {
	lock, err := AcquireLock(e.Jail.Root(), task, e.Limits.StaleLockAfter)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer func() { _ = lock.Release() }()

	if e.Limits.Timeout > 0 {
		var cancel context.CancelFunc
		ctx, cancel = context.WithTimeout(ctx, e.Limits.Timeout)
		defer cancel()
	}

	summary := &UnattendedRunSummary{Task: task}
	prompt := task

	for step := 1; step <= e.Limits.MaxSteps; step++ {
		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
			return summary, err
		}
		res, err := e.Executor.RunStep(ctx, prompt)
		if err != nil {
			return summary, err
		}
		summary.Steps = step
		summary.TokensUsed += res.TokensUsed
		summary.FinalReply = res.Reply

		if e.Limits.MaxTokens > 0 && summary.TokensUsed > e.Limits.MaxTokens {
			return summary, fmt.Errorf("%w: used %d > limit %d", ErrTokenLimitExceeded, summary.TokensUsed, e.Limits.MaxTokens)
		}

		// Verify all edited files remain inside the workspace jail.
		for _, edited := range res.EditedFiles {
			if _, jailErr := e.Jail.CheckWrite(edited); jailErr != nil {
				return summary, jailErr
			}
		}

		// Tier 1 (Inner Loop): run targeted affected tests when files were modified.
		if len(res.EditedFiles) > 0 {
			tRes, _ := e.RunInnerLoopTests(ctx, res.EditedFiles, candidateTestFiles, 3)
			summary.InnerTests = append(summary.InnerTests, tRes)
			if !tRes.Passed && !res.Done {
				prompt = "Tier-1 targeted tests failed:\n" + tRes.Output + "\nFix the failing tests before continuing."
				continue
			}
		}

		if res.Done {
			summary.Gate = e.ReviewGate(ctx, GateOptions{})
			return summary, nil
		}
	}

	return summary, fmt.Errorf("%w: exceeded %d steps", ErrStepLimitExceeded, e.Limits.MaxSteps)
}

package runengine

import (

type fakeExecutor struct {
	steps        []StepResult
	stepIdx      int
	targetedCall []string
	fullCalled   int
	fullPass     bool
}

func (f *fakeExecutor) RunStep(_ context.Context, _ string) (StepResult, error) {
	if f.stepIdx >= len(f.steps) {
		return StepResult{Reply: "done", Done: true}, nil
	}
	res := f.steps[f.stepIdx]
	f.stepIdx++
	return res, nil
}

func (f *fakeExecutor) RunTargetedTests(_ context.Context, targets []string) (TestRunResult, error) {
	f.targetedCall = append([]string(nil), targets...)
	return TestRunResult{
		Tier:    "targeted_inner_loop",
		Passed:  true,
		Targets: targets,
		Output:  "ok targeted",
	}, nil
}

func (f *fakeExecutor) RunFullSuite(_ context.Context) (TestRunResult, error) {
	f.fullCalled++
	if !f.fullPass {
		return TestRunResult{
			Tier:    "full_suite_gate",
			Passed:  false,
			Targets: []string{"./..."},
			Output:  "FAIL ./internal/broken",
		}, errors.New("exit status 1")
	}
	return TestRunResult{
		Tier:    "full_suite_gate",
		Passed:  true,
		Targets: []string{"./..."},
		Output:  "ok ./...",
	}, nil
}

func TestJailBlocksPathTraversalAndProtectedPaths(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	jail, err := NewJail(dir)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("NewJail: %v", err)
	}

	// Valid write and read inside workspace jail
	if err := jail.WriteFile("pkg/hello.go", []byte("package pkg\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("expected valid write inside jail, got %v", err)
	}
	got, err := jail.ReadFile("pkg/hello.go")
	if err != nil || string(got) != "package pkg\n" {
		t.Fatalf("ReadFile mismatch: %q, err=%v", string(got), err)
	}
	entries, err := jail.ListDir(".")
	if err != nil || len(entries) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("ListDir failed: %v (%v)", entries, err)
	}

	// Reject parent traversal
	if _, err := jail.Resolve("../outside.txt"); !errors.Is(err, ErrJailEscape) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrJailEscape for ../outside.txt, got %v", err)
	}
	if err := jail.WriteFile("../../escape.sh", []byte("echo nope"), 0o644); !errors.Is(err, ErrJailEscape) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrJailEscape on write, got %v", err)
	}

	// Reject protected .git and .mimir/run.lock writes
	if err := jail.WriteFile(".git/config", []byte("bad"), 0o644); !errors.Is(err, ErrProtectedPath) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrProtectedPath for .git/config, got %v", err)
	}
	if err := jail.WriteFile(".mimir/run.lock", []byte("bad"), 0o644); !errors.Is(err, ErrProtectedPath) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrProtectedPath for .mimir/run.lock, got %v", err)
	}
}

func TestRunLockConcurrencyAndStaleRecovery(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()

	lock1, err := AcquireLock(dir, "task-1", 10*time.Minute)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("AcquireLock 1 failed: %v", err)
	}

	// Second concurrent lock must fail with ErrRunLocked
	if _, err := AcquireLock(dir, "task-2", 10*time.Minute); !errors.Is(err, ErrRunLocked) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrRunLocked on active lock, got %v", err)
	}

	// Release and re-acquire
	if err := lock1.Release(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Release failed: %v", err)
	}
	lock2, err := AcquireLock(dir, "task-2", 10*time.Minute)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("AcquireLock after release failed: %v", err)
	}
	_ = lock2.Release()

	// Write a stale lock older than StaleAfter and verify automatic recovery
	staleMeta := LockMetadata{
		PID:       999999,
		Task:      "crashed-task",
		StartedAt: time.Now().UTC().Add(-2 * time.Hour),
	}
	raw, _ := json.Marshal(staleMeta)
	lockPath := filepath.Join(dir, ".mimir", "run.lock")
	if err := os.WriteFile(lockPath, raw, 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write stale lock: %v", err)
	}

	recovered, err := AcquireLock(dir, "fresh-task", 30*time.Minute)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("expected stale lock recovery, got %v", err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = recovered.Release() }()
}

func TestTwoTierTestingLaw_InnerTargetedVsOuterFullSuite(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	fx := &fakeExecutor{fullPass: true}
	eng, err := New(dir, fx, DefaultLimits())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("New engine: %v", err)
	}

	candidates := []string{
		"internal/sdlc/sdlc_test.go",
		"internal/critic/epistemic_test.go",
		"internal/server/server_test.go",
	}

	// Tier 1: Inner edit loop selects only affected tests via Huginn-Decider
	innerRes, err := eng.RunInnerLoopTests(context.Background(), []string{"internal/critic/epistemic.go"}, candidates, 1)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("RunInnerLoopTests: %v", err)
	}
	if innerRes.Tier != "targeted_inner_loop" {
		t.Fatalf("expected targeted_inner_loop tier, got %s", innerRes.Tier)
	}
	if len(fx.targetedCall) != 1 || fx.targetedCall[0] != "internal/critic/epistemic_test.go" {
		t.Fatalf("expected Huginn-Decider to pick internal/critic/epistemic_test.go, got %v", fx.targetedCall)
	}
	if fx.fullCalled != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("inner loop must not run full suite, fullCalled=%d", fx.fullCalled)
	}

	// Tier 2: ReviewGate always runs full test suite
	gate := eng.ReviewGate(context.Background(), GateOptions{})
	if !gate.Passed {
		t.Fatalf("expected ReviewGate to pass, got %+v", gate)
	}
	if fx.fullCalled != 1 || gate.FullSuiteResult.Tier != "full_suite_gate" {
		t.Fatalf("expected ReviewGate to run full suite once, fullCalled=%d tier=%s", fx.fullCalled, gate.FullSuiteResult.Tier)
	}
}

func TestReviewAndShipGate_ChecklistSDLCAndEpistemicEnforcement(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	fx := &fakeExecutor{fullPass: true}
	eng, err := New(dir, fx, DefaultLimits())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("New engine: %v", err)
	}

	// 1. Pending todo blocks gate
	td := eng.Todos.Add("Build runengine")
	rep := eng.ReviewGate(context.Background(), GateOptions{})
	if rep.Passed || rep.ChecklistPassed {
		t.Fatalf("expected pending todo to block ReviewGate, got %+v", rep)
	}

	// Mark todo completed
	eng.Todos.SetStatus(td.ID, tools.TodoCompleted)

	// 2. Missing required SDLC deliverable blocks gate
	rep = eng.ReviewGate(context.Background(), GateOptions{
		RequiredPhases: []sdlc.PhaseID{sdlc.PhasePlanning},
	})
	if rep.Passed || rep.SDLCPassed || len(rep.MissingArtifacts) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("expected missing 01-PLAN.md to block ReviewGate, got %+v", rep)
	}

	// Save the Planning deliverable
	if _, err := eng.SDLC.SaveDeliverable(sdlc.PhasePlanning, "Charter ready"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SaveDeliverable: %v", err)
	}

	// 3. Unbacked epistemic claim blocks gate
	rep = eng.ReviewGate(context.Background(), GateOptions{
		RequiredPhases:   []sdlc.PhaseID{sdlc.PhasePlanning},
		RetrievedContext: "go test ./... passed in 12 packages.",
		DraftReport:      "Our engine is 10x faster and achieves 99.4% accuracy across all benchmarks.",
	})
	if rep.Passed || rep.EpistemicPassed {
		t.Fatalf("expected unbacked claims to block Epistemic Gate, got %+v", rep)
	}

	// 4. Grounded report + completed todos + deliverable + green full suite passes ShipGate
	shipRep := eng.ShipGate(context.Background(), GateOptions{
		RequiredPhases:   []sdlc.PhaseID{sdlc.PhasePlanning},
		RetrievedContext: "go test ./... passed in 12 packages.",
		DraftReport:      "go test ./... passed in 12 packages.",
	})
	if !shipRep.Passed {
		t.Fatalf("expected ShipGate to pass, got:\n%s", shipRep.FormatMarkdown())
	}
	if shipRep.SDLCPhase != string(sdlc.PhaseDeployment) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ShipGate to advance SDLC to deployment, got %s", shipRep.SDLCPhase)
	}
}

func TestRunUnattended_EnforcesLimitsAndLock(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	limits := DefaultLimits()
	limits.MaxSteps = 3
	limits.MaxTokens = 500

	fx := &fakeExecutor{
		fullPass: true,
		steps: []StepResult{
			{Reply: "edited critic", TokensUsed: 150, EditedFiles: []string{"internal/critic/epistemic.go"}, Done: false},
			{Reply: "finished", TokensUsed: 150, Done: true},
		},
	}
	eng, err := New(dir, fx, limits)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("New engine: %v", err)
	}

	summary, err := eng.RunUnattended(context.Background(), "update critic", []string{"internal/critic/epistemic_test.go"})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("RunUnattended failed: %v", err)
	}
	if summary.Steps != 2 || len(summary.InnerTests) != 1 || !summary.Gate.Passed {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected summary: %+v", summary)
	}

	// Verify token budget enforcement
	fxOver := &fakeExecutor{
		fullPass: true,
		steps: []StepResult{
			{Reply: "huge step", TokensUsed: 900, Done: false},
		},
	}
	engOver, _ := New(dir, fxOver, limits)
	_, err = engOver.RunUnattended(context.Background(), "blow token budget", nil)
	if !errors.Is(err, ErrTokenLimitExceeded) {
		t.Fatalf("expected ErrTokenLimitExceeded, got %v", err)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "900") {
		t.Fatalf("expected token usage in error, got %v", err)
	}
}

package sdlc

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// PhaseID identifies one of the 7 sequential phases of the Software Development Life Cycle.
type PhaseID string

const (
	PhasePlanning       PhaseID = "planning"       // Step 1: Project Plan & Charter
	PhaseAnalysis       PhaseID = "analysis"       // Step 2: Software Requirement Specification (SRS)
	PhaseDesign         PhaseID = "design"         // Step 3: System Design Document (SDD)
	PhaseImplementation PhaseID = "implementation" // Step 4: Working Source Code & Builds
	PhaseTesting        PhaseID = "testing"        // Step 5: QA Test Reports & Bug-Free Build
	PhaseDeployment     PhaseID = "deployment"     // Step 6: Live Production Release
	PhaseMaintenance    PhaseID = "maintenance"    // Step 7: Updates, Patches & Logs
)

// Methodology defines how the harness moves through the 7 SDLC steps.
type Methodology string

const (
	MethodAgile     Methodology = "agile"     // Iterative sprints looping steps 1-6 continuously
	MethodWaterfall Methodology = "waterfall" // Linear: each phase must be 100% signed off before next begins
	MethodDevOps    Methodology = "devops"    // Continuous: automates Implementation (4) -> Testing (5) -> Deployment (6)
)

// PhaseSpec defines the metadata, deliverable, allowed tools, and compact micro-prompt
// for a single SDLC phase so the main prompt never suffers from instruction bloat.
type PhaseSpec struct {
	Step         int
	ID           PhaseID
	Title        string
	CoreGoal     string
	Activities   string
	Deliverable  string
	ArtifactFile string
	Persona      string
	AllowedTools []string
	MicroPrompt  string
	WebOverlay   string // Optional compact overlay loaded ONLY on web/app tasks during relevant phases
}

// LookupPhase returns the PhaseSpec for a given PhaseID or step number ("1".."7").
func LookupPhase(idOrStep string) (PhaseSpec, bool) {
	q := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(idOrStep))
	for _, p := range AllPhases() {
		if string(p.ID) == q || fmt.Sprintf("%d", p.Step) == q || strings.ToLower(p.Title) == q {
			return p, true
		}
	}
	return PhaseSpec{}, false
}


==============================================================================
FILE: internal/sdlc/sdlc.go
==============================================================================
package sdlc

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// PhaseRecord tracks sign-off status and deliverable path for a single SDLC phase.
type PhaseRecord struct {
	Phase       PhaseID   `json:"phase"`
	SignedOff   bool      `json:"signed_off"`
	Deliverable string    `json:"deliverable,omitempty"`
	UpdatedAt   time.Time `json:"updated_at,omitempty"`
}

// Manager coordinates the 7-Phase SDLC state machine, methodology rules
// (Agile, Waterfall, DevOps), deliverable artifacts (.mimir/sdlc/), and
// phase-scoped prompt/tool loading so the main prompt remains tiny.
type Manager struct {
	mu         sync.RWMutex
	workDir    string
	current    PhaseID
	method     Methodology
	autoDetect bool
	records    map[PhaseID]PhaseRecord
}

// NewManager creates an SDLC Manager rooted at workDir.
// Defaults to MethodAgile, PhaseImplementation, and autoDetect=true so each
// user request automatically loads only the SDLC phase micro-prompt it needs.
func NewManager(workDir string) *Manager {
	if workDir == "" {
		workDir = "."
	}
	return &Manager{
		workDir:    workDir,
		current:    PhaseImplementation,
		method:     MethodAgile,
		autoDetect: true,
		records:    make(map[PhaseID]PhaseRecord),
	}
}

// CurrentPhase returns the active PhaseSpec.
func (m *Manager) CurrentPhase() PhaseSpec {
	m.mu.RLock()
	defer m.mu.RUnlock()
	spec, ok := LookupPhase(string(m.current))
	if !ok {
		spec, _ = LookupPhase(string(PhaseImplementation))
	}
	return spec
}

// Methodology returns the active SDLC execution model ("agile", "waterfall", "devops").
func (m *Manager) Methodology() Methodology {
	m.mu.RLock()
	defer m.mu.RUnlock()
	return m.method
}

// SetMethodology switches between Agile, Waterfall, and DevOps execution models.
func (m *Manager) SetMethodology(method string) error {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	switch strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(method)) {
	case string(MethodAgile), "scrum":
		m.method = MethodAgile
		return nil
	case string(MethodWaterfall), "linear":
		m.method = MethodWaterfall
		m.autoDetect = false // Waterfall enforces strict linear phase progression
		return nil
	case string(MethodDevOps), "cicd", "ci/cd":
		m.method = MethodDevOps
		return nil
	default:
		return fmt.Errorf("unknown SDLC methodology %q (choose agile, waterfall, or devops)", method)
	}
}

// AutoDetect reports whether Mímir automatically selects the SDLC phase from the prompt.
func (m *Manager) AutoDetect() bool {
	m.mu.RLock()
	defer m.mu.RUnlock()
	return m.autoDetect
}

// SetAutoDetect enables or disables automatic per-prompt SDLC phase routing.
func (m *Manager) SetAutoDetect(on bool) {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	m.autoDetect = on
}

// SetPhase transitions to the requested SDLC phase. In Waterfall mode, jumping ahead
// requires the preceding phase to be signed off first.
func (m *Manager) SetPhase(idOrStep string) (PhaseSpec, error) {
	target, ok := LookupPhase(idOrStep)
	if !ok {
		return PhaseSpec{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown SDLC phase %q (use 1..7 or planning, analysis, design, implementation, testing, deployment, maintenance)", idOrStep)
	}
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()

	curSpec, _ := LookupPhase(string(m.current))
	if m.method == MethodWaterfall && target.Step > curSpec.Step {
		rec := m.records[m.current]
		if !rec.SignedOff {
			return curSpec, fmt.Errorf("waterfall gate blocked: phase %d (%s - %s) must be completed and signed off before advancing to phase %d (%s)",
				curSpec.Step, curSpec.Title, curSpec.Deliverable, target.Step, target.Title)
		}
	}
	m.current = target.ID
	return target, nil
}

// SaveDeliverable writes the primary deliverable markdown document for the current
// (or specified) phase into .mimir/sdlc/ and marks the phase signed off.
func (m *Manager) SaveDeliverable(phaseID PhaseID, content string) (string, error) {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	if phaseID == "" {
		phaseID = m.current
	}
	spec, ok := LookupPhase(string(phaseID))
	if !ok {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown SDLC phase %q", phaseID)
	}
	fullPath := filepath.Join(m.workDir, filepath.FromSlash(spec.ArtifactFile))
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(fullPath), 0o755); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	header := fmt.Sprintf("# SDLC Step %d: %s -- %s\n- **Methodology**: `%s`\n- **Persona**: `%s`\n- **Updated**: `%s`\n\n",
		spec.Step, spec.Title, spec.Deliverable, m.method, spec.Persona, time.Now().Format(time.RFC3339))
	if err := os.WriteFile(fullPath, []byte(header+strings.TrimSpace(content)+"\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	m.records[spec.ID] = PhaseRecord{
		Phase:       spec.ID,
		SignedOff:   true,
		Deliverable: spec.ArtifactFile,
		UpdatedAt:   time.Now(),
	}
	return spec.ArtifactFile, nil
}

// SignOff marks the active phase as signed off without overwriting its deliverable file.
func (m *Manager) SignOff(phaseID PhaseID) PhaseSpec {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	if phaseID == "" {
		phaseID = m.current
	}
	spec, _ := LookupPhase(string(phaseID))
	rec := m.records[spec.ID]
	rec.Phase = spec.ID
	rec.SignedOff = true
	rec.UpdatedAt = time.Now()
	if rec.Deliverable == "" {
		rec.Deliverable = spec.ArtifactFile
	}
	m.records[spec.ID] = rec
	return spec
}

// Advance moves to the next sequential phase according to the active SDLC Methodology:
// - Agile: cycles 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 1 (iterative sprint loop)
// - Waterfall: strictly requires current phase SignedOff before moving to Step + 1
// - DevOps: chains Implementation (4) -> Testing (5) -> Deployment (6) -> Maintenance (7)
func (m *Manager) Advance() (PhaseSpec, error) {
	m.mu.Lock()
	curSpec, _ := LookupPhase(string(m.current))
	method := m.method
	rec := m.records[m.current]
	m.mu.Unlock()

	if method == MethodWaterfall && !rec.SignedOff {
		return curSpec, fmt.Errorf("waterfall gate: sign off Step %d (%s - %s) before advancing",
			curSpec.Step, curSpec.Title, curSpec.Deliverable)
	}

	nextStep := curSpec.Step + 1
	if method == MethodAgile && nextStep > 6 {
		nextStep = 1 // Agile sprint loop (1..6)
	} else if nextStep > 7 {
		nextStep = 7
	}
	return m.SetPhase(fmt.Sprintf("%d", nextStep))
}

// DetectPhaseFromPrompt classifies a user prompt into the matching SDLC PhaseID
// in <1ms so Mímir loads ONLY that phase's compact micro-prompt without bloating the base prompt.
func DetectPhaseFromPrompt(input string) PhaseID {
	q := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(input))
	if q == "" {
		return PhaseImplementation
	}

	// Step 1: Planning
	for _, kw := range []string{"project plan", "charter", "scope", "feasibility", "roadmap", "estimate cost", "sprint plan", "todo list"} {
		if strings.Contains(q, kw) {
			return PhasePlanning
		}
	}
	// Step 2: Analysis
	for _, kw := range []string{"requirements", "srs", "stakeholder", "constraints", "analyze repo", "ingest", "what does this", "explain how"} {
		if strings.Contains(q, kw) {
			return PhaseAnalysis
		}
	}
	// Step 3: Design
	for _, kw := range []string{"architecture", "blueprint", "database schema", "db schema", "wireframe", "sdd", "system design", "api contract", "folder structure"} {
		if strings.Contains(q, kw) {
			return PhaseDesign
		}
	}
	// Step 5: Testing
	for _, kw := range []string{"run test", "unit test", "qa report", "verify", "linter", "benchmark", "squash bug", "test suite"} {
		if strings.Contains(q, kw) {
			return PhaseTesting
		}
	}
	// Step 6: Deployment
	for _, kw := range []string{"deploy", "dockerfile", "ci/cd", "release", "production", "container", "hostinger", "dokploy"} {
		if strings.Contains(q, kw) {
			return PhaseDeployment
		}
	}
	// Step 7: Maintenance
	for _, kw := range []string{"monitor", "telemetry", "uptime", "patch vulnerability", "log audit", "maintenance", "hotfix"} {
		if strings.Contains(q, kw) {
			return PhaseMaintenance
		}
	}
	// Default Step 4: Implementation
	return PhaseImplementation
}

// ResolvePhaseForTurn returns the active PhaseSpec for a turn (auto-switching when
// AutoDetect is enabled and Methodology is not strict Waterfall).
func (m *Manager) ResolvePhaseForTurn(input string) PhaseSpec {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	if m.autoDetect && m.method != MethodWaterfall && strings.TrimSpace(input) != "" {
		m.current = DetectPhaseFromPrompt(input)
	}
	spec, ok := LookupPhase(string(m.current))
	if !ok {
		spec, _ = LookupPhase(string(PhaseImplementation))
	}
	return spec
}

// BuildPhasePrompt returns ONLY the compact micro-prompt for the active SDLC step
// (plus the 1-line Web/SEO overlay ONLY if isWebTask is true and the phase has one,
// and compact PRODUCT.md / DESIGN.md context during Steps 3-5 when present).
// This keeps total lifecycle prompt overhead under ~75 tokens instead of bloating the system prompt.
func (m *Manager) BuildPhasePrompt(input string, isWebTask bool) string {
	spec := m.ResolvePhaseForTurn(input)
	m.mu.RLock()
	method := m.method
	workDir := m.workDir
	m.mu.RUnlock()

	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("\n\n")
	b.WriteString(spec.MicroPrompt)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, " (Method: %s | Deliverable: %s)", method, spec.Deliverable)
	if isWebTask && spec.WebOverlay != "" {
		b.WriteString("\n")
		b.WriteString(spec.WebOverlay)
		if spec.Step >= 3 && spec.Step <= 5 {
			if dc := loadCompactDesignDocs(workDir); dc != "" {
				b.WriteString("\n")
				b.WriteString(dc)
			}
		}
	}
	return b.String()
}

func loadCompactDesignDocs(workDir string) string {
	if strings.TrimSpace(workDir) == "" {
		workDir = "."
	}
	var parts []string
	for _, name := range []string{"PRODUCT.md", "DESIGN.md"} {
		raw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(workDir, name))
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		compact := strings.Join(strings.Fields(strings.TrimSpace(string(raw))), " ")
		if compact == "" {
			continue
		}
		if len(compact) > 220 {
			compact = compact[:220] + "..."
		}
		parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("[%s]: %s", name, compact))
	}
	return strings.Join(parts, " | ")
}

// AllowedToolSet returns a map of tool names permitted in the active phase.
func (m *Manager) AllowedToolSet() map[string]bool {
	spec := m.CurrentPhase()
	allowed := make(map[string]bool, len(spec.AllowedTools))
	for _, name := range spec.AllowedTools {
		allowed[name] = true
	}
	return allowed
}

// FormatBoard renders a clean markdown/terminal table of all 7 SDLC phases,
// highlighting the active phase and sign-off status.
func (m *Manager) FormatBoard() string {
	m.mu.RLock()
	cur := m.current
	method := m.method
	auto := m.autoDetect
	records := make(map[PhaseID]PhaseRecord, len(m.records))
	for k, v := range m.records {
		records[k] = v
	}
	m.mu.RUnlock()

	var b strings.Builder
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "SDLC Framework [Methodology: %s | Auto-Phase: %v]\n", method, auto)
	for _, p := range AllPhases() {
		marker := "  "
		if p.ID == cur {
			marker = "->"
		}
		status := "pending"
		if rec, ok := records[p.ID]; ok && rec.SignedOff {
			status = "signed-off (" + rec.Deliverable + ")"
		} else if p.ID == cur {
			status = "ACTIVE"
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s [%d/7] %-14s | Persona: %-8s | Deliverable: %-38s | %s\n",
			marker, p.Step, p.Title, p.Persona, p.Deliverable, status)
	}
	return strings.TrimRight(b.String(), "\n")
}


==============================================================================
FILE: internal/sdlc/sdlc_test.go

package sdlc

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestAllPhasesCompactNoBloat(t *testing.T) {
	phases := AllPhases()
	if len(phases) != 7 {
		t.Fatalf("expected 7 SDLC phases, got %d", len(phases))
	}
	for i, p := range phases {
		if p.Step != i+1 {
			t.Errorf("phase %s step = %d, want %d", p.ID, p.Step, i+1)
		}
		// Ensure micro-prompts are tiny (<300 chars) so neither big nor tiny LLMs suffer prompt bloat.
		if len(p.MicroPrompt) > 300 {
			t.Errorf("phase %s MicroPrompt too bloated (%d chars): %s", p.ID, len(p.MicroPrompt), p.MicroPrompt)
		}
		if len(p.AllowedTools) == 0 {
			t.Errorf("phase %s has empty AllowedTools", p.ID)
		}
	}
}

func TestDetectPhaseFromPrompt(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		prompt string
		want   PhaseID
	}{
		{"Define the project plan, scope, and feasibility charter", PhasePlanning},
		{"Gather the SRS requirements and analyze repo constraints", PhaseAnalysis},
		{"Blueprint the system design architecture and database schema", PhaseDesign},
		{"Add a new handler function in internal/server/server.go", PhaseImplementation},
		{"Run unit tests and linter to verify quality", PhaseTesting},
		{"Deploy the production container via CI/CD pipeline", PhaseDeployment},
		{"Monitor telemetry logs and patch vulnerability", PhaseMaintenance},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		if got := DetectPhaseFromPrompt(tc.prompt); got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("DetectPhaseFromPrompt(%q) = %q, want %q", tc.prompt, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestWaterfallGateAndSaveDeliverable(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	mgr := NewManager(dir)
	if err := mgr.SetMethodology("waterfall"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SetMethodology: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := mgr.SetPhase("1"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SetPhase(1): %v", err)
	}
	// Advancing in Waterfall without signing off Step 1 must fail.
	if _, err := mgr.Advance(); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected Waterfall gate to block advancing before Step 1 sign-off")
	}
	// Saving the deliverable signs off Step 1 and writes .mimir/sdlc/01-PLAN.md.
	relPath, err := mgr.SaveDeliverable(PhasePlanning, "Scope: 4-stack polyglot harness.")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SaveDeliverable: %v", err)
	}
	if relPath != ".mimir/sdlc/01-PLAN.md" {
		t.Errorf("relPath = %q, want .mimir/sdlc/01-PLAN.md", relPath)
	}
	next, err := mgr.Advance()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Advance after sign-off failed: %v", err)
	}
	if next.ID != PhaseAnalysis {
		t.Errorf("next phase = %q, want %q", next.ID, PhaseAnalysis)
	}
}

func TestBuildPhasePromptLoadsOnlyActivePhase(t *testing.T) {
	mgr := NewManager(t.TempDir())
	// Backend testing prompt -> loads ONLY Step 5 Testing micro-prompt, no WebOverlay, no Planning/Deployment bloat.
	p := mgr.BuildPhasePrompt("Run unit tests to verify the package", false)
	if !strings.Contains(p, "SDLC 5/7: TESTING") {
		t.Errorf("expected Step 5 TESTING micro-prompt, got: %s", p)
	}
	if strings.Contains(p, "SDLC 1/7") || strings.Contains(p, "SDLC 3/7") || strings.Contains(p, "Web/SEO") {
		t.Errorf("expected zero bloat from other phases or web overlay, got: %s", p)
	}

	// Web design prompt -> loads ONLY Step 3 Design micro-prompt + compact 1-line WebOverlay.
	w := mgr.BuildPhasePrompt("Design the system architecture and wireframe for our SaaS website", true)
	if !strings.Contains(w, "SDLC 3/7: DESIGN") || !strings.Contains(w, "[Web/SEO Design]") {
		t.Errorf("expected Step 3 DESIGN + compact Web/SEO Design overlay, got: %s", w)
	}
}

package server

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/agent"

// steerProbeProvider drives one tool call on its first Generate so the agent
// loop reaches the steer-drain point, and records every message it is shown
// so tests can prove whether a steering instruction reached the model.
type steerProbeProvider struct {
	mu    sync.Mutex
	calls int
	seen  []string
}

func (p *steerProbeProvider) ID() string { return "steerprobe" }
func (p *steerProbeProvider) Generate(_ context.Context, req llm.GenerateRequest) (llm.GenerateResponse, error) {
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	p.calls++
	for _, m := range req.Messages {
		p.seen = append(p.seen, m.Content)
	}
	if p.calls == 1 {
		return llm.GenerateResponse{
			ToolCalls:    []llm.ToolCall{{ID: "tc1", Name: "todo", Arguments: "{}"}},
			FinishReason: "tool_calls",
		}, nil
	}
	return llm.GenerateResponse{Content: "probe reply", FinishReason: "stop"}, nil
}
func (p *steerProbeProvider) Stream(context.Context, llm.GenerateRequest) (<-chan llm.StreamEvent, error) {
	return nil, nil
}
func (p *steerProbeProvider) sawSteering(msg string) bool {
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	for _, s := range p.seen {
		if strings.Contains(s, "[User steering instruction]: "+msg) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// mobileFixture builds a Handler with a real session store holding one
// session owned by user_alice and one by user_bob, plus the probe agent.
type mobileFixture struct {
	handler http.Handler
	prov    *steerProbeProvider
	alice   string // alice's session ID
	bob     string // bob's session ID
}

func newMobileFixture(t *testing.T) *mobileFixture {
	t.Helper()
	store, err := cortex.NewMemoryStoreAt(filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "cortex.json"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("store: %v", err)
	}
	sessStore, err := cortex.NewFileSessionStore(t.TempDir())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("session store: %v", err)
	}
	sessA, err := sessStore.CreateSession(context.Background(), "Alice chat", "user_alice")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("create alice session: %v", err)
	}
	sessB, err := sessStore.CreateSession(context.Background(), "Bob chat", "user_bob")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("create bob session: %v", err)
	}
	prov := &steerProbeProvider{}
	ag := agent.New(agent.Config{Provider: prov, Tools: tools.NewRegistry(), Cortex: store, Model: "m"})
	return &mobileFixture{
		handler: Handler(ag, store, sessStore, nil, nil),
		prov:    prov,
		alice:   sessA.ID,
		bob:     sessB.ID,
	}
}

// postAs issues a POST with the caller identity injected into the request
// context, following the fake-auth pattern of TestServerSessionIDORProtection
// (the auth middleware passes a pre-set identity through in local mode).
func postAs(h http.Handler, path, body, userID string) *httptest.ResponseRecorder {
	req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, path, strings.NewReader(body))
	if userID != "" {
		req = req.WithContext(context.WithValue(req.Context(), ctxUserID, userID))
	}
	w := httptest.NewRecorder()
	h.ServeHTTP(w, req)
	return w
}

func (f *mobileFixture) chat(t *testing.T) {
	t.Helper()
	w := postAs(f.handler, "/chat", `{"prompt":"go"}`, "")
	if w.Code != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("probe /chat status = %d, want 200 (body: %s)", w.Code, w.Body.String())
	}
}

// TestMobileEndpointsRequireAuthWhenConfigured proves FIX 1's first half:
// with an AuthStore configured, /api/mobile/steer and /api/mobile/mode reject
// requests carrying no credentials, like /chat does. (On the unfixed code
// both are registered on the public mux and answer 200.)
func TestMobileEndpointsRequireAuthWhenConfigured(t *testing.T) {
	store, err := cortex.NewMemoryStoreAt(filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "cortex.json"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("store: %v", err)
	}
	ag := agent.New(agent.Config{Provider: &fakeText{"ok"}, Tools: tools.NewRegistry(), Cortex: store, Model: "m"})
	// A non-nil AuthStore switches the middleware to credential checking.
	// No Authorization header is sent, so validation is never reached and
	// the nil client is never dereferenced.
	auth := cortex.NewAuthStore(nil)
	srv := httptest.NewServer(Handler(ag, store, nil, auth, nil))
	defer srv.Close()

	for _, path := range []string{"/api/mobile/steer", "/api/mobile/mode"} {
		resp, err := http.Post(srv.URL+path, "application/json",
			strings.NewReader(`{"session_id":"s1","message":"hi","mode":"bypass"}`))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("post %s: %v", path, err)
		}
		resp.Body.Close()
		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusUnauthorized {
			t.Errorf("%s without credentials: status = %d, want 401", path, resp.StatusCode)
		}
	}
}

// TestMobileSteerForeignSessionRejected proves a caller cannot steer another
// user's session, and that the rejected steer never enters the agent's queue.
func TestMobileSteerForeignSessionRejected(t *testing.T) {
	f := newMobileFixture(t)
	w := postAs(f.handler, "/api/mobile/steer",
		`{"session_id":"`+f.alice+`","message":"pwned steer"}`, "user_bob")
	if w.Code != http.StatusForbidden {
		t.Fatalf("foreign steer status = %d, want 403 (body: %s)", w.Code, w.Body.String())
	}
	f.chat(t)
	if f.prov.sawSteering("pwned steer") {
		t.Error("rejected foreign steer reached the agent run: steer queue was polluted")
	}
}

// TestMobileSteerUnknownSessionRejected proves a steer naming a session that
// does not exist is rejected and not enqueued.
func TestMobileSteerUnknownSessionRejected(t *testing.T) {
	f := newMobileFixture(t)
	w := postAs(f.handler, "/api/mobile/steer",
		`{"session_id":"no-such-session","message":"ghost steer"}`, "user_alice")
	if w.Code != http.StatusForbidden {
		t.Fatalf("unknown-session steer status = %d, want 403", w.Code)
	}
	f.chat(t)
	if f.prov.sawSteering("ghost steer") {
		t.Error("unknown-session steer reached the agent run")
	}
}

// TestMobileSteerOwnSessionAccepted is the positive control: the owner can
// steer their own session and the instruction reaches the next run OF THAT
// SESSION (delivery is session-bound, so the run must carry the session ID).
func TestMobileSteerOwnSessionAccepted(t *testing.T) {
	f := newMobileFixture(t)
	w := postAs(f.handler, "/api/mobile/steer",
		`{"session_id":"`+f.alice+`","message":"please pivot"}`, "user_alice")
	if w.Code != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("own steer status = %d, want 200 (body: %s)", w.Code, w.Body.String())
	}
	w = postAs(f.handler, "/chat",
		`{"prompt":"go","session_id":"`+f.alice+`"}`, "user_alice")
	if w.Code != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("own-session /chat status = %d, want 200 (body: %s)", w.Code, w.Body.String())
	}
	if !f.prov.sawSteering("please pivot") {
		t.Error("accepted own-session steer never reached the agent run")
	}
}

// TestMobileModeOwnership proves the mode endpoint applies the same
// ownership rule: foreign and unknown sessions are rejected, the owner's
// own session accepts the mode (stored per session, as before).
func TestMobileModeOwnership(t *testing.T) {
	f := newMobileFixture(t)

	w := postAs(f.handler, "/api/mobile/mode",
		`{"session_id":"`+f.alice+`","mode":"bypass"}`, "user_bob")
	if w.Code != http.StatusForbidden {
		t.Errorf("foreign mode set status = %d, want 403", w.Code)
	}

	w = postAs(f.handler, "/api/mobile/mode",
		`{"session_id":"no-such-session","mode":"bypass"}`, "user_alice")
	if w.Code != http.StatusForbidden {
		t.Errorf("unknown-session mode set status = %d, want 403", w.Code)
	}

	w = postAs(f.handler, "/api/mobile/mode",
		`{"session_id":"`+f.alice+`","mode":"bypass"}`, "user_alice")
	if w.Code != http.StatusOK {
		t.Errorf("own mode set status = %d, want 200 (body: %s)", w.Code, w.Body.String())
	}

	// Local mode (caller "local") may set a mode on any existing session,
	// matching the /chat and item-route ownership rule.
	w = postAs(f.handler, "/api/mobile/mode",
		`{"session_id":"`+f.bob+`","mode":"ro"}`, "")
	if w.Code != http.StatusOK {
		t.Errorf("local mode set status = %d, want 200 (body: %s)", w.Code, w.Body.String())
	}
}

// errStreamProvider fails the stream immediately with an error whose text
// contains control characters (FIX 3 probe).
type errStreamProvider struct{ err error }

func (p *errStreamProvider) ID() string { return "errstream" }
func (p *errStreamProvider) Generate(context.Context, llm.GenerateRequest) (llm.GenerateResponse, error) {
	return llm.GenerateResponse{}, p.err
}
func (p *errStreamProvider) Stream(context.Context, llm.GenerateRequest) (<-chan llm.StreamEvent, error) {
	return nil, p.err
}

// TestChatStreamErrorFrameIsValidJSON proves FIX 3: the /chat/stream error
// frame is marshaled JSON, so an error containing control bytes still
// produces a parseable frame carrying the exact message. (The hand-rolled
// %q frame emitted \xNN escapes, which are not valid JSON.)
func TestChatStreamErrorFrameIsValidJSON(t *testing.T) {
	store, err := cortex.NewMemoryStoreAt(filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "cortex.json"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("store: %v", err)
	}
	wantErr := "stream blew up\x01\x02badly"
	ag := agent.New(agent.Config{
		Provider: &errStreamProvider{err: errors.New(wantErr)},
		Tools:    tools.NewRegistry(), Cortex: store, Model: "m",
	})
	srv := httptest.NewServer(Handler(ag, store, nil, nil, nil))
	defer srv.Close()

	resp, err := http.Post(srv.URL+"/chat/stream", "application/json", strings.NewReader(`{"prompt":"hi"}`))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("post: %v", err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	body := new(strings.Builder)
	buf := make([]byte, 4096)
	for {
		n, rerr := resp.Body.Read(buf)
		body.Write(buf[:n])
		if rerr != nil {
			break
		}
	}
	var last string
	for _, line := range strings.Split(body.String(), "\n") {
		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "data: ") {
			last = strings.TrimPrefix(line, "data: ")
		}
	}
	if last == "" {
		t.Fatalf("no data frames in stream response: %q", body.String())
	}
	var frame map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(last), &frame); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("final error frame is not valid JSON: %v (frame: %s)", err, last)
	}
	if frame["type"] != "error" {
		t.Errorf("frame type = %v, want error", frame["type"])
	}
	if frame["err"] != wantErr {
		t.Errorf("frame err = %q, want the exact provider error %q", frame["err"], wantErr)
	}
}

FILE: internal/server/auth.go

package server

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"net/http"
	"strings"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/cortex"
)

type contextKey string

const ctxUserID contextKey = "user_id"

func authMiddleware(auth *cortex.AuthStore) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
		if auth == nil {
			// Local self-hosted mode (file-backed Cortex): no auth wall required.
			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
				if r.Context().Value(ctxUserID) == nil {
					ctx := context.WithValue(r.Context(), ctxUserID, "local")
					next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(ctx))
					return
				}
				next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
			})
		}
		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
			ah := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
			if ah == "" || !strings.HasPrefix(ah, "Bearer ") {
				http.Error(w, `{"error":"authorization required"}`, http.StatusUnauthorized)
				return
			}
			token := strings.TrimPrefix(ah, "Bearer ")
			userID, err := auth.ValidateToken(r.Context(), token)
			if err != nil {
				http.Error(w, `{"error":"invalid or expired token"}`, http.StatusUnauthorized)
				return
			}
			ctx := context.WithValue(r.Context(), ctxUserID, userID)
			next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(ctx))
		})
	}
}

func userIDFromContext(ctx context.Context) string {
	uid, _ := ctx.Value(ctxUserID).(string)
	return uid
}

// writeErrorJSON writes an error response whose body is built by marshaling
// (F20): dynamic error text is JSON-escaped, never concatenated into a JSON
// literal where quotes in the message could break or inject the document.
func writeErrorJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, msg string) {
	body, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]string{"error": msg})
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	w.WriteHeader(status)
	_, _ = w.Write(body)
}

func sendCodeHandler(auth *cortex.AuthStore) http.HandlerFunc {
	return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		if auth == nil {
			writeJSON(w, map[string]string{"status": "local-mode"})
			return
		}
		var req struct {
			Email string `json:"email"`
		}
		if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req); err != nil {
			http.Error(w, `{"error":"invalid request body"}`, http.StatusBadRequest)
			return
		}
		if req.Email == "" {
			http.Error(w, `{"error":"email is required"}`, http.StatusBadRequest)
			return
		}
		if err := auth.SendOTP(r.Context(), req.Email); err != nil {
			writeErrorJSON(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
			return
		}
		writeJSON(w, map[string]string{"status": "sent"})
	}
}

func verifyCodeHandler(auth *cortex.AuthStore) http.HandlerFunc {
	return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		if auth == nil {
			writeJSON(w, map[string]any{
				"user":  map[string]any{"id": "local", "email": "local@mimir"},
				"token": "local-dev-token",
			})
			return
		}
		var req struct {
			Email string `json:"email"`
			Code  string `json:"code"`
		}
		if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req); err != nil {
			http.Error(w, `{"error":"invalid request body"}`, http.StatusBadRequest)
			return
		}
		if req.Email == "" || req.Code == "" {
			http.Error(w, `{"error":"email and code are required"}`, http.StatusBadRequest)
			return
		}
		user, tok, err := auth.VerifyOTP(r.Context(), req.Email, req.Code)
		if err != nil {
			writeErrorJSON(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, err.Error())
			return
		}
		writeJSON(w, map[string]any{
			"user":  map[string]any{"id": user.ID, "email": user.Email, "created_at": user.CreatedAt},
			"token": tok.Token,
		})
	}
}

func meHandler(auth *cortex.AuthStore) http.HandlerFunc {
	return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		if auth == nil {
			writeJSON(w, map[string]any{
				"id":    "local",
				"email": "local@mimir",
			})
			return
		}
		userID := userIDFromContext(r.Context())
		rows, err := auth.Query(r.Context(), "SELECT * FROM user WHERE id = user:"+userID)
		if err != nil || len(rows) == 0 {
			http.Error(w, `{"error":"user not found"}`, http.StatusNotFound)
			return
		}
		b, _ := json.Marshal(rows[0])
		var raw struct {
			ID        string `json:"id"`
			Email     string `json:"email"`
			CreatedAt string `json:"created_at"`
		}
		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &raw); err != nil {
			writeErrorJSON(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "decode user row: "+err.Error())
			return
		}
		writeJSON(w, map[string]any{
			"id":         cortex.StripRecordID(raw.ID),
			"email":      raw.Email,
			"created_at": raw.CreatedAt,
		})
	}
}

<script>
var emailSent = null;

function sendCode(){
  var email = document.getElementById('authEmail').value.trim();
  if(!email){ document.getElementById('authError').textContent = 'Email is required.'; return; }
  document.getElementById('authError').textContent = '';
  var btn = document.getElementById('authBtn');
  btn.disabled = true; btn.textContent = 'Sending...';
  fetch('/auth/send-code', {method:'POST', headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body:JSON.stringify({email:email})})
    .then(function(r){
      if(!r.ok) return r.json().then(function(d){ throw new Error(d.error || 'Failed to send code'); });
      return r.json();
    })
    .then(function(){
      emailSent = email;
      document.getElementById('authStep1').style.display = 'none';
      document.getElementById('authStep2').style.display = '';
      document.getElementById('authError2').textContent = '';
      document.getElementById('authCode').value = '';
      document.getElementById('authCode').focus();
      document.getElementById('authTitle').textContent = 'Enter the code';
      document.getElementById('authSub').textContent = 'A 6-digit code was sent to ' + email;
    })
    .catch(function(e){ document.getElementById('authError').textContent = e.message; })
    .finally(function(){ btn.disabled = false; btn.textContent = 'Send login code'; });
}

function verifyCode(){
  var code = document.getElementById('authCode').value.trim();
  if(!code || code.length < 6){ document.getElementById('authError2').textContent = 'Enter the 6-digit code.'; return; }
  document.getElementById('authError2').textContent = '';
  var btn = document.getElementById('authBtnCode');
  btn.disabled = true; btn.textContent = 'Verifying...';
  fetch('/auth/verify-code', {method:'POST', headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body:JSON.stringify({email:emailSent, code:code})})
    .then(function(r){
      if(!r.ok) return r.json().then(function(d){ throw new Error(d.error || 'Invalid code'); });
      return r.json();
    })
    .then(function(d){
      localStorage.setItem('mimir-token', d.token);
      localStorage.setItem('mimir-email', emailSent);
      window.location.href = '/app';
    })
    .catch(function(e){ document.getElementById('authError2').textContent = e.message; })
    .finally(function(){ btn.disabled = false; btn.textContent = 'Verify & sign in'; });
}

function backToEmail(){
  emailSent = null;
  document.getElementById('authStep2').style.display = 'none';
  document.getElementById('authStep1').style.display = '';
  document.getElementById('authEmail').value = '';
  document.getElementById('authError').textContent = '';
  document.getElementById('authError2').textContent = '';
  document.getElementById('authTitle').textContent = 'Sign in to Mimir';
  document.getElementById('authSub').textContent = 'Enter your email to receive a login code.';
}

// If already logged in, go straight to app
(function(){
  var token = localStorage.getItem('mimir-token');
  if(token) window.location.href = '/app';
})();
</script>
