func TestFactory_SubmitAndListTasks(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	f := NewFactory(FactoryConfig{
		RootDir:      dir,
		MaxWorkers:   2,
		TargetBranch: "main",
	})

	task1, err := f.Submit("Build Telephony Gateway", "Integrate Twilio voice and SMS webhooks.")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Submit task1 failed: %v", err)
	}
	if task1.ID != "task-1" {
		t.Errorf("expected task-1, got %s", task1.ID)
	}
	if task1.State != StateBacklog {
		t.Errorf("expected StateBacklog, got %s", task1.State)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(task1.Branch, "task-1") {
		t.Errorf("expected branch to contain task-1, got %s", task1.Branch)
	}

	task2, err := f.Submit("SEO and LLMs.txt", "Generate robots.txt and llms.txt.")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Submit task2 failed: %v", err)
	}
	if task2.ID != "task-2" {
		t.Errorf("expected task-2, got %s", task2.ID)
	}

	tasks := f.ListTasks()
	if len(tasks) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("expected 2 tasks, got %d", len(tasks))
	}
	if tasks[0].Title != "Build Telephony Gateway" || tasks[1].Title != "SEO and LLMs.txt" {
		t.Errorf("unexpected task order: %+v", tasks)
	}

	status := f.FormatStatus()
	if !strings.Contains(status, "Build Telephony Gateway") || !strings.Contains(status, "SEO and LLMs.txt") {
		t.Errorf("FormatStatus missing task titles:\n%s", status)
	}
}

func TestFactory_StateTransitionsAndArtifacts(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	f := NewFactory(FactoryConfig{
		RootDir:      dir,
		TargetBranch: "main",
	})

	task, err := f.Submit("Add Feature X", "Detailed description")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Submit failed: %v", err)
	}

	if err := f.updateState(task.ID, StateSpec, "odin"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("updateState: %v", err)
	}
	if err := f.recordArtifact(task.ID, ".mimir/sdlc/01-SPEC-task-1.md"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("recordArtifact: %v", err)
	}

	got, ok := f.GetTask(task.ID)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("GetTask failed")
	}
	if got.State != StateSpec || got.AssignedTo != "odin" {
		t.Errorf("expected StateSpec/odin, got %s/%s", got.State, got.AssignedTo)
	}
	if len(got.Artifacts) != 1 || got.Artifacts[0] != ".mimir/sdlc/01-SPEC-task-1.md" {
		t.Errorf("unexpected artifacts: %v", got.Artifacts)
	}

	// Test failure state transition
	if err := f.failTask(task.ID, "simulated test failure"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failTask: %v", err)
	}
	failed, _ := f.GetTask(task.ID)
	if failed.State != StateFailed || !strings.Contains(failed.Error, "simulated test failure") {
		t.Errorf("expected failed state with error message, got %+v", failed)
	}
}

// N12: IDs come from a persisted counter, so a factory reloaded from disk
// never reissues an ID that an earlier instance already handed out.
func TestFactory_UniqueIDsAcrossReload(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	cfg := FactoryConfig{RootDir: dir, TargetBranch: "main"}

	f1 := NewFactory(cfg)
	if _, err := f1.Submit("One", "first"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := f1.Submit("Two", "second"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	f2 := NewFactory(cfg) // reload from disk
	third, err := f2.Submit("Three", "third")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if third.ID != "task-3" {
		t.Fatalf("expected task-3 after reload, got %s", third.ID)
	}
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for _, task := range f2.ListTasks() {
		if seen[task.ID] {
			t.Fatalf("duplicate task ID %s", task.ID)
		}
		seen[task.ID] = true
	}
}

// N12: branch slugs are git-ref-safe regardless of title punctuation.
func TestFactory_SanitizesBranchSlug(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	f := NewFactory(FactoryConfig{RootDir: dir, TargetBranch: "main"})

	task, err := f.Submit("Fix: Auth!! (ASAP) ### v2.0", "desc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want := "swarm/task-1-fix-auth-asap-v2-0"
	if task.Branch != want {
		t.Errorf("expected branch %q, got %q", want, task.Branch)
	}

	safe := regexp.MustCompile(`^swarm/task-\d+-[a-z0-9-]+$`)
	bang, err := f.Submit("!!!", "desc")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !safe.MatchString(bang.Branch) {
		t.Errorf("branch for punctuation-only title is not ref-safe: %q", bang.Branch)
	}
}

func gitCmd(t *testing.T, dir string, args ...string) {
	t.Helper()
	cmd := exec.Command("git", args...)
	cmd.Dir = dir
	if out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("git %v: %v\n%s", args, err, out)
	}
}

func initGitRepo(t *testing.T, dir string) {
	t.Helper()
	if _, err := exec.LookPath("git"); err != nil {
		t.Skip("git not available")
	}
	gitCmd(t, dir, "init")
	gitCmd(t, dir, "symbolic-ref", "HEAD", "refs/heads/main")
	gitCmd(t, dir, "config", "user.email", "swarm-test@example.com")
	gitCmd(t, dir, "config", "user.name", "Swarm Test")
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "README.md"), []byte("# test repo\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	gitCmd(t, dir, "add", ".")
	gitCmd(t, dir, "commit", "-m", "init")
}

// N6: ExecuteTask never merges on its own. A gate-passed task waits in
// StateAwaitingMerge until ApproveMerge is called, and ApproveMerge lands
// the merge on TargetBranch only.
func TestApproveMerge_GatesAndTargetsBranch(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	initGitRepo(t, dir)
	f := NewFactory(FactoryConfig{RootDir: dir, TargetBranch: "main"})
	task, err := f.Submit("Add Feature Z", "Detailed description")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	// Simulate Thor's committed work on the task branch.
	wtDir, err := f.setupWorktree(task.Branch)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("setupWorktree: %v", err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(wtDir, "feature.txt"), []byte("z\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	gitCmd(t, wtDir, "add", ".")
	gitCmd(t, wtDir, "commit", "-m", "feat: feature z")
	f.teardownWorktree(wtDir)
	if err := f.updateState(task.ID, StateAwaitingMerge, "none"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("updateState: %v", err)
	}

	// Approving from the wrong checked-out branch is refused and the task
	// stays awaiting merge (retryable).
	gitCmd(t, dir, "checkout", "-b", "other")
	if err := f.ApproveMerge(context.Background(), task.ID); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected refusal when main worktree is not on the target branch")
	}
	got, _ := f.GetTask(task.ID)
	if got.State != StateAwaitingMerge {
		t.Fatalf("expected task to stay StateAwaitingMerge after refusal, got %s", got.State)
	}
	gitCmd(t, dir, "checkout", "main")

	// Approval on the target branch merges and flips the state.
	if err := f.ApproveMerge(context.Background(), task.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ApproveMerge: %v", err)
	}
	got, _ = f.GetTask(task.ID)
	if got.State != StateMerged {
		t.Fatalf("expected StateMerged, got %s", got.State)
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, "feature.txt")); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("merged file missing from target branch worktree: %v", err)
	}

	// A task that never passed the gates cannot be approved.
	other, err := f.Submit("Backlog Task", "not run")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := f.ApproveMerge(context.Background(), other.ID); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected error approving a task that is not awaiting merge")
	}
}

// FIX 3 (audit): saveToDisk swallowed every error, so Submit reported
// success for tasks that were never persisted (and the persisted nextID
// guarantee silently broke with them). A failed persist must fail the
// submit and roll back the in-memory task.
func TestFactory_SubmitFailsWhenStoreUnwritable(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	// Block the store path: .mimir exists as a regular file, so creating
	// .mimir/swarm fails regardless of process privileges.
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, ".mimir"), []byte("not a dir"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	f := NewFactory(FactoryConfig{RootDir: dir, TargetBranch: "main"})
	if _, err := f.Submit("Doomed Task", "cannot persist"); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected Submit to fail when the task store cannot be written")
	}
	if got := f.ListTasks(); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("failed Submit must roll back the in-memory task, got %d tasks", len(got))
	}
}

// FIX 3: a corrupt task store must not be silently discarded. It is
// preserved under a side name and the factory starts empty; later saves
// write a fresh store and never touch the preserved bytes.
func TestFactory_CorruptStorePreserved(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	storeDir := filepath.Join(dir, ".mimir", "swarm")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(storeDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	garbage := []byte("{not json!!")
	storePath := filepath.Join(storeDir, "tasks.json")
	if err := os.WriteFile(storePath, garbage, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	f := NewFactory(FactoryConfig{RootDir: dir, TargetBranch: "main"})
	if got := f.ListTasks(); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("corrupt store must start empty, got %d tasks", len(got))
	}
	matches, err := filepath.Glob(storePath + ".corrupt-*")
	if err != nil || len(matches) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("expected exactly one preserved corrupt store, got %v (err %v)", matches, err)
	}
	preserved, err := os.ReadFile(matches[0])
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if string(preserved) != string(garbage) {
		t.Fatalf("preserved store content changed: %q", preserved)
	}

	// The factory still works, and the fresh save does not touch the
	// preserved copy.
	if _, err := f.Submit("Fresh Task", "after corruption"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Submit after corrupt store recovery failed: %v", err)
	}
	preserved2, _ := os.ReadFile(matches[0])
	if string(preserved2) != string(garbage) {
		t.Fatal("preserved corrupt store was modified by a later save")
	}
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(storePath)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if string(raw) == string(garbage) {
		t.Fatal("fresh store was not written after recovery")
	}
}

// stubProvider is a deterministic llm.Provider that finishes immediately
// with no tool calls, so Thor's agent pass completes without a model.
type stubProvider struct{}

func (stubProvider) ID() string { return "stub" }

func (stubProvider) Generate(context.Context, llm.GenerateRequest) (llm.GenerateResponse, error) {
	return llm.GenerateResponse{Content: "done", FinishReason: "stop"}, nil
}

func (stubProvider) Stream(context.Context, llm.GenerateRequest) (<-chan llm.StreamEvent, error) {
	return nil, nil
}

// captureSlog redirects the default slog logger into a buffer for the
// duration of the test.
func captureSlog(t *testing.T) *bytes.Buffer {
	t.Helper()
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	prev := slog.Default()
	slog.SetDefault(slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(&buf, nil)))
	t.Cleanup(func() { slog.SetDefault(prev) })
	return &buf
}

// FIX 5 (audit): the factory's trust boundaries (submit, gate outcome,
// merge approval, merge) must leave a log record carrying only the task
// ID and branch, never task description contents.
func TestFactory_TrustBoundaryLogging(t *testing.T) {
	buf := captureSlog(t)
	dir := t.TempDir()
	initGitRepo(t, dir)
	// Loki runs `go test ./...` in the worktree, so the repo needs a Go
	// module with a buildable package.
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "go.mod"), []byte("module swarmtest\n\ngo 1.24\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "main.go"), []byte("package main\n\nfunc main() {}\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	gitCmd(t, dir, "add", ".")
	gitCmd(t, dir, "commit", "-m", "add go module")

	f := NewFactory(FactoryConfig{
		RootDir:      dir,
		TargetBranch: "main",
		AgentConfig: agent.Config{
			Provider: stubProvider{},
			Cortex:   cortex.NewMemoryStore(),
			Model:    "stub-model",
		},
	})
	task, err := f.Submit("Logging Feature", "TOPSECRET description marker")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := f.ExecuteTask(context.Background(), task.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ExecuteTask: %v", err)
	}
	got, _ := f.GetTask(task.ID)
	if got.State != StateAwaitingMerge {
		t.Fatalf("expected StateAwaitingMerge, got %s (error %q)", got.State, got.Error)
	}
	if err := f.ApproveMerge(context.Background(), task.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ApproveMerge: %v", err)
	}

	out := buf.String()
	for _, want := range []string{"task submitted", "passed all gates", "merge approved", "merge performed", task.ID, task.Branch} {
		if !strings.Contains(out, want) {
			t.Errorf("log is missing %q\nlog:\n%s", want, out)
		}
	}
	if strings.Contains(out, "TOPSECRET") {
		t.Fatalf("log leaked task description contents:\n%s", out)
	}
}

func TestFactory_FailureLogging(t *testing.T) {

	for _, want := range []string{"task failed", task.ID, task.Branch} {
		if !strings.Contains(out, want) {
			t.Errorf("log is missing %q\nlog:\n%s", want, out)
		}
	}
	if strings.Contains(out, "TOPSECRET") {
		t.Fatalf("log leaked task description contents:\n%s", out)
	}
}

package tools

import "github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/sdlc"

// Default builds the native tool registry (the built-in, lean toolset).
// Small-model mode (F31) uses exactly this focused set: bash, read/write/list, todo.
func Default(workDir string) *Registry {
	r := NewRegistry()
	r.Register(&ShellTool{WorkDir: workDir})
	r.Register(&ReadFileTool{WorkDir: workDir})
	r.Register(&WriteFileTool{WorkDir: workDir})
	r.Register(&EditBlockTool{WorkDir: workDir})
	r.Register(&ListDirectoryTool{WorkDir: workDir})
	r.Register(&TodoTool{Store: NewTodoStore()})
	r.Register(&QuestionTool{})
	r.Register(&SkillTool{})
	r.Register(&IngestRepoTool{WorkDir: workDir})
	r.Register(&SDLCTool{Manager: sdlc.NewManager(workDir)})
	r.Register(&EpistemicAuditTool{})
	r.Register(&WebAuditTool{WorkDir: workDir})
	return r
}

package tools

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strings"
)

// EditBlockTool does a targeted search/replace in a file (F3.4). It tries an exact
// match first, then a whitespace-normalized fallback. expected_replacements controls
// how many occurrences to replace (default 1; 0 = all).
type EditBlockTool struct {
	WorkDir string
}

func (t *EditBlockTool) Name() string { return "edit_block" }
func (t *EditBlockTool) Description() string {
	return "Replace an exact block of text in a file within the workspace. Use old_string/new_string; set expected_replacements to 0 to replace all occurrences."
}
func (t *EditBlockTool) Parameters() any {
	return map[string]any{
		"type": "object",
		"properties": map[string]any{
			"path":                  map[string]any{"type": "string"},
			"old_string":            map[string]any{"type": "string"},
			"new_string":            map[string]any{"type": "string"},
			"expected_replacements": map[string]any{"type": "integer", "description": "0 = replace all; default 1"},
		},
		"required": []string{"path", "old_string", "new_string"},
	}
}

func (t *EditBlockTool) Run(ctx context.Context, args map[string]any) (string, error) {
	path, _ := args["path"].(string)
	oldStr, _ := args["old_string"].(string)
	newStr, _ := args["new_string"].(string)
	if oldStr == newStr {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("old_string and new_string are identical")
	}
	resolved, err := resolveWithinWorkDir(t.WorkDir, path)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	data, err := os.ReadFile(resolved)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	content := string(data)

	n := 1
	if v, ok := args["expected_replacements"].(float64); ok {
		n = int(v)
	}

	count := strings.Count(content, oldStr)
	if count == 0 {
		// 1. CRLF / LF line-ending normalization fallback (critical on Windows).
		if strings.Contains(content, "\r\n") && !strings.Contains(oldStr, "\r\n") {
			crlfOld := strings.ReplaceAll(oldStr, "\n", "\r\n")
			crlfNew := strings.ReplaceAll(newStr, "\n", "\r\n")
			if c := strings.Count(content, crlfOld); c > 0 {
				if n == 0 {
					content = strings.ReplaceAll(content, crlfOld, crlfNew)
				} else {
					content = replaceN(content, crlfOld, crlfNew, n)
				}
				if err := os.WriteFile(resolved, []byte(content), 0o644); err != nil {
					return "", err
				}
				return fmt.Sprintf("edited %s (CRLF-normalized, %d replacement(s))", path, min(n, c)), nil
			}
		}

		return "", notFoundErr(path, content, oldStr)
	}
	if n == 0 {
		content = strings.ReplaceAll(content, oldStr, newStr)
	} else {
		if count < n {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("expected %d occurrence(s) of old_string but found %d in %s", n, count, path)
		}
		content = replaceN(content, oldStr, newStr, n)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(resolved, []byte(content), 0o644); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	replaced := n
	if n == 0 {
		replaced = count
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("edited %s (%d replacement(s))", path, replaced), nil
}

// notFoundErr builds a self-healing error with smolcoder-style bounded line/offset
// location hints so small and fast models immediately see where the target block
// actually lives without re-reading the entire file.
func notFoundErr(path, content, oldStr string) error {
	hint := closestBlockHint(content, oldStr)
	preview := content
	if r := []rune(preview); len(r) > 1500 {
		preview = string(r[:1500]) + "\n...[truncated]"
	}
	if hint != "" {
		return fmt.Errorf(
			"old_string not found in %s. %s\nDo NOT give up or reply yet: copy the EXACT text from the hint or call read_file on %s, then retry edit_block. Current file preview:\n-----\n%s\n-----",
			path, hint, path, preview)
	}
	return fmt.Errorf(
		"old_string not found in %s. Do NOT give up or reply yet: call read_file on %s and copy the EXACT text (including any accented or special characters, byte-for-byte) into old_string, then retry edit_block. Current file content:\n-----\n%s\n-----",
		path, path, preview)
}

// closestBlockHint finds the line number and character offset in content that best
// matches the first non-empty line of oldStr (inspired by smolcoder's editFile offset hints).
func closestBlockHint(content, oldStr string) string {
	var needle string
	for _, l := range strings.Split(oldStr, "\n") {
		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(l)
		if len(trimmed) >= 4 {
			needle = trimmed
			break
		}
	}
	if needle == "" {
		return ""
	}
	lines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
	offset := 0
	for i, line := range lines {
		if strings.Contains(line, needle) || strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(line), strings.ToLower(needle)) {
			start := max(0, i-2)
			end := min(len(lines), i+6)
			snippet := strings.Join(lines[start:end], "\n")
			return fmt.Sprintf("Closest match is at line %d (byte offset %d):\n```text\n%s\n```", i+1, offset, snippet)
		}
		offset += len(line) + 1
	}
	return ""
}

func replaceN(s, old, new string, n int) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	i := 0
	for k := 0; k < n; k++ {
		j := strings.Index(s[i:], old)
		if j < 0 {
			break
		}
		b.WriteString(s[i : i+j])
		b.WriteString(new)
		i += j + len(old)
	}
	b.WriteString(s[i:])
	return b.String()
}

func (t *EpistemicAuditTool) Description() string {
	return "Run the Epistemic Critic & Verification Node against <retrieved_context> and <draft_report> to flag UNVERIFIED_TRAINING_DATA, EXTRAPOLATION, vendor bias, and hype, and compute pass_audit."

func (t *EpistemicAuditTool) Parameters() any {

		"type": "object",
		"properties": map[string]any{
			"retrieved_context": map[string]any{
				"type":        "string",
				"description": "The raw sources, snippets, and tool outputs retrieved during the session",
			},

				"type":        "string",
				"description": "The synthesized draft report or copy to audit against retrieved_context",
			},
			"format": map[string]any{
				"type":        "string",
				"description": "Output format: json (default) or markdown",
			},
		},
		"required": []string{"retrieved_context", "draft_report"},
	}
}

		return "", fmt.Errorf("draft_report is required")

	}
	raw, err := json.MarshalIndent(report, "", "  ")
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return string(raw), nil
}

		"properties": map[string]any{
			"path":    map[string]any{"type": "string"},
			"content": map[string]any{"type": "string"},
		},
		"required": []string{"path", "content"},
	}

func (t *WriteFileTool) Run(ctx context.Context, args map[string]any) (string, error) {

	content, _ := args["content"].(string)
	resolved, err := resolveWithinWorkDir(t.WorkDir, path)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if dir := filepath.Dir(resolved); dir != "." && dir != "" {
		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(resolved, []byte(content), 0o644); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("wrote %d bytes to %s", len(content), path), nil
}

// ListDirectoryTool lists a directory's entries (E3.2).
type ListDirectoryTool struct {
	WorkDir string
}

func (t *ListDirectoryTool) Name() string { return "list_directory" }
func (t *ListDirectoryTool) Description() string {
	return "List files and directories at a path within the workspace."
}
func (t *ListDirectoryTool) Parameters() any {
	return map[string]any{
		"type": "object",
		"properties": map[string]any{
			"path": map[string]any{"type": "string"},
		},
		"required": []string{"path"},
	}
}

func (t *ListDirectoryTool) Run(ctx context.Context, args map[string]any) (string, error) {

	resolved, err := resolveWithinWorkDir(t.WorkDir, path)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err

	if err != nil {
		return "", err

}

// resolveWithinWorkDir maps targetPath into the workspace and proves the
// result stays inside it, resolving symlinks on the longest existing
// prefix so a planted link cannot smuggle the path outside.
//
// Known ceiling (accepted, audit FIX 4): the containment proof and the
// caller's subsequent open are two separate steps, so this check has a
// TOCTOU race. A symlink swapped in between the check and the open can
// still redirect the open outside the workspace. Closing the race needs
// descriptor-relative opens (openat2 style), which path-based
// confinement cannot provide portably. The race is only winnable by a
// writer who can already create entries inside the workspace while a
// tool call runs, so the residual risk sits inside the trust domain the
// workspace already grants. The limitation is accepted and recorded
// here rather than engineered around.
func resolveWithinWorkDir(workDir, targetPath string) (string, error) {
	if strings.TrimSpace(targetPath) == "" {
		targetPath = "."
	}
	if workDir == "" {
		workDir = "."
	}
	absWorkDir, err := filepath.Abs(workDir)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	// Resolve symlinks in the root itself (e.g. /tmp aliases) so the
	// containment checks below compare real paths on both sides.
	if resolvedRoot, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(absWorkDir); err == nil {
		absWorkDir = resolvedRoot
	}
	var candidate string
	if filepath.IsAbs(targetPath) {
		candidate = filepath.Clean(targetPath)
	} else {
		candidate = filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(absWorkDir, targetPath))
	}
	if !pathWithinDir(absWorkDir, candidate) {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("security violation: path %q escapes workspace boundary %q", targetPath, workDir)
	}
	// Symlink check (N9): a purely lexical check lets a symlink inside the
	// workspace point anywhere on disk. Resolve the longest existing
	// prefix of the candidate and re-check containment on the real path.
	// A not-yet-existing final component is fine: its parent is resolved.
	resolved, err := resolveExistingPrefix(candidate)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("security violation: cannot resolve path %q: %w", targetPath, err)
	}
	if !pathWithinDir(absWorkDir, resolved) {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("security violation: path %q escapes workspace boundary %q via symlink", targetPath, workDir)
	}
	return resolved, nil
}

// pathWithinDir reports whether candidate is dir itself or lives under it.
func pathWithinDir(dir, candidate string) bool {
	rel, err := filepath.Rel(dir, candidate)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	return rel == "." || (rel != ".." && !strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)))
}

// resolveExistingPrefix resolves symlinks on the longest prefix of path
// that exists on disk and reattaches the remaining (not yet existing)
// components unchanged.
func resolveExistingPrefix(path string) (string, error) {
	p := path
	var suffix []string
	for {
		if _, err := os.Lstat(p); err == nil {
			resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(p)
			if err != nil {
				return "", err
			}
			for i := len(suffix) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
				resolved = filepath.Join(resolved, suffix[i])
			}
			return resolved, nil
		}
		parent := filepath.Dir(p)
		if parent == p {
			return path, nil
		}
		suffix = append(suffix, filepath.Base(p))
		p = parent
	}
}

package tools

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
)

// Option is one choice in a question.
type Option struct {
	Label       string `json:"label"`
	Description string `json:"description"`
}

// Question is a structured question posed to the user (like opencode's question tool).
type Question struct {
	Question string   `json:"question"`
	Header   string   `json:"header"`
	Options  []Option `json:"options"`
	Multiple bool     `json:"multiple"`
}

// QuestionTool lets the agent ask the user structured multiple-choice questions (F45).
// The TUI (Charmbracelet Huh-style selector) or GUI renders the options as interactive
// choices; a "type your own answer" option is always added.
type QuestionTool struct {
	// AskFunc, when set by the TUI or HTTP server, blocks to let the user pick
	// an option interactively and returns their formatted answer.
	AskFunc func(ctx context.Context, questions []Question) (string, error)
}

func (t *QuestionTool) Name() string { return "question" }
func (t *QuestionTool) Description() string {
	return "Ask the user a structured question with options to gather preferences, decisions, or clarifications. Use during Discovery and whenever you need the user to choose."
}
func (t *QuestionTool) Parameters() any {
	return map[string]any{
		"type": "object",
		"properties": map[string]any{
			"questions": map[string]any{
				"type": "array",
				"items": map[string]any{
					"type": "object",
					"properties": map[string]any{
						"question": map[string]any{"type": "string"},
						"header":   map[string]any{"type": "string"},
						"multiple": map[string]any{"type": "boolean"},
						"options": map[string]any{
							"type": "array",
							"items": map[string]any{
								"type": "object",
								"properties": map[string]any{
									"label":       map[string]any{"type": "string"},
									"description": map[string]any{"type": "string"},
								},
								"required": []string{"label", "description"},
							},
						},
					},
					"required": []string{"question", "header", "options"},
				},
			},
		},
		"required": []string{"questions"},
	}
}

func (t *QuestionTool) Run(ctx context.Context, args map[string]any) (string, error) {
	rawQs, _ := args["questions"].([]any)
	questions := parseQuestions(rawQs)
	if t.AskFunc != nil && len(questions) > 0 {
		return t.AskFunc(ctx, questions)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("posed %d question(s) to the user (awaiting selection)", len(rawQs)), nil
}

func parseQuestions(raw []any) []Question {
	var out []Question
	for _, item := range raw {
		m, ok := item.(map[string]any)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		q := Question{
			Question: strField(m, "question"),
			Header:   strField(m, "header"),
		}
		if mult, ok := m["multiple"].(bool); ok {
			q.Multiple = mult
		}
		if opts, ok := m["options"].([]any); ok {
			for _, ro := range opts {
				if om, ok := ro.(map[string]any); ok {
					q.Options = append(q.Options, Option{
						Label:       strField(om, "label"),
						Description: strField(om, "description"),
					})
				}
			}
		}
		if q.Question != "" {
			out = append(out, q)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func strField(m map[string]any, key string) string {
	v, _ := m[key].(string)
	return v
}

package tools

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/sdlc"
)

// SDLCTool allows Mímir to inspect, advance, or save deliverables for the 7-Phase
// Software Development Life Cycle (Planning, Analysis, Design, Implementation,
// Testing, Deployment, Maintenance) across Agile, Waterfall, and DevOps models.
type SDLCTool struct {
	Manager *sdlc.Manager
}

func (t *SDLCTool) Name() string { return "sdlc" }

func (t *SDLCTool) Description() string {
	return "Manage the 7-Phase SDLC (status, set_phase, advance, set_method, save_deliverable) so only the active lifecycle phase prompt & deliverable are loaded."
}

func (t *SDLCTool) Parameters() any {
	return map[string]any{
		"type": "object",
		"properties": map[string]any{
			"action": map[string]any{
				"type":        "string",
				"description": "One of: status, set_phase, advance, set_method, save_deliverable, sign_off",
			},
			"phase": map[string]any{
				"type":        "string",
				"description": "Phase step (1..7) or ID (planning, analysis, design, implementation, testing, deployment, maintenance)",
			},
			"method": map[string]any{
				"type":        "string",
				"description": "SDLC execution methodology: agile, waterfall, or devops",
			},
			"content": map[string]any{
				"type":        "string",
				"description": "Markdown content when action is save_deliverable (writes .mimir/sdlc/0X-*.md and signs off the phase)",
			},
		},
		"required": []string{"action"},
	}
}

func (t *SDLCTool) Run(_ context.Context, args map[string]any) (string, error) {
	if t.Manager == nil {
		t.Manager = sdlc.NewManager(".")
	}
	action, _ := args["action"].(string)
	phaseStr, _ := args["phase"].(string)
	methodStr, _ := args["method"].(string)
	content, _ := args["content"].(string)

	switch strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(action)) {
	case "status", "board", "":
		return t.Manager.FormatBoard(), nil
	case "set_phase", "phase":
		spec, err := t.Manager.SetPhase(phaseStr)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("SDLC active phase -> [%d/7] %s (Persona: %s | Deliverable: %s)",
			spec.Step, spec.Title, spec.Persona, spec.Deliverable), nil
	case "advance", "next":
		spec, err := t.Manager.Advance()
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("Advanced SDLC -> [%d/7] %s (Persona: %s | Deliverable: %s)",
			spec.Step, spec.Title, spec.Persona, spec.Deliverable), nil
	case "set_method", "method":
		if t.Manager.Methodology() == sdlc.MethodWaterfall {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("security policy: SDLC methodology cannot be changed by the model while in strict Waterfall mode (use the CLI or TUI)")
		}
		if err := t.Manager.SetMethodology(methodStr); err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("SDLC methodology set to %q", t.Manager.Methodology()), nil
	case "save_deliverable", "deliverable":
		if strings.TrimSpace(content) == "" {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("content is required for save_deliverable")
		}
		var pid sdlc.PhaseID
		if phaseStr != "" {
			if spec, ok := sdlc.LookupPhase(phaseStr); ok {
				pid = spec.ID
			}
		}
		path, err := t.Manager.SaveDeliverable(pid, content)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("Saved SDLC deliverable to %s.", path), nil
	case "sign_off", "signoff":
		if t.Manager.Methodology() == sdlc.MethodWaterfall {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("security policy: sign_off in strict Waterfall mode requires user approval via `mimir sdlc signoff` or TUI /sdlc signoff")
		}
		var pid sdlc.PhaseID
		if phaseStr != "" {
			if spec, ok := sdlc.LookupPhase(phaseStr); ok {
				pid = spec.ID
			}
		}
		spec := t.Manager.SignOff(pid)
		return fmt.Sprintf("Signed off SDLC Step %d (%s - %s).", spec.Step, spec.Title, spec.Deliverable), nil
	default:
		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown sdlc action %q (use status, set_phase, advance, set_method, save_deliverable, sign_off)", action)
	}
}

package tools

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"runtime"
)

const maxShellOutputBytes = 32 * 1024 // 32 KB context cap (sausheong/harness pattern)

// ShellTool runs a shell command and returns its output (E3.1).
type ShellTool struct {
	WorkDir string
}

func (t *ShellTool) Name() string        { return "bash" }
func (t *ShellTool) Description() string { return "Run a shell command and return stdout/stderr." }
func (t *ShellTool) Parameters() any {
	return map[string]any{
		"type": "object",
		"properties": map[string]any{
			"command": map[string]any{"type": "string", "description": "The command to run"},
		},
		"required": []string{"command"},
	}
}

func (t *ShellTool) Run(ctx context.Context, args map[string]any) (string, error) {
	command, _ := args["command"].(string)
	if command == "" {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("command is required")
	}
	var cmd *exec.Cmd
	if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
		cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "powershell", "-NoProfile", "-Command", command)
	} else {
		cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "bash", "-c", command)
	}
	if t.WorkDir != "" {
		cmd.Dir = t.WorkDir
	}
	var out bytes.Buffer
	cmd.Stdout = &out
	cmd.Stderr = &out
	err := cmd.Run()
	result := capShellOutput(out.String())
	if err != nil {
		return result, fmt.Errorf("command failed: %w", err)
	}
	return result, nil
}

func capShellOutput(s string) string {
	if len(s) <= maxShellOutputBytes {
		return s
	}
	spillFile, err := os.CreateTemp("", "mimir-bash-*.log")
	spillNote := ""
	if err == nil {
		_ = os.Chmod(spillFile.Name(), 0o600)
		_, _ = spillFile.WriteString(s)
		_ = spillFile.Close()
		spillNote = fmt.Sprintf(" Full output (%d bytes) saved to %s.", len(s), filepath.Clean(spillFile.Name()))
	}
	head := s[:16*1024]
	tail := s[len(s)-12*1024:]
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s\n\n... [output truncated: %d bytes omitted.%s] ...\n\n%s",
		head, len(s)-28*1024, spillNote, tail)
}

package tools

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
)

// SkillTool implements progressive SKILL.md disclosure (inspired by microsoft/agent-framework-go
// and htekdev/ai-harness). It searches workspace .mimir/skills and the centralized H:\AI\skills
// library so the agent can pull specialized domain instructions on demand without bloating
// the base system prompt.
type SkillTool struct {
	SearchDirs []string
}

func (t *SkillTool) Name() string { return "load_skill" }
func (t *SkillTool) Description() string {
	return "List or load a specialized SKILL.md instruction file by name (action='list' or action='load')."
}
func (t *SkillTool) Parameters() any {
	return map[string]any{
		"type": "object",
		"properties": map[string]any{
			"action": map[string]any{"type": "string", "enum": []string{"list", "load"}},
			"name":   map[string]any{"type": "string", "description": "Skill folder name when action='load'"},
		},
		"required": []string{"action"},
	}
}

func (t *SkillTool) dirs() []string {
	if len(t.SearchDirs) > 0 {
		return t.SearchDirs
	}
	return []string{".mimir/skills", `H:\AI\skills`}
}

func (t *SkillTool) Run(ctx context.Context, args map[string]any) (string, error) {
	action, _ := args["action"].(string)
	switch action {
	case "list":
		var names []string
		seen := map[string]bool{}
		for _, d := range t.dirs() {
			entries, err := os.ReadDir(d)
			if err != nil {
				continue
			}
			for _, e := range entries {
				if !e.IsDir() || seen[e.Name()] {
					continue
				}
				skillPath := filepath.Join(d, e.Name(), "SKILL.md")
				if _, err := os.Stat(skillPath); err == nil {
					seen[e.Name()] = true
					names = append(names, e.Name())
				}
			}
		}
		if len(names) == 0 {
			return "no skills found", nil
		}
		if len(names) > 60 {
			return fmt.Sprintf("%d skills available (first 60): %s", len(names), strings.Join(names[:60], ", ")), nil
		}
		return "available skills: " + strings.Join(names, ", "), nil
	case "load":
		name, _ := args["name"].(string)
		name = filepath.Clean(strings.TrimSpace(name))
		if name == "" || strings.Contains(name, "..") {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("valid skill name required")
		}
		for _, d := range t.dirs() {
			p := filepath.Join(d, name, "SKILL.md")
			if data, err := os.ReadFile(p); err == nil {
				return string(data), nil
			}
		}
		return "", fmt.Errorf("skill %q not found", name)
	default:
		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown action %q (use 'list' or 'load')", action)
	}
}

FILE: internal/tools/todo.go

package tools

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"sort"
	"sync"
)

// TodoStatus is the state of a to-do item.
type TodoStatus string

const (
	TodoPending    TodoStatus = "pending"
	TodoInProgress TodoStatus = "in_progress"
	TodoCompleted  TodoStatus = "completed"
	TodoBlocked    TodoStatus = "blocked"
)

// Todo is one to-do item (the small model's working memory; F31/E3.5).
type Todo struct {
	ID      int        `json:"id"`
	Ord     int        `json:"ord"`
	Content string     `json:"content"`
	Status  TodoStatus `json:"status"`
}

// TodoStore is an in-memory to-do list (backed by SurrealDB in E1.4/E3.5).
type TodoStore struct {
	mu     sync.Mutex
	nextID int
	items  map[int]*Todo
}

func NewTodoStore() *TodoStore {
	return &TodoStore{nextID: 1, items: map[int]*Todo{}}
}

func (s *TodoStore) Add(content string) *Todo {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	t := &Todo{ID: s.nextID, Ord: s.nextID, Content: content, Status: TodoPending}
	s.items[t.ID] = t
	s.nextID++
	return t
}

func (s *TodoStore) SetStatus(id int, status TodoStatus) bool {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if t, ok := s.items[id]; ok {
		t.Status = status
		return true
	}
	return false
}

func (s *TodoStore) List() []*Todo {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	out := make([]*Todo, 0, len(s.items))
	for _, t := range s.items {
		out = append(out, t)
	}
	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Ord < out[j].Ord })
	return out
}

// TodoTool exposes the to-do store as an agent Tool.
type TodoTool struct{ Store *TodoStore }

func (t *TodoTool) Name() string { return "todo" }
func (t *TodoTool) Description() string {
	return "Manage the task to-do list (add, update status, list)."
}
func (t *TodoTool) Parameters() any {
	return map[string]any{
		"type": "object",
		"properties": map[string]any{
			"action":  map[string]any{"type": "string", "enum": []string{"add", "update", "list"}},
			"content": map[string]any{"type": "string"},
			"id":      map[string]any{"type": "integer"},
			"status":  map[string]any{"type": "string"},
		},
		"required": []string{"action"},
	}
}

func (t *TodoTool) Run(ctx context.Context, args map[string]any) (string, error) {
	action, _ := args["action"].(string)
	switch action {
	case "add":
		content, _ := args["content"].(string)
		todo := t.Store.Add(content)
		return fmt.Sprintf("added todo #%d: %s", todo.ID, todo.Content), nil
	case "update":
		id, _ := args["id"].(float64)
		status, _ := args["status"].(string)
		if t.Store.SetStatus(int(id), TodoStatus(status)) {
			return fmt.Sprintf("todo #%d -> %s", int(id), status), nil
		}
		return "", fmt.Errorf("todo #%d not found", int(id))
	case "list":
		var s string
		for _, todo := range t.Store.List() {
			s += fmt.Sprintf("#%d [%s] %s\n", todo.ID, todo.Status, todo.Content)
		}
		return s, nil
	default:
		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown action %q", action)
	}
}


==============================================================================
FILE: internal/tools/tool.go
==============================================================================
// Package tools defines the built-in system tools (F3): terminal, filesystem,
// code execution, and the tool registry the agent calls into.
package tools

import "context"

// Tool is one capability the agent can call.
type Tool interface {
	// Name returns the tool name (e.g. "bash", "read_file").
	Name() string
	// Description explains the tool to the model.
	Description() string
	// Parameters returns the tool's JSON Schema (an object schema).
	Parameters() any
	// Run executes the tool with the given arguments and returns its output.
	Run(ctx context.Context, args map[string]any) (string, error)
}

// Registry holds the available tools.
type Registry struct {
	tools map[string]Tool
}

// NewRegistry returns an empty tool registry.
func NewRegistry() *Registry {
	return &Registry{tools: map[string]Tool{}}
}

// Register adds a tool to the registry.
func (r *Registry) Register(t Tool) {
	r.tools[t.Name()] = t
}

// Get returns a tool by name.
func (r *Registry) Get(name string) (Tool, bool) {
	t, ok := r.tools[name]
	return t, ok
}

// All returns every registered tool.
func (r *Registry) All() []Tool {
	out := make([]Tool, 0, len(r.tools))
	for _, t := range r.tools {
		out = append(out, t)
	}
	return out
}

// IsWriteTool reports whether a tool mutates files or executes shell commands.
// In read-only ("ro") mode, write tools are hidden from the model's tool schema
// so smaller models cannot hallucinate edits (smolcoder pattern).
func IsWriteTool(name string) bool {
	switch name {
	case "write_file", "edit_block", "bash":
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}

// ForMode returns the tools visible for the given permission mode ("ro", "edit", "bypass").
func (r *Registry) ForMode(mode string) []Tool {
	if mode != "ro" {
		return r.All()
	}
	out := make([]Tool, 0, len(r.tools))
	for _, t := range r.tools {
		if !IsWriteTool(t.Name()) {
			out = append(out, t)
		}
	}
	return out
}

package tools

func TestTodoStoreLifecycle(t *testing.T) {
	s := NewTodoStore()
	todo := s.Add("write tests")
	if todo.ID != 1 || todo.Status != TodoPending {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected todo: %+v", todo)
	}
	if !s.SetStatus(1, TodoCompleted) {
		t.Fatal("SetStatus failed")
	}
	list := s.List()
	if len(list) != 1 || list[0].Status != TodoCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected list: %+v", list)
	}
}

	tool := &TodoTool{Store: NewTodoStore()}
	ctx := context.Background()
	if _, err := tool.Run(ctx, map[string]any{"action": "add", "content": "ship it"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("add failed: %v", err)
	}
	out, err := tool.Run(ctx, map[string]any{"action": "list"})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("list failed: %v", err)
	}
	if out == "" {
		t.Error("expected non-empty todo list")
	}
}

func TestWorkspaceConfinementPreventEscapes(t *testing.T) {
	wsDir := t.TempDir()
	outsideDir := t.TempDir()
	outsideFile := filepath.Join(outsideDir, "secret.txt")
	if err := os.WriteFile(outsideFile, []byte("sensitive info"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	r := Default(wsDir)

	// 1. read_file outside workspace should fail
	rf, ok := r.Get("read_file")
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("read_file not found")
	}
	if _, err := rf.Run(context.Background(), map[string]any{"path": outsideFile}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected security error reading file outside workspace")
	}

	// 2. read_file with relative path escaping workspace should fail
	if _, err := rf.Run(context.Background(), map[string]any{"path": "../secret.txt"}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected security error for path traversal ../")
	}

	// 3. write_file outside workspace should fail
	wf, ok := r.Get("write_file")
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("write_file not found")
	}
	if _, err := wf.Run(context.Background(), map[string]any{"path": outsideFile, "content": "malicious"}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected security error writing file outside workspace")
	}

	// 4. write_file inside workspace should succeed
	insideFile := filepath.Join(wsDir, "ok.txt")
	if _, err := wf.Run(context.Background(), map[string]any{"path": "ok.txt", "content": "safe"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to write inside workspace: %v", err)
	}
	data, err := os.ReadFile(insideFile)
	if err != nil || string(data) != "safe" {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected content: %s, %v", string(data), err)
	}
}

// N9: a symlink inside the workspace pointing outside must not pass the
// confinement check for read, write, or list; a symlink that stays inside
// the workspace keeps working.
func TestWorkspaceConfinementRejectsSymlinkEscape(t *testing.T) {
	wsDir := t.TempDir()
	outsideDir := t.TempDir()
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(outsideDir, "secret.txt"), []byte("sensitive info"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.Symlink(outsideDir, filepath.Join(wsDir, "escape")); err != nil {
		t.Skipf("symlinks unavailable: %v", err)
	}
	// Positive control: an in-workspace symlink target.
	realDir := filepath.Join(wsDir, "real")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(realDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(realDir, "ok.txt"), []byte("inside"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.Symlink(realDir, filepath.Join(wsDir, "alias")); err != nil {
		t.Skipf("symlinks unavailable: %v", err)
	}

	r := Default(wsDir)
	ctx := context.Background()

	rf, _ := r.Get("read_file")
	if _, err := rf.Run(ctx, map[string]any{"path": "escape/secret.txt"}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected security error reading through symlink escape")
	}
	if out, err := rf.Run(ctx, map[string]any{"path": "alias/ok.txt"}); err != nil || out != "inside" {
		t.Fatalf("expected in-workspace symlink read to succeed, got %q, %v", out, err)
	}

	wf, _ := r.Get("write_file")
	if _, err := wf.Run(ctx, map[string]any{"path": "escape/new.txt", "content": "malicious"}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected security error writing through symlink escape")
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(outsideDir, "new.txt")); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
		t.Fatal("write through symlink escape created a file outside the workspace")
	}
	// Writing a not-yet-existing file through an in-workspace path is fine.
	if _, err := wf.Run(ctx, map[string]any{"path": "alias/new.txt", "content": "fine"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("expected write via in-workspace symlink parent to succeed: %v", err)
	}

	lf, _ := r.Get("list_directory")
	if _, err := lf.Run(ctx, map[string]any{"path": "escape"}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected security error listing through symlink escape")
	}
}

package tools

func TestAuditWebDirectory_CatchesImpeccableSlopAndMissingSEOGEO(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()

	slopHTML := "<!doctype html>\n<html><head></head><body>\n" +
		"<div class=\"card\"><div class=\"card bg-gradient-to-r from-purple-600 to-indigo-600\">\n" +

	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("AuditWebDirectory: %v", err)
	}
	if rep.PassAudit {
		t.Fatalf("expected slop HTML to fail audit, got PASS:\n%s", rep.FormatMarkdown())

	rulesHit := make(map[string]bool)
	for _, f := range rep.Findings {

	expectedRules := []string{
		"IMPECCABLE_EM_DASH",
		"IMPECCABLE_AI_SLOP_COPY",
		"IMPECCABLE_PURPLE_GRADIENT",

		"GEO_MISSING_ROBOTS_TXT",
		"GEO_MISSING_SITEMAP_XML",
		"GEO_MISSING_LLMS_TXT",
	}
	for _, rule := range expectedRules {
		if !rulesHit[rule] {

		}
	}
}

	if err != nil || !strings.Contains(out, "`PASS`") {

	}

	if _, err := tool.Run(context.Background(), map[string]any{"path": "."}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("expected in-workspace audit to succeed: %v", err)
	}
}

package tools

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"strings"
)

// WebFinding represents a single deterministic violation from the Impeccable Design
// or 4-Layer SEO/GEO & Conversion detector suite.
type WebFinding struct {
	RuleID      string `json:"rule_id"`
	Layer       string `json:"layer"`    // "impeccable_ui", "layer1_seo_geo", "layer2_entity", "layer3_provenance", "layer4_lead_gen"
	Severity    string `json:"severity"` // "HIGH", "MEDIUM", "LOW"
	File        string `json:"file"`
	Description string `json:"description"`
	Remediation string `json:"remediation"`
}

// WebAuditReport is the structured output of AuditWebDirectory.
type WebAuditReport struct {
	RootDir          string       `json:"root_dir"`
	ScannedFiles     int          `json:"scanned_files"`
	HasProductDoc    bool         `json:"has_product_md"`
	HasDesignDoc     bool         `json:"has_design_md"`
	HasRobotsTxt     bool         `json:"has_robots_txt"`
	HasSitemapXML    bool         `json:"has_sitemap_xml"`
	HasLLMsTxt       bool         `json:"has_llms_txt"`
	ValidJSONLDCount int          `json:"valid_jsonld_count"`
	Findings         []WebFinding `json:"findings"`
	PassAudit        bool         `json:"pass_audit"`
}

// FormatMarkdown renders the deterministic Web/SEO/GEO + Impeccable Design audit report.
func (r WebAuditReport) FormatMarkdown() string {
	var b strings.Builder
	verdict := "PASS"
	if !r.PassAudit {
		verdict = "FAIL"
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "## Mimir Web, SEO/GEO & Impeccable Design Audit: `%s`\n", verdict)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Scanned Files**: `%d`\n", r.ScannedFiles)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Durable Context (`PRODUCT.md` / `DESIGN.md`)**: `product=%v`, `design=%v`\n", r.HasProductDoc, r.HasDesignDoc)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Discovery Files**: `robots.txt=%v`, `sitemap.xml=%v`, `llms.txt=%v`\n", r.HasRobotsTxt, r.HasSitemapXML, r.HasLLMsTxt)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Valid Schema.org JSON-LD Blocks**: `%d`\n", r.ValidJSONLDCount)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Total Findings**: `%d`\n", len(r.Findings))

	if len(r.Findings) > 0 {
		b.WriteString("\n### Findings\n")
		for _, f := range r.Findings {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **[%s | %s]** `%s` (%s): %s -- *Fix: %s*\n",
				f.Severity, f.RuleID, f.File, f.Layer, f.Description, f.Remediation)
		}
	}
	return strings.TrimRight(b.String(), "\n")
}

var (
	aiSlopPhrases = []string{
		"in today's fast-paced world",
		"unleash the power",
		"revolutionize the way",
		"delve into",
		"seamless digital landscape",
		"elevate your digital journey",
		"unlock the full potential",
		"game-changing solution",
		"synergistic ecosystem",
	}

	purpleGradientTokens = []string{
		"from-purple-",
		"from-indigo-",
		"via-purple-",
		"to-purple-",
		"to-indigo-",
		"linear-gradient(135deg, #8b5cf6",
		"linear-gradient(90deg, #6366f1",
	}

	reH1Tag          = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)<h1[\s>]`)
	reJSONLD         = regexp.MustCompile(`(?is)<script[^>]*type=["']application/ld\+json["'][^>]*>(.*?)</script>`)
	reMarketingStats = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)\b(\d+(?:\.\d+)?%\s+(?:faster|higher|more|increase|conversion|uptime)|\d+(?:\.\d+)?x\s+(?:faster|more|roi|growth))\b`)
	reNestedCard     = regexp.MustCompile(`(?is)<div[^>]*class=["'][^"']*\bcard\b[^"']*["'][^>]*>.*?<div[^>]*class=["'][^"']*\bcard\b[^"']*["']`)
)

// LoadDesignContext reads durable PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md files from workDir (if present)
// and returns a compact summary (<600 chars) for injection during SDLC Steps 3-5 on web/UI tasks.
func LoadDesignContext(workDir string) string {
	if strings.TrimSpace(workDir) == "" {
		workDir = "."
	}
	var parts []string
	for _, name := range []string{"PRODUCT.md", "DESIGN.md"} {
		p := filepath.Join(workDir, name)
		raw, err := os.ReadFile(p)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		text := strings.TrimSpace(string(raw))
		if text == "" {
			continue
		}
		// Collapse whitespace to keep context compact for both big and tiny models.
		compact := strings.Join(strings.Fields(text), " ")
		if len(compact) > 260 {
			compact = compact[:260] + "..."
		}
		parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("[%s]: %s", name, compact))
	}
	return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
}

// AuditWebDirectory runs deterministic Impeccable UI anti-slop detectors and
// Mimir's 4-Layer SEO/GEO & Conversion detectors across a web project directory.
func AuditWebDirectory(rootDir string) (WebAuditReport, error) {
	if strings.TrimSpace(rootDir) == "" {
		rootDir = "."
	}
	absRoot, err := filepath.Abs(rootDir)
	if err != nil {
		return WebAuditReport{}, err
	}

	rep := WebAuditReport{
		RootDir:  absRoot,
		Findings: []WebFinding{},
	}

	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(absRoot, "PRODUCT.md")); err == nil {
		rep.HasProductDoc = true
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(absRoot, "DESIGN.md")); err == nil {
		rep.HasDesignDoc = true
	}

	var htmlFiles []string
	_ = filepath.WalkDir(absRoot, func(path string, d os.DirEntry, walkErr error) error {
		if walkErr != nil {
			return nil
		}
		name := d.Name()
		if d.IsDir() {
			if name == ".git" || name == "node_modules" || name == "vendor" || name == ".next" || name == "dist" || name == ".mimir" {
				return filepath.SkipDir
			}
			return nil
		}
		lowerName := strings.ToLower(name)
		switch lowerName {
		case "robots.txt":
			rep.HasRobotsTxt = true
		case "sitemap.xml":
			rep.HasSitemapXML = true
		case "llms.txt":
			rep.HasLLMsTxt = true
		}

		ext := strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(name))
		switch ext {
		case ".html", ".htm", ".astro", ".tsx", ".jsx", ".vue", ".svelte", ".php", ".css":
			rep.ScannedFiles++
			rel, relErr := filepath.Rel(absRoot, path)
			if relErr != nil {
				rel = name
			}
			rel = filepath.ToSlash(rel)
			raw, readErr := os.ReadFile(path)
			if readErr != nil {
				return nil
			}
			content := string(raw)
			auditSingleWebFile(&rep, rel, ext, content)
			if ext == ".html" || ext == ".htm" || ext == ".astro" || ext == ".php" {
				htmlFiles = append(htmlFiles, rel)
			}
		}
		return nil
	})

	// Layer 1 Discovery file checks when at least one HTML/page file exists in the project.
	if len(htmlFiles) > 0 {
		if !rep.HasRobotsTxt {
			rep.Findings = append(rep.Findings, WebFinding{
				RuleID:      "GEO_MISSING_ROBOTS_TXT",
				Layer:       "layer1_seo_geo",
				Severity:    "MEDIUM",
				File:        "robots.txt",
				Description: "Missing /robots.txt crawler directives file",
				Remediation: "Create robots.txt allowing search and AI answer engine crawlers and referencing Sitemap.",
			})
		}
		if !rep.HasSitemapXML {
			rep.Findings = append(rep.Findings, WebFinding{
				RuleID:      "GEO_MISSING_SITEMAP_XML",
				Layer:       "layer1_seo_geo",
				Severity:    "MEDIUM",
				File:        "sitemap.xml",
				Description: "Missing /sitemap.xml index file",
				Remediation: "Generate sitemap.xml listing canonical URLs with <lastmod> timestamps.",
			})
		}
		if !rep.HasLLMsTxt {
			rep.Findings = append(rep.Findings, WebFinding{
				RuleID:      "GEO_MISSING_LLMS_TXT",
				Layer:       "layer1_seo_geo",
				Severity:    "MEDIUM",
				File:        "llms.txt",
				Description: "Missing /llms.txt AI answer-engine summary file",
				Remediation: "Add /llms.txt with concise entity facts, product/service summary, pricing units, and canonical docs links.",
			})
		}
	}

	highCount := 0
	for _, f := range rep.Findings {
		if f.Severity == "HIGH" {
			highCount++
		}
	}
	rep.PassAudit = highCount == 0
	return rep, nil
}

func auditSingleWebFile(rep *WebAuditReport, relPath, ext, content string) {
	lower := strings.ToLower(content)

	// 1. Impeccable Detector: Em dash check (\u2014)
	if strings.Contains(content, "\u2014") || strings.Contains(lower, "&mdash;") {
		rep.Findings = append(rep.Findings, WebFinding{
			RuleID:      "IMPECCABLE_EM_DASH",
			Layer:       "impeccable_ui",
			Severity:    "HIGH",
			File:        relPath,
			Description: "Contains banned em dash character or &mdash; entity",
			Remediation: "Replace em dashes with standard hyphens (-), double hyphens (--), colons, or clean sentence breaks.",
		})
	}

	// 2. Impeccable Detector: Formulaic AI Slop Copy
	for _, phrase := range aiSlopPhrases {
		if strings.Contains(lower, phrase) {
			rep.Findings = append(rep.Findings, WebFinding{
				RuleID:      "IMPECCABLE_AI_SLOP_COPY",
				Layer:       "impeccable_ui",
				Severity:    "HIGH",
				File:        relPath,
				Description: fmt.Sprintf("Contains generic AI slop filler copy (%q)", phrase),
				Remediation: "Replace filler copy with specific, verifiable entity facts, concrete numbers, or direct product capabilities.",
			})
			break
		}
	}

	// 3. Impeccable Detector: Purple/Indigo Gradient Cliche
	for _, tok := range purpleGradientTokens {
		if strings.Contains(lower, tok) {
			rep.Findings = append(rep.Findings, WebFinding{
				RuleID:      "IMPECCABLE_PURPLE_GRADIENT",
				Layer:       "impeccable_ui",
				Severity:    "MEDIUM",
				File:        relPath,
				Description: fmt.Sprintf("Uses formulaic AI purple/indigo gradient token (%q)", tok),
				Remediation: "Use intentional brand palette tokens defined in DESIGN.md instead of default purple/indigo gradients.",
			})
			break
		}
	}

	// 4. Impeccable Detector: Card-in-Card Nesting Soup
	if reNestedCard.MatchString(content) {
		rep.Findings = append(rep.Findings, WebFinding{
			RuleID:      "IMPECCABLE_NESTED_CARDS",
			Layer:       "impeccable_ui",
			Severity:    "MEDIUM",
			File:        relPath,
			Description: "Nested .card inside .card container detected (visual clutter)",
			Remediation: "Flatten nested cards using clean spacing, dividers, or definition lists.",
		})
	}

	// 5. Layer 3 Provenance Detector: Unlabeled marketing stats in web copy
	if ext != ".css" {
		if matches := reMarketingStats.FindAllString(content, -1); len(matches) > 0 {
			if !strings.Contains(lower, "[vendor claim]") && !strings.Contains(lower, "source:") && !strings.Contains(lower, "citation") {
				rep.Findings = append(rep.Findings, WebFinding{
					RuleID:      "PROVENANCE_UNLABELED_STAT",
					Layer:       "layer3_provenance",
					Severity:    "HIGH",
					File:        relPath,
					Description: fmt.Sprintf("Unbacked performance/conversion claim %q without [vendor claim] or source citation", matches[0]),
					Remediation: "Ground the statistic in a cited benchmark or label first-party figures explicitly with [vendor claim].",
				})
			}
		}
	}

	// Full document HTML checks (only when file is a full HTML document with <html or <!doctype)
	isFullHTMLDoc := (ext == ".html" || ext == ".htm" || ext == ".php") &&
		(strings.Contains(lower, "<!doctype html") || strings.Contains(lower, "<html"))
	if !isFullHTMLDoc {
		return
	}

	// 6. Impeccable Heading Hierarchy: Exactly one <h1> per document
	h1Count := len(reH1Tag.FindAllStringIndex(content, -1))
	if h1Count == 0 {
		rep.Findings = append(rep.Findings, WebFinding{
			RuleID:      "IMPECCABLE_HEADING_HIERARCHY",
			Layer:       "impeccable_ui",
			Severity:    "HIGH",
			File:        relPath,
			Description: "HTML document is missing a primary <h1> heading",
			Remediation: "Include exactly one descriptive <h1> heading stating the primary page entity and offer.",
		})
	} else if h1Count > 1 {
		rep.Findings = append(rep.Findings, WebFinding{
			RuleID:      "IMPECCABLE_HEADING_HIERARCHY",
			Layer:       "impeccable_ui",
			Severity:    "MEDIUM",
			File:        relPath,
			Description: fmt.Sprintf("HTML document has %d <h1> tags (expected exactly 1)", h1Count),
			Remediation: "Keep a single primary <h1> and demote secondary section headers to <h2>/<h3>.",
		})
	}

	// 7. Layer 1 Technical SEO: <title>, <meta name="description">, semantic landmarks
	if !strings.Contains(lower, "<title>") {
		rep.Findings = append(rep.Findings, WebFinding{
			RuleID:      "SEO_MISSING_TITLE",
			Layer:       "layer1_seo_geo",
			Severity:    "HIGH",
			File:        relPath,
			Description: "Missing <title> tag in HTML document",
			Remediation: "Add a unique <title> tag (50-60 chars) in <head>.",
		})
	}
	if !strings.Contains(lower, `name="description"`) && !strings.Contains(lower, `name='description'`) {
		rep.Findings = append(rep.Findings, WebFinding{
			RuleID:      "SEO_MISSING_META_DESCRIPTION",
			Layer:       "layer1_seo_geo",
			Severity:    "MEDIUM",
			File:        relPath,
			Description: "Missing <meta name=\"description\"> tag in HTML document",
			Remediation: "Add a concise <meta name=\"description\" content=\"...\"> summarizing the page offer.",
		})
	}
	for _, landmark := range []string{"<header", "<main", "<footer"} {
		if !strings.Contains(lower, landmark) {
			rep.Findings = append(rep.Findings, WebFinding{
				RuleID:      "SEO_SEMANTIC_LANDMARKS",
				Layer:       "layer1_seo_geo",
				Severity:    "MEDIUM",
				File:        relPath,
				Description: fmt.Sprintf("Missing semantic HTML5 landmark %s>", landmark),
				Remediation: "Wrap page regions in semantic <header>, <nav>, <main>, and <footer> landmarks.",
			})
			break
		}
	}

	// 8. Layer 1 GEO/AEO: Schema.org JSON-LD validation
	scripts := reJSONLD.FindAllStringSubmatch(content, -1)
	if len(scripts) == 0 {
		rep.Findings = append(rep.Findings, WebFinding{
			RuleID:      "GEO_MISSING_SCHEMA_JSONLD",
			Layer:       "layer1_seo_geo",
			Severity:    "HIGH",
			File:        relPath,
			Description: "Missing <script type=\"application/ld+json\"> Schema.org structured data",
			Remediation: "Embed valid Schema.org JSON-LD (SoftwareApplication, LocalBusiness, Product, or FAQPage).",
		})
	} else {
		for _, match := range scripts {
			rawJSON := strings.TrimSpace(match[1])
			var parsed map[string]any
			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(rawJSON), &parsed); err != nil {
				rep.Findings = append(rep.Findings, WebFinding{
					RuleID:      "GEO_INVALID_SCHEMA_JSONLD",
					Layer:       "layer1_seo_geo",
					Severity:    "HIGH",
					File:        relPath,
					Description: fmt.Sprintf("Malformed JSON-LD structured data: %v", err),
					Remediation: "Fix syntax errors inside <script type=\"application/ld+json\"> so crawlers can parse it.",
				})
				continue
			}
			_, hasCtx := parsed["@context"]
			_, hasType := parsed["@type"]
			if !hasCtx || !hasType {
				rep.Findings = append(rep.Findings, WebFinding{
					RuleID:      "GEO_INCOMPLETE_SCHEMA_JSONLD",
					Layer:       "layer1_seo_geo",
					Severity:    "MEDIUM",
					File:        relPath,
					Description: "JSON-LD block is missing required @context or @type property",
					Remediation: "Include \"@context\": \"https://schema.org\" and an explicit \"@type\".",
				})
				continue
			}
			rep.ValidJSONLDCount++
		}
	}
}

// WebAuditTool exposes AuditWebDirectory as a native Mimir tool ("web_seo_audit").
type WebAuditTool struct {
	WorkDir string
}

func (t *WebAuditTool) Name() string { return "web_seo_audit" }

func (t *WebAuditTool) Description() string {
	return "Run deterministic Impeccable UI anti-slop detectors and 4-Layer SEO/GEO & Conversion checks (semantic HTML5, JSON-LD Schema.org, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, llms.txt, em dashes, purple gradient cliches, and unbacked claims) across a web directory."
}

func (t *WebAuditTool) Parameters() any {
	return map[string]any{
		"type": "object",
		"properties": map[string]any{
			"path": map[string]any{
				"type":        "string",
				"description": "Target directory to audit (defaults to current workspace directory).",
			},
		},
	}
}

func (t *WebAuditTool) Run(_ context.Context, args map[string]any) (string, error) {
	pathArg, _ := args["path"].(string)
	target := strings.TrimSpace(pathArg)
	if target == "" {
		target = t.WorkDir
	}
	if target == "" {
		target = "."
	}
	// The path is model-supplied, so it gets the same workspace confinement
	// (including symlink resolution) as the file tools (N9).
	workDir := t.WorkDir
	if workDir == "" {
		workDir = "."
	}
	resolved, err := resolveWithinWorkDir(workDir, target)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("web_seo_audit: %w", err)
	}
	rep, err := AuditWebDirectory(resolved)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return rep.FormatMarkdown(), nil
}

package tui

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/agent"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/cortex"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/llm"
	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/tools"
)

// runTUIPair drives the TUI through /pair against the given WebURL and
// returns everything it printed.
func runTUIPair(t *testing.T, webURL string) string {
	t.Helper()
	store, err := cortex.NewMemoryStoreAt(filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "cortex.json"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("store: %v", err)
	}
	reg := tools.Default(t.TempDir())
	ag := agent.New(agent.Config{
		Provider: &fakeTUIProvider{},
		Tools:    reg,
		Cortex:   store,
		Model:    "qwen3:8b",
		Usage:    llm.NewTracker(),
		Local:    true,
	})
	var out bytes.Buffer
	err = Run(context.Background(), Options{
		Version:   "0.2.0-test",
		Agent:     ag,
		Tools:     reg,
		Cortex:    store,
		StoreDesc: "file-backed test",
		WebURL:    webURL,
		In:        strings.NewReader("/pair\n/quit\n"),
		Out:       &out,
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("TUI Run failed: %v", err)
	}
	return out.String()
}

// TestTUIPairUsesServerSession proves FIX 5: /pair asks the running
// server for a pairing session (whose relay manager lives as long as the
// server) instead of minting one in a throwaway in-process manager whose
// QR could never complete pairing.
func TestTUIPairUsesServerSession(t *testing.T) {
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		if r.URL.Path != "/api/pair" {
			http.NotFound(w, r)
			return
		}
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"session":{"id":"srv-session-123"},"pair_uri":"mimir://pair?session=srv-session-123","ascii_qr":"QR-ART-FROM-SERVER"}`))
	}))
	defer srv.Close()

	got := runTUIPair(t, srv.URL)
	if !strings.Contains(got, "srv-session-123") {
		t.Errorf("/pair did not present the server-issued session.\nFull output:\n%s", got)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(got, "QR-ART-FROM-SERVER") {
		t.Errorf("/pair did not present the server-issued QR payload.\nFull output:\n%s", got)
	}
}

// TestTUIPairWithoutServerExplains proves the failure path: with no
// reachable server, /pair says so and explains how to start one, instead
// of printing a QR for a session that can never pair.
func TestTUIPairWithoutServerExplains(t *testing.T) {
	got := runTUIPair(t, "http://127.0.0.1:1")
	if !strings.Contains(got, "could not reach") {
		t.Errorf("/pair against a dead server should explain the problem.\nFull output:\n%s", got)
	}
	if strings.Contains(got, "Scan this QR code") {
		t.Errorf("/pair printed a scannable QR for a session that can never pair.\nFull output:\n%s", got)
	}
}

package tui

import (
	"bufio"
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"github.com/David2024patton/Mimir/internal/tools"
)

// PromptQuestions renders a Charmbracelet Huh-inspired interactive terminal form
// for Mímir's QuestionTool. Users can pick an option by number/letter or type a
// custom write-in response directly.
func PromptQuestions(ctx context.Context, in io.Reader, out io.Writer, questions []tools.Question) (string, error) {
	reader := bufio.NewReader(in)
	var answers []string

	for idx, q := range questions {
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return "", ctx.Err()
		default:
		}

		header := q.Header
		if header == "" {
			header = fmt.Sprintf("Question %d", idx+1)
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(out, "\n%s╭─ %s ─%s\n", ansiGold+ansiBold, header, ansiReset)
		fmt.Fprintf(out, "%s│%s %s%s%s\n", ansiGold, ansiReset, ansiBold, q.Question, ansiReset)
		if q.Multiple {
			fmt.Fprintf(out, "%s│%s %s(Select one or more numbers separated by commas, or type a custom answer)%s\n",
				ansiGold, ansiReset, ansiDim, ansiReset)
		} else {
			fmt.Fprintf(out, "%s│%s %s(Enter option number 1-%d, or type a custom write-in answer)%s\n",
				ansiGold, ansiReset, ansiDim, len(q.Options), ansiReset)
		}

		for i, opt := range q.Options {
			desc := ""
			if opt.Description != "" {
				desc = " - " + ansiDim + opt.Description + ansiReset
			}
			fmt.Fprintf(out, "%s│%s   %s[%d]%s %s%s%s%s\n",
				ansiGold, ansiReset, ansiCyan+ansiBold, i+1, ansiReset, ansiBold, opt.Label, ansiReset, desc)
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(out, "%s╰─▸%s ", ansiGold+ansiBold, ansiReset)

		line, err := reader.ReadString('\n')
		if err != nil && len(line) == 0 {
			return "", err
		}
		choice := strings.TrimSpace(line)
		resolved := resolveChoice(choice, q.Options, q.Multiple)
		answers = append(answers, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %s", header, resolved))
	}

	return strings.Join(answers, "\n"), nil
}

func resolveChoice(input string, options []tools.Option, multiple bool) string {
	if input == "" {
		if len(options) > 0 {
			return options[0].Label
		}
		return "(skipped)"
	}
	if multiple && strings.Contains(input, ",") {
		parts := strings.Split(input, ",")
		var picked []string
		for _, p := range parts {
			p = strings.TrimSpace(p)
			if n, err := strconv.Atoi(p); err == nil && n >= 1 && n <= len(options) {
				picked = append(picked, options[n-1].Label)
			} else if p != "" {
				picked = append(picked, p)
			}
		}
		return strings.Join(picked, ", ")
	}
	if n, err := strconv.Atoi(input); err == nil && n >= 1 && n <= len(options) {
		return options[n-1].Label
	}
	return input
}

// Package tui implements Mímir's interactive terminal interface (inspired by
// Charmbracelet Bubble Tea / Lipgloss / Glamour / Huh and smolcoder).
package tui

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// ANSI 256 / TrueColor Lipgloss-inspired palette for Mímir's Norse/Book-Spine aesthetic.
const (
	ansiReset   = "\033[0m"
	ansiBold    = "\033[1m"
	ansiDim     = "\033[2m"
	ansiItalic  = "\033[3m"
	ansiGold    = "\033[38;5;214m" // Mímir gold accent
	ansiCyan    = "\033[38;5;81m"  // Tool & code accent
	ansiGreen   = "\033[38;5;114m" // Success / diff +
	ansiRed     = "\033[38;5;203m" // Error / diff -
	ansiPurple  = "\033[38;5;141m" // Memory / Cortex neuron
	ansiGray    = "\033[38;5;244m" // Subtle border / status
	ansiBgBadge = "\033[48;5;236m" // Pill background
)

// RenderBanner renders the compact Charmbracelet/smolcoder-style startup card.
func RenderBanner(version, providerID, model, mode, effort, storeDesc, webURL string, toolCount int) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("\n")
	b.WriteString(ansiGold + ansiBold + "  ╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮\n" + ansiReset)
	title := fmt.Sprintf("Mímir %s", version)
	sub := "the agent that remembers · tiny self-hosted CLI & TUI"
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  %s│%s  %s%-16s%s %s%-46s%s %s│%s\n",
		ansiGold, ansiReset, ansiBold, title, ansiReset, ansiDim, sub, ansiReset, ansiGold, ansiReset)
	b.WriteString(ansiGold + "  ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n" + ansiReset)

	provLine := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s", providerID, model)
	if providerID == "" || providerID == "none" {
		provLine = "none (run Ollama on :11434 or set MIMIR_BASE_URL / MIMO_API_KEY)"
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  %s│%s  %sModel:%s   %-55s%s│%s\n",
		ansiGold, ansiReset, ansiCyan, ansiReset, truncate(provLine, 55), ansiGold, ansiReset)

	effStr := effort
	if effStr == "" {
		effStr = "default"
	}
	modeLine := fmt.Sprintf("mode=%s  ·  effort=%s  ·  tools=%d", mode, effStr, toolCount)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  %s│%s  %sState:%s   %-55s%s│%s\n",
		ansiGold, ansiReset, ansiGreen, ansiReset, truncate(modeLine, 55), ansiGold, ansiReset)

	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  %s│%s  %sCortex:%s  %-55s%s│%s\n",
		ansiGold, ansiReset, ansiPurple, ansiReset, truncate(storeDesc, 55), ansiGold, ansiReset)

	if webURL != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  %s│%s  %sWeb UI:%s  %-55s%s│%s\n",
			ansiGold, ansiReset, ansiGold, ansiReset, truncate(webURL, 55), ansiGold, ansiReset)
	}

	b.WriteString(ansiGold + "  ╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯\n" + ansiReset)
	b.WriteString(ansiDim + "  Commands: /help · /model · /mode [ro|edit|bypass] · /effort [off|low|med|high] · /todo · /web · /quit\n\n" + ansiReset)
	return b.String()
}

// RenderStatusBar renders the 1-line status bar shown before each prompt.
func RenderStatusBar(providerID, model, mode, effort string, estTokens, totalTokens int, local, smol bool) string {
	modeBadge := ansiGreen + "[" + mode + "]" + ansiReset
	switch mode {
	case "ro":
		modeBadge = ansiCyan + "[ro (read-only)]" + ansiReset
	case "bypass":
		modeBadge = ansiGold + "[bypass]" + ansiReset
	}
	smolBadge := ""
	if smol {
		smolBadge = " " + ansiGold + "⚡smol" + ansiReset
	}
	eff := effort
	if eff == "" {
		eff = "auto"
	}
	ctxPct := (estTokens * 100) / 32768
	if ctxPct > 100 {
		ctxPct = 100
	}
	costLabel := "cloud"
	if local {
		costLabel = "$0 local"
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s●%s %s%s/%s%s%s %s·%s effort:%s %s·%s ctx:%d%% (%d tok, %s) %s·%s %s",
		ansiGold, ansiReset,
		ansiBold, providerID, model, ansiReset, smolBadge,
		ansiGray, ansiReset, eff,
		ansiGray, ansiReset, ctxPct, totalTokens, costLabel,
		ansiGray, ansiReset, modeBadge)
}

// RenderToolPill formats a compact collapsible-style tool execution pill with diff highlighting.
func RenderToolPill(name, args, result, errStr string) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	icon := ansiCyan + "▸" + ansiReset
	status := ansiGreen + "✓" + ansiReset
	if errStr != "" {
		status = ansiRed + "✗ " + truncate(errStr, 70) + ansiReset
	}
	summary := summarizeToolArgs(name, args)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  %s %s%s%s %s%s%s %s\n",
		icon, ansiBgBadge+ansiBold, " "+name+" ", ansiReset, ansiDim, summary, ansiReset, status)

	// Show a compact 4-line preview for shell/read/edit outputs
	if strings.TrimSpace(result) != "" && errStr == "" {
		lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(result), "\n")
		maxLines := 4
		if len(lines) < maxLines {
			maxLines = len(lines)
		}
		for i := 0; i < maxLines; i++ {
			line := lines[i]
			color := ansiDim
			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "+") {
				color = ansiGreen
			} else if strings.HasPrefix(line, "-") {
				color = ansiRed
			}
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "    %s│ %s%s\n", ansiGray, color+truncate(line, 88), ansiReset)
		}
		if len(lines) > maxLines {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "    %s╰─ ... (%d more lines)%s\n", ansiDim, len(lines)-maxLines, ansiReset)
		}
	}
	return b.String()
}

// FormatMarkdown applies lightweight Glamour-style terminal highlighting to Markdown blocks
// and converts [choice]...[/choice] blocks into numbered terminal option cards.
func FormatMarkdown(text string) string {
	lines := strings.Split(text, "\n")
	var out strings.Builder
	inCode := false
	inChoice := false

	for _, line := range lines {
		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
		if trimmed == "[choice]" {
			inChoice = true
			out.WriteString(ansiGold + "  ╭─ Options ─────────────────────────────────────────╮\n" + ansiReset)
			continue
		}
		if trimmed == "[/choice]" {
			inChoice = false
			out.WriteString(ansiGold + "  ╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────╯\n" + ansiReset)
			continue
		}
		if inChoice {
			fmt.Fprintf(&out, "  %s│%s %s%s%s\n", ansiGold, ansiReset, ansiCyan+ansiBold, trimmed, ansiReset)
			continue
		}
		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "```") {
			inCode = !inCode
			out.WriteString(ansiGray + "  " + line + ansiReset + "\n")
			continue
		}
		if inCode {
			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "+") {
				out.WriteString("  " + ansiGreen + line + ansiReset + "\n")
			} else if strings.HasPrefix(line, "-") {
				out.WriteString("  " + ansiRed + line + ansiReset + "\n")
			} else {
				out.WriteString("  " + ansiCyan + line + ansiReset + "\n")
			}
			continue
		}
		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "#") {
			out.WriteString(ansiGold + ansiBold + line + ansiReset + "\n")
			continue
		}
		out.WriteString(line + "\n")
	}
	return strings.TrimRight(out.String(), "\n")
}

func summarizeToolArgs(name, rawArgs string) string {
	rawArgs = strings.TrimSpace(rawArgs)
	if len(rawArgs) > 72 {
		return rawArgs[:69] + "..."
	}
	return rawArgs
}

func truncate(s string, maxLen int) string {
	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "\n", " ")
	if len(s) <= maxLen {
		return s
	}
	if maxLen <= 3 {
		return s[:maxLen]
	}
	return s[:maxLen-3] + "..."
}
